models.persona: The chess master: master-strength player, twenty years coaching club players from their first games to 2000+, author of the four-pattern under-1000 curriculum in chess-study/MISSION.md and of lesson 0001 whose three looks became the hold. Every position named here was checked with scripts/engine_check.py before it was written down; nothing is from memory.
models.perspective_summary: What decides games under 1000 is not topics but a short ladder of looks, and the order is the order in which they lose games: a piece put where a pawn takes it; a piece put where a cheaper or unanswered piece takes it; the thing their last move pointed at; the free piece walked past; the mate in one, theirs and yours. After those come the slower bleeds that separate 900 from 1200: finishing a won game without a stalemate, moving a guard or opening a line onto your own piece, getting the king castled by move ten with the queen at home, counting before taking on a defended square, and finally one move hitting two things, which is the door to the next band. Hold On already evidences seven of these ten from its hold log (hanging_after_move split by pawnAmongTakers and by the takes_back variant, ignored_attack by its three sub-cases, free_piece_ignored, allowed_mate, missed_mate, allowed_stalemate, plus the two rewards as positive evidence). Three need a new kind of moment: finishing needs a drill from a set position (four positions verified this session at depth 30), the opening needs the game's move list and one quiet line at move ten, and two-targets needs the threat category the gate does not have yet. A human coach never knows a habit is formed from a quiz; he knows it when he goes three whole games without needing to say the word, and the games were long enough and full enough that the look had chances to fail. That is the mastery rule here, with one addition the log makes possible: the gate keeps computing the verdict even after the coach's hand has stopped showing it, so silence can be measured without the scaffold. As the player climbs, the game itself changes: the hand fades one rung at a time (not a global budget, which would switch off a look he never learned), the opponent's gifts change kind (a knight a pawn can take first, an undefended knight later, an allowed mate in one when the mate rung is current, and fewer of them), the opponent strengthens one measured notch once the five material rungs are quiet, and the drills come first from his own played-anyway positions and only then from set ones. I give one model in full, the ladder of looks, and a second, the map of your own games, as the honest alternative; my recommendation is the ladder with one thing borrowed from the map: when two rungs are both eligible, the one that cost him more material in his last five games is the one announced and the one the gifts target.

models.name: The ladder of looks
models.one_sentence_for_a_beginner: Each rung is one thing you look for before you let go of the piece; a rung is yours when I have gone three whole games without needing to stop your hand for it, and then I stop stopping it.
models.the_idea: A ladder of ten habits, each a look the player does before a move lands, ordered by what loses games under 1000 and then by what separates 900 from 1200. It is a ladder and not a syllabus because every rung is evidenced by the same thing a coach watches for: whether the hand had to stop him, and how often, over whole games. Hold On fits a ladder better than any product on the brief's list because the hold already is the coach's hand, the log already names the look that failed (category, sub-case, pawn among takers, takes-back variant, net loss), and the gate is a pure function that can keep judging every move after the hand stops showing, so silence can be measured honestly. Three things make it a model rather than a list: a computable mastery rule per rung over full games with an opportunity condition (so three short clean games prove nothing), a decay rule (a slip after mastery is named once, a second slip within three games brings the hand back), and a next rule that turns the ladder's state into the next game's hand, gifts, opening line, question and drill. The rungs are not the four MISSION patterns because patterns are lesson chunks; rungs are habits, and the first pattern alone is four rungs. The MISSION's four projects are reachable from the rungs (pattern 1 closes when rungs 1 to 4 are quiet, pattern 2 when rung 6 is, pattern 3 when rung 8 is, pattern 4 when rungs 5, 7 and 10 are).

nodes.name_as_result: I stop leaving pieces where a pawn takes them.
nodes.what_it_is: The first and most frequent loss under 1000: a knight or bishop lands on a square a pawn attacks (4...Nxe4 in the Italian with d3 played, 5...Ng4 against h3, a bishop to g5 with ...h6 coming). The look is the second of lesson 0001's three, from their chair: before the piece lands, which pawns touch that square.
evidence: Negative: every HoldRecord with category hanging_after_move, variant null (not a capture), pawnAmongTakers true, whatever the outcome (back, anyway, ended) and, once the hand is off for this rung, the new outcome 'quiet' (the gate matched, the move landed, the opponent took).
Neutral for mastery, used only for copy: the taps on those holds (right first tap, partial, wrong, named); a right first tap on the second wrong-tap glow still counts as a hold against the rung.
Opportunity: player moves in the window (ceil(plies/2) per game); pawns are on every board so no further exposure test is needed.
Ignored: holds in the tutorial position, and holds in 'again' drills (those count only for the rung they resumed).
nodes.mastery_rule: Over the last three full games (a full game has plies >= 40, or ended in mate-win or resign at any length; give-ups under forty plies are not full), zero records of this rung's kind in holds (outcomes back, anyway, ended, quiet) and at least sixty player moves summed across the three. Computed as quiet(log) in path.js; a unit test feeds three synthetic clean games of 44, 52 and 60 plies and expects quiet, and three of 24 plies and expects not quiet.
nodes.how_it_is_practised: While current: the next game's opening line names it in words from the last game's count ('Three pawns took a piece last game. Before the piece lands, the pawns that touch that square.'); every hold of this kind asks in the remembering form at 0 ms ('Hold on. The pawns again. Which one reaches that square? Tap it.'), a template with a Claude-written variant after consent; the opponent's gifts are of kind 'pawn' only (a minor piece a pawn can take, the giftCandidates filter attackedByPawn), so the same look that saves his knight wins theirs; the close card's path line counts this rung's holds in words. The hand is on for every unmastered rung from game one; what the rung changes is what is announced, asked and given.
nodes.retire_or_decay: Quiet: the hold of this kind no longer fires; the gate still computes it and logs outcome 'quiet' with netLoss; the close card says 'The pawns, once: I let it go. You had been quiet for four games.' One slip after quiet is named on the close card and in the next opening line; a second slip within any three consecutive full games wakes the rung (hand back, the path page reads 'Back for now.'), and a woken rung needs two full games of silence, not three, to go quiet again.

nodes.name_as_result: I stop leaving pieces where a cheaper piece, or one nobody answers, takes them.
nodes.what_it_is: The same look with a piece instead of a pawn as the taker: a queen to a square a knight reaches, a rook where a bishop takes it, a knight left attacked and undefended. Harder than the pawn look because the taker's line is longer and the counting of defenders starts to matter.
evidence: Negative: HoldRecords with category hanging_after_move, variant null, pawnAmongTakers false, any outcome including 'quiet'.
Positive (copy only): 'escaped' rewards where the attacker was a piece, recorded as a per-game count once the game record carries it.

Opportunity: player moves in the window; also at least one game in the window in which the bot's record shows a sampled or gift move that attacked a piece of his (the bot attacks something nearly every game; the condition exists so a three-game window of book-only openings and early resignations cannot pass).
nodes.mastery_rule: Last three full games, zero records of this kind, at least sixty player moves, and pawn-look is quiet (a piece look that is quiet while the pawn look still needs the hand is luck, not a habit). Evaluated after pawn-look in ladder order in one pass so the prerequisite's state is known.
nodes.how_it_is_practised: While current: gifts switch to kind 'undefended' only (a bot minor attacked by his piece and defended by nothing, never a pawn-takeable one), so the free piece in front of him needs the piece look to see; the remembering question for this kind reads 'Hold on. Not a pawn this time. What reaches that square? Tap it.'; the opening line names the taker of the last game's holds in piece words ('Last game their bishop took twice. Look along the long lines.'). Rate stays 0.12 until a clean game, then 0.08 as now.
nodes.retire_or_decay: As pawn-look: quiet turns the hold of this kind off and logs it; one slip named, a second slip within three full games wakes it; two full games of silence to re-quiet.

nodes.name_as_result: I answer what their last move pointed at.
nodes.what_it_is: Lesson 0001's first look: what did their last move attack. Under 1000 the player looks at his own move's square before the opponent's last move, and castles into a lost bishop (the Ruy after 3...a6: O-O instead of Ba4). This is the ignored_attack 'already' sub-case: the piece was attacked before his move and his move did not answer it.
evidence: Negative: HoldRecords with category ignored_attack and sub 'already', any outcome including 'quiet'.

Positive and the opportunity condition: 'escaped' rewards (a non-pawn piece of his worth two or more was hanging before his move and nothing hangs after; computed by gate.reward whatever the quiet budget says) recorded as game.escaped; the window must contain at least two, which proves the opponent attacked something and he answered.
Excluded: sub-cases lost_guard and opened_line belong to guards-and-lines.
nodes.mastery_rule: Last three full games, zero ignored_attack/already records, at least sixty player moves, at least two escapes summed, and pawn-look quiet.
nodes.how_it_is_practised: While current: the 'escaped' reward wins over 'free taken' when both apply in a move (today reward 1 wins), still under the four-line budget, so the line he reads most often is 'You looked. The bishop was on your knight.'; the remembering question reads 'Hold on. Their last move pointed at something of yours. Tap it.'; the opening line: 'Before your move, their last move. What did it touch?'. The bot's sampler is unchanged; the opponent attacks things on its own.
nodes.retire_or_decay: Standard: quiet turns the 'already' hold off and logs it; one slip named, second within three full games wakes; two games of silence to re-quiet.

nodes.name_as_result: I take what is free, and leave what is not.
nodes.what_it_is: The third look from his own chair: what can I take, and is it free (attacked and undefended, or attacked by something cheaper). Missing it does not lose a game, it fails to win one, which is why it is fourth and not first; against this opponent, whose verified gifts are the only way it ever gives anything, it is what wins.
evidence: Negative: HoldRecords with category free_piece_ignored, any outcome including 'quiet'.
Positive: game.freeTaken (the 'free_taken' reward count, already recorded).

Opportunity: game.giftsOffered (new per-game count of bot moves with how 'gift' and verified true); the window must contain at least two offered gifts, and freeTaken summed must be at least giftsOffered minus one (he took nearly everything he was given).
nodes.mastery_rule: Last three full games, zero free_piece_ignored records, giftsOffered summed >= 2, freeTaken summed >= giftsOffered - 1.
nodes.how_it_is_practised: While current: GIFT_RATE does not step down after a clean game (the step-down resumes once this rung is quiet), so he keeps getting things to take; the gift kind follows the lower of pawn-look and piece-look (pawn-takeable while pawn-look is open, undefended after); a free_piece_ignored played anyway makes the close card offer 'Play it again from here' (the same position resumes with the hand active; 'Answered' is the capture made, logged as an 'again' drill with answered true); the remembering question reads 'Hold on. Something of theirs is free again. Tap it.'
nodes.retire_or_decay: Quiet: the free_piece_ignored hold is off and logged; the gift notch steps down to 0.08 and stays; a slip is named ('A free knight walked past once. I am watching.'); a second within three full games wakes the rung and the rate returns to 0.12 for the next game.

nodes.name_as_result: I see a mate in one before it lands, theirs and mine.
nodes.what_it_is: The rarest loss and the most expensive: a move that allows mate next move (g4 after 1.f3 e5), and a mate on the board walked past (Qh3 instead of Qxf7#). Weighted by cost, not frequency, which is why its hand never fades and why its window is five games.
evidence: Negative: HoldRecords with category allowed_mate or missed_mate, any outcome (these are ALWAYS_HOLD, so 'quiet' never occurs for them except by the pair rule).
Positive: game.result 'mate-win' (he delivered a mate), at least two in the window.
Opportunity: the mate gift (below) recorded as giftsOffered with piece 'mate'; a missed_mate hold against an offered mate gift counts double in the copy, not in the rule.
nodes.mastery_rule: Last five full games, zero allowed_mate and zero missed_mate records, at least two mate-win results. Computed over a longer window because the events are rare; a unit test with five clean games and two mate-wins expects quiet, with one mate-win expects not quiet.
nodes.how_it_is_practised: While current: the sampler's guard that forbids allowing a mate in one for the player is relaxed to a gift: from the bot's fifteenth move, when the player is already ahead by three points or more, with probability GIFT_RATE, a sampled move that allows exactly one mate in one and hangs nothing else is kept (chess.js enumerates it, exactly as hasMateInOne does now in reverse), logged as a gift of piece 'mate'; missed_mate then holds as today ('Hold on. You have a checkmate on the board. Tap the square.'). The remembering question for allowed_mate reads 'Hold on. Their check again. Where does it land? Tap it.' The opening line names the last game's mate event in words. This is a bot change and is re-measured with scripts/bot_sim.py before it ships (the guard's relaxation must not change the 1320 and held-1320 scores by more than one game in ten).
nodes.retire_or_decay: The hand never fades for these categories (ALWAYS_HOLD stands). Quiet changes only the announcement: the mate gift stops, the opening line moves on. Any allowed_mate or missed_mate record after quiet wakes the rung at once (one slip, not two, because a mate is a game).

nodes.name_as_result: I can finish a won game with the queen or a rook, without a stalemate.
nodes.what_it_is: Pattern 2's result as a habit: when the opponent has only a king, mate it inside a reasonable number of moves and never stalemate it. Hold On's bot resigns in won positions unless it has only king and pawns against his queen or rook, so real games give few reps; this rung needs the drill from a set position.
evidence: Drill records (new store key holdon.v1.drills): { id, date, kind: 'two_rooks'|'queen_mate'|'rook_mate'|'again', fen, result: 'mate'|'draw'|'over'|'gaveup', moves, stalemateHolds, nodeId }. Positive: result 'mate' with moves <= the kind's cap (two_rooks 15, queen_mate 20, rook_mate 25). Negative: result 'draw' or 'over' (the cap reached), and any allowed_stalemate hold inside a drill.

Game conversions, counted as drills of the piece he had: when the bot plays on with king and pawns against his queen or rook, the game record stores conversion {fromPly, mated, moves} (derived at write time by chess.js over the move list); mated within 20 moves is a positive queen_mate or rook_mate record.
Negative in games: allowed_stalemate HoldRecords anywhere in the last five games.

Set positions, verified this session at depth 30 with engine_check.py mate: two rooks '8/8/8/4k3/8/8/8/R2RK3 w - - 0 1' forced mate in 8 (1.Ra4 Ke6 2.Rb1 ... 8.Rh8#); queen '4k3/8/8/8/8/8/8/4K2Q w - - 0 1' mate in 8; queen centred '8/8/8/3k4/8/8/8/3QK3 w - - 0 1' mate in 9; rook '4k3/8/8/8/8/8/8/R3K3 w - - 0 1' mate in 13. The caps are about twice the optimal, which is where a beginner with the box technique lands.
nodes.mastery_rule: At least two two_rooks drills mated within 15, three queen_mate within 20, two rook_mate within 25 (conversions in games count toward the queen and rook totals), spread over at least three distinct dates, and the last five drill-or-game records contain no allowed_stalemate hold and no drill result draw or over. mate-in-one-both-ways must be quiet first (a drill ends with a mate in one he has to see).
nodes.how_it_is_practised: While current: the close card offers one drill a day beside Again, a quiet button in the ladder's order ('Finish one with two rooks', then the queen, then the rook): the board loads the verified FEN with data-mode=drill, the line reads one sentence ('Mate with two rooks. Their king must be driven to the edge one rank at a time.'), the opponent plays full strength (Skill Level 20, depth 12) so the stalemate tricks are real, the hand is active for allowed_stalemate and for hanging the queen or rook, the cap ends the drill with 'Twenty moves. From the start, once more?' [Again] [A game], and mate ends it with 'Checkmate. Well played.' A drill takes two to four minutes and is never the primary action. In games the bot keeps its king-and-pawns play-on rule.
nodes.retire_or_decay: Quiet by drills does not decay by games but by time: thirty days without a drill or a conversion, the close card offers one again ('Still got it? Finish one with the rook.'); a failed drill (draw, cap, or a stalemate hold) wakes the rung, and one more passed drill of that kind re-quiets it.

nodes.name_as_result: I notice when my move takes a guard away or opens a line onto my own piece.
nodes.what_it_is: The two-piece look: a defended piece loses its defender because the defender moved, or a piece that was not attacked at all becomes attacked because the moved piece was standing in the way (a pinned piece moving, a piece stepping off a file). These are ignored_attack's lost_guard and opened_line sub-cases, separated from 'already' because they are a different look (what my own move changes about my other pieces) and come later.
evidence: Negative: HoldRecords with category ignored_attack and sub 'lost_guard' or 'opened_line', any outcome including 'quiet'.
Opportunity: player moves in the window (eighty, a longer window because the events are rarer than the first three rungs').
nodes.mastery_rule: Last four full games, zero lost_guard or opened_line records, at least eighty player moves summed, their-last-move quiet.
nodes.how_it_is_practised: While current: the remembering questions for the two sub-cases read 'Hold on. Your move leaves something of yours alone. Tap it.' and 'Hold on. Your move opens a line again. Tap along it.'; the opening line: 'Before the piece moves, what was it guarding, and what was it standing in front of?'. The ask after Hear me out prefers attacked_piece when offered. Nothing in the opponent changes.
nodes.retire_or_decay: Standard: quiet turns these two sub-case holds off and logs them; one slip named, a second within three full games wakes; two games of silence to re-quiet.

nodes.name_as_result: I get out of the opening alive: a pawn in the centre, knights and bishops out, king castled by move ten, queen at home.
nodes.what_it_is: Pattern 3 as a habit. The gate can never evidence it: 2.Qh5 costs 81 centipawns at depth 18 (verified this session, pgn trace of 1.e4 e5 2.Qh5 Nc6 3.Bc4 g6 4.Qf3 Nf6), under the 200 threshold, so the early queen is tempo, not material, and a late castle costs nothing on the move it is not played. The evidence must come from the move list, which the game record does not keep today.
evidence: New per-game facts derived at write time by chess.js over game.moves (the SAN list, added to GameSummary): castledMove (his move number when O-O or O-O-O was played, null if never), minorsOutBy10 (knights and bishops off b1, g1, c1, f1 by his tenth move, 0 to 4), earlyQueen (a queen move among his first four moves that is not a capture of a piece worth two or more), centrePawnBy3 (e4 or d4 by his third move).
Negative from the existing log: HoldRecords with outcome anyway or quiet, netLoss >= 2, ply <= 30 (a piece given away in his first fifteen moves), in the categories where his own piece is lost.
A game counts for this rung only when it reached his tenth move (plies >= 19) even if it was not a full game otherwise.
nodes.mastery_rule: Last three games that reached move ten, each with castledMove <= 10, minorsOutBy10 >= 3, earlyQueen false, centrePawnBy3 true, and no given-away record with ply <= 30.
nodes.how_it_is_practised: While current: a third reward kind under the quiet budget, said once at his tenth move when the four facts hold ('Castled, knights and bishops out. The opening is done.'), and silence when they do not; the close card's path line says what was missing in words ('Castled on move fourteen. The king is safest by ten.'); the book varies among its verified Black replies (the 4.d3 Be7, 4.Nc3 Bc5, 4.O-O Bc5, 4.d4 exd4 and 4.Ng5 d5 lines, chosen by game id) so ten moves cannot be memorised as one line; when he plays 2.Qh5 the book's 2...Nc6 3.Bc4 g6 line answers it and the move-ten line stays silent, which is the lesson. The ask after Hear me out in the opening prefers safe_square.
nodes.retire_or_decay: Quiet: the move-ten line stops (silence is the reward now). A game that reaches move ten failing two of the four facts is a slip, named once; two such games within three wake the rung and the move-ten line returns.

nodes.name_as_result: I count before I take on a defended square.
nodes.what_it_is: The capture that loses: taking a defended pawn with a knight (4.Nxe5 in the tutorial), a defended pawn with a bishop that gives check (4.Bxf7+), a knight with a rook when a pawn takes back. The hold's takes_back variant already isolates it. It is the gateway to the 1000-1400 band's counting of captures on a square, and it is placed after the piece look because a player who still hangs pieces to quiet moves is not ready to count exchanges.
evidence: Negative: HoldRecords with category hanging_after_move, variant 'takes_back', netLoss >= 2, any outcome including 'quiet'.

Opportunity: player moves in the window (eighty) and at least six captures by him in the window (a new per-game count game.captures derived from the move list), so a window of capture-free games cannot pass.
nodes.mastery_rule: Last four full games, zero takes_back records with netLoss >= 2, at least eighty player moves, at least six captures by him, piece-look quiet.
nodes.how_it_is_practised: While current: a third gift kind, 'counted' (a bot piece defended once and attacked twice by cheaper pieces of his, verified at depth 10 as gifts are now: his best reply is the first capture, gaining 200 cp or more), so the count wins material as well as saving it; the remembering question reads 'Hold on. Before you take there: count what takes back. Tap the first one.'; the opening line: 'Before you take, count. Theirs on that square, then yours.' The new gift kind is a bot.js enumeration change and is re-measured with bot_sim.py.
nodes.retire_or_decay: Standard: quiet turns the takes_back hold off and logs it; one slip named, a second within three full games wakes; two games of silence to re-quiet.

nodes.name_as_result: I see one move hitting two things before it lands.
nodes.what_it_is: Pattern 4's third lesson and the first idea of the 1000-1200 band: a reply that is not a capture but attacks two of his pieces (or a piece and a mate) so that whatever he does next loses two points or more. The gate's v1 rule holds only on one-move losses; this needs the 'threat' category the spec listed as an iteration-two candidate. The rung is defined now and enabled when the category exists; until then path.js reports it 'later' and the ladder page shows it in muted ink with no count.
evidence: Negative (future): HoldRecords with category 'threat': after his move, post line 1's reply is not a capture, every player reply in the pv loses 200 cp or more, the pv's third ply captures a piece of his worth two or more, and chess.js confirms the reply attacks two pieces of his worth two or more (or one piece and a mate in one). Answer set: the two attacked squares, either right.
Opportunity: player moves in the window (eighty).
nodes.mastery_rule: Enabled only when gate.js exports the threat category. Then: last four full games, zero threat records, at least eighty player moves, their-last-move and count-before-taking quiet.
nodes.how_it_is_practised: When enabled and current: the threat hold ('Hold on. After this, one of their moves hits two of yours. Tap one of them.') with Show me playing the reply and the capture as two ghost plies; the sampler's Skill Level steps from 3 to 5 for the first time (the opponent has to be able to make the double attack), re-measured with bot_sim.py; gifts at 0.04. The verdict itself is for the next band: this rung quiet is the ladder's top.
nodes.retire_or_decay: Standard decay once enabled. Not shown as 'quiet' before the category exists; the page never claims a habit it cannot measure.

models.next_rule: path.js exports state(games, holds, drills, {today}) and plan(state), both pure, deterministic, and tested over synthetic logs. state: evaluate the rungs in ladder order in one pass; each rung is 'quiet' when its mastery rule holds over the windows (full game: plies >= 40 or result mate-win or resign; 'again' drills never count as games), 'woken' when it was quiet and its decay rule fired since, 'later' when a prerequisite is not quiet or the rung is not enabled, else 'open'. current = the first rung in ladder order whose state is open or woken; when two open rungs are both prerequisite-free at the same ladder depth (take-what-is-free beside pawn-look, opening-alive beside everything), the one with the larger summed netLoss in the last five full games is current, ties to ladder order. plan(state) returns for the next game: hand = the categories (with sub-cases and the pawn and takes_back splits) of every rung whose state is open, woken or later, plus ALWAYS_HOLD; a verdict for a quiet rung is logged with outcome 'quiet' and the move lands. gifts = { kind: 'pawn' while pawn-look is not quiet, 'undefended' while piece-look is not quiet, 'counted' while count-before-taking is current, 'none' when pawn-look, piece-look, take-what-is-free and count-before-taking are all quiet; rate: 0.12 held while take-what-is-free is current, else the existing step-down to 0.08, 0.04 once the four material rungs are quiet; mateGift: true while mate-in-one-both-ways is current }. skill = 3 until two-targets is enabled and current, then 5. drill = { kind: the first unmet drill of finish-the-game's sequence } when that rung is current and no drill was played today, else { kind: 'again', holdId } when the last game has a played-anyway or quiet record of the current rung's kind, else null. openingLine = the template for current keyed by the last game's evidence of that rung (count in words, piece words from the records), overridable by a validated Claude line. questions = the remembering variants for the current rung's categories only. closeLine = the template for what this game did to the current rung ('The pawns: not once this game. Two more games like this and I stop stopping your hand for them.'), plus the slip line when a quiet rung slipped. All of this is one JSON object game.js reads at newGame() and at endGame(); scripts/test_path.mjs builds logs with a helper game({plies, result, holds: [{category, sub, pawnAmongTakers, variant, netLoss, ply, outcome}], escaped, giftsOffered, freeTaken, captures, moves}) and asserts states and plans for: three clean full games (pawn-look quiet, current moves on), three clean short games (nothing quiet), a quiet-outcome slip then a second within three (woken, hand includes the category again), drills on three dates (finish-the-game quiet) and a drill stalemate (not quiet), move lists castling on move 8 and 14, the hand excluding a quiet category and including ALWAYS_HOLD, the gift kind by state, every line at most 28 words and passing validate.templateRules, and the same log giving the same state twice.
felt_in_game: The hand fades one rung at a time: a hold of a quiet rung's kind does not fire; the move lands, the opponent takes, and the close card says 'The pawns, once: I let it go. You had been quiet for four games.' The gate never goes blind; it logs what it would have held.

The opening line of every game from the second onward names the current rung in one sentence built from his own last game ('Three pawns took a piece last game. Before the piece lands, the pawns that touch that square.'), zero calls, on screen at 0 ms.

The question that remembers: a hold of the current rung's kind asks in the remembering form at 0 ms ('Hold on. The pawns again. Which one reaches that square? Tap it.'), a stored template or a validated Claude variant prefetched at game start.

The gifts change kind and rate with the rung: a knight a pawn can take while the pawn look is open, an undefended knight after, a defended-once-attacked-twice piece when counting is current, an allowed mate in one when the mate rung is current, fewer gifts as the material rungs go quiet, none at the top.
The reward that gets the words follows the rung: 'You looked' beats 'Free knight' while their-last-move is current; the move-ten line exists only while opening-alive is open.
The close card gains one path line in the coach's voice and, when due, one quiet drill button beside Again ('Finish one with two rooks', 'Play it again from here'); Again stays primary.
Drills happen on the same board with the same hand: a verified set position, one sentence, a full-strength defender, a move cap, 'Checkmate. Well played.' or 'From the start, once more?'.
The opponent strengthens one measured notch (sampler Skill 3 to 5) only when two-targets is enabled and current; every opponent change is re-run through scripts/bot_sim.py before it ships.
A slip after mastery is real: the piece is lost, the coach names it once, and the hand returns only on the second slip, so the fade is never a trap.
models.shown: Never the first screen, never a dashboard. The ladder lives as the close card's second face: under the counts and the hold captions, one muted link 'Where you are'. Tapping it replaces the card's contents (the board above stays on the final position) with the ladder as one serif list in the coach's voice: quiet rungs in --muted with the words 'Quiet for three games.' or 'Quiet since Tuesday.' after them; the current rung in --ink, first word 'Now:', followed by its result-sentence and one count in words from the last three games ('Now: what their last move pointed at. Twice in the last three games.'); open rungs below it in --muted with their result-sentence and no count; a woken rung reads 'Back for now.' after its sentence; two-targets reads its sentence with 'Later.' until the gate can measure it. Under the list, one quiet button [Back] that restores the counts, and Again. The link row above the board is unchanged. What it never shows: a rating, a percentage, a bar, a streak number, a tick or a lock, a road of circles, the word mastered or level, any count above twelve (NUMBER_WORDS runs to twelve; a larger count reads 'many'), the engine's numbers, anything red. The copy test gains the ladder's templates (every line at most 28 words, templateRules, the banned words). A player who never taps the link still feels the whole model in the game; the page is the mirror, not the mechanism.
models.llm_role: Four moments, all quick tier, none with tools, none before the view has consented through Hear me out, every fact in every prompt computed by path.js and chess.js first, every reply through validate.js with one new rule (a rung may be named only by its result-phrase from the fixed list, masked like squares, so Claude cannot claim a rung the state does not have). K3, the close line (one call per game end, cached 24 h by game id): input is path state in words (the current rung's result-phrase, rungs that went quiet this game, slips, this game's holds in piece words, the last three games' counts in words, the drill offered, his last Hear me out sentence if any); output {one_thing <= 18 words, next_game <= 12 words}; the template close line is on screen already and the sentences fade in. K4, the question that remembers (the one stable load-time prompt, fired at newGame() after three games of log, cached by the previous game id and the current rung): input is the current rung, its last three games' holds with piece words and squares, and the template questions for its categories; output {remembered <= 20 words, questions: {category: <= 16 words, first two words 'Hold on.', no square at all because the position is not known yet}}; stored, used at 0 ms when a hold of that kind fires; the template variant stands when the call fails. K5, the drill line for 'Play it again from here' (on the explicit tap, with the hold's fact sheet and his Hear me out words from that hold): output {line <= 20 words} such as 'You said you were going for his king. Here is that moment again. Your move.'; template without it: 'Same position as last game. Your move.' Nothing else: Claude never decides a rung's state, never chooses the hand, the gifts or the drill, never evaluates a position, and the ladder page is templates only. Without Claude the game is identical minus the three lines' phrasing; every felt lever is path.js and the engine.
models.engine_role: Everything that is chess. gate.verdict() keeps running on every move whatever the hand shows, so the evidence for quiet rungs is the same engine-and-chess.js verdict as before (depth 12 multipv 2 post-search, depth 14 pre-search), logged with outcome 'quiet'. The set drill positions are verified at depth 30 with engine_check.py mate this session: two rooks 8/8/8/4k3/8/8/8/R2RK3 w mate in 8, queen 4k3/8/8/8/8/8/8/4K2Q w mate in 8, queen 8/8/8/3k4/8/8/8/3QK3 w mate in 9, rook 4k3/8/8/8/8/8/8/R3K3 w mate in 13; recorded in data/positions.json with the command. The drill defender is Stockfish at Skill Level 20, depth 12, so the stalemate traps the hold watches for are the real ones. The gift kinds are chess.js enumerations (attackedByPawn, undefended, and the new defended-once-attacked-twice) each verified at depth 10 exactly as gifts are now (best reply is the capture, gain >= 200 cp, under +900); the mate gift is chess.js's mate-in-one enumeration run in reverse. The opening facts are chess.js over the stored move list. The early queen's true cost (81 cp at depth 18) is why it is a move-list fact and not a hold. Any bot change (gift kinds, mate gift, Skill 5) ships only after scripts/bot_sim.py reproduces the measured targets within one game in ten.
models.persistence: store.js keeps its {get, set, append, list} interface and gains a mirror. Changes to shapes: GameSummary adds moves (SAN list), escaped, giftsOffered, captures, castledMove, minorsOutBy10, earlyQueen, centrePawnBy3, conversion; HoldRecord gains outcome 'quiet' for suppressed verdicts (pair rule, quiet rule, and now the faded hand), written where givenAway is incremented today; a new key holdon.v1.drills (last 20 DrillRecords). KEEP.GAMES rises from 5 to 12 and KEEP.HOLDS from 30 to 80 because the widest window is five full games plus the slips rule's three. The path state is never stored: it is a pure function of the log recomputed at newGame() and endGame() in well under a millisecond, so there is nothing to drift. When db and user resolve in the viewer, store.js mirrors games, holds and drills to data/users/{self}/{games,holds,drills} (writes need interact; the owner always has it) and on load merges by id with localStorage, newest date wins, so the ladder is the same on the laptop and the phone; outside the viewer, or for a friend sent a Viewer link, localStorage alone and no copy mentions devices. Consent stays per view and unstored. KEYS.GIFT_RATE stays as the notch the plan computes into.
models.first_session: Identical to today for the first fifteen minutes: the tutorial on the Italian, the first hold, both buttons, a real game, the close card with its counts and captions. New on that first close card: one path line in the coach's voice ('First rung: pieces where a pawn takes them. I will stop your hand for everything; this is the one I am counting.') and the muted link 'Where you are', which shows the ladder with one rung in ink and the rest in muted ink without counts. Zero Claude calls unless he pressed Hear me out. His second game opens with the rung named from his own first game ('Two pawns took a piece last game. Before the piece lands, the pawns that touch that square.'), and if a hold of that kind fires it asks in the remembering form. If he is a returner who never hangs to pawns, three full games later pawn-look, piece-look and their-last-move can all go quiet together (out-of-order quiet is allowed where prerequisites are met in the same pass) and the ladder places him at the free piece or the guards without a placement test: the first three games are the placement.
models.why_new: Chess.com Lessons, Lichess Practice and Chessable measure learning inside the lesson and infer nothing from play; Aimchess reads online games into a stats dashboard and prescribes drills from it; Dr. Wolf counts skills from its own interruptions but never stops interrupting, never lets the hand fade, and names the problem; Duolingo's road counts XP. None defines mastery as the coach's measured silence over whole real games with an opportunity condition, none keeps judging after the scaffold is withdrawn so the silence is honest, none changes the opponent's gifts by the rung the player is on, and none builds its drills first from the player's own played-anyway moments and only then from set positions. The model is explainable in one sentence to a beginner, computable from a log the page already writes plus three small fields, and testable without a browser.
risks: Accidental mastery from three short or empty games: the full-game rule, the summed player-move floors and the per-rung opportunity conditions (escapes, gifts offered, captures, reaching move ten) are the defence, each with a synthetic-log test; the thresholds are named constants in path.js and the first three weeks of Sambudh's log decide them.

The faded hand costs him a real piece and feels like betrayal: the close card names it the same game, the first slip never brings the hand back silently, the second does, and mates never fade. If his log shows a quiet rung slipping twice in its first three faded games more than once, the fade is delayed by one game (a constant).

Every opponent lever (gift kinds, the mate gift, Skill 5, rates below 0.08) changes a measured recipe: none ships until scripts/bot_sim.py reproduces the 1320 and held-1320 targets within one game in ten; the constants stay named in contract.js.
Drills eat his ten to fifteen minutes: capped at 15 to 25 moves, offered once a day, never the primary button, and a drill is a state of the same page he leaves with one tap.

The opening rung needs the move list in the game record (a shape change) and a third reward kind inside the four-line budget; the silence scenario (at most four lines in a twenty-move clean game) must still pass with it.

Claude narrating a rung he has not earned: path state is in the prompt as words, the validator masks rung phrases against the fixed list and rejects any other, counts are words, and the template line is always on screen first.
The ladder page turning into a dashboard under 'for clarity': the copy test covers its templates; one serif list, counts in words to twelve, no marks that are not words.

localStorage's five-game window is too short for the five-game rules: KEEP rises to twelve games and eighty holds; the db mirror is what makes the ladder survive the move to the phone, and until db resolves the copy promises nothing across devices.
two-targets is defined but not measurable until the threat category exists; the page shows it as 'Later.' and never claims it quiet, and the ladder's top is honestly the next band's door.

models.name: The map of your own games
models.one_sentence_for_a_beginner: I work on whatever cost you the most pieces in your last five games, and I stop stopping your hand for a look once it has been quiet for three games.
models.the_idea: Not a fixed ladder but a map of five looks weighted by the player's own log: the next thing is the look that cost him the most material in his last five full games, the hand fades by a global per-game budget that falls toward zero across clean games (the spec's deferred 'fading hand'), and the opponent's gifts are chosen to target the costly look. It fits Hold On because the hold log already carries netLoss per record, so cost is a sum, and because it is what a human coach does with a stack of a student's games: reads them, finds the bleeding, and works there. It is the honest alternative to the ladder: more personal, less orderly. I recommend the ladder with this model's cost-weighting as the tie-break between eligible rungs and its targeted gift kind; on its own, the map has a cold start of five games and an unstable 'now' that flips between games, and its global hand budget can switch off a look he never learned, which is the one thing a coach must not do.

nodes.name_as_result: I stop giving pieces away with my own move.
nodes.what_it_is: Everything hanging_after_move: a piece put where a pawn or a piece takes it, and a capture on a defended square that loses the exchange. Pattern 1's first and second lessons as one look.
evidence: Negative, weighted: HoldRecords with category hanging_after_move, any outcome including 'quiet', cost = netLoss (two or more by construction).
Opportunity: player moves in the window.
nodes.mastery_rule: Cost zero over the last three full games with at least sixty player moves. Cost over the last five full games decides whether it is the current look.
nodes.how_it_is_practised: When current: gifts of kind 'pawn' (the simplest free piece) at 0.12; the remembering questions for hanging holds; the opening line names the taker that cost most last game.
nodes.retire_or_decay: Quiet while cost stays zero; any record of its kind adds to the cost and the next game's argmax may make it current again; no separate wake rule.

nodes.name_as_result: I answer what their last move pointed at, and I do not uncover my own pieces.
nodes.what_it_is: Everything ignored_attack: already attacked, lost its guard, opened a line. Pattern 1's first look and pattern 4's first lesson as one look.
evidence: Negative, weighted: HoldRecords with category ignored_attack (all sub-cases), cost = netLoss.
Positive and opportunity: game.escaped counts, at least two in the window.
nodes.mastery_rule: Cost zero over the last three full games, sixty player moves, two escapes.
nodes.how_it_is_practised: When current: the 'escaped' reward takes priority for words; the remembering questions for the three sub-cases; the opening line: 'Before your move, their last move.'
nodes.retire_or_decay: By cost, as pieces.

nodes.name_as_result: I take what is free.
nodes.what_it_is: free_piece_ignored and the gifts: pattern 1's capture look.
evidence: Negative, weighted: free_piece_ignored records, cost = netLoss (the value of the piece walked past, or value minus cheapest attacker).
Positive: freeTaken; opportunity: giftsOffered >= 2 in the window.
nodes.mastery_rule: Cost zero over the last three full games with giftsOffered >= 2 and freeTaken >= giftsOffered - 1.
nodes.how_it_is_practised: When current: GIFT_RATE held at 0.12, gift kind 'undefended' (a piece that needs the free look, not the pawn look), 'Play it again from here' offered for any free_piece_ignored played anyway.
nodes.retire_or_decay: By cost; the gift notch steps down when quiet.

nodes.name_as_result: I see mates in one, I deliver mine, and I never stalemate.
nodes.what_it_is: allowed_mate, missed_mate, allowed_stalemate and the finishing drills: pattern 2 and pattern 4's second lesson as one look.
evidence: Negative, weighted: allowed_mate and missed_mate records at cost 9 each, allowed_stalemate at cost 9 (a thrown-away win), a failed finishing drill at cost 5.
Positive: mate-win results and passed drills (the same drill records and verified positions as the ladder's finish-the-game rung).
nodes.mastery_rule: Cost zero over the last five full games with at least two mate-wins and the drill totals of the ladder's finish-the-game rung.
nodes.how_it_is_practised: When current: the mate gift (the sampler may allow one mate in one when he is three points ahead, as in the ladder), drills offered once a day from the verified set positions, the bot plays on with king and pawns as now. The hand never fades for mates.
nodes.retire_or_decay: By cost for the game categories; by time for drills (thirty days).

nodes.name_as_result: I get out of the opening alive.
nodes.what_it_is: Pattern 3 from the move list: centre pawn, minors out, castled by ten, queen at home, nothing given away in the first fifteen moves.
evidence: Negative, weighted: each game that reached move ten and failed a fact costs 1 per fact; any given-away record with ply <= 30 costs its netLoss.
Facts derived at write time by chess.js over game.moves, as in the ladder's opening-alive rung.
nodes.mastery_rule: Cost zero over the last three games that reached move ten.
nodes.how_it_is_practised: When current: the move-ten line under the quiet budget and the book varying its verified replies; otherwise silent.
nodes.retire_or_decay: By cost.

models.next_rule: path.js (map variant): cost(node) = sum of the weighted negative records in the last five full games; current = argmax cost among nodes with cost >= 4, ties to the order pieces, their-move, free, mates, opening; if no node reaches 4, current = the first node not quiet in that order (so the cold start of the first games announces 'pieces'). Hand budget per game = 6, falling by 2 after each consecutive game with givenAway 0 and rising back to 6 after any game with givenAway > 0; a hold beyond the budget is logged 'quiet' and the move lands; ALWAYS_HOLD and net losses of five or more ignore the budget. Gifts: kind by current (pieces: pawn, free: undefended, mates: the mate gift, their-move and opening: pawn), rate 0.12 while current is pieces or free, else the step-down. Drill: the finishing sequence when mates is current and no drill today, 'Play it again from here' when the last game has a played-anyway record of the current look. Opening line: the template for current with the cost in words ('Pieces cost you the most lately: a knight and two pawns in three games.'). Tested over the same synthetic logs as the ladder, with the added cases: argmax switching between games, the budget falling 6, 4, 2, 0 and resetting, and the tie order.
felt_in_game: The hand fades as a whole: after one clean game four holds a game, after two clean games two, after three none except mates and five-point losses; one piece given away brings all six back.
The opening line names the look that cost him most, in words and piece names, from his own last five games.
The gifts target that look: pawn-takeable pieces while pieces cost him most, undefended ones while free does, an allowed mate when mates does.
The remembering question is asked for the current look's categories.
The close card line says what the game did to the cost ('Nothing given away this game. Four holds next game, not six.').
models.shown: The same second face of the close card, but ordered by cost rather than by rung: five serif lines, the costly look first and in --ink ('What cost you most lately: pieces given away with your own move. A knight and two pawns in three games.'), the others in --muted in descending cost with their cost in piece words or 'Quiet.' A line for the hand: 'Next game I stop your hand four times at most.' Never a number as a numeral, never a bar, never a percentage.
models.llm_role: The same K3 close line and K5 drill line as the ladder, with the cost summary in piece words in the prompt instead of rung states; K4's remembering questions for the current look. The map adds one thing Claude does well that a table cannot: it reads the five games' holds as a story ('Both knights went where a pawn could reach them, both on the queen's side') and writes the close line from it; validated by the same pipeline. Without Claude: the cost template lines.
models.engine_role: Identical to the ladder: every record's netLoss comes from the gate's engine-and-chess.js verdict; the drill positions and the gift kinds are the same verified ones; the opening facts are chess.js over the move list.
models.persistence: The same shape changes and keys as the ladder (moves, escaped, giftsOffered, captures, opening facts, 'quiet' outcomes, holdon.v1.drills, KEEP raised, db mirror); the hand budget is derived from the last games' givenAway and never stored.
models.first_session: Identical to today; the first close card says 'I will work on whatever costs you most. For now: pieces given away with your own move.' and the map shows five lines with the first in ink. The cost ordering means nothing until the fifth game, which is this model's weakness: for four games it is the ladder's first rung by default.
models.why_new: Aimchess computes weaknesses from online games into a dashboard; this computes them from the coach's own holds inside the game, in piece words, and acts on them in the next game's gifts and hand rather than prescribing a drill elsewhere. The global fading hand is the spec's deferred idea made exact and testable.
risks: Cold start: five games before the cost ordering means anything; the default order covers it but the copy must not claim a reading before game five.

An unstable 'now': the current look can flip every game; a beginner feels pulled about. The ladder's fixed order is the cure, which is why the cost belongs inside the ladder as a tie-break and not above it.

The global hand budget switches off holds for looks he never learned once he has three clean games; a clean game is not the same as a learned look. Mates and five-point losses are the only exceptions, and that is not enough; per-rung fading is safer.
Weighting by netLoss makes one queen hang outweigh five knight hangs, which is the opposite of how habits form; a cap per record (five) softens it but the sum is still a cost, not a habit count.

models.persona: The learning scientist: skill acquisition, mastery learning, deliberate practice, spaced retrieval, knowledge tracing (Bayesian and Elo-style), zone of proximal development, interleaving.
models.perspective_summary: Hold On's hold log is a record of failures, not of tests, and a mastery model built on counts of holds per game rewards two things it should not: the player who never puts a piece near the enemy, and the game in which the opponent never attacked anything. The honest unit is the exposure: a player move on which the position actually tested a look, with a pass or a fail. Every exposure predicate is computable from facts the page already builds on every drop (factsBefore, the pre-search, factsAfter, the verdict), and the verdict runs even when a hold is suppressed, so the coach's hand can fade without losing a single data point. On that ledger a per-look Beta-Bernoulli estimate with per-game forgetting and a credible upper bound is both defensible and sayable in one sentence (a look is yours when the game has tested it often and you passed nearly every time lately); it refuses to call one slip in eighty 'learned' and refuses to call sixty clean exposures 'luck'. The scaffold then fades per look in three stages (ask, pause, let go), the un-cued stage being the real retrieval test, with one-stage regression on a slip, which makes a false mastery cheap. Because the only sessions are games, review is not a calendar: the opponent manufactures the exposures the model wants (gifts, asking moves) at rates the model sets, and the hand returns for one game after an absence. The next node is the look costing the most pieces among those whose prerequisites hold; tap grades separate 'can see it when asked' from 'looks before moving' and choose between the drill and more reps. I offer two models: the Looks Ledger (exposure-based, nine looks, recommended) and the Game Ladder (the master's own three-of-five rule over four patterns, cheap and honest about being censored and coarse); the second works best as the words layer over the first.

models.name: The Looks Ledger
models.one_sentence_for_a_beginner: Each look becomes yours when the game has tested it often and you passed nearly every time lately; then my hand lets go of that look and moves to the one that is costing you most.
models.the_idea: A ledger of exposures, not a tally of holds: knowledge tracing per look (a Beta-Bernoulli estimate of the fail rate per exposure with per-game forgetting, the simplest honest cousin of BKT), a three-stage fading scaffold per look whose un-cued stage is the real test (Wood, Bruner and Ross made measurable), and an opponent that manufactures the exposures the model wants (deliberate practice scheduled by the bot, not by a calendar). Why it fits Hold On: on every drop the page already has factsBefore, the pre-search, factsAfter and the verdict, which together say whether the position tested a look and whether he passed; the verdict is still categorised when a hold is suppressed, so fading the hand loses no evidence; and the hold is itself the cue, so the stages map onto the existing states (ask = today's hold; pause = 'Hold on. Look once more.' with both buttons at once; let-go = silence, the capture lands, one honest sentence). The log is sparse, noisy and censored, and each defect has one answer: exposures fix censoring (a clean game with no contact moves is no evidence, correctly), the credible bound fixes noise (one slip in eighty is not mastery, sixty clean is not luck), forgetting fixes staleness (the window is about seven games), and one-step regression fixes the cost of being wrong (a false mastery costs one let-go slip, which is felt and named). Shape in code: app/js/path.js, pure, no DOM, no engine: exposures(chessBefore, factsBefore, pre, lastGift) -> flags per node computed once per position while the pre-search runs (about twenty scratch moves with pieceInfo(), a few ms); trial(flags, move, verdict, post) -> {node: 'pass'|'fail'|null} per player move; fold(model, gameId, trials, meta) -> model, idempotent by gameId; estimate(model) -> per node {mean, upper80, ready}; current(model); stageFor(model, verdict) -> 'ask'|'pause'|'let-go'; plan(model, today) -> {openLine, letGo, review, giftRate, askRate}; words(model) -> the sentences the path state shows. scripts/test_path.mjs runs it over synthetic logs: a passive player with no exposures never masters anything however clean; three games of forty clean exposures master pawns; one slip in eighty does not; a slip at let-go regresses to pause and at pause to ask; a twenty-one-day gap makes the next game a review game; folding the same gameId twice changes nothing; current() picks the costliest look with prerequisites met and does not flicker inside a twenty percent margin; every string from words() passes scripts/copy_check.js.

nodes.name_as_result: I see the pawns before the piece lands
nodes.what_it_is: The look from their chair, restricted to pawn takers: before a knight, bishop, rook or queen lands, which enemy pawn reaches that square. The most frequent hold under 1000 and the one the copy already names ('the pawns').
evidence: Exposure (the denominator): a player move outside the tutorial with an engine verdict, in whose pre-position at least one legal non-capturing move of a piece worth two or more lands on a square where that piece would hang to a pawn (scratch move on chessBefore, facts.pieceInfo(sc, to).hanging with the cheapest attacker a pawn); computed once with factsBefore while the pre-search runs.

Fail (moves the estimate up): verdict.category 'hanging_after_move' with pawnAmongTakers true and variant null, whether held (outcome back or anyway), suppressed ('pair', 'quiet') or let go (new suppressed value 'faded'); a fail counts as an exposure even if the predicate had missed it.
Pass (moves it down): an exposure move with no such fail, including moves the engine accepts at cpLoss under 200 although a pawn attacks the landing square (a pin, compensation).

Side channel, not in the estimate: the first tap of each hold of this node, right at once versus wrong; firstTapRight/firstTapN under 0.5 over three or more holds marks the node perception-weak (gets the drill), at or above 0.5 habit-weak (gets reps).
Not evidence: take-back versus play-anyway (a decision, not the look), cold-engine moves, tutorial holds, coachShown.
nodes.mastery_rule: Posterior Beta(1 + A, 19 + B) where A and B are the fail and pass counts discounted per game played (lambda 0.85 per game; one extra lambda per full fourteen days without a game, at most three). Ready to fade when the 0.8 quantile of the posterior is below 1/40 AND B >= 40 AND no fail in the last two games that had at least one exposure. In numbers: about 45 clean exposures with no slip (a game and a half of open play), or about 130 after one slip, fewer as the slip fades.
nodes.how_it_is_practised: When current: the game opens with 'One thing this game: before the piece lands, the pawns.'; a hold of this node, when the node has two or more fails in the last five games, asks the remembered variant 'Hold on. This one again. Which pawn reaches that square? Tap it.' at 0 ms from the template table; the K2 ask list puts what_takes_it first; if perception-weak the close card offers 'Play it again from here' on the worst fail; no opponent change (every open position tests it). At pause: the piece lifts, amber, dim, the line 'Hold on. Look once more.', both buttons at once, no tap graded, Show me available. At let-go: the move lands, the opponent takes, the line 'There it goes. A knight for a pawn.'; the first let-go game is announced at its start: 'Today I will not hold a piece that lands where a pawn takes it. That look is yours.'
nodes.retire_or_decay: Fail at let-go: back to pause. Fail at pause: back to ask (the posterior moves too, so re-fading needs new passes). A gap of fourteen days or more returns let-go to pause for the first game back (the review game: 'It has been a while. I will hold a little more today.') and discounts the counts; a clean review game restores let-go. Three clean review games in a row at let-go make it 'yours' on the path state; nothing is deleted, the lifetime counts stay in the doc.

nodes.name_as_result: I see what reaches the square
nodes.what_it_is: The same look with non-pawn takers: before the piece lands, which knight, bishop, rook or queen reaches that square and whether it is cheaper or the square is unguarded.
evidence: Exposure: a legal non-capturing move of a piece worth two or more exists in the pre-position after which that piece would hang with the cheapest attacker not a pawn (same scratch pass as pawns, the other branch).
Fail: 'hanging_after_move' with pawnAmongTakers false and variant null, held, suppressed or faded.
Pass: an exposure move with no such fail.
Side channel: first-tap grade as for pawns.
Not evidence: outcome, cold-engine moves, tutorial.
nodes.mastery_rule: Beta(1 + A, 19 + B), lambda 0.85 per game, ready when the 0.8 quantile is below 1/40 AND B >= 40 AND no fail in the last two exposed games.
prerequisites: pawns at stage pause or beyond
nodes.how_it_is_practised: Opening line 'One thing this game: before the piece lands, what reaches that square.'; remembered variant 'Hold on. This one again. What reaches that square? Tap it.'; K2 lists what_takes_it first; the drill when perception-weak; pause and let-go as for pawns with the piece words of the hold.
nodes.retire_or_decay: One stage back on a fail; the fourteen-day review rule; 'yours' after three clean review games at let-go.

nodes.name_as_result: Before I take, I see what takes back
nodes.what_it_is: The capture variant of the look: counting what takes back before taking a defended piece.
evidence: Exposure: the pre-position has a legal capture whose target square is defended by the enemy (chess.attackers(target, 'b') non-empty on the pre-board, pins ignored).
Fail: 'hanging_after_move' with variant 'takes_back', held, suppressed or faded.
Pass: an exposure move with no such fail: he captured safely, or declined the capture.
Side channel: first-tap grade.
Not evidence: even trades the gate never holds; outcome.
nodes.mastery_rule: Beta(1 + A, 9 + B), lambda 0.85, ready when the 0.8 quantile is below 1/25 AND B >= 20 AND no fail in the last two exposed games; about thirty defended captures declined or made safely, four games or so.
nodes.how_it_is_practised: Opening line 'One thing this game: before you take, what takes back.'; remembered variant 'Hold on. This one again. Before you take: what takes back? Tap it.'; K2 lists what_takes_back first; the drill when perception-weak; no opponent change; pause and let-go as above.
nodes.retire_or_decay: One stage back on a fail; the fourteen-day review rule; 'yours' after three clean review games at let-go.

nodes.name_as_result: I see what their last move attacked
nodes.what_it_is: The master's first look, lesson 0001's 'what did their last move attack': a piece of his already under attack before he moves.
evidence: Exposure: factsBefore.hanging.w contains a piece worth two or more (the precondition of the 'escaped' reward).
Fail: 'ignored_attack' with sub 'already', held, suppressed or faded.
Pass: an exposure move with no such fail; the 'escaped' reward is the clearest pass, and a counter the engine accepts at cpLoss under 200 passes too.
Side channel: first-tap grade; here partial taps (the attacker's square) count as right for the perception measure, since he found the attacker.
Not evidence: outcome, cold-engine moves.
nodes.mastery_rule: Beta(1 + A, 4 + B), lambda 0.85, ready when the 0.8 quantile is below 1/8 AND B >= 8 AND no fail in the last two exposed games; eight clean attacked moments with no slip, two or three games.
nodes.how_it_is_practised: Opening line 'One thing this game: what their last move attacked.'; remembered variant 'Hold on. This one again. One of yours is already under attack. Tap it.'; the opponent asks the question: while this node is current the sampler prefers, among its sampled candidates, an asking move after which a White piece worth two or more is attacked by a cheaper piece or attacked and undefended, with probability ASK_RATE 0.3, the existing guards unchanged, measured by scripts/bot_sim.py; the drill when perception-weak; pause and let-go as above.
nodes.retire_or_decay: One stage back on a fail; at pause ASK_RATE 0.15, at let-go 0.1 (the review rate: the opponent keeps asking, less often); the fourteen-day review rule.

nodes.name_as_result: I keep the guard on
nodes.what_it_is: The other two sub-cases of the attacked look: a piece held together by a guard, and moving the guard or stepping off the line that defended it.
evidence: Exposure: factsBefore has a White piece worth two or more that is attacked and not hanging (defenders present, cheapest attacker not cheaper): a piece held by its guard.
Fail: 'ignored_attack' with sub 'lost_guard' or 'opened_line', held, suppressed or faded; an opened_line fail counts as an exposure even when the predicate did not see a held piece.
Pass: an exposure move with no such fail.
Side channel: first-tap grade.
Not evidence: outcome.
nodes.mastery_rule: Beta(1 + A, 4 + B), lambda 0.85, ready when the 0.8 quantile is below 1/8 AND B >= 8 AND no fail in the last two exposed games.
prerequisites: attacked at stage pause or beyond
nodes.how_it_is_practised: Opening line 'One thing this game: the piece that guards another stays where it is.'; remembered variant 'Hold on. This one again. Something of yours just lost its guard. Tap it.'; the drill is the main tool here (opened lines are perception, not habit): 'Play it again from here' on the last fail, resumed with the hold at ask; the asking-move preference creates guarded pieces as a side effect; pause and let-go as above.
nodes.retire_or_decay: One stage back on a fail; the fourteen-day review rule; 'yours' after three clean review games at let-go.

nodes.name_as_result: I take what is free
nodes.what_it_is: The reward look: a piece of theirs that nothing defends, or the opponent's own verified gift, taken.
evidence: Exposure: factsBefore.hanging.b contains a piece worth two or more AND pre.best captures it (the engine agrees it is free), OR the opponent's last move was a verified gift (state().lastGift.verified).
Fail: 'free_piece_ignored', held, suppressed or faded.
Pass: an exposure move with no such fail: the 'free_taken' reward, or another move the engine liked as much.
Side channel: first-tap grade.
Not evidence: a free piece the engine calls poisoned (no exposure); outcome.
nodes.mastery_rule: Beta(1 + A, 4 + B), lambda 0.85, ready when the 0.8 quantile is below 1/8 AND B >= 8 AND no fail in the last two exposed games.
nodes.how_it_is_practised: Opening line 'One thing this game: when something of theirs is free, take it.'; GIFT_RATE 0.12 while current (the opponent sets the exercises); remembered variant 'Hold on. This one again. Something of theirs is free right now. Tap it.'; K2 lists what_is_free first; the drill from a free piece walked past, resumed from the position before his move with Show me's ghost of his own capture; pause: GIFT_RATE 0.08; let-go: GIFT_RATE 0.05, the review rate, replacing today's clean-game step-down rule.
nodes.retire_or_decay: A gift ignored at let-go returns to pause and GIFT_RATE to 0.08; at pause to ask and 0.12; the fourteen-day review rule.

nodes.name_as_result: I see their mate before it lands
nodes.what_it_is: The master's pattern 4 look that the gate can see: the mate in one the opponent has next move, mostly the queen near his king.
evidence: Exposure: in the pre-position with the turn passed to Black (chess.js on the FEN with 'b' to move and en passant cleared, skipped when White is in check), Black has a mate in one via facts.mateInOneMoves; plus any fail.
Fail: 'allowed_mate' (always held: ALWAYS_HOLD), or a game lost by mate whose final move had no verdict because the engine was cold.
Pass: an exposure move after which post.replyMateIn !== 1.
Not evidence: tap grades (too sparse); outcome.
nodes.mastery_rule: Beta(1 + A, 2 + B), lambda 0.85, 'yours' in words only when the 0.8 quantile is below 1/4 AND B >= 4 AND no fail in the last two exposed games; the hold never fades (ALWAYS_HOLD is law).
nodes.how_it_is_practised: The hold itself, every time; never current (its practice is the hold); when the last game ended in a mate against him the opening line is 'One thing this game: when their queen is near your king, their check first.'; the path state says 'always held: it comes back when the game asks'.
nodes.retire_or_decay: Words only: a fail returns 'yours' to 'later'; the hand never changes.

nodes.name_as_result: I see my own mate in one
nodes.what_it_is: The mate he has on the board and walks past.
evidence: Exposure: pre.mateIn === 1 (factsBefore.mateInOne non-empty).
Fail: 'missed_mate' (always held).
Pass: his move is mate (the game ends 'mate-win' on that move).
Not evidence: tap grades; outcome.
nodes.mastery_rule: Beta(1 + A, 2 + B), lambda 0.85, 'yours' in words when the 0.8 quantile is below 1/4 AND B >= 4 AND no fail in the last two exposed games; the hold never fades.
nodes.how_it_is_practised: The hold; the close card's 'Play it again from here' on a missed mate ('Answered' when he mates); never current.
nodes.retire_or_decay: Words only; a fail returns 'yours' to 'later'.

nodes.name_as_result: I finish a won game
nodes.what_it_is: The master's pattern 2 as the game tests it: converting a won ending without a stalemate when the bot plays on with king and pawns.
evidence: Exposure (per game): the game reached a position with him five or more points up and the bot on king and pawns only (the play-on rule), or an 'allowed_stalemate' hold fired.
Fail: 'allowed_stalemate' (always held), or a game ending in a draw, give-up or start-again from such a position.
Pass: result 'mate-win' from such a position.
Not evidence: bot resignation (the game did not test finishing).
nodes.mastery_rule: Beta(1 + A, 2 + B) over games, lambda 0.85, 'yours' in words when the 0.8 quantile is below 1/4 AND B >= 4; the hold never fades.
nodes.how_it_is_practised: The stalemate hold; the close card offers 'Play it again from here' on the last such ending from his own game (never a set position: the path is built from his games); never current.
nodes.retire_or_decay: Words only; a fail returns 'yours' to 'later'.

models.next_rule: Decided at game end only, never mid-game. Candidates: nodes in {pawns, reach, takes-back, attacked, guard, free} at stage 'ask' whose prerequisites are at 'pause' or beyond (sparse nodes are never current: their practice is the hold, which never fades). For each candidate cost = posteriorMean(fail) x exposuresPerGame x lossPoints, with exposuresPerGame = (exposures in the last five games + 2 x priorRate) / (games + 2), priorRate {pawns 30, reach 20, takes-back 8, attacked 4, guard 3, free 3} and lossPoints {pawns 3, reach 3, takes-back 2, attacked 3, guard 3, free 3}. Pick the largest; ties go to the list order, which is the master's. Hysteresis: the current node changes only when a candidate's cost exceeds the current's by twenty percent. Before the first game ends current = pawns. When no candidate remains, current = null, the opening line is 'Your move.' and only the review schedule and the rates apply. In words: I work on the look that is costing you the most pieces right now, among the ones I can practise with you.
felt_in_game: The opening line of every game from the second on names the current look in the coach's voice ('One thing this game: before the piece lands, the pawns.'), a stored string, zero calls at load.

The hand fades per look, not per game: a look at pause lifts the piece and says 'Hold on. Look once more.' with both buttons at once and nothing graded; a look at let-go lets the move land, the opponent takes, and one honest sentence follows; the first let-go game is announced before it starts; mates, stalemate and losses of five or more are always held, as today.

The question that remembers: a hold of the current look, when it has slipped twice or more in the last five games, asks 'Hold on. This one again. Which pawn reaches that square? Tap it.' from the template table at 0 ms.

The opponent sets the exercises: GIFT_RATE is the free node's stage (0.12 current, 0.08 pause, 0.05 let-go) and the sampler prefers asking moves at ASK_RATE while attacked is current, both measured by scripts/bot_sim.py before they ship.
The hand comes back after an absence: fourteen days without a game turn let-go into pause for one game, said once at its start.

Play it again from here: when this game had a slip of the current look and his first tap was wrong, the close card offers the position before that move with the hold at ask; 'Answered' means he kept the piece this time; it is logged as a drill trial that counts in the estimate but not toward letting go.
Nothing else changes: the beat, the silence, the rewards and the quiet budget are untouched.
models.shown: One more state of the same page, 'Where I am', reached from a quiet --muted link under the close card and, from game two on, from the otherwise empty link row in idle; never the first screen, never during a hold, never a dialog. The board gives way to a column in the board's space: three headings in the master's words in Plex Sans ('I stop giving pieces away', 'I see their next move', 'I finish a won game'), under each the looks as serif sentences in the player's own first person: --ink for 'yours', --coach with a small amber dot (the hold's amber, nothing new) before the one being worked on, --muted for the rest; under each sentence one Plex Sans caption in words only: 'yours', 'nearly: my hand is lighter here', 'working on it', 'later', 'not tested much yet', 'always held: it comes back when the game asks'. At the top, the coach's two sentences (Claude's, or the template) and the next game's one line. One button, 'Your move', returns to the game. It never shows counts, percentages, bars, ratings, streaks, a road, XP, badges, anything red, or the words the copy guard bans; the opening pattern is not listed, because the game does not test it yet, and the page says so in one line only if asked (it does not).
models.llm_role: Claude never computes mastery, never sees raw counts, never decides a stage; the model is pure code and Claude narrates its words. K3 'where I am': one quick-tier call per game id, cached 24 h, fired when the close card is filled (the template line is already on screen; the sentences fade in) or when the path state opens; the prompt is the persona block plus the path rendered in words (per look: its sentence, its stage word, 'tested often, slipped twice' style phrases, the last slip's caption in piece words, the current look, whether the hand lets go or comes back next game); the contract is {where: at most two sentences of 20 words, next_game: at most 12 words}; validated by validate.js with an empty allowed-square set, no digits, no banned words, no question mark; rejected or absent, the templates COPY.PATH.WHERE[node][stage] stand and the next game's line is the template. K1 gains a Pathway block (the current look's sentence and its recent slips in words) so and_then and anyway can say 'Third time this week a pawn was waiting', validated as today; the question stays the page's. K2's offered asks list the current look first, tagged 'the one they are working on'; Claude still chooses, the page grades. K4 'play it again': when the drill opens, one quick call for {lead: at most 18 words, ask: an offered kind or null}, fallback 'Same position as last time. Your move.' Without Claude the pathway is identical: the stages, the lines, the drill and the opponent are all templates and code.
models.engine_role: Unchanged pipeline, no new searches. Exposures come from chess.js on facts the page already builds: one scratch pass over the pre-position's legal non-capturing piece moves with facts.pieceInfo() (about twenty moves, a few ms, computed with factsBefore while the pre-search runs and cached), chess.attackers() on capture targets, factsBefore.hanging, pre.best and pre.mateIn, and a null-move mate-in-one test on the FEN with the turn flipped. The bot's asking-move preference is chess.js over the sampler's candidates under the existing guards; GIFT_RATE is read from the model instead of the clean-game notch; both are re-measured with scripts/bot_sim.py (gifts per game, plies, the score bands) before shipping. The drill reuses load(fen) and the hold pipeline. The engine still never speaks and Claude still never evaluates a position.
models.persistence: One JSON doc holdon.v1.path {v: 1, games, lastGameAt, folded: [last ten game ids], nodes: {id: {A, B, stage, sinceFail, lastExposedGame, enteredStageAt, lifetimeN, lifetimeK, firstTapRight, firstTapN}}, current, review: boolean}, updated once at endGame by folding the game's trials (idempotent by game id). The GameSummary gains trials: {id: {n, k}} and a path snapshot {current, stages} for the scenarios and the K3 prompt; the HoldRecord gains stage ('ask'|'pause'|'let-go'|'drill') and the suppressed value 'faded'. localStorage first, always; mirrored to db at data/users/{self}/path.json and games/{id} when db and user resolve; on load the doc with the larger games counter wins, ties to the later lastGameAt, so laptop and phone converge without a merge of counts; viewers who are not the owner never write. Nothing mid-game: a reload drops the current game's trials, stated plainly.
models.first_session: Identical to the MVP's first thirty seconds; the tutorial hold is not a trial. The first real game fills the ledger silently (thirty or so pawns and reach exposures, a handful of attacked and free, perhaps one mate threat) with no visible change until the close card, which gains one sentence in the card's words, 'Next game I am watching one thing: before the piece lands, the pawns.', and a quiet 'Where I am' link. Opening it in session one shows nearly everything in --muted with 'not tested much yet', the first look with the amber dot and 'working on it', and the coach's template line; honest and almost empty by design. The second game opens with that look's line, and if the first game slipped twice on pawns the next pawn hold asks 'This one again'.
models.why_new: Every incumbent separates study from play and infers little from how you actually play: Aimchess prescribes drills from aggregates of online games (counts with no exposure denominator and no scaffold inside the game), Dr. Wolf's skills are counters, Duolingo's road is content order, Chessable's repetition schedules lines, not habits, and Lichess Practice is fixed drills. Here the item is the move, the exposure predicate is computed by chess facts on the fly, the mastery readout is the silence of a coach who stops holding, the scaffold fades per look with the un-cued stage as the real test, and the opponent is the review scheduler, leaving gifts and asking moves at rates the model sets. As far as the team's search found, no product builds a path from exposures measured inside the player's own real games.
risks: The exposure predicates are the whole model: a denominator that is too permissive makes false masteries, one too strict never masters; the synthetic tests (passive player, one-in-thirty hanger, closed-position games) and the first five real games decide the thresholds, which are named constants in contract.js.
The scratch pass per position costs a few ms on a phone; it runs while the pre-search runs and is cached with factsBefore, and the budget is measured on a real Android before it ships.

Let-go means real losses on purpose; the mate, stalemate and five-point holds never fade, the mercy offer stays, the let-go game is announced before it starts, and one slip brings the hand back a stage.
Sparse looks (mates, finishing) may never reach 'yours'; the path state says 'always held: it comes back when the game asks' and they never gate the current look.
Checking mastery after every game is sequential testing; the credible bound, the two-game guard and cheap reversal keep a false mastery to one felt slip.
The asking-move preference and the model-set GIFT_RATE change the measured opponent; both are re-simulated and capped, and the guards are untouched.
