Two devices can diverge before db resolves; the larger-games-counter rule is simple and may drop a game played offline on the other device, which the copy never claims otherwise.

Claude's narration could drift from the model; the prompt carries only the model's words, the validator forbids digits and banned words, the narration never changes a stage, and the template stands on any rejection.
Nine sentences can read as a syllabus; the three headings, words-only captions and the copy guard are the defence, and the user test is whether Sambudh opens 'Where I am' a second time.

models.name: The Game Ladder
models.one_sentence_for_a_beginner: Every clean game loosens my hand one notch on the thing we are working on, a game with two slips tightens it, and when the hand is all the way off and you still play clean, it is yours.
models.the_idea: The master's own verdict rule, three of five games clean, turned into a scaffold ladder inside the game: one node per pattern, evidence only at game level (the GameSummary's holds, givenAway, result, plies, and a stored move list), a hand that fades per pattern by consecutive clean games, and SM-2 made of games rather than days (review games at plus one, plus three, plus eight after the hand lets go). It fits Hold On because it needs no new per-move computation, it is exactly what MISSION.md already promises, and it is trivially testable. It is the honest cheap model: censored (a clean game with no contact counts as clean), coarse (about five bits of evidence per game), slow (five games per node), and coupled (one pattern mixes six looks, so the question that remembers cannot choose). Its best use is as the words layer over the Looks Ledger: the three headings on the path state are this model's nodes, and their captions come from its three-of-five rule computed over the Ledger's per-game trials. path.js exports the same surface (fold, estimate, current, stageFor, plan, words) over game summaries, and scripts/test_path.mjs runs it over synthetic game lists: three of five clean masters, two of five does not, a short game does not qualify, a two-slip game regresses one stage, review games fall at the right game numbers, and a slip in a review game returns to pause.

nodes.name_as_result: I stop giving pieces away
nodes.what_it_is: Pattern 1 as the gate sees it: hanging after the move, an ignored attack, a free piece walked past.
evidence: Qualifying game: at least thirty player moves, or ended by mate or resignation.
Fail: each hold (any outcome) or suppressed verdict in hanging_after_move, ignored_attack or free_piece_ignored, from the GameSummary's holds and givenAway.
Clean game: a qualifying game with zero such fails.
Not evidence: tutorial, cold-engine moves, games under thirty moves ended by give-up.
nodes.mastery_rule: Three of the last five qualifying games clean while at let-go. Stages by consecutive clean games: ask to pause after two, pause to let-go after two more; a game with two or more fails regresses one stage; one fail holds the stage.
nodes.how_it_is_practised: The opening line names the pattern ('One thing this game: no pieces given away.'); the hand per stage as in the Ledger (ask, 'Hold on. Look once more.', silence); GIFT_RATE by stage (0.12, 0.08, 0.05); review games at plus one, plus three and plus eight after let-go with the hand at pause for that game.
nodes.retire_or_decay: A slip in a review game returns to pause and restarts the review schedule; fourteen days without a game makes the next game a review game.

nodes.name_as_result: I finish a won game
nodes.what_it_is: Pattern 2 as the game tests it: the conversion when the bot plays on with king and pawns.
evidence: Qualifying game: reached a position five or more points up with the bot on king and pawns, or had an allowed_stalemate hold.
Fail: allowed_stalemate, or a draw, give-up or start-again from such a position.
Pass: mate-win from such a position.
nodes.mastery_rule: Three of the last five qualifying games passed; the hold never fades (ALWAYS_HOLD).
nodes.how_it_is_practised: The stalemate hold; 'Play it again from here' on his own last such ending; the opening line when the last such game was drawn: 'One thing this game: before the last move, can their king move at all?'
nodes.retire_or_decay: Words only; a fail returns 'yours' to 'later'.

nodes.name_as_result: I get out of the opening alive
nodes.what_it_is: Pattern 3 measured, not held: castled by move ten, knights and bishops out, nothing given away in the first fifteen moves.
evidence: Needs moves: [san] stored on the GameSummary (a few hundred bytes).
Qualifying game: reached move fifteen.
Pass: castled by move ten, both knights and both bishops off their start squares by move twelve, and no give fail before ply thirty.
Fail: a qualifying game that misses any of the three.
nodes.mastery_rule: Eight of the last ten qualifying games passed (the master's own number).
nodes.how_it_is_practised: The opening line only ('One thing this game: knights and bishops out, king castled by move ten.'); no hold exists for it; the path state shows it; the book stays eight lines.
nodes.retire_or_decay: Words only; two misses in a row return 'yours' to 'working on it'.

nodes.name_as_result: I see their next move
nodes.what_it_is: Pattern 4 as the gate sees it: the mate in one they have next move.
evidence: Qualifying game: at least thirty player moves or ended by mate.
Fail: allowed_mate holds, or a mate-loss whose final move had no verdict.
Clean: a qualifying game with zero such fails.
nodes.mastery_rule: Three of the last five qualifying games clean; the hold never fades.
nodes.how_it_is_practised: The hold; the opening line after a mate against him; nothing else, because the pattern's other looks (their next capture, two targets) live inside give and the gate has no threat category yet.
nodes.retire_or_decay: Words only; a fail returns 'yours' to 'later'.

models.next_rule: Strictly linear in the master's order: the first node among give, finish, open, next that is not 'yours' and whose prerequisite is met; give until it reaches pause, then the others in order; decided at game end; the opening line and the hand follow the current node; when all four are 'yours' the line is 'Your move.' and only review games remain.
felt_in_game: The opening line names the pattern being worked on.
The hand fades per pattern by consecutive clean games and tightens on a two-slip game.
Review games bring the hand back for one game at plus one, plus three and plus eight.
GIFT_RATE follows the give node's stage.
The close card's 'Play it again from here' on the worst slip of the current pattern.
models.shown: The same 'Where I am' state with four sentences instead of nine, the same colours, words-only captions ('yours', 'nearly', 'working on it', 'later', 'not tested yet'), the coach's two sentences on top; no numbers, nothing red, no road.
models.llm_role: The same K3 narration and K4 drill lead-in as the Ledger, at the pattern level, with the same validator and templates; K1 and K2 gain the current pattern's sentence only. Without Claude the ladder is identical.
models.engine_role: Nothing new; the GameSummary stores the move list for the open node; GIFT_RATE is read from the ladder.
models.persistence: holdon.v1.path {v: 1, games, nodes: {id: {stage, cleanStreak, lastFive: [booleans], reviewAt: [game numbers]}}, current}; GameSummary gains moves and fails per node; mirrored to db as in the Ledger with the same larger-counter rule.
models.first_session: Identical to the MVP; after the first game the close card says 'Next game I am watching one thing: no pieces given away.' and the path state shows four sentences with the first marked 'working on it'.
models.why_new: It is the mission's own measure made into a scaffold that lives inside the game rather than a stats page; cheap, transparent, and honest about being coarse; no incumbent fades its coach by the player's clean games.
risks: Censoring: a passive clean game counts as clean, so a player who avoids contact masters give without the look; the Ledger's exposures are the fix, which is why this model is best as the words layer over it.
Weak inference: a player clean in half his games passes three of five half the time, and one clean in three games passes about one time in six per five-game window.
Slow: five qualifying games per node, with the master's thirty-minute sessions that is weeks per node, and short games do not qualify at all.
Coupled: one node mixes six looks, so the question that remembers and the opponent's exercises cannot be chosen by the model.
The open node depends on new stored data and has no hold to practise it; it can only be measured and named.
Pattern 4's other looks overlap pattern 1's ignored_attack, so the four nodes do not map cleanly onto the gate; the headings stay the master's, the evidence is the gate's.

models.persona: Product designer on the Hold On team: owns how the pathway is felt before it is shown, the one visible pathway state inside Hold On's visual world (serif line, sand and sage board, amber as the only raised voice, nothing red, no numbers dashboard), the copy the path speaks in, and the list of things to refuse.
models.perspective_summary: Hold On's thesis is that progress is silence: the coach stops interrupting. So the pathway cannot be a thing you earn next to the game; it has to be the coach's hand itself, withdrawing one look at a time, and the visible path can only ever be a quiet reading of that withdrawal. I looked at the page at 400 px in its three states (idle with the remembered line, held with the lifted knight on the amber square, and the close card under the board) and at the data it already records: every hold has a category and sub-case, a taker square, tap grades, an outcome; every game has holds, free pieces taken, a result, a ply count. That log is enough to define a path in code. I propose two models. Model A, 'The hand you no longer need', is a ladder of six looks in the chess master's order, each named as a result in the player's words, each in one of four states (not come up yet, the coach's, watching, yours), with mastery computed over the last three counted games and the hand literally withdrawing (the hold stops firing) on looks that are yours. It is felt first as which question the coach asks, which holds no longer come, and how often the opponent leaves a piece; it is shown as one state of the same page that takes exactly the board's footprint, six serif lines in three inks with a single amber dot, reached from the two moments he is already reading rather than playing. Model B, 'Three looks, in your words', is the minimal alternative: three nodes, no new screen, the hold keeps firing but says less at each stage (full question, bare question, silent hold) until the look is yours, and the three lines live on the close card, written by Claude in the player's own words on request. Both keep every chess fact in the engine, both are pure functions over the log with node tests, both are explainable in one sentence, and both refuse XP, streaks, badges, percentages, ticks and counts in numerals. I recommend A as the primary model with B's fading words as a candidate for how a held node is practised in a later iteration.

models.name: The hand you no longer need
models.one_sentence_for_a_beginner: The coach holds six looks for you and hands each one back when you stop needing it.
models.the_idea: A ladder, not a graph and not a road: six looks a player makes before letting go of a piece, in the chess master's order of what loses games under 1000. Each look is a node named as a result in the player's own words. Every node is measured all the time from the hold log, so the ladder is an order of attention, not a gate: the coach works on the first look it still holds for you (the focus), while a later look can already be yours. Progress is the coach's hand withdrawing, one look at a time, and the visible path is nothing more than a reading of which looks the coach still holds, which it is watching, and which are yours. It fits Hold On because the product already measures exactly this (a hold is a look that was missed; a reward is a look that was made; a clean game against a punish-always opponent is a test passed), because the hand fading is the product's own deferred feature made precise, and because the whole thing is one pure function over data the page already stores.

nodes.name_as_result: I see what their last move hit.
nodes.what_it_is: The first of the three looks (lesson 0001, last-move-threat): before anything else, what did the opponent's last move attack, and is it answered. In Hold On this is the ignored_attack hold in its 'already' sub-case: a piece of his was already under attack and his move did something else.
evidence: against: a HoldRecord with category ignored_attack and sub 'already', any outcome (back, anyway, and the two new outcomes let_land and unheld)

for: the 'escaped' reward (the 'You looked. The pawn was on your bishop.' line: before his move a piece of his worth two or more hung, after it nothing hangs); needs a per-game 'escaped' count added to GameSummary beside freeTaken

texture, not mastery: tap grades on those holds; a first tap graded 'right' on the attacked piece means he sees it when asked, which K3 uses to phrase the narration ('you see it when I ask; the step is seeing it before I ask')
nodes.mastery_rule: Let W be the last three counted games (a counted game has plies >= 40, is not the tutorial, any result). yours when W is full, W holds zero against-events for this node, and either the stored log holds at least one against-event from before W (the look was tested and faded) or the sum of 'escaped' over W is at least two (the look was shown). Otherwise held when any against-event is in W; watching when exactly one against-event is in W and the same rule was true over the window one counted game earlier; not_yet when the whole stored log holds no evidence for or against.
prerequisites: none for measurement; every node is measured from every game
for being the focus: it is the first node in ladder order whose state is held, else the first that is watching
nodes.how_it_is_practised: While this is the focus: a hold in ignored_attack/already uses the remembered question variant when the previous counted game also had one ('Hold on. This one again. One of yours is under attack. Tap it.', a copy.json template, at 0 ms, no Claude); the Hear me out prompt names it as the player's current look so Claude prefers the attacked_piece ask when it is offered; the close card's 'Play it again from here' picks this game's worst moment in this node first. While yours: the hold for this category does not open (except ALWAYS_HOLD and net loss >= 5); the move lands, the opponent takes, and the line says the honest sentence ('There it goes. A rook for a knight. That one was yours; I let it land.'), logged outcome let_land.
nodes.retire_or_decay: One let_land or any against-event in W moves yours to watching (the hold returns for this node; the opening line says 'I am holding that one again for a game.'); a second within W moves it to held. Time decay: if the last counted game is older than fourteen days, every yours node is treated as watching for the next game ('It has been a while. I am holding these again for one game.'). Nothing is ever retired for good; the ladder is the band's work and stays six lines until a later band exists.

nodes.name_as_result: I look where it lands first.
nodes.what_it_is: The look from their chair (lesson 0001 p3, hanging-piece): where my piece lands, what takes it, and is the exchange a loss. In Hold On this is hanging_after_move in both variants (a piece landing on a square a pawn or a cheaper piece takes; a capture that is taken back for a loss). The pawn-taker case is the one that loses most games and the copy already says 'the pawns first'; it stays one node with the taker named in the sub-line and the narration, not two nodes.
evidence: against: a HoldRecord with category hanging_after_move (variant takes_back or not), any outcome; the taker piece is derivable from record.fen and record.best (as closeCaption already does), so 'a pawn was waiting' versus 'their knight was waiting' is available to the narration

for: each counted game with zero such events. This is the one node where absence is proof on its own: the opponent takes everything left en prise and leaves about two verified gifts a game, so twenty player moves against it are twenty tests of this look
texture: first-tap grades ('right' on the taker versus 'named'); the 'Next time, the pawns first' sentence count
nodes.mastery_rule: yours when W is full (three counted games) and W holds zero hanging_after_move events of any outcome. held when any such event is in W. watching when exactly one is in W and the rule was true over the window one counted game earlier. not_yet only while fewer than three counted games exist and no event has ever fired.
prerequisites: for focus: first held node in ladder order after their_last_move
nodes.how_it_is_practised: While focus: the remembered variant ('Hold on. This one again. If the knight lands there, what takes it? Tap it.') when the previous counted game had one; K2's prompt names it as the current look (safe_square is the natural follow-up ask); the replay offer prefers this node's worst moment. While yours: the hand withdraws for this category (the piece lands, is taken, the honest line, outcome let_land), except mates, stalemate and net loss >= 5, which always hold.
nodes.retire_or_decay: Same as their_last_move: one event in W returns the hold (watching), two make it held; fourteen idle days make every yours node watching for one game.

nodes.name_as_result: I take what is free.
nodes.what_it_is: The third look (capture-count, piece-values): is anything of theirs free right now, and is it worth more than what takes back. In Hold On this is the free_piece_ignored hold on the way down and the 'Free knight. You looked.' reward on the way up, including the opponent's own verified gifts.
evidence: against: a HoldRecord with category free_piece_ignored, any outcome
for: GameSummary.freeTaken (the free_taken reward count, which counts a taken verified gift by construction)
texture: the gate's lastGift records (a gift left and not taken is a quiet miss; a gift left and taken is a hit) if the game summary gains a giftsLeft count
nodes.mastery_rule: yours when W is full, W holds zero free_piece_ignored events, and the sum of freeTaken over W is at least two (so a player who never captures cannot own this look by absence). held when any against-event is in W, or when the for-count is under two while against-events exist in the log. watching as the other nodes. not_yet when the log holds no free_piece_ignored event and freeTaken is zero in every stored game.
nodes.how_it_is_practised: This node owns the opponent's gift rate: GIFT_RATE stays at the high notch (0.12) while this node is not_yet, held or watching, and steps to the low notch (0.08) only when it is yours; the current 'step down after any clean game' rule becomes 'step down when what_is_free is yours'. While focus: the remembered variant for free_piece_ignored ('Hold on. This one again. Something of theirs is free right now. Tap it.'); K2 prefers the what_is_free ask when offered. While yours: the hold for free_piece_ignored does not open; the move lands and the line says nothing (there is no punishment to show for a missed free piece), the miss is logged let_land with netLoss, and the close card caption reads 'Their bishop was free: walked past.'
nodes.retire_or_decay: One let_land in W returns the hold and the high gift notch (watching); two make it held. Fourteen idle days as the other nodes.

nodes.name_as_result: I see what my move leaves open.
nodes.what_it_is: The subtler half of the look from their chair (pattern 4, threat-to-piece): the piece that moves stops guarding something, or steps off a line and opens it. In Hold On these are the ignored_attack sub-cases lost_guard and opened_line.
evidence: against: a HoldRecord with category ignored_attack and sub 'lost_guard' or 'opened_line', any outcome
for: none recorded directly; the look is proven only by having faded (an against-event before W and none in W)
texture: the partial tap on the attacker's square versus the right tap on the victim ('That is the pawn. Now tap the piece it reaches.')
nodes.mastery_rule: yours when W is full, W holds zero lost_guard or opened_line events, and the stored log holds at least one such event from before W. held when any such event is in W. watching as the other nodes. not_yet while the log holds no such event at all (shown as 'Not come up yet.' and never blocking the focus).
prerequisites: for focus: ladder order; a not_yet node is skipped by the focus rule
nodes.how_it_is_practised: While focus: the remembered variant ('Hold on. This one again. Your move opens a line to something of yours. Tap it.' / '... just lost its guard. Tap it.'); the replay offer prefers this node. While yours: the hand withdraws for these two sub-cases only (ignored_attack/already stays governed by their_last_move), with the same honest let_land line.
nodes.retire_or_decay: As the other nodes; because for-evidence does not exist, yours can only be kept by continued absence, so this node is the first to fall to watching after a lapse.

nodes.name_as_result: I see the mate next move.
nodes.what_it_is: Their check that mates and mine that mates (pattern 4, mate-in-one-threat; pattern 2's checkmate): the two holds that never go quiet. In Hold On these are allowed_mate and missed_mate.
evidence: against: a HoldRecord with category allowed_mate or missed_mate, any outcome
for: a GameSummary with result 'mate-win' (he delivered a mate he saw)
texture: on allowed_mate, whether the first tap was right on the mating square
nodes.mastery_rule: yours when W is full, W holds zero allowed_mate or missed_mate events, and either the log holds such an event from before W or W holds at least one mate-win. held when any such event is in W. not_yet while the log holds no event and no mate-win.
nodes.how_it_is_practised: These categories are ALWAYS_HOLD and the hand never withdraws from them, yours or not: a mate is the one thing the coach stops every time. 'Yours' here only changes the words: the hold's question drops 'Hold on.' to 'Their queen has a check next move. Where does it land? Tap it.' is NOT allowed (the first two words are a copy rule), so instead yours changes the close-card caption voice and the narration, nothing on the board. While focus: the remembered variant and the replay offer.
nodes.retire_or_decay: An allowed_mate or missed_mate event in W returns it to held at once (no watching stage: a mate is not a one-off).

nodes.name_as_result: I finish a won game.
nodes.what_it_is: Turning a won position into a result without throwing it away (pattern 2, checkmate-vs-stalemate and the mates with queen or rook). In Hold On this is the allowed_stalemate hold against, and a mate-win or the opponent's resignation for.
evidence: against: a HoldRecord with category allowed_stalemate, any outcome; a GameSummary with result 'draw' or 'giveup' while five or more points ahead (needs a materialAtEnd field, the player-side diff from facts.material, added to GameSummary)
for: a GameSummary with result 'mate-win' or 'resign'
nodes.mastery_rule: yours when W is full, W holds zero against-events, and W holds at least two for-events. held when any against-event is in W. not_yet while the log holds no event of either kind (the common case for a player who is still losing; shown as 'Not come up yet.').
prerequisites: for focus: ladder order; usually not_yet and skipped
nodes.how_it_is_practised: allowed_stalemate is ALWAYS_HOLD; the hand never withdraws. While focus: the bot's 'play on' exception (it plays on with king and pawns against his queen or rook) is the only rep the opponent gives; the replay offer prefers the stalemate moment. Nothing else changes; this node is honest about being thin until the bot plays on more often.
nodes.retire_or_decay: An against-event in W returns it to held; fourteen idle days as the others.

models.next_rule: At game start path.js computes pathState(games, holds, now) → {nodes: [{id, state, againstInW, forInW, everBefore}], focus, countedGames}. focus = the first node in ladder order with state held, else the first with state watching, else null. The game's hold policy is frozen for the whole game from that state: for every node whose state is yours, its categories (and for what_it_leaves, only its two sub-cases) do not open the hold UI; the gate still runs and logs the verdict as outcome let_land with the honest sentence after the opponent's reply; ALWAYS_HOLD categories and any hold with netLoss >= 5 open regardless. The remembered question variant is used for a hold in the focus node's categories when the previous counted game had at least one hold in the same category. GIFT_RATE is the high notch unless what_is_free is yours. The opening line is K3's stored next_game line if cached for the last game, else the template keyed by (focus, nodes that became yours since the last game, decay flag): 'The pawns are yours now. I will not stop your hand on them.' / 'Their last move is what I still hold. Look there first.' / 'It has been a while. I am holding these again for one game.' / 'There is nothing left for me to hold. The other side plays harder now.' (that last one also moves SKILL from 3 to 4 as a named lever, measured by bot_sim before it ships). On the close card, 'Play it again from here' picks this game's worst moment (netLoss desc) among holds in the focus node, else the worst overall; a replay in which no hold fires on that move and cpLoss < 200 marks that record answered: true for the narration, and never counts toward mastery (real games only).
felt_in_game: The question that remembers: a hold in the focus look opens with 'Hold on. This one again. ...' at 0 ms, from copy.json, when the last game had the same kind of hold; the player feels the coach knows what he keeps doing before any screen says so.

The hand withdraws: the first game after a look becomes yours opens with 'The pawns are yours now. I will not stop your hand on them.'; a knight dropped where a pawn takes it now lands, is taken, and the line says 'There it goes. A knight for a pawn. That one was yours; I let it land.' The game got real on exactly the thing he learned.
The hand comes back: one such loss and the next game opens with 'I am holding that one again for a game.'; the amber returns on that look only.

The opponent changes: while 'I take what is free' is the coach's, the bot keeps leaving about two verified gifts a game; when it is yours the gifts thin out, and when every look is yours the opponent steps up one notch and the opening line says so.

Hear me out leans toward the focus: when his hold offers the focus look as an ask (what_is_free, attacked_piece, safe_square), the coach's follow-up question is that look, so the argument ends on the thing he is working on.

Play it again from here: the close card offers the worst moment in the focus look, resumed against the same opponent with the hold active; keeping the piece this time reads as 'Answered' in that caption next game.
The close card's captions already read in piece words; the path adds nothing to the card itself, so the first thing felt after a game is unchanged.
models.shown: One more state of the same page, data-view=path on .stage, entered by a link and left by a link, no reload. Entry: a 'Where I am' link in the existing 24 px link row under the coach line, present only in two moments where he is already reading, not playing: on the close card (state over) and in idle at ply 0 before the first move of a game (under the remembered line). Never in a hold, never after the first move, never in the tutorial, never before the first real game has ended. In the path state the board wrapper fades out over 150 ms (0 under reduced motion and data-fast) and #path takes exactly the board's footprint, the same --board width and height (368 × 368 at 400 px), so the header, the four-line coach box, the link row and the 56 px action bar do not move and nothing scrolls; the path is never bigger than the board. Inside: an ordered list of six lines, one per node, each one line of the serif at 19 px (every result sentence is under 34 characters so it fits on one line at 368 px: 'I see what their last move hit.' / 'I look where it lands first.' / 'I take what is free.' / 'I see what my move leaves open.' / 'I see the mate next move.' / 'I finish a won game.'), each followed by one 14 px Plex Sans sub-line in --muted in the coach's voice, 12 px between nodes (6 × 26 + 6 × 22 + 5 × 12 = 348 px, inside 368). The state is carried by ink and by the sub-line, with one mark: lines the coach still holds are in --coach (the coach's blue, its voice: 'I still stop your hand here.' / 'I still stop your hand here. Twice last game.'); lines that are yours are in --ink (your voice: 'Yours now.' / 'Yours for three games.'); lines not come up yet are in --muted ('Not come up yet.'); a watching line is in --coach with 'Came back once. I am watching it with you.' The focus node alone carries a 10 px amber dot in the left margin, the hold's own --hold with the same 1 px --bg hairline the amber ring uses, so the only time amber appears off the board it means exactly what it means on the board: the coach's hand is here. Under the focus node only, the sub-line says what yours takes, in words, once: 'I still stop your hand here. Three games without one, and it is yours.' The coach line above shows the narration: K3's sentence when cached or just fetched ('You stopped leaving knights where pawns take them. Their last move is what you still miss.'), else the template ('Two of these are yours. I still hold three.' / 'One game is not enough to know you. Here is what I will be watching.' / 'There is nothing left for me to hold. The other side plays harder now.'). The link row holds 'Back to the board'; Escape also returns; the action bar is empty; the theme and Give up behave as always. A beginner reads it top to bottom in five seconds: ink above the dot is done, the dot is now, blue below is later, grey is not yet, and the sentence at the top says it in words. First visit (after game one): mostly muted lines, one or two in blue, the dot on the first blue, 'One game is not enough to know you.' Hundredth visit: six lines in ink, no dot, 'There is nothing left for me to hold.' It never shows: a numeral anywhere, a count, a tick or check mark, a bar, a ring, a percentage, a streak, a badge, a level, a date, the engine's evaluation, a thumbnail board, a tab in the header, a card grid, red, or any line about a look the coach cannot measure.
models.llm_role: One new call, K3, quick tier, no tools, fired only on the explicit tap of 'Where I am' (so the consent dialog, if this is the view's first call, lands on a tap over a stable state with no board underneath), cached 24 h keyed by the last game's id in holdon.v1.path.k3 so re-opening is instant and a second game in the same day refreshes it. Without consent or when sample is null, the link still works and the template narration shows at 0 ms; when a call fires, the coach line shows 'Looking...' with the existing soft pulse for about a second and the validated sentence appears whole; on any error the template appears and nothing says Claude was asked. Facts in the prompt (about 1.5 KB, PERSONA block shared with K2/K1, PROMPT_VERSION v3): the six node names and their computed states; the last five games' hold records rendered in words by the page (kind, sub-case, the taker piece, the outcome, whether the first tap was right or the answer had to be shown, early or late in the game), the escaped and freeTaken counts in words, the player's own Hear me out sentences from the last game if any (a new optional 'said' field on HoldRecord, his own words in his own private store), and the rule's focus. No FEN, no board. Contract: {where: at most two sentences, 18 words in all, in the coach's voice, what he stopped doing and what he still misses; next_game: at most 12 words, the line that opens the next game; focus: one node id among the held or watching nodes, or null; ask: one ask kind among those possible for the focus node's category, or null}. Validation by the same pipeline: no square tokens at all (there is no board in this state), no digits, no SAN, no banned words, the word caps, focus must be in the held-or-watching set (else the rule's focus wins), ask must be in the focus node's set. What Claude does that a table cannot: reads the texture of the log (a look he sees when asked but not before, a sub-case that keeps returning, his own stated plan) and says where he is in a sentence that is his, picks which of two held looks to work on from that texture, and writes the one line that opens the next game; the table still decides what is yours, what is held, and what the hand does. K2 gains one fact line ('The player's current look: what_is_free') so Hear me out's chosen ask leans toward the focus; K1 is unchanged. Every chess fact in every sentence was computed by the page first.
models.engine_role: Unchanged and still first: gate.js decides every hold, answer set, sub-case and net loss; facts.js and chess.js grade every tap; the bot's punish-always rule is what makes a clean counted game a test and what makes a let_land honest (the piece is taken every time). Two additions, both engine-side and pure: the gate runs on yours-node categories exactly as before and returns a verdict the page commits instead of opening, so let_land records carry the same category, netLoss, best and refutation as a hold; and 'Play it again from here' resumes from the stored FEN with the normal pre-search, verdict and opponent recipe, so 'answered' means the engine saw no hold-sized loss on that move. GIFT_RATE and SKILL remain named constants measured by scripts/bot_sim.py; the path only chooses which notch is in force for a game, and the SKILL 3 → 4 step for the all-yours state ships only after a ten-game sim at that notch.
models.persistence: The path is derived, never stored: path.js exports pathState(games, holds, now) and holdPolicy(pathState) as pure functions, unit-tested over synthetic logs in scripts/test_path.mjs (empty log → all not_yet, focus null; two hanging holds then three clean counted games → where_it_lands yours, focus moves to the next held; one let_land in W → watching, two → held; a 38-ply game is not counted; what_is_free needs freeTaken >= 2; the_mate_next_move needs prior evidence or a mate-win; fourteen idle days → yours reads as watching for one game; focus order). Stored, through the same store.js interface: holdon.v1.games raised from five to ten summaries (the watching rule needs the window one game earlier; the 'ever before W' tests need history) with two new fields, escaped and materialAtEnd; holdon.v1.holds raised from thirty to sixty records with the new outcomes let_land and unheld (suppressed pair/quiet verdicts, so givenAway has a record behind every count) and the optional said and answered fields; holdon.v1.path.k3 {gameId, where, next_game, focus, ask, at}. localStorage stays the always-there layer; when db and user resolve, store.js mirrors games, holds and path.k3 to data/users/{self}/ and reads them back at boot so the path survives the move from laptop to phone; a Viewer of a shared link plays with the path computed from their own localStorage and writes nothing to db. Consent is never stored. The hold policy is computed once at game start and frozen for the game so the hand never changes mid-game.
models.first_session: Nothing is different until the first real game ends. The tutorial dare, the first hold, Show me, Take it back, the fresh game, the holds, the close card: identical. On the close card of game one the link row gains one quiet link, 'Where I am', beside nothing. If he taps it, the board fades and six lines take its place: the one or two looks that fired in blue with 'I still stop your hand here. Twice this game.', the amber dot on the first of them, the rest in grey with 'Not come up yet.', and the coach line 'One game is not enough to know you. Here is what I will be watching.' If the view has not consented, no call is made and no dialog appears; the template is the whole experience. 'Back to the board' returns him to the close card and [Again]. If he never taps it, he never sees it, and the second game still opens with the remembered line as today. The hand cannot withdraw before three counted games, so nothing in session one is let land.
models.why_new: Chess.com Lessons, Lichess Practice, Chessable and Aimchess all keep learning beside playing and count it; Duolingo paths draw a road and pay XP; Dr. Wolf keeps skill counters. None of them defines progress as a coach going quiet in your real games, measured by holds that stop coming against an opponent built to punish exactly the look in question. Here the path is derived from the silence, the hand literally withdraws on what is yours (and comes back if it was too soon), the opponent's gifts follow one node, the only visible path is six sentences in the player's own words set in the board's footprint with the hold's own amber as its single mark, and the LLM narrates where he is from the texture of his own log rather than from a score. Nothing in it is a count, and the first screen never changes.
risks: The withdrawn hand lets a real piece be taken without a word before it lands; a returning player who regressed could feel betrayed. Defences: it is announced in the opening line before it happens, one loss brings the hold back for that look, mates, stalemate and five-point losses always hold, and fourteen idle days bring every hold back for a game. Sambudh's first let_land decides whether 'That one was yours; I let it land.' reads as respect or as a trap.

Three counted games is a small sample; a look can read as yours by luck. The counted-game threshold (40 plies) and the watching stage are the defence, and the number three is one constant in path.js; the first weeks' logs decide whether it becomes four.

Two nodes (what_it_leaves, finishing) may sit at 'Not come up yet.' for a long time because the product cannot manufacture their reps; that is honest, but a six-line path with two grey lines for months may read as unfinished. If so, the ladder shows the two as a single quieter line until they have evidence.

A list of six lines is still a list; the design holds the dashboard off only by refusing numerals, ticks, bars and counts, by keeping the path the size of the board, and by reaching it only from the close card and ply 0. copy_check must grow a rule for the path strings (no digits, no square tokens) and the harness must assert #path is never present while data-state is held.

K3's consent dialog lands on the 'Where I am' tap for a view that has never pressed Hear me out; the coach line shows 'Looking...' while the dialog is up, which is the same pattern as K2, but it is the first time a dialog can appear outside a hold. The link's 44 px target and a stable, boardless state make it acceptable; if the first phone test says otherwise, K3 fires only after consent and the template serves everyone else.

Raising the stored windows (ten games, sixty holds) and adding fields touches store.js, game.js's summary writer and the db mirror in the same iteration as the path; the migration must tolerate old five-game arrays without fields (treat missing escaped as zero, missing materialAtEnd as unknown, missing outcomes as before).
SKILL 3 → 4 for the all-yours state is unmeasured; it ships as a lever only after bot_sim at that notch meets the same gift, length and guard targets.

models.name: Three looks, in your words
models.one_sentence_for_a_beginner: The coach says less and less about each of your three looks until it says nothing, and then the look is yours.
models.the_idea: The fading voice instead of the fading hand: the hold always fires, but on each look the coach's words thin out across four stages (the full question, a bare question, a silent hold, yours) as the player keeps answering right on the first tap, and come back when he stops. Only three nodes, the chess master's three looks before every move (theirs, mine, free); the mates and stalemate stay outside the path as the holds that never change. There is no new screen: the path is three serif sentences on the close card he already reads, and the opening line of the next game is one of them in the coach's voice. On request the three sentences are rewritten by Claude in the player's own words, from what he typed into Hear me out. It fits Hold On because the coach's voice is already the only instrument the product has, because three looks is what lesson 0001 teaches and what a beginner can recite, and because it asks for no state of the page that is not already there.

nodes.name_as_result: I check what their last move did.
nodes.what_it_is: What did their last move attack or set up, including a mate next move. In Hold On: ignored_attack in all three sub-cases, and allowed_mate.
evidence: against: a HoldRecord with category ignored_attack (any sub) or allowed_mate, any outcome
for: the 'escaped' reward count per game (new GameSummary field)

stage evidence: on each hold of this look, whether the first tap was graded 'right' against the hold's own look (ask null or own), 'partial', 'wrong' or 'named', and whether the outcome was back or anyway
nodes.mastery_rule: Stage over the last three holds of this look across games: advance one stage (full → bare → silent) when all three were answered right on the first tap and at least one was taken back; retreat one stage when two of the three were 'named' or were played anyway after a wrong tap. yours when the last three counted games (plies >= 40) hold zero against-events for this look and the log holds at least one such event before them or escaped over those games is at least two. yours can be reached from any stage.
prerequisites: none; the three looks are measured in parallel
focus: the first look in order theirs, mine, free whose stage is not yours
nodes.how_it_is_practised: At stage full the hold reads its normal template ('Hold on. One of yours is already under attack. Tap it.'). At stage bare the look's clause is withheld: 'Hold on. Tap it.' At stage silent the piece lifts, the square breathes amber, the board dims and the line stays empty; words come only after a wrong tap (the normal hint), and Show me and both buttons work as always. allowed_mate never goes below bare: a mate keeps at least 'Hold on. Tap it.' The remembered variant and the Hear me out ask preference apply when this is the focus.
nodes.retire_or_decay: A hold answered 'named' or played anyway after wrong taps counts toward the retreat rule at once; fourteen days without a counted game drop every stage by one and turn yours into silent for the next game ('It has been a while.').

nodes.name_as_result: I look where it lands first.
nodes.what_it_is: Where my piece lands, what takes it. In Hold On: hanging_after_move in both variants.
evidence: against: a HoldRecord with category hanging_after_move, any outcome
for: a counted game with zero such events (the punish-always opponent makes every landing a test)
stage evidence: first-tap grades and outcomes on the last three such holds
nodes.mastery_rule: Stages as for theirs over the last three hanging_after_move holds. yours when the last three counted games hold zero hanging_after_move events.
nodes.how_it_is_practised: Stage full: the normal template. Stage bare: 'Hold on. Tap it.' Stage silent: the lifted piece, the amber, no words. The pawn-taker case keeps its 'Next time, the pawns first.' sentence after a play-anyway at every stage, because that sentence is said after the decision, not before it.
nodes.retire_or_decay: As theirs; a second-wrong-tap naming on a silent hold drops the stage to bare immediately for the rest of the game, so a player who has forgotten the look is not left in silence twice.

nodes.name_as_result: I take what is free.
nodes.what_it_is: Is anything of theirs free, including a mate in one of my own (the freest thing on the board). In Hold On: free_piece_ignored and missed_mate against; the free_taken reward and a mate-win for.
evidence: against: a HoldRecord with category free_piece_ignored or missed_mate, any outcome
for: GameSummary.freeTaken per game; result 'mate-win'
stage evidence: first-tap grades on the last three such holds
nodes.mastery_rule: Stages as for theirs. yours when the last three counted games hold zero against-events and the sum of freeTaken over them is at least two.
nodes.how_it_is_practised: This look owns GIFT_RATE: the high notch until yours, then the low notch. Stage full: the normal template. Stage bare: 'Hold on. Tap it.' Stage silent: the lifted piece and the amber with no words; for a missed free piece the amber is on the landing square as usual and Show me plays his own missed capture as today. missed_mate never goes below bare.
nodes.retire_or_decay: As theirs; a let-go gift that was left and not taken does not count against (it was never held), so the stage moves only on holds and the yours rule only on counted games.

models.next_rule: At game start path.js computes {looks: [{id, stage, yours}], focus} where stage is read from stored holdon.v1.path.stages (this model stores stages because the retreat rule depends on the stage at the time of each hold, which the log alone does not carry) and yours is derived from the last three counted games. focus = the first of theirs, mine, free that is not yours. The game's hold copy policy is frozen from the stages: for each hold, the question template is chosen by (category → look → stage): full → the category's template; bare → 'Hold on. Tap it.'; silent → no line (the coach box keeps its height and stays empty; aria-live announces 'Hold on.' for screen readers only). The remembered variant applies on the focus look when the previous counted game had a hold of the same category and the stage is full. GIFT_RATE follows free. The opening line is the focus look's sentence in the coach's voice at its stage ('Where it lands. I will ask you with fewer words this game.' / 'Where it lands. I will stop your hand and say nothing.' / 'What is free is yours now. Their last move is what I still ask.'), from templates, or Claude's stored line when 'In my words' was pressed after the last game. The close card's 'Play it again from here' picks the worst moment on the focus look.
felt_in_game: The question thins: on the look he keeps getting right, the hold still comes but says only 'Hold on. Tap it.'; he feels the coach trusting him to know what to look for before any card says so.
The silent hold: the piece lifts, the square breathes amber, the line is empty. He looks, taps, and only then the coach speaks ('Yes, the pawn. A knight for a pawn.'). The silence is the praise.
The voice comes back: two holds where the answer had to be shown and the next hold on that look asks in full again; nothing is announced, the words are simply there.
The remembered question on the focus look ('Hold on. This one again. ...') at 0 ms, from the template table.
The opponent's gifts thin out when 'I take what is free' is yours, and the opening line says which look the coach still asks about.
Hear me out's chosen question leans toward the focus look because the prompt names it.
models.shown: No new state of the page. On the close card, between the summary sentence and the caption lines, three lines in the serif at 17 px in --ink (the close-sum style), one per look, in the player's words, each followed by one 14 px Plex Sans sub-line in --muted in the coach's voice naming the stage: 'I still ask you in full.' / 'I ask with fewer words now.' / 'I stop your hand and say nothing.' / 'Yours.' The focus look's sentence is first in reading order and carries the 10 px amber dot in the left margin (the hold's own --hold, with the 1 px --bg hairline); the other two follow in look order. Under the three lines one quiet link, 'In my words', which rewrites the three sentences from his own Hear me out words (an explicit action, so consent lands here); after it the lines are Claude's, stored, until a stage changes. The next game's opening line is the focus look's sentence in the coach's voice. On the first close card the three lines are the curriculum's sentences with 'I still ask you in full.' under each; on the hundredth, three lines with 'Yours.' and a summary that reads 'I did not stop your hand.' The card never shows a numeral for the path, a tick, a bar, a percentage, a streak, a date, a thumbnail, or any fourth line for the mates (those stay outside the path and are never scored). The card stays under the board; the board stays the hero; the close card already scrolls into view when long and nothing else moves.
models.llm_role: One call, K3b, quick tier, no tools, only on the explicit tap of 'In my words' on the close card (consent lands on that tap over the stable over state), cached by game id in holdon.v1.path.k3. Facts: the three looks with their stages and yours flags, the last five games' holds rendered in words (look, taker piece, first-tap grade, outcome), freeTaken and escaped in words, and the player's own Hear me out sentences from the stored holds' new 'said' field in guillemets. Contract: {lines: three strings, one per look in order, each at most 12 words, first person, the player's voice, built from his own words where they exist ('I go for the king before I look at the pawns.'); next_game: at most 12 words in the coach's voice; ask: one ask kind for the focus look or null}. Validation: no square tokens, no digits, no SAN, no banned words, the caps, three lines exactly, ask within the focus look's set. What Claude does that a table cannot: turns 'im attacking his king' plus a log of knight-for-pawn holds into a sentence the player recognises as his own, and chooses the ask from the texture of his taps. Without Claude the three curriculum sentences and the template opening line are the whole product; no control is ever shown disabled; the 'In my words' link is simply absent when sample is null. K2 gains the 'current look' fact line; K1 is unchanged.
models.engine_role: Unchanged: the gate decides every hold at every stage, the answer sets grade every tap, the opponent punishes every landing; the silent hold is the same verdict with the words withheld, so a wrong tap gets the engine's own hint and a second wrong tap glows the engine's answer square exactly as today. GIFT_RATE's notch is chosen by the free look's state; the constants stay in bot.js and in bot_sim.py.
models.persistence: holdon.v1.path.stages {theirs, mine, free: 'full'|'bare'|'silent', since: gameId} is the one stored path object (stages are not derivable from the log without replaying the rule, so they are stored and also recomputable by a migration that replays the rule over the hold log). yours is derived from the last three counted games. holds and games as today, with escaped added to GameSummary and said and the let-go flag added to HoldRecord; the stored windows are enough at five and thirty for this model. holdon.v1.path.k3 caches Claude's lines. All of it mirrors to data/users/{self}/ when db and user resolve, read back at boot; a Viewer never writes. path.js stays pure: stageAfter(stage, lastThreeHolds), yoursFor(look, countedGames), focus(looks), unit-tested over synthetic logs (three right first taps → advance; two named → retreat; silent never below bare for the mate categories; fourteen idle days → drop one; yours needs freeTaken >= 2 for free).
models.first_session: Identical game, identical tutorial, identical holds. The first close card gains three serif lines under the summary ('I check what their last move did.' / 'I look where it lands first.' / 'I take what is free.'), each with 'I still ask you in full.' beneath, the amber dot on the first, and, if sample is available, the quiet 'In my words' link, which he can ignore. The second game opens with the focus look's sentence in the coach's voice instead of the count-based remembered line. No question thins before three holds on a look have been answered right first time, which rarely happens inside one session.
models.why_new: Every incumbent adds words as you progress (badges, counters, a longer path); this one removes them. Progress is the coach's question getting shorter inside the hold, in the real game, on the move he was about to play, until a hold is just a lifted piece on an amber square and he knows why. The path is three sentences he could say out loud, on the card he already reads, with no screen of its own, and the LLM's one job is to write them in his words.
risks: A silent hold after a break, or on a look he has half-forgotten, reads as a bug: a piece that will not land and a page that says nothing. Defences: fourteen idle days drop every stage, a second-wrong-tap naming drops a silent look to bare for the rest of the game, the mates never go below bare, and the opening line announces the stage ('I will stop your hand and say nothing.'). If Sambudh's first silent hold confuses him, the silent stage is cut and the model is full → bare → yours.

A bare question ('Hold on. Tap it.') on an ignored_attack hold hides which of his pieces to think about, which is the whole look; that is the point, but the 8 s buttons timer and the hint after one wrong tap must be measured on a phone so a bare hold never feels like a dead end.

Three nodes leave the mates, stalemate and the opening outside the path; a player whose games are lost to Scholar's mate sees a path that does not mention it. Honest, since the product holds those every time, but the card should keep its caption lines so the mate holds are still read.
Stored stages can diverge from the log if localStorage is lost before db resolves; the replay migration recomputes them, and the db mirror is the real fix.

Claude's lines in the player's words can misread him ('I go for the king' when he typed it once in jest); the lines are shown only after an explicit tap, are validated, and the curriculum sentences return the moment a stage changes, so a wrong line lives at most one game.

Without a view of its own, the hundredth visit's path is three lines with 'Yours.' on a card and nothing else; if the user wants a place to look at the path between games, Model A's board-footprint state is the addition, and the two models combine cleanly (A's ladder with B's fading words as how a held node is practised).

models.persona: The beginner, Sambudh's stand-in: played a bit years ago, had a number under 1000 and forgot it, never opened a book or a course, loses most games because a knight went where a pawn could take it or because I did not notice my bishop was already under attack. Phone in one hand, ten to fifteen minutes, usually on the sofa or in a queue. I close any app that shows me a bar, a percentage, a red mark, or a lesson list before it lets me play.
models.perspective_summary: What a "path" would have to mean for me to care: not a list of things to learn, but one thing I am on right now, in plain words, and some sign that it is changing. Like the gym: I am on pull-ups, and last week was worse than this week. If it is a syllabus (twelve lessons, four patterns, concept ids) I will nod and never come back, because I did not come here to be taught, I came to play and to stop losing the same way. The path has to be made out of what I actually did in my own games, and it has to say it in one sentence I could repeat to a friend. What would make me feel I am getting somewhere after three games: the coach stopping my hand less for the same thing, and the coach saying so in a line, not me having to count. Best of all: the coach telling me it has stopped watching for something because I stopped doing it. Second best: a position where I gave a piece away coming back, me not giving it away this time, and the coach saying "answered". Either of those in three games and I would believe the thing works on me. What would feel like school and make me close the tab: "Lesson 3 of 12", a locked node, a winding road with XP, a percentage or a 3/5 mastery, a streak flame, a quiz I have to pass before a game, a pop-up congratulating me, the word curriculum, a drill I did not choose with no way to skip it, "you missed two days", or a screen of numbers when the game ends. Also: being told I have mastered something when I know I have not; I would stop trusting the coach. Day four, opening the page: the board, "Your move." or one line that remembers me ("The pawns are yours now. Today I watch for the free ones."), and that is all. Not a welcome-back screen, not a summary, not "here is your progress". If I want to see where I stand I will tap one quiet link, and what I see there should be words, not a chart. What I would tell a friend I am working on: "not giving pieces away to pawns; the coach stopped watching for it, so now it is free pieces," or "clearing my own moments; two left from Tuesday." Both are one thing, in my words, with a sense of done. Two models from my seat follow. The first makes the coach's own silence the path: each look I keep missing is a node, mastery is three clean games, and the proof is the coach taking its hand off that look and me staying clean. The second makes my own moments the path: every piece I gave away comes back as a game that starts right there until I keep it twice. They can combine (the second supplies the drill for the first), but each stands on its own, is computable from the hold log, is felt in the game before anything is shown, and keeps every copy rule.

models.name: The coach goes quiet
models.one_sentence_for_a_beginner: The coach watches one look at a time; when it has had nothing to stop my hand for over three games it stops watching for that look, and if I stay clean with its hand off, that look is mine.
models.the_idea: A ladder of looks, where mastery is measured by the coach's silence in my real games and proven by the coach withdrawing its hand. Every hold Hold On already records belongs to one of eight looks named as results in my words (the pawns, their pieces, what takes back, already under attack, what my move uncovers, what is free, their mate, finishing). Each look is in one of four states: not yet seen, watching, quiet, yours. A look turns quiet when three real games in a row of real length had no hold of its kind; then the coach announces it has stopped watching for it (the fading hand, per look, never for mates or losses of five or more); three more clean games with the hand off and the look is mine. One hold of that kind at any time and it is back to watching, said gently. The look I am 'on' is the one the coach has been stopping my hand for most lately, so the path is built from my games, not from a course. It fits Hold On because the product already is a coach that says nothing on a clean move; this just gives the silence a shape I can see coming ('one more game and I stop watching for the pawns'), and makes the withdrawal of the hand the test, which is the only honest proof of a habit. The eight looks are the chess master's pattern 1, pattern 4 and the mate half of pattern 2, split the way the gate already splits them; the opening pattern is not a node because the hold never fires on it, and the path only ever claims what the log shows.

nodes.name_as_result: I stop putting pieces where a pawn takes them.
nodes.what_it_is: The look from their chair at the landing square, for the cheapest taker: is a pawn one diagonal away, or one push away. The most common way I lose a knight or bishop.
evidence: AGAINST: any hold with category hanging_after_move where pawnAmongTakers is true and the best (capturing) taker is a pawn; outcome 'back' weighs 1, outcome 'anyway' or 'unheld' (a verdict matched but suppressed by the pair rule, the quiet rule or the fade, which the log must start recording) weighs 2.
FOR: a game with at least 20 observed player moves (moves that had a verdict; engine-cold moves do not count) and zero such holds counts as one clean game.
NEUTRAL: nothing in the tutorial counts.
nodes.mastery_rule: watching -> quiet when the last three games with observed >= 20 each contain zero pawns-holds (any outcome). quiet -> yours when, with the fade active for this node, three further games with observed >= 20 contain zero pawns-holds. A game with observed < 20 is skipped, not counted either way.
nodes.how_it_is_practised: While current: the next game opens with the line 'Still on the pawns. Before the piece lands, look for them.' (template, no call). On the second and later pawns-holds across games the question takes the remembering form at 0 ms: 'Hold on. This one again. Which pawn reaches that square? Tap it.' After a right tap on any other hold where safe_square is offered and the budget allows, one extra graded tap, once a game: 'And one more: tap a square where it is safe from the pawns.' While quiet: the gate suppresses pawns-holds with netLoss < 5 (logged outcome 'unheld', suppressed 'faded'); the game opens once with 'I have stopped watching for the pawns. Everything else I still hold.'
nodes.retire_or_decay: Never on time. One pawns-hold while quiet or yours returns the node to watching with 'The pawns again. I am watching for them.' and the play-anyway sentence after a faded one reads 'There it goes. A knight for a pawn. I was not watching for the pawns; I am again.' The clean-game counter restarts from zero. 'Yours' stays on the list as words ('The pawns, yours since Tuesday') as long as it holds.

nodes.name_as_result: I stop putting pieces where a cheaper piece takes them.
nodes.what_it_is: The same landing-square look, when the taker is a knight, bishop, rook or queen rather than a pawn, or when the exchange is simply bad (a rook for a knight). Harder than the pawns because the attacker is further away.
evidence: AGAINST: hanging_after_move holds with variant null and no pawn among the takers (the best taker is a piece); back 1, anyway or unheld 2.
FOR: a game with observed >= 20 and zero such holds.
nodes.mastery_rule: Same as pawns: three consecutive games with observed >= 20 and zero pieces-holds -> quiet; three more with the fade active -> yours.
nodes.how_it_is_practised: Opening line 'Still on their pieces. Look at what reaches the square, not only the pawns.' Remembering question form: 'Hold on. This one again. What reaches that square from further away? Tap it.' The extra tap when offered: 'And one more: tap the piece of theirs that reaches it.' Fade as pawns when quiet.
nodes.retire_or_decay: As pawns: one hold of its kind returns it to watching; no time decay. Prerequisite is soft: it only decides ties and what is named as next, it never locks.

nodes.name_as_result: I notice when something of mine is already under attack.
nodes.what_it_is: The first of the chess master's three looks: what did their last move attack. The hold fires when I move something else and leave the attacked piece to be taken.
evidence: AGAINST: ignored_attack holds with sub 'already'; back 1, anyway or unheld 2.

FOR: the reward 'you_looked' (kind escaped: a piece of mine hung before my move and nothing hangs after) counts as one positive look; a game with observed >= 20 and zero 'already' holds counts as a clean game. Positive looks are shown in copy ('You looked, three times this game') but the mastery rule uses clean games only, so a rewarded look never masks a hold.
nodes.mastery_rule: Three consecutive games with observed >= 20 and zero ignored_attack/already holds -> quiet; three more with the fade active -> yours.
nodes.how_it_is_practised: Opening line 'Still on what their last move attacked. Before you move, find it.' Remembering form: 'Hold on. Their last move attacked something of yours. Tap it.' When attacked_piece is offered on another hold: the extra tap 'And one more: tap the piece of yours already under attack.' The escaped reward wins the quiet budget over the free-piece reward while this node is current. Fade when quiet, netLoss < 5 only.
nodes.retire_or_decay: One 'already' hold returns it to watching. No time decay.

nodes.name_as_result: Before I take, I check what takes back.
nodes.what_it_is: Counting on one square before a capture: I take a pawn with the bishop and the king takes the bishop. The capture variant of the landing look.
evidence: AGAINST: hanging_after_move holds with variant 'takes_back' (his move was a capture), any taker; back 1, anyway or unheld 2.
FOR: a game with observed >= 20 and zero takes_back holds; the reward 'free_taken' counts as a positive look in copy only.
nodes.mastery_rule: Three consecutive games with observed >= 20 and zero takes_back holds -> quiet; three more with the fade active -> yours.
nodes.how_it_is_practised: Opening line 'Still on what takes back. Count before you take.' Remembering form: 'Hold on. This one again. Before you take there: what takes back? Tap it.' No extra tap (the hold's own question is already the drill). Fade when quiet, netLoss < 5 only.
nodes.retire_or_decay: One takes_back hold returns it to watching. No time decay.

nodes.name_as_result: I take what is free.
nodes.what_it_is: Their piece sitting where I can take it for nothing, walked past. The other half of the hanging-piece habit, and the one the opponent is built to feed with its verified gifts.
evidence: AGAINST: free_piece_ignored holds; back 1, anyway or unheld 2.

FOR: the reward 'free_taken' (my capture of a free piece or of the bot's verified gift) is a positive look; a game is clean for this node when it had exposure (at least one verified gift left by the bot, state().lastGift.verified, or at least one free_piece_ignored hold) and zero free_piece_ignored holds.
nodes.mastery_rule: Three consecutive exposed games (a verified gift was offered, or the pre-search found a free capture for me at least once; the game summary gains a 'freeOffered' count) with zero free_piece_ignored holds -> quiet; three more exposed clean games with the fade active -> yours. Games with no exposure are skipped.
nodes.how_it_is_practised: Opening line 'Still on the free ones. Look at what you can take before you plan.' While current the opponent's GIFT_RATE goes up one notch (0.12 to 0.16; the 0.08 step after a clean game still applies on top) so the look comes up more often, and the free_taken reward wins the quiet budget. Remembering form: 'Hold on. This one again. Something of theirs is free right now. Tap it.' Fade when quiet (a faded free_piece_ignored is not 'given away'; it is logged unheld and counts against the node only).
nodes.retire_or_decay: One free_piece_ignored hold returns it to watching and GIFT_RATE returns to the current notch. No time decay.

nodes.name_as_result: I check what my move leaves behind.
nodes.what_it_is: My move takes a guard away or opens a line onto something of mine (a pinned piece moving, a piece stepping off a file). Subtler than the first looks, so it sits later in the order.
evidence: AGAINST: ignored_attack holds with sub 'lost_guard' or 'opened_line'; back 1, anyway or unheld 2.
FOR: a game with observed >= 20 and zero such holds.
nodes.mastery_rule: Three consecutive games with observed >= 20 and zero lost_guard/opened_line holds -> quiet; three more with the fade active -> yours.
nodes.how_it_is_practised: Opening line 'Still on what your move leaves behind. Before it lands, look at what it was guarding.' Remembering form: 'Hold on. The piece you are moving was guarding something. Tap it.' Fade when quiet, netLoss < 5 only.
nodes.retire_or_decay: One hold of its kind returns it to watching. No time decay.

nodes.name_as_result: I see their mate in one coming.
nodes.what_it_is: Their queen or rook has a mating check next move and my move does not stop it. Pattern 4's mate-in-one-threat, the f7 and back-rank ones.
evidence: AGAINST: allowed_mate holds, any outcome, weight 2 (the hold always fires; there is no fade for this node).

FOR: a game that reached observed >= 20 with zero allowed_mate holds; 'mate-loss' results count against in copy ('That one got away') but not in the rule, because a mate I could not have stopped with one look is not evidence of this look.
nodes.mastery_rule: Three consecutive games with observed >= 20 and zero allowed_mate holds -> quiet. There is no 'yours' for this node: the hand never comes off a mate, so quiet is the top state and is worded 'quiet', never 'yours'.
nodes.how_it_is_practised: Opening line 'Still on their check. Before you move, find where their queen lands.' Remembering form: 'Hold on. Their queen again. Where does the check land? Tap it.' Never faded (ALWAYS_HOLD).
nodes.retire_or_decay: One allowed_mate hold returns it to watching. No time decay.

nodes.name_as_result: I finish it: mate when it is there, never stalemate.
nodes.what_it_is: Pattern 2 in the game: playing the mate in one when the engine has it, and not stalemating a won king. The bot usually resigns, so this node needs exposure before it can say anything.
evidence: AGAINST: missed_mate holds and allowed_stalemate holds, any outcome, weight 2.

FOR: a 'mate-win' result; a game is exposed for this node when the player was five or more points up at any pre-search (the summary gains a 'wonPosition' flag) or a missed_mate/allowed_stalemate hold occurred.
nodes.mastery_rule: Three consecutive exposed games with zero missed_mate and zero allowed_stalemate holds, at least two of them ending 'mate-win' -> quiet. No 'yours' (mates and stalemates are never faded).
nodes.how_it_is_practised: While current the opponent plays on in every won position instead of resigning (the open question in PRODUCT.md answered by the path: the king-and-pawns exception widens to all material while finish is current, capped by the existing mercy rules), so I get the mate rep inside the game. Opening line 'Still on finishing. When the mate is there, play it; watch their king's squares.' Remembering form: 'Hold on. You have a checkmate on the board again. Tap the square.' Never faded.
nodes.retire_or_decay: One missed_mate or allowed_stalemate hold returns it to watching and the bot's resignation rule returns to normal. No time decay.

models.next_rule: path.js is a pure reducer: reduce(state, gameSummary) -> state, run at game end, plus current(state) and plan(state) -> { focus, faded, openingLine }. Map each hold record to a node by (category, sub, variant, pawnAmongTakers, best taker piece). Weight: back 1, anyway or unheld 2; mate and finish nodes 2 always. current = the watching node with the highest weighted count over the last three counted games; ties go to the order pawns, pieces, under-attack, takes-back, free, uncovers, mate-threat, finish; if every watching node has zero in the last three games, current = the watching node with the most recent hold; if nothing is watching, current = null and the opening line is 'Nothing on my list. Your move.' Claude may break a tie between the top two only (see llm_role), never override the count. faded = every node in state quiet whose fade is allowed (not mate-threat, not finish); the gate receives gameState.faded and suppresses matching verdicts with netLoss < 5 as 'faded' (still logged, still counted as given away when material was lost). The next game's opponent: GIFT_RATE +1 notch while free is current; play-on-when-won while finish is current; otherwise unchanged. The drill, when one is offered at all, is Model 2's moment of the current node's kind if one is due ('Play it again from here'), never a position I did not play. The whole rule runs over a synthetic log in scripts/test_path.mjs: three clean 20-move games after two pawn holds make pawns quiet and faded; a faded pawns hold makes it watching again; a 12-move game counts for nothing; current picks the right node with the tie order; every opening line renders with no digit.
felt_in_game: The opening line names the one look I am on, from my own holds, before any screen exists: 'Still on the pawns. Two games clean; one more and I stop watching for them.'
The hold itself remembers: the second time across games the same kind fires, the question says so ('This one again') and asks the look I keep skipping, at 0 ms, from the stored path, not from a call.

The hand comes off, one look at a time, announced before the game: 'I have stopped watching for the pawns. Everything else I still hold.' If I slip, the piece is taken for real, the sentence says it was not watching and is again, and nothing is hidden.
The opponent changes with the node: more free pieces left when I am on the free ones; it plays on to let me mate when I am on finishing.
The rewards are aimed: whichever positive look belongs to my current node wins the four-line quiet budget.
The close card ends with one path sentence instead of a count: 'The pawns: quiet. Next I watch their pieces.'
models.shown: Never first and never a dashboard. Three places. (1) The opening line at the start of games two onward: the current remembered line is replaced by the path's opening line from COPY.PATH keyed by node and state (or Claude's validated next_game line when one is stored). (2) The close card: one serif line .close-path under the captions, in the coach's voice, words only ('The pawns: two games quiet. One more and I stop watching for them.' / 'The pawns are yours.' / 'The pawns again. I am watching for them.'). (3) A state of the same page, 'Where I am', reached from a --muted link in the 24 px link row (visible only in state over and in idle before the first move, next to nothing else), leaving the board where it is and dimmed as in a hold, and replacing the close card's content with at most eight serif lines, one per look that has ever been seen plus the one that would be next, each as 'The pawns, yours since Tuesday.' / 'Their pieces, watching.' / 'What takes back, quiet.' / 'The free ones, not yet seen.'; the current look carries the amber inset, the one colour allowed to raise its voice; a 'Back' link returns. It never shows a count of holds, a percentage, a bar, a node that has never come up, a locked anything, a date other than a weekday in words, a streak, or a rating; copy_check runs over COPY.PATH and the rendered state asserts no digit anywhere in it.
models.llm_role: One call, quick tier, no tools, at the close card (an explicit end of game), cached 24 h keyed by gameId, never at load and never inside a hold. Input: the path state in words (each seen node with its state and clean-game count), this game's holds as fact sheets (category, piece, square, takers in piece words, taps and grades, outcome, net loss in piece words, and the sentence I typed in Hear me out if any), and the last three games' per-node counts. Output {one_thing: at most 18 words, next_game: at most 12 words, focus: a node id from the top two of the count or null}. one_thing fades into the close card under the template line; next_game is stored and becomes the next game's opening line at 0 ms; focus breaks a tie only. What Claude does that the table cannot: say the shape of the habit from the positions ('Both times it was your knight going to the fifth rank in front of their pawns.'), read my Hear me out sentence back to me ('Tuesday you were attacking their king; both pieces went to pawns on the way.'), and choose between two tied looks by what my taps show (I tap the attacker but never the attacked piece, so under-attack before pieces). validate.js runs on both lines (squares only from this game's holds, no SAN, no digits, no banned words, caps); a rejected reply shows the template and increments __coachRejects. Without Claude (sample null, declined, error, or the friend's copy): identical path, the template lines from COPY.PATH, the count's own tie order; no control is ever shown disabled.
models.engine_role: Unchanged in what it decides: every hold, category, sub-case, taker, net loss and reward still comes from chess.js and the Worker before anything is logged, so every node's evidence is engine fact. Three small additions: gate.verdict takes gameState.faded and returns suppressed 'faded' (category still reported, so the record is honest and givenAway still counts); game.js logs suppressed verdicts (pair, quiet, faded) as hold records with outcome 'unheld' and counts observed moves (moves that had a verdict) and exposure flags (freeOffered, wonPosition) into the game summary; bot.js reads two path flags (giftRate notch up while free is current; play on when won while finish is current). The engine never sees the path and the path never evaluates a position.
models.persistence: holdon.v1.path: { version, nodes: { id: { state, seen, cleanRun, fadeRun, since, lastHoldAt } }, current, faded, nextLine } written by the reducer at game end; derivable from the hold log, so a missing or corrupt key is rebuilt from holdon.v1.holds and holdon.v1.games on load. GameSummary gains observed, freeOffered, wonPosition; HoldRecord gains suppressed ('pair'|'quiet'|'faded'|null) and the outcome value 'unheld'. The 30-hold cap stays because the node counters live in the path state. Behind the same store.js interface the key mirrors to db at data/users/{self}/path when db and user resolve (the owner's page only; a Viewer plays with the laptop's state but never writes); localStorage stays the always-there layer, so the path survives the move from laptop to phone and a private window still plays.
models.first_session: Nothing of the path is visible before the first game ends. The tutorial hold and the first real game happen exactly as today. At the first close card one sentence appears under the captions, built from that game's holds: 'Both holds were a pawn you did not see. I am watching for the pawns.' (or 'I never stopped your hand. Nothing on my list yet.'). The 'Where I am' link shows one or two lines at most ('The pawns, watching.' and 'Their pieces, next.'), so it cannot look like a syllabus. The second game opens with 'Still on the pawns. Before the piece lands, look for them.' and the first pawn hold of that game says 'This one again.' That is the whole first-session path: one look, named, remembered.
models.why_new: Dr. Wolf counts skills, Aimchess prescribes drills from stats, Chess.com Lessons and Duolingo paths are course lists; all of them separate the path from the game. Here the path is made only of holds in my real games, mastery is the coach's measured silence, and the proof is the coach taking its hand off that one look and announcing it, which no product found does. The visible path is words and a weekday, no numbers, no locks; it exists because the game already felt it.
risks: Too little evidence: three games of twenty observed moves is a week for me; the path may say 'watching' for a long time. That is honest, but the copy must never nag about it ('Still on the pawns' is fine; 'You have not played' never).

The fade can feel like betrayal the first time a faded piece is taken. Mitigation is in the design: announced before the game, one look at a time, never a mate or a five-point loss, back to watching at once with a sentence that owns it; if Sambudh's first fade still frightens him, a 'Keep watching' link under the announcement is the escape hatch.
Suppressed verdicts are not logged today; without logging pair, quiet and faded suppressions as 'unheld' the path would call two early play-anyways a clean game.
Engine-cold moves on a slow phone would inflate clean games; 'observed' must be the denominator or the path lies.
