Claude's one_thing could claim a pattern that is not there; the validator cannot check truth, only words, so focus may only break ties and the template line always stands.
The 'Where I am' state is one argument away from becoming a stats card; the no-digit assertion and the rule that unseen nodes are not drawn are the defence.
Eight nodes is already a lot of words to maintain in COPY; each node needs five or six lines and all of them must pass copy_check.

models.name: Your own moments
models.one_sentence_for_a_beginner: Every piece I gave away comes back as a game that starts right there, with the coach's hand on, until I keep it twice.
models.the_idea: A map of my own games: the path is a short stack of my own moments, each a position where I played a hold anyway or lost a piece unheld, and each comes back as the start of a real game against the same opponent until I answer it twice on two different days. Not a puzzle set: the moment is a game that begins where I went wrong, the hold is live, and if I keep the piece the game simply goes on from there, ten moves shorter than a fresh one, which fits ten minutes better than a fresh game does. Mastery is per moment and plain: answered once today, again another day, then it is gone. The stack is the path, and the look I am 'on' is simply the kind of moment I have most of. It fits Hold On because the product's deferred features already describe it (Play it again from here, the question that remembers, the spacing from learno's model reduced to 'today, then another day'), and because it is the most direct feeling of getting somewhere a beginner can have: I lost a knight there on Tuesday and today I did not.

nodes.name_as_result: I keep the piece I gave away.
nodes.what_it_is: A moment made from a hanging_after_move or ignored_attack hold with outcome 'anyway' or 'unheld' and netLoss >= 2, where I was not already five or more points down before the move (a lost position is not a lesson about one look). The position before my move, the opponent as it was, the hold live.
evidence: CREATED: at game end, from each qualifying hold record { fen, san, category, sub, node, netLoss, gameId, date }, newest first, at most two moments created per game (the worst by netLoss), stack capped at twelve.

ANSWERED: the moment is loaded as the game start; my first move commits clean (no verdict category matched, cpLoss < 200) and the piece that was lost then is not hanging after my move per chess.js. Playing the same losing move again fires the hold as usual and is graded as a normal hold; taking it back and then moving clean still counts as answered (the look happened).
NOT ANSWERED: the first move is held or suppressed-with-loss, or I skip the moment with 'Fresh game instead'. A skip is not counted against anything.
nodes.mastery_rule: A moment is retired when answered on two separate calendar days (answered.length === 2 and the two dates differ). The node 'kept' reads as mastered in words when the stack holds zero open moments of this kind and at least one moment of this kind was ever retired.
nodes.how_it_is_practised: When a moment is due (never answered, or answered once on an earlier day), [Again] or the page load opens on it instead of the start position, the board as it was, the line 'One of yours, from Tuesday. Your move.' (or Claude's stored line), the link row holding one --muted 'Fresh game instead' link. The hold is never faded on a moment. After a clean first move: 'Answered. That one is yours today.' and the game continues from there against the normal opponent; if the position after my move is five or more points against me the line says 'Answered. Here is a fresh game.' and the start position loads.
nodes.retire_or_decay: Retired after the second answer on a different day with 'That one is gone.' at the close card. A moment untouched for thirty days is dropped silently (no line, no guilt). A moment answered then played anyway later from the same position is not re-created: one moment per fen.

nodes.name_as_result: I take the free piece I walked past.
nodes.what_it_is: A moment made from a free_piece_ignored hold played anyway or unheld. The position before my move; the free piece still there.
evidence: CREATED: as kept, from free_piece_ignored holds with outcome anyway or unheld.

ANSWERED: my first move is the capture of that piece (the reward kind free_taken fires on that square), or the pre-search's best move for me at the moment is no longer that capture because the opponent's piece... no: the stored fen is fixed, so answered means exactly: I take it.
NOT ANSWERED: any other first move; a free_piece_ignored hold on the first move is graded as a normal hold.
nodes.mastery_rule: Answered on two separate days -> retired. The kind reads mastered when no open 'took' moments remain and at least one was retired.
nodes.how_it_is_practised: Opens as kept, with the line 'One of yours, from Tuesday. Something was there for you. Your move.' (the line never names the square or the piece). Taking it plays the normal green ring and 'Free knight. You looked.' which here also means answered; the game goes on.
nodes.retire_or_decay: As kept.

nodes.name_as_result: I stop their mate when it is one move away.
nodes.what_it_is: A moment made from an allowed_mate hold played anyway (the hand is never faded for mates, so unheld cannot occur). The position before my move.
evidence: CREATED: allowed_mate holds with outcome anyway.
ANSWERED: my first move is not held as allowed_mate (the gate confirms no mate in one against me after it).
NOT ANSWERED: an allowed_mate hold on the first move.
nodes.mastery_rule: Answered on two separate days -> retired.
nodes.how_it_is_practised: Opens with 'One of yours, from Tuesday. Their queen was closer than it looked. Your move.' The hold's own question fires if I repeat the move; after a clean move the game continues.
nodes.retire_or_decay: As kept.

nodes.name_as_result: I play the mate when it is there.
nodes.what_it_is: A moment made from a missed_mate hold played anyway. The position with my mate in one on the board.
evidence: CREATED: missed_mate holds with outcome anyway.
ANSWERED: my first move is checkmate (the game ends 'Checkmate. Well played.' and the moment is marked answered; the close card then offers Again as usual).
NOT ANSWERED: anything else; missed_mate fires as a normal hold.
nodes.mastery_rule: Answered on two separate days -> retired.
nodes.how_it_is_practised: Opens with 'One of yours, from Tuesday. You had it here. Your move.' A mate ends the game in one move, so this is the only moment that is thirty seconds long; it is still a game, not a puzzle, and the close card follows.
nodes.retire_or_decay: As kept.

nodes.name_as_result: I finish a won game without stalemate.
nodes.what_it_is: A moment made from an allowed_stalemate hold played anyway. The won position before the stalemating move.
evidence: CREATED: allowed_stalemate holds with outcome anyway.

ANSWERED: the game continuing from the moment ends in mate-win within twenty of my moves with no allowed_stalemate hold along the way (the summary of that game records moment answered only at its end).
NOT ANSWERED: a stalemate, a draw, or twenty moves without mate (the line says 'Still theirs to escape. Another day.').
nodes.mastery_rule: Answered on two separate days -> retired. The bot plays on from a moment of this kind whatever its material.
nodes.how_it_is_practised: Opens with 'One of yours, from Tuesday. You were winning here. Finish it; watch their king's squares. Your move.' The opponent never resigns inside this moment.
nodes.retire_or_decay: As kept.

models.next_rule: path.js (pure): moments(state, gameSummary) -> state adds up to two new moments per game (the two worst qualifying holds by netLoss, mates first), one per fen, cap twelve (oldest unanswered dropped first, never a once-answered one). due(state, today) -> the list of moments never answered or answered once on an earlier calendar day. nextMoment(state, today) -> the oldest due moment, except that a moment created from the game just ended is never due the same day (it comes back tomorrow; today's is only offered through the close card's 'Play it again from here' link, which is a choice, not the default). At most one moment per game start; after a skip ('Fresh game instead') no moment is offered again until the next game start. With Claude available the stored moment line is used; without it the template line for the kind. Every rule is tested in scripts/test_path.mjs over a synthetic log: two anyway holds in one game create two moments; the same fen twice creates one; a moment answered twice on the same day is still open; answered on two days is retired; a thirteenth moment drops the oldest unanswered; a game-day moment is not due until tomorrow; a lost-position hold (five down before the move) creates nothing.
felt_in_game: Day two the page does not open on the start position: it opens on my own Tuesday board with the same opponent and the line 'One of yours, from Tuesday. Your move.' Nothing to read, just the move I got wrong, waiting.

If I play the same move the coach's hand is there as before; if I play something clean the coach says 'Answered. That one is yours today.' and the game goes on from there, so the drill and the game are one thing.
Games get shorter and sharper: starting at move twelve fits my ten minutes better than starting at move one.
The close card ends with my moments in words: 'Two of yours waiting; one from Tuesday answered.' and, right after a bad game, a single link 'Play it again from here' on the worst one.
Nothing is ever forced: 'Fresh game instead' is always one tap away and is never counted.
models.shown: Never first, never a count. (1) The game start on a moment is itself the display: the board, the one line, the 'Fresh game instead' link in the 24 px link row. (2) The close card: 'Play it again from here' as a --muted link beside Again when this game produced a moment (resumes it now, with the hold live; it stays due tomorrow regardless), and one serif line under the captions: 'One of yours from this game will come back. Two from Tuesday are waiting.' (3) The 'Where I am' state of the same page (same link, same dimmed board) lists the open moments as caption lines in the close card's own voice, reusing closeCaption: 'Knight to e5, a pawn was waiting. From Tuesday, answered once.' and retired ones for a week as 'Bishop to f7, a king was waiting. Gone.' The list never shows a number of moments, a success rate, a due date as a date, a calendar, or a puzzle rating; at most twelve lines; if empty: 'Nothing of yours waiting. Your move.'
models.llm_role: One quick-tier call at the close card when a moment is created (an explicit end of game; cached 24 h keyed by the moment id; at most one call per game even when two moments are created, the second gets the template), no tools. Input: the moment's fact sheet as the K2 prompt already builds it (the held move in piece words, what took it, net loss in piece words, the squares that may be named), what I did then (my taps and their grades, played anyway, and the sentence I typed in Hear me out if any) and the weekday. Output {line: at most 16 words, names no answer square and no move}. It is stored on the moment and said when the moment reopens, at 0 ms, from the store, zero calls at load. What Claude adds that a table cannot: it reads my own plan back to me without giving the answer ('Tuesday you wanted this knight near their king; something was waiting on the way.'), and it chooses, among several due moments, the one that matches the look I am on in Model 1 if both models ship (the table's fallback is oldest first). validate.js runs with the moment's allowed squares minus its answer squares, no SAN, no digits, no banned words, the cap; a rejected line falls back to the kind's template ('One of yours, from Tuesday. Your move.'). Without Claude the page is identical minus that sentence; nothing is shown disabled and no copy mentions the coach being absent.
models.engine_role: The moment is loaded through the same path as load(fen) with the game counters reset (a real new game id), the pre-search runs on the stored fen, and the gate decides my first move exactly as it would in any game, so 'answered' is the gate's own clean verdict, not a stored answer; the stored category is used only to pick the template line and the answered test per kind (free_taken reward for 'took', checkmate for 'gave-the-mate', mate-win within twenty moves for 'no-stalemate'). The opponent plays from the position with the normal recipe (the book cannot apply; a verified gift can). The bot never resigns inside a 'no-stalemate' moment. The engine never knows the position is a moment.
models.persistence: holdon.v1.moments: an array of at most twelve { id, fen, san, category, sub, node, netLoss, gameId, created (ISO), answered: [ISO dates], line, skippedToday } written at game end and after each moment game start; retired moments are kept for seven days with a retired date so the 'Gone.' line can be shown, then dropped. Mirrored to db at data/users/{self}/moments behind store.js when db and user resolve, so the Tuesday moment from the laptop opens on the phone on Wednesday; localStorage stays the always-there layer; a Viewer of a shared link plays moments from the owner's store but never writes answers.
models.first_session: The first game ends; if I played a hold anyway or lost a piece unheld, the close card says 'One of yours from this game will come back.' and shows 'Play it again from here' as a quiet link. If I tap it, the board goes back to that moment with the hold live and the line 'Here it is again. Your move.'; I keep the piece and read 'Answered. That one is yours today.' and the game goes on from there; that is the strongest 'I got somewhere' available in one sitting. If I do not tap it, nothing else of the path appears in session one. Day two the page opens on that moment with 'One of yours, from Tuesday. Your move.' and 'Fresh game instead' beside it.
models.why_new: Replaying a mistake exists: Lichess's Learn from your mistakes, Chess.com's retry in Game Review, Aimchess's puzzles from your games, Chessable's spaced lines. The difference here is that the moment is a held position that becomes a real game continuing against the same opponent, with the coach's hand on it, scheduled by day and retired by evidence from the game itself, with no puzzle framing, no rating and no counts. The spacing is learno's idea cut to the size of a phone: today, then another day, then gone.
risks: A moment can be a position I was already losing; the five-points-down filter and the 'Answered. Here is a fresh game.' exit keep it from becoming a slow loss I did not choose.
A page that opens on a moment instead of the start position could feel like being assigned homework; the 'Fresh game instead' link must be as easy as Again and skipping must never be mentioned again.

Two answers on two days means a moment can sit for a week if I play once a week; the thirty-day silent drop keeps the stack from becoming a backlog, and the stack is capped at twelve so it never looks like a to-do list.

Answering by taking the piece back and then moving clean is a softer test than moving clean first; it is still counted, because the look happened, but the copy must not say 'you saw it' when the hold had to fire.
Moments from the same opening keep repeating the same fen family; one moment per fen is enforced but near-identical positions are not, and that is accepted (it is how habits are).
Claude's stored line could age badly if the moment is re-created or edited; the line is keyed to the moment id and never reused for another fen.
Moments must not feed Model 1's clean-game counts (a replayed position with foreknowledge is not evidence of a habit); if both models ship, moment games are excluded from the reducer.

models.persona: Game designer on the Hold On team: progression felt in the rules of play (the opponent, the gifts, the hand, the openings, set positions), the loop across sessions, legible goals without numbers, difficulty curves, earned unlocks, one celebration per node without confetti.
models.perspective_summary: Progression in Hold On cannot be points, badges or a road of nodes, because the product's own measure of success is already silence: the hold firing less from game to game. So the pathway must be the retreat of help, and it must change the rules of play before it is ever drawn. I propose two systems that share the same node ids and the same evidence (the hold log, the new 'landed' outcome for verdicts that matched but did not hold, the gift and threat events the opponent already knows it made, and four cheap per-game fields). Model A, The Quiet Ladder, is the spine: each look has a hand state (asking, quiet, off) computed from the log, the opponent's gifts climb the ladder with the player (free minors, then one-move threats, then mate threats, then free checkmates, then an opponent that will not resign), and the summit is a real game announced before it starts with the hand off. Model B, Doors, is the daily hook: every piece given away becomes a position that comes back as tomorrow's first game, then a week later with less help, then a month later with none, which is SM-2 mapped onto the fading hand on the player's own positions. Both are pure functions over a synthetic log, both are felt in the game first, and the visible pathway in both is the board showing his own positions with nine serif sentences in three inks, never a count. A ships first; B reuses A's hand states and adds the door schedule.

models.name: The Quiet Ladder
models.one_sentence_for_a_beginner: The coach stops your hand for every kind of look it has to ask about; each look you stop needing, it stops asking about, and the game it has nothing left to ask is the one you are playing on your own.
models.the_idea: A ladder of silences. Every node is a look (the nine results below, grouped in four lanes), and every node has a hand state computed from the log: asking (the hold fires with its category question, as today), quiet (the hold fires and lifts the piece but the line says only 'Hold on. You know this one. Tap it.', with no hint on the first wrong tap), and off (the gate still runs and logs, but the piece lands, the opponent takes it, the coach says nothing, and the close card tells the truth). Progress is the hand lifting one look at a time, in the wrist before it is on a screen. The opponent climbs with the player: only the current node shapes the opponent, and the shaping is the same gift machinery the bot already has pointed at a different look (verified free minors for 'I take what is free'; verified one-move threats for 'their last move'; mate threats for 'their mate'; a free checkmate for 'my mate'; an opponent that will not resign for 'finish'). The summit of the first lane is a real game announced before it starts: 'Today I keep my hands in my pockets.' in which only the holds that are a game remain (mates, stalemate, five points, the existing ALWAYS_HOLD and BIG_LOSS rules). This fits Hold On because silence is already the measure of success and the ladder turns it into a goal the player can feel; it also replaces the deferred per-game hold budget, which would spend the same patience on a look he has learned and a look he has not, with a hand that lifts only where the evidence says so and comes back the moment a piece lands. Three hand states give each node a difficulty curve (the question, then no question, then no hold), and every climb has one earned moment: the first game that opens with a promise.

nodes.name_as_result: I see the pawn before my piece lands
nodes.what_it_is: The first look from their chair: before a piece lands, which enemy pawn reaches that square. The gate's hanging_after_move with a pawn among the takers (gate.js pawnHold), the commonest hold under 1000 and the tutorial's own lesson (Nxe5 in the 6...d6 position). Lane one, 'Before it lands'.
evidence: Against, weight two: a HoldRecord with category hanging_after_move, a pawn among the takers, outcome 'anyway', netLoss >= 2

Against, weight two: the same category and takers with the new outcome 'landed' (the verdict matched but the hold was suppressed by the pair rule, the quiet-after-two rule or an off hand; game.js already computes this for givenAway, it now logs it)
Against, weight one: the same with outcome 'back' (the hand was needed, even though he saw it when asked)
For: an instance of this kind whose first tap was graded right (taps[0].grade === 'right' and taps[0].ask is null, i.e. the hold's own look)
For: a counted game (>= 20 player moves, i.e. plies >= 40 at the end, or ended earlier by his checkmate) with zero instances of this kind
Ignored: tutorial holds (hold.tutorial), holds with outcome 'ended', games under 20 player moves that ended by give-up or mercy
nodes.mastery_rule: asking -> quiet: over the last two counted games, at most one instance of this kind per game, none with outcome 'anyway' or 'landed', and every instance answered right on the first tap. quiet -> off: three consecutive counted games with zero instances of this kind (holds and landings). Both computed by path.derive(games, holds) with no other state.
nodes.how_it_is_practised: asking and current: the hold asks the category question as today; the next game opens with this look's line ('The pawns. Before the piece lands, look for them.'); K1's fact sheet carries 'this is the look being worked on' so a follow-up like 'This one again' is only ever said when true; the opponent is plain (its gift rate at its notch, no shaping, because no bot move can make him land on a pawn-covered square; the book's Italian with ...d6 and ...h6 already builds the squares where it happens). quiet: the hold fires, lifts the piece, breathes amber, but the line is 'Hold on. You know this one. Tap it.'; a first wrong tap gets 'Not that one.' with no hint; the second wrong tap names the answer as today; grading is unchanged (chess.js, the category's answer set). off: no hold; the piece lands, the opponent takes (punish-always), the line stays silent, and the close card caption reads 'Knight to e5, a pawn was waiting: it landed.' The first off game opens with the promise 'I will not ask about the pawns today. They are yours.' and, if nothing of this kind landed, closes with 'I never asked about the pawns. Nothing landed on one.'
nodes.retire_or_decay: off -> quiet on one 'landed' of this kind with netLoss >= 2 (the next game opens 'The pawns, once, and I said nothing. I will ask again.'); off -> asking on two in one game; quiet -> asking on an 'anyway' or two holds of this kind in one game. Nothing retires permanently: off is 'yours' for exactly as long as nothing lands, and the two-event decay plus the two-game climb give hysteresis so the state cannot flap game to game.

nodes.name_as_result: I see what takes my piece before it lands
nodes.what_it_is: The same look when the taker is not a pawn: a knight, bishop, rook, queen or king that reaches the square, including the capture variant ('Before you take there: what takes back?', the tutorial's Bxf7+). hanging_after_move with no pawn among the takers. Harder than pawns because the taker is often far away or is the recapture after his own capture.
evidence: Against, weight two: hanging_after_move with no pawn among the takers, outcome 'anyway' or 'landed', netLoss >= 2
Against, weight one: the same with outcome 'back'
For: first tap right on the hold's own look (a right tap on the engine's best taker; a 'partial' on a dearer taker counts as needed-the-hand, weight one)
For: a counted game with zero instances of this kind
Ignored: tutorial, 'ended', short games
nodes.mastery_rule: asking -> quiet: last two counted games, at most one instance per game, none 'anyway' or 'landed', every first tap right. quiet -> off: three consecutive counted games with zero instances.
nodes.how_it_is_practised: As pawns: the category question while asking, the bare 'You know this one' while quiet, silence while off. When current, the opening line is 'What takes it. Before the piece lands, look from their chair.' and the capture variant keeps its own question. No opponent shaping; the Show me ghost (the capture and the recapture) is the practice, and in quiet state Show me stays available before the tap so the look can still be checked without being told.
nodes.retire_or_decay: Same as pawns: off -> quiet on one landing with netLoss >= 2, off -> asking on two in one game, quiet -> asking on an 'anyway' or two holds in one game.

nodes.name_as_result: I notice what their last move attacked
nodes.what_it_is: The chess master's first look: what did their last move point at. The gate's ignored_attack with sub-case 'already' (a piece of his was attacked before his move and his move did not answer it). The look that loses the Ruy's bishop on b5 after ...a6.
evidence: Against, weight two: ignored_attack sub 'already', outcome 'anyway' or 'landed', netLoss >= 2
Against, weight one: the same with outcome 'back'

For: the 'you_looked' reward (REWARD_ESCAPED: a piece of his worth >= 2 was hanging before his move and nothing hangs after), logged as a reward event {kind: 'you_looked', ply} whether or not the line was said under the quiet budget
For: a threat event the opponent logged {kind: 'threat', ply, square, parried: true} (parried: the next player move was not an ignored_attack hold or landing on that piece)
Against, weight two: a threat event with parried false
For: a counted game with zero instances
nodes.mastery_rule: asking -> quiet: last two counted games, zero 'anyway' or 'landed' of this kind, at most one 'back' per game answered right first, and at least two parried threats or you_looked events across the two games. quiet -> off: three consecutive counted games with zero instances and every threat event parried.
nodes.how_it_is_practised: When current, the opponent is shaped: in the sampler step, at the gift rate (and forced once by the bot's twelfth move if no roll has succeeded, so the opening line 'Their last move. What did it point at?' is true), bot.js enumerates threat candidates with chess.js (after the move a player piece worth >= 2 is attacked and undefended or attacked by a cheaper piece, the move gives no check, hangs nothing of the bot's worth >= 5, allows no mate in one) and verifies up to six at depth 10 (the bot's eval after the move stays within 100 cp of its full-strength top move, so the threat is a real move and not a gift in disguise). The threat is logged with how: 'threat'. If he answers it, the you_looked reward fires under the existing budget; if he ignores it the hold is ignored_attack 'already' with its question, or 'You know this one' while quiet, or silence while off. The book's Ruy line (3.Bb5 a6) is kept in rotation while this node is current.
nodes.retire_or_decay: off -> quiet on one landing of this kind or one unparried verified threat; off -> asking on two in one game; quiet -> asking on an 'anyway'. Threat shaping stops the moment the node is no longer current, so the opponent does not keep manufacturing a look he has learned.

nodes.name_as_result: I keep my guards and my lines
nodes.what_it_is: The two rarer ignored_attack sub-cases: lost_guard (his move took away the defender of a piece) and opened_line (his move stepped off a file or a pinned piece moved, opening an enemy line onto something of his). The look behind 'Something of yours just lost its guard' and 'Your move opens a line to something of yours'.
evidence: Against, weight two: ignored_attack sub 'lost_guard' or 'opened_line', outcome 'anyway' or 'landed', netLoss >= 2
Against, weight one: the same with outcome 'back'
For: first tap right on the attacked piece (a partial on the attacker's square is needed-the-hand)
For: a counted game with zero instances
Windows are five games, not two or three, because these sub-cases fire perhaps once in three games
nodes.mastery_rule: asking -> quiet: over the last four counted games, zero 'anyway' or 'landed' of this kind and every 'back' answered right first. quiet -> off: five consecutive counted games with zero instances.
nodes.how_it_is_practised: The hold's own two questions while asking; 'You know this one' while quiet; silence while off. When current, the opening line is 'Your guards. When a piece moves, what was it protecting?' and K1's and_then clause is invited to name the guard that moved ('And the knight was the only thing guarding that square.'). No opponent shaping: the bot cannot make him remove his own guard, and a shaped pin would be a threat category the gate does not have.
nodes.retire_or_decay: off -> quiet on one landing; off -> asking on two in one game; quiet -> asking on an 'anyway'. Because the node is rare, a decay to asking is announced in the next game's line so it does not feel arbitrary: 'A guard went missing last game. I will ask about those again.'

nodes.name_as_result: I take what is free
nodes.what_it_is: The other half of the look: a piece of theirs that nothing guards, walked past. The gate's free_piece_ignored (against) and the two things the game already rewards (a free piece taken, the opponent's own verified gift taken). Lane two, on its own, because taking is a different reflex from not giving.
evidence: Against, weight two: free_piece_ignored, outcome 'anyway' or 'landed' (for this category 'landed' means the verdict matched and was suppressed; nothing of his is lost but the free piece was walked past)
Against, weight one: the same with outcome 'back' (he then took it)
Against, weight one: a gift event {kind: 'gift', ply, square, piece, taken: false} (state().lastGift.verified was true and his next move did not capture on that square)
For: a gift event with taken true
For: a reward event {kind: 'free_taken', ply} (logged whether or not the line was said)
For: a counted game with zero free_piece_ignored instances and every verified gift taken
nodes.mastery_rule: asking -> quiet: last two counted games, zero free_piece_ignored 'anyway' or 'landed', every verified gift in those games taken, and at least two free_taken or gift-taken events across the two games. quiet -> off: three consecutive counted games with zero instances, every gift taken, and at least two gifts offered across the three (so off is earned by taking, not by luck).
nodes.how_it_is_practised: This is the node the existing gift machine already trains, so when current the shaping is a promise kept: giftDue is forced once by the bot's twelfth move if no roll has succeeded, so the opening line 'Something of theirs will be free today. Take it.' is true; while asking, gift candidates are sorted so a minor attacked by a pawn comes first (the simplest free piece); while quiet, undefended-attacked-by-a-piece first (the harder one). The hold's question while asking; 'You know this one' while quiet (the answer set is the free piece, as today); while off the walked-past free piece lands silently and the close card says 'A free knight was there: it stayed.' Off also moves the gift rate to a third notch (GIFT_RATE_STEPS gains 0.05): the opponent stops leaving pieces because he takes every one.
nodes.retire_or_decay: off -> quiet on one free_piece_ignored landing or one gift walked past; off -> asking on two in one game; quiet -> asking on an 'anyway'. The gift-rate notch steps back up one with the hand, which is the decay he feels: the opponent starts leaving pieces again.

nodes.name_as_result: I see their mate before it lands
nodes.what_it_is: Their next mate: f7, h7 with the queen, the back rank. The gate's allowed_mate (his move allows mate in one). The look that ends games on move four against the early queen. Lane three, 'The end'.
evidence: Against, weight three: allowed_mate with outcome 'anyway' or 'landed' (a mate is the game, so this outweighs a material hold)
Against, weight one: allowed_mate with outcome 'back'

For: a mate-threat event the opponent logged {kind: 'mate_threat', ply, parried: true} (after the bot's shaped move the bot would have had mate in one if he passed; parried: his next move was not an allowed_mate hold or landing)
Against, weight two: a mate_threat event with parried false
For: a counted game with zero allowed_mate instances and every mate threat parried
Windows are three and five games because the natural rate is low; the shaping makes the chances happen
nodes.mastery_rule: asking -> quiet: over the last three counted games, zero allowed_mate 'anyway' or 'landed', at most one 'back' answered right first, and at least two mate threats parried. quiet -> off: five consecutive counted games with zero allowed_mate instances and every mate threat parried.
nodes.how_it_is_practised: When current, the sampler step is shaped at the gift rate (forced once after the bot's tenth move if possible): bot.js enumerates moves after which, with the turn flipped in a scratch FEN (skipped when the player is in check or an en-passant square is set), chess.js finds a bot mate in one, that give no check, hang nothing of the bot's worth >= 5 and are within 100 cp of the full-strength top move at depth 10 (a real threat, not a lunge). Logged with how: 'mate_threat'. The opening line is 'Their queen will come for your king today. See it before it lands.' (only when the bot still has its queen; else 'Their pieces will come for your king today.'). If he parries, nothing is said (silence is the reward; the event is logged). If he does not, the hold is allowed_mate with 'Their queen has a check next move. Where does it land? Tap it.' while asking, 'Hold on. You know this one. Tap it.' while quiet. allowed_mate is in ALWAYS_HOLD, so off for this node means the question goes quiet, never that the hold stops: the first off game opens 'I will not tell you where their check lands today. You will.'
nodes.retire_or_decay: Any allowed_mate landing or 'anyway' sends the node to asking at once, whatever its state (a mate is the game, no hysteresis). quiet -> asking also on two unparried verified mate threats in one game.

nodes.name_as_result: I can finish a won game
nodes.what_it_is: Checkmate versus stalemate, the queen-and-king and rook-and-king mates, delivered in a real game. The gate's allowed_stalemate (against), a draw while five or more points ahead (against), a game won by his checkmate (for), and how long the ending took.
evidence: Against, weight three: allowed_stalemate with outcome 'anyway' or 'landed'
Against, weight one: allowed_stalemate with outcome 'back'
Against, weight two: a game result 'draw' with the new GameSummary field materialAtEnd >= 5 (chess.js material difference at the final position)
For: a game result 'mate-win' with the new field finishPlies <= 40 (plies from the first position where the bot had only king and pawns, or was nine or more points down, to the mate)
Against, weight one: a 'mate-win' with finishPlies > 40 (he got there, slowly)
Neutral: 'resign' results tell nothing about finishing, which is why the shaping below exists
nodes.mastery_rule: asking -> quiet: over the last five counted games, two results 'mate-win' with finishPlies <= 40 and zero allowed_stalemate instances and zero draws while ahead. quiet -> off: two more such mate-wins with zero stalemate instances after reaching quiet.
nodes.how_it_is_practised: When current, the opponent will not resign: the resignation rule is suspended whenever he has a queen or a rook (the spec's narrow king-and-pawns exception widens for this node only), and the bot defends the ending at full strength (Skill 20, depth 12, so stalemate traps are real), while mercy for him is unchanged. The opening line is 'Black will not give up today. Finish it.' The stalemate hold asks 'After this, can their king move at all? Tap their king.' while asking, 'You know this one' while quiet; allowed_stalemate is in ALWAYS_HOLD so off means the quiet copy, never no hold. The one celebration: the first game that ends 'Checkmate. Well played.' after a bot that did not give up, closed with 'It did not give up and you finished it anyway.'
nodes.retire_or_decay: off -> quiet on one stalemate landing or draw while ahead; off -> asking on two; quiet -> asking on a stalemate 'anyway'. When the node is not current the resignation rule returns to the spec's, because a thirty-move conversion does not fit his fifteen minutes unless it is the lesson.

nodes.name_as_result: I see my mate
nodes.what_it_is: The mate in one he has and does not play. The gate's missed_mate (against) and the mate chances the pre-search already knows about (for, when taken). The highest rung of lane three.
evidence: Against, weight two: missed_mate with outcome 'anyway' or 'landed' (ALWAYS_HOLD, so 'landed' only via the pair rule)
Against, weight one: missed_mate with outcome 'back'
For: a mate-chance event {kind: 'mate_chance', ply, taken: true} logged by game.js whenever the pre-search's line 1 is mate in 1 for him and his move was that mate (the result 'mate-win' follows)
Against, weight two: a mate_chance with taken false that was not held (cannot happen while the gate is on; recorded for completeness when the engine was cold)
For: a counted game with every mate chance taken
nodes.mastery_rule: asking -> quiet: the last three mate chances (across counted games) all taken, with zero missed_mate 'anyway' or 'landed'. quiet -> off: five mate chances taken in a row with zero missed_mate instances.
nodes.how_it_is_practised: When current, the sampler's guard that rejects a move allowing mate in one for the player is turned, at the gift rate, into a preference: the mate gift, verified (chess.js hasMateInOne after the move; the bot's full-strength eval already at -200 or worse, so the gift is a losing side losing faster, not an absurd move; nothing of the bot's worth >= 5 newly hanging). Logged with how: 'mate_gift'. The opening line is 'If a checkmate appears today, take it.' If he plays it: 'Checkmate. Well played.' as today, plus once, the first time, 'You found it with nobody pointing.' If he misses it, the missed_mate hold asks 'You have a checkmate on the board. Tap the square.' while asking and 'You know this one' while quiet.
nodes.retire_or_decay: Any missed_mate 'anyway' or landing sends the node to asking at once. The mate gift stops when the node is not current.

nodes.name_as_result: I get out of the opening alive
nodes.what_it_is: The three principles as a result in the log: a pawn in the centre, knights and bishops out, king castled by move ten, and no piece given away in the first fifteen moves. Lane four, on top of lanes one and two, because the opening is where the other looks are cheapest to skip.
evidence: For: GameSummary.castledPly <= 20 (game.js records the ply of his castling move)
For: GameSummary.minorsOutPly <= 24 (the first ply at which both his knights and both his bishops had left b1, g1, c1 and f1)
For: no instance of pawns, takers, their_last_move, guards or free with ply <= 30 in that game (HoldRecord.ply)
Against: any of the three failing in a counted game; a game that ended before ply 30 by mercy or give-up counts against (he did not get out alive)
Neutral: games under 20 player moves won by his checkmate
nodes.mastery_rule: asking -> quiet: three of the last four counted games meet all three conditions. quiet -> off: five of the last six.
nodes.how_it_is_practised: There is no hold category for this node, so its practice is the opening and the close. When current, the book deepens to the bot's sixth move on the Italian and Ruy main lines (each reply verified under 50 cp at depth 18 like today's eight) so the first ten moves are stable enough for the principles to be visible, the opening line is 'Knights and bishops out, king castled by move ten. Then we talk.', and the close card gains one sentence about the opening in piece words ('Castled by move eight, everything out. Out alive.' / 'The king never castled.'). While quiet the opening line goes back to 'Your move.' and the close sentence stays; while off the close sentence goes too.
nodes.retire_or_decay: off -> quiet when two of the last three counted games fail a condition; quiet -> asking when three of four fail. The deeper book stays while the node is quiet and returns to the eight lines when off.

models.next_rule: At boot and at Again, path.derive(games, holds, events) is recomputed from the stored log and nothing else. (1) Counted games are those with >= 20 player moves or ended by his checkmate; windows are counted games. (2) Each node's hand state is the highest state its mastery rule supports, then lowered by its decay rule, evaluated over the window ending at the last game (asking, quiet, off). (3) The current node is one node: candidates are the nodes not off whose prerequisites are all quiet or off, plus any node with against-weight >= 3 in the last three counted games whatever its prerequisites; each candidate's score is its against-weight over the last three counted games; the highest wins, ties go to lane order (lane one, two, three, four) then position in the lane; with no evidence at all the current node is pawns. (4) The opponent for the next game is the gift-rate notch (existing rule, plus the 0.05 notch when free is off) and the shaping of the current node only: threat moves for their_last_move, a forced gift for free, mate threats for their_mate, the mate gift for my_mate, no resignation for finish, the deeper book for out_alive, nothing for pawns, takers and guards. (5) The gate's suppression set is the nodes in off (their category and sub-case, or the pawn/no-pawn split for hanging_after_move) and the quiet-copy set is the nodes in quiet; ALWAYS_HOLD categories are never suppressed, only given the quiet copy. (6) The opening line is the stored K3 line if one was written for the game that just ended, else the current node's template line, prefixed by a promise or a decay sentence when a hand state changed since the last game (transitions are the diff between derive over the last N games and derive over the last N minus one). (7) There is no drill: the next game is the drill. One more rule, the summit: when pawns, takers, their_last_move, guards and free are all off, the game opens 'Today I keep my hands in my pockets.' and only ALWAYS_HOLD and BIG_LOSS holds fire.
felt_in_game: The hold's voice changes per look before anything is drawn: the full question, then 'Hold on. You know this one. Tap it.' with no hint on the first wrong tap, then nothing at all: the piece lands, the opponent takes, the close card tells.

The game opens with a line that is a promise or a confession about one look ('I will not ask about the pawns today. They are yours.' / 'The pawns, once, and I said nothing. I will ask again.'), and the promise is checkable at the close.

The opponent's gifts climb the ladder with him: a free minor to take, then a piece of his threatened, then a check that would be mate, then a mate for him to find, then an opponent that will not resign so he has to deliver it.
The gift rate steps down a notch when free goes off: the opponent stops leaving pieces because he takes every one.
Show me stays available before the tap in quiet holds, so the look can be checked without being told, which is the second SM-2 review ('without the board's hint') inside a real game.
The summit game: 'Today I keep my hands in my pockets.' and no amber square appears for a material look all game; the close card is the only witness.
The ending is played when finish is current: Black does not give up, and the first checkmate against a bot that did not resign is the node's one celebration.
models.shown: One more state of the same page, 'Where I am', #board[data-state=path], reached from a --muted link under the close card's summary, and, only after the first hand state ever changes, from the idle link row for the first ten seconds of a game ('I have stopped asking about the pawns. See where you are.'). It is never the first screen. The board stays the hero: it shows the position of his most recent hold or landing of the selected look, the piece lifted with its shadow over the amber square and the board dimmed, no question, input locked. The serif line reads the look's result sentence in his voice and, after it, Claude's narration or the template ('You are on the pawns. What takes it is next.'). Under the board, where the close card lives, the nine sentences in the serif in four short paragraphs (the lanes), each in one of three inks: --muted for a look the coach still asks about (asking), --ink for one it has gone quiet on (quiet), --coach for one that is his (off), and the current look alone carries a thin --coach underline. Tapping a sentence re-aims the board at that look's last position; a sentence with no position yet leaves the board on the start position. One link, 'Back', returns to the close card or idle. It never shows counts, percentages, dates as numbers, streaks, bars, ticks, badges or a next-up arrow; the only time it says a number is a number word inside a sentence ('quiet for three games'), never as a figure.
models.llm_role: Three calls, all quick tier, all validated by validate.js, all with template fallbacks so the ladder is identical without Claude. (a) K3, the close line, one call when the close card is on screen, cached 24 h by game id: the prompt is the fact sheet of this game's holds, the last five games' category counts, the hand states before and after this game and the transitions, and asks for {one_thing <= 18 words, next_game <= 12 words} in the coach's voice; it names the look that moved and the look he skips most in his own words ('Both holds today were a knight landing where a pawn could reach it.' / 'The pawns are yours now. Next, what takes the knight.'); next_game is stored and becomes the opening line, which costs no call. (b) K5, the narration, when 'Where I am' opens, cached by a hash of the hand states plus the last three games' counts: three sentences of at most 20 words, where he is, what is quiet, what is next, no numbers ('You stopped leaving knights where pawns reach them two games ago. The piece that takes is what we are on. Their queen on your king is after that.'); squares allowed are the shown position's. (c) K1 unchanged, with two facts added to the sheet: the current look and this hold's hand state, so 'This one again' or 'You know this one' is only ever said when the log says so. What Claude never does: decide a hand state, choose the current node, suppress or fire a hold, or name a square outside the fact sheet. Without Claude: the template close line keyed by node and transition, the template narration, the template follow-ups; nothing looks missing.
models.engine_role: Unchanged as the source of every chess fact and gains three jobs. (1) The gate runs on every drop even for off looks, so a landing is a logged verdict with its category, sub-case, netLoss and ply, not a guess. (2) Shaping candidates are enumerated by chess.js and verified by the Worker exactly as gifts are today: threat moves and mate threats at depth 10 within 100 cp of the full-strength top move; the mate gift only when the bot's full-strength eval is already -200 or worse; the forced gift uses the existing six-candidate depth-10 check. (3) The pre-search already knows a mate in one for him; game.js logs it as a mate_chance event. finishPlies and materialAtEnd come from chess.js counts; castledPly and minorsOutPly from the move list as it is played. Everything stays under the verdict budget because shaping runs in the bot's reply step, which already has the look search and up to six depth-10 checks.
models.persistence: The ladder is derived, never stored: path.derive is a pure function of the log, recomputed at every boot and Again, so a corrupted or missing path state cannot exist and the tests feed synthetic logs straight in. The log grows by: HoldRecord outcome 'landed' (matched, suppressed, with the suppression reason: pair, quiet, hand); GameSummary fields castledPly, minorsOutPly, materialAtEnd, finishPlies and events: [{kind: 'gift'|'threat'|'mate_threat'|'mate_gift'|'mate_chance'|'free_taken'|'you_looked', ply, square?, piece?, taken?, parried?}]; KEEP.GAMES rises from 5 to 10 and KEEP.HOLDS from 30 to 60 so five-game windows have margin. Stored besides the log: holdon.v1.path.said (node ids whose promise line has been said, so a celebration is said once), holdon.v1.path.k3 (the stored next_game line keyed by game id), the gift-rate notch as today. All of it behind store.js, localStorage as the always-there layer, mirrored to db at data/users/{id}/games, holds, path when db and user resolve; on boot the db copy wins when it is newer by game date, and a Viewer who cannot write plays with the ladder derived from localStorage only.
models.first_session: The tutorial is unchanged: Bxf7+ held, the king tapped, taken back. The first real game opens on 'Your move.' with every node asking and pawns current by default; the opponent is plain (gifts at 0.12, no shaping, because pawns shapes nothing). He gives a knight to a pawn, is held, takes it back; later plays one anyway. The close card reads as today plus the K3 line or its template: 'Two holds today, both a pawn you did not see. The pawns are what we are on.' and a --muted link 'Where I am'. If he taps it he sees the board on his knight hanging to the pawn, lifted and amber, and nine sentences, one underlined ('I see the pawn before my piece lands'), all in --muted, nothing else, no numbers; the line says 'You are on the pawns. What takes it is next.' The second game opens 'The pawns. Before the piece lands, look for them.' Nothing climbs in session one; the first climb (pawns to quiet) needs two clean counted games, so the earliest promise line is game four, and that is the first thing on the ladder he is pulled back for.
models.why_new: Dr. Wolf counts skills up with numbers and never steps back; Chess.com Lessons and Lichess Practice are courses beside the game; Aimchess reads your online games into a dashboard and prescribes drills; Chessable repeats lines. None makes the absence of coaching the progression, none changes the opponent's gifts to match the look you are on, and none announces a game with the hand off as the earned thing. The closest thing in games generally is training wheels coming off, and no chess product does it per look with evidence from real play.
risks: Off switches the thesis off for one look: a piece lands silently. Mitigated by punish-always (the lesson is still real), ALWAYS_HOLD and BIG_LOSS never suppressed, decay on the first landing, and the close caption 'it landed'; measured by givenAway not rising in the game after a node goes off.

Rare nodes (their_mate, guards, finish) could sit in asking forever on natural evidence alone; the shaping manufactures the chances, so the shaping must be tested to produce at least one event per two games in bot_sim.py or the rule windows are unreachable.

Shaped moves may read as alien (a lunge that threatens mate): the 100 cp bound against the full-strength top move and the depth-10 check are the defence, and the sampler already plays Skill Level 3 moves.

Flapping between quiet and asking would feel like a coach who cannot make up its mind: the two-game climb and two-event decay are hysteresis, and the scenario asserts a synthetic log of alternating clean and one-landing games stays in quiet.
'You know this one' can read as smug after a wrong tap; the second-tap naming is the floor and the copy is one line that can be rewritten without touching the model.

Nine sentences in three inks must be legible in dark mode and at 400 px with the board above them: the close card already proves a list under the board fits; the path state must be screenshot in all four harness runs.

The log additions (landed outcomes, events, four fields) touch game.js and bot.js, the two largest files; the hold log's shape is versioned (holdon.v1 stays, missing fields read as absent) so old logs derive a valid ladder.

models.name: Doors
models.one_sentence_for_a_beginner: Every piece you give away becomes a door: the same position comes back as tomorrow's first game, then a week later with less help, then a month later with none, and when you have walked through it three times that look is yours.
models.the_idea: A map of your own games. A door is a position of his, the one before a move that gave material away (played anyway, or landed unheld), saved with its look. The first game of a session can open at a door instead of the start position: the board shows the position, the ghost of what he did last time plays once and rewinds (Show me reused as memory), and the line says 'Yesterday. This is where the knight went. Your move.' He walks through by keeping the piece: a different move that is not held and does not land, then nine more of his moves with nothing of that look landing; the opponent plays on from there punish-always and the game runs to its end like any other. A door comes back on the chess master's SM-2 schedule with the hand fading each time: the next day with the hold asking, a week later with the hold quiet ('Hold on. You know this one.'), a month later with the hand off for that look; three walks through and the door closes, and two closed doors make the look his. Set doors exist for the ending (king and queen, king and rook, king and two rooks against a bare king defended at full strength) and open when the log shows Black keeps resigning before he ever mates. It fits Hold On because the question travels with the position (the brief's own novel object), because nothing on the map is a number, and because the loop across sessions is one sentence on the close card: 'Tomorrow: the knight from today is waiting.' It is the complement of the ladder: the ladder fades the hand per look, Doors fades it per position.

nodes.name_as_result: I stop leaving pieces where a pawn takes them
nodes.what_it_is: The doors made from hanging_after_move moments with a pawn among the takers: his knight on e5 with a pawn on d6, saved as the position before the move.
evidence: A door is made from a HoldRecord of this kind with outcome 'anyway' or 'landed', netLoss >= 2, and the pre-search's evalBefore >= -300 (stored on the record; a door is never a lost position)

A walk: {date, stage, result: 'through'|'again'} appended to the door; 'through' at stage 0 means the first move from the door was not played anyway and did not land (a hold taken back and then a clean move counts), at stage 1 the first move was not held at all, at stage 2 nothing landed, and in every stage the next nine player moves held no 'anyway' or 'landed' of this kind
A door closed: three 'through' walks at stages 0, 1 and 2
In regular games the same instances as the ladder (anyway, landed, back, first-tap grade) count toward the hand state
nodes.mastery_rule: Yours when two doors of this kind are closed, or when no door of this kind was made in the last five counted games and every open door of this kind is at stage >= 1. Yours sets the hand to quiet in regular games; it never sets off (in this model the hand is off only inside a stage-2 door, for ten moves).
nodes.how_it_is_practised: Stage 0 (next day): the door opens, the ghost of his old move and the pawn's capture plays with the -N float and rewinds, the line is the door's open_line, the hold for this look is asking. Stage 1 (a week later): no ghost, 'A week ago, here. Your move.', the hold is quiet. Stage 2 (a month later): 'You have been here. Your move.', the hand is off for this look for his next ten moves. Walking through is silent until the tenth move: then one line, the door's through_line ('Not this time. The knight stayed home.'), and the game goes on.
nodes.retire_or_decay: 'again' at any stage resets the door to stage 0, due tomorrow; a door failed three times opens with Show me pre-played and Claude's line, and after five fails is dropped with 'I will stop bringing this one back.' A new door of this kind makes the look not-yours until the rule holds again. Closed doors are kept as sentences on the map and never reopen.

nodes.name_as_result: I stop leaving pieces where a piece takes them
nodes.what_it_is: Doors from hanging_after_move moments with no pawn among the takers, including captures that lose to the recapture.
evidence: Door made from such a HoldRecord with outcome 'anyway' or 'landed', netLoss >= 2, evalBefore >= -300
Walks and closings as for pawns
Regular-game instances as for the ladder
nodes.mastery_rule: Two closed doors, or no door made in the last five counted games with every open door at stage >= 1.
nodes.how_it_is_practised: As pawns, with the ghost playing the capture and the recapture when there is one. At stage 1 Show me stays available before the tap so he can check without being told.
nodes.retire_or_decay: As pawns.

nodes.name_as_result: I answer what their last move attacked
nodes.what_it_is: Doors from ignored_attack moments (all three sub-cases): the position before the move in which something of his was attacked and he did something else.
evidence: Door made from ignored_attack with outcome 'anyway' or 'landed', netLoss >= 2, evalBefore >= -300
Walks: 'through' additionally requires the attacked piece (record.best) to be neither captured nor hanging after his first move from the door
Regular-game instances as for the ladder, plus you_looked and threat events
nodes.mastery_rule: Two closed doors, or no door made in the last five counted games with every open door at stage >= 1.
nodes.how_it_is_practised: At stage 0 the ghost plays their capture of the attacked piece; the line 'Yesterday. Their last move pointed at the bishop. Your move.' is the only time a door line names the piece under attack (it is a memory, not a hint, and it is stage 0 only). Stage 1: 'A week ago, here. Your move.' Stage 2: hand off for ten moves. The opponent plays from the door at full strength for its first reply (the threat is still there) and then its usual ladder.
nodes.retire_or_decay: As pawns.

nodes.name_as_result: I take what is free
nodes.what_it_is: Doors from free_piece_ignored moments and from verified gifts walked past: the position in which something of theirs was free and he did something else.
evidence: Door made from free_piece_ignored with outcome 'anyway' or 'landed', or from a gift event with taken false, evalBefore >= -300
Walks: 'through' means his first move from the door captured the free piece (record.best, or the gift square); there is no ten-move tail for this look
Regular-game instances: free_piece_ignored holds, gift events, free_taken rewards
nodes.mastery_rule: Two closed doors, or no door made in the last five counted games with every open door at stage >= 1.
nodes.how_it_is_practised: Stage 0: the ghost plays his own missed capture with no number (as Show me does for this category), the line 'Yesterday. Something of theirs was free here. Your move.', the hold asking if he again does something else. Stage 1: no ghost, 'A week ago, here.', quiet. Stage 2: hand off; if he walks past it again the close card says so. Through: 'Free knight. You looked.' fires as the reward and the game continues.
nodes.retire_or_decay: As pawns.

nodes.name_as_result: I see the mate, theirs and mine
nodes.what_it_is: Doors from allowed_mate moments (he must parry) and missed_mate moments (he must deliver), kept as one node because both are the one-move look at a king.
evidence: Door made from allowed_mate or missed_mate with outcome 'anyway' or 'landed' (both are ALWAYS_HOLD, so 'landed' only via the pair rule), no evalBefore floor for missed_mate (he was winning), evalBefore >= -300 for allowed_mate

Walks: an allowed_mate door is 'through' when his first move allows no mate in one (chess.js) and the next nine moves hold no allowed_mate; a missed_mate door is 'through' when his first move is the mate
Regular-game instances as for the ladder's their_mate and my_mate
nodes.mastery_rule: Two closed doors, or no door made in the last five counted games with every open door at stage >= 1.
nodes.how_it_is_practised: Stage 0: for allowed_mate the ghost plays their mating move and rewinds (the line 'Yesterday. Their queen landed here. Your move.'), for missed_mate the ghost plays his own mate with no number ('Yesterday. You had this. Your move.'); the hold is asking. Stage 1: no ghost, quiet. Stage 2: the quiet copy (these categories are never off). The opponent's first reply from an allowed_mate door is full strength so the threat is real.
nodes.retire_or_decay: 'again' on a mate door resets to stage 0 tomorrow and also sets the ladder's hand for that look to asking at once.

nodes.name_as_result: I can mate with a queen or a rook
nodes.what_it_is: Three set doors that are not from his log: king and queen, king and rook, king and two rooks against a bare king (8/8/8/4k3/8/8/8/4K2Q w - - 0 1, 8/8/8/4k3/8/8/8/R3K3 w - - 0 1, 8/8/8/4k3/8/8/8/R3K2R w - - 0 1), each verified as a forced mate in the repo's positions.json. The chess master's pattern 2 project as a game.
evidence: The doors open (become due) when the last five counted games hold two or more 'resign' wins and zero 'mate-win', or any allowed_stalemate instance, or a 'draw' with materialAtEnd >= 5

A walk: 'through' means checkmate within 40 plies of the door with zero allowed_stalemate 'anyway' or 'landed'; 'again' means a stalemate, a draw, or the fortieth ply without mate (the line 'Not this time. The box is still open.')
Regular games: 'mate-win' results and allowed_stalemate instances as for the ladder
nodes.mastery_rule: Yours when all three set doors are closed (through at stages 0, 1 and 2: with the stalemate hold asking, then quiet, then off), and no allowed_stalemate instance in the last five counted games.
nodes.how_it_is_practised: The door opens with 'Black keeps giving up before the end. Here is the end. Your move.' the first time and 'The end again. Your move.' after; the bot defends at Skill 20 depth 12 (the gift and sampler ladder is off at set doors; the bot never resigns here); the stalemate hold fires per stage; the forty-ply clock is felt, not shown: at the thirtieth ply the line says once 'The box is open. Close it.' A through at stage 2 on the two-rook door is the node's celebration: 'Checkmate. Nobody pointed.' The three doors open in the order two rooks, queen, rook, because the ladder mate is the easiest to feel.
nodes.retire_or_decay: 'again' resets that door to stage 0 due tomorrow; a stalemate in a regular game while five up reopens the queen door at stage 0 whatever its state.

models.next_rule: At boot and at Again: doors.derive(doors, games, now) is pure. (1) Doors are made at game end from this game's qualifying records (one per piece-and-square pair; a new door for a pair with an open door replaces it and resets its stage); at most two open doors per look and eight in all, oldest dropped; dueAt is tomorrow 04:00 local for a new door. (2) If sessionStorage holdon.door is unset (one door per session, so a session is one door and then fresh games) and the engine reports ready within 2 s of boot and at least one door has dueAt <= now: open the due door with the lowest stage, then the oldest madeAt; set the session flag; load its FEN as the game's start position with the door's stage deciding the hand for its look (asking, quiet, off) and the memory ghost at stage 0; the opponent's first reply from an attacked or allowed_mate door is full strength, then the usual ladder. (3) Else the start position with the remembered line. (4) A walk is judged by game.js at the tenth player move from the door (or at the first move for free and missed_mate doors, or at mate or ply 40 for set doors) and appended; 'through' sets dueAt to +7 days at stage 1, +30 days at stage 2, or closes the door; 'again' sets stage 0, dueAt tomorrow. (5) The hand in regular games: a look that is yours gets the quiet copy; nothing is ever off outside a stage-2 door. (6) The close card's last line is the hook, templated: 'Tomorrow: the knight from today is waiting.' when a door was made, 'Next week: the bishop from today comes back.' after a through, 'Nothing waits for tomorrow.' when none; it is never a count.
felt_in_game: The first game of a session opens on his own position, not the start position, with the ghost of what he did last time playing once and rewinding.
The same position comes back with less help each time: the question, then 'You know this one', then nothing, on a schedule he never sees as dates, only as 'Tomorrow', 'Next week', 'In a month'.
A walk through is silent for ten moves and then one line; a walk that fails is one honest line and the door is sealed for tomorrow.
The ending becomes a game: three set positions where the bot defends at full strength and will not resign, with the stalemate hold fading across the three visits.
In regular games, a look that is his gets the quiet hold, so the doors change the ordinary game too.
The close card ends with what is waiting tomorrow, which is the only pull-back line in the product and is true by construction.
models.shown: One more state of the same page, 'Where you have been', #board[data-state=path], reached from a --muted link under the close card summary, and from the idle link row only in the first ten seconds of a game that opened at a door ('This is a door. See the others.'). The board shows the selected door's position with the old move's piece lifted over its amber square and the board dimmed, no question. The serif line reads the door's open_line and when it returns in words ('Tomorrow.' / 'Next week.' / 'In a month.' / 'Closed.'). Under the board the doors as serif sentences, one per door, grouped by look in lane order; open doors in --ink, doors due today with a thin --coach underline, closed doors replaced by the look's result sentence in --coach ('I stop leaving pieces where a pawn takes them'), looks with no door yet in --muted. Tapping a sentence re-aims the board. Never shown: counts of doors, dates as numbers, intervals as days, streaks, bars, ticks. The set doors appear as 'The end' with one sentence per position ('King and two rooks. Tomorrow.').
models.llm_role: Two calls, quick tier, validated, with template fallbacks. (a) K4, the door lines, one call per door when it is made, while the close card is already on screen, cached by door id: the prompt is the hold's fact sheet (the position before the move, the move in piece words, what took it, the net loss) and the K2 ground rules, asking for {open_line <= 14 words: what happened here in piece words, past tense, naming no move and no square outside the fact sheet ('This is where the knight went where a pawn could reach it.'); through_line <= 12 words: said after he walks through ('Not this time. The knight stayed home.')}; template fallback 'Last time, here, a {piece} went where a {taker} was waiting. Your move.' / 'Through. The {piece} stayed.' (b) K5, the map narration when 'Where you have been' opens, cached by a hash of the open door ids: at most three sentences of 20 words saying what the doors have in common, from the doors' fact sheets, no numbers ('Three of these are the same knight landing next to their pawns. The bishop one is their last move, ignored.'); this is the thing a table cannot do: finding the one shape across his positions and saying it in words. K2 and K1 are unchanged inside door holds, with 'this is a door, stage one' in the fact sheet so 'You have been here' is only said when true. Claude never picks which door opens, never sets a stage, never judges a walk; doors.derive and chess.js do. Without Claude: template lines, no narration, the same doors.
models.engine_role: Every door is a position the engine already judged (the verdict's evalBefore and the hold's refutation are on the record), so opening one needs no new facts; the ghost replays the stored refutation. The engine must be warm to play from a mid-game FEN, hence the 2 s boot check and the fallback to the start position with the door kept due. A walk's 'through' is chess.js (nothing of that look held or landed for ten moves, the attacked piece safe, the capture made, mate delivered) plus the gate running as usual. Set doors are verified forced mates in positions.json; the bot defends them at Skill 20 depth 12 with the gift and sampler ladder off. The opponent's first reply from a threat or mate door is the full-strength top move so the threat he failed to see is still on the board.
models.persistence: holdon.v1.doors: an array of at most eight door objects {id, look, fen, san, category, sub, best, netLoss, evalBefore, madeAt, gameId, stage: 0|1|2, dueAt, walks: [{date, stage, result}], lines: {open_line, through_line}|null, fails}, plus the three set doors keyed by name with the same shape; HoldRecord gains evalBefore (a stored number never shown). Doors are the one stored thing that is not derived from the log, because their schedule is a clock; everything else (yours, the hand in regular games, what is due) is doors.derive(doors, games, now), pure and tested with a fixed now. sessionStorage holdon.door marks the one door of this session and dies with the tab. Mirrored to db at data/users/{id}/doors when db and user resolve, localStorage always; on boot the copy with the newer walk wins per door id; a Viewer who cannot write gets doors from localStorage only and the close card says nothing about tomorrow.
models.first_session: The tutorial is unchanged. The first real game runs as today; if he plays a hold anyway or a piece lands unheld, the close card ends 'Tomorrow: the knight from today is waiting.' and shows the --muted link 'Where you have been', which, if tapped, shows the board on that knight lifted over its square and one sentence under it ('This is where the knight went where a pawn could reach it. Tomorrow.'). If the game was clean: 'Nothing waits for tomorrow. Well played.' and the map shows nine muted sentences and the board on the start position. Nothing opens in session one: the first door is sealed until 04:00, which is the hook. Session two opens on his knight with the ghost playing the pawn's capture, and the line 'Yesterday. This is where the knight went. Your move.'
models.why_new: Lichess's 'Learn from your mistakes' replays your game's errors once, right after the game, as puzzles with the answer available; Chess.com's Game Review shows the better move; Chessable schedules lines you studied, not positions you lost; Aimchess prescribes generic drills from stats. None brings your own position back as tomorrow's real game, on a spaced schedule, with the coach's help fading each visit, and none makes the close of today's game a promise about tomorrow's first position. The novel object, as the brief says, is the question travelling with the position; here it travels through time.
risks: A door position can be worse than it looks (he was losing, the eval floor of -300 is a guess): a door that is 'again' three times opens with Show me pre-played, and five fails drop it with one honest line, so no door becomes a wall.
A week and a month may outrun his engagement; a due door he never comes back for simply waits, and a stage-2 walk a year later is still a stage-2 walk; nothing expires, nothing nags.
Mid-game FENs need a warm engine; on a cold phone the door is skipped silently and stays due, and the scenario covers the cold-boot fallback.

One door per session keeps the session mostly fresh games, but a player who wants doors will find only one a day; the map's 'Open it' link on a due door is the escape hatch (a second door per session on an explicit tap, never automatic).
Door games skip the opening, so out_alive has no door and lives only in the ladder; Doors is a complement, not the whole pathway.

The set doors need positions.json entries verified as forced mates and the bot's resignation and ladder switched off at doors; a bug there makes the ending drill either trivial or endless, so the forty-ply clock and the stalemate hold are both asserted in the scenario.

models.persona: The LLM engineer: owner of coach.js and validate.js. I decide when Claude is called, what facts the prompt holds, what shape the reply must have, how it is checked before a word reaches the line or a mark reaches a square, and what the page does, identically, when Claude is absent, declined, rate-limited or wrong.
models.perspective_summary: The pathway must never be Claude's. Where the player is, what counts as evidence, when a look is mastered, what the next game is: all of that is a pure function over the hold log (path.js) that runs in node over a synthetic log with no browser and no model, exactly as gate.js is a pure function over fact sheets. What Claude adds is the four things a table cannot phrase: it narrates where the player is in the player's own words (the sentences he typed into Hear me out, which the log does not keep today and must), it writes the one question the coach asks on the next hold of the look he keeps missing (prefetched, so it is on screen at 0 ms and never swaps under his eyes), it frames the played-anyway position he is about to replay, and it writes the line that opens the next game. All four come from ONE quick-tier call per game, K3, fired at the close card and only in a view that has already consented through Hear me out (so no dialog can ever appear over a board), default cache because the input (game id plus the log) is stable, and its outputs are stored, not spoken, so the next game opens with Claude's line at 0 ms and zero calls even on the phone via the db mirror. A fifth, optional thing is an explicit-tap call on the path state (K5) that explains one look over one of his own held positions, cached per record. Validation is the existing pipeline with one new wrapper: K3 runs validateText with an EMPTY allowed-square set, because its words will be shown over positions Claude has not seen, so any square, any digit, any SAN token and any banned word rejects, plus shape rules (the question starts 'Hold on.' and ends 'Tap it.', names only the piece words the node allows, ask_first is in the offered set). I ran this wrapper against the real validate.js today: the example reply passes and seven bad replies each reject for their own reason. Four log changes are needed before any of this is honest: holdRecord() in game.js drops taps[].ask (so a tap on a K2-chosen look is indistinguishable from the hold's own look), the Hear me out text is not stored (add `said`), the record lacks answer/refutation (needed to replay a hold without the engine), and suppressed verdicts are not logged (add outcome 'unheld' for the hands-off game). Without Claude the pathway is identical: every line it writes has a template keyed by node, and the only thing missing is his own words.

models.name: The hand that fades
models.one_sentence_for_a_beginner: There are eight looks a coach keeps stopping your hand for; the path is the order you stop needing them, and you can tell you have moved because the coach goes quiet about that one.
models.the_idea: A short ladder of looks, not of chess concepts: each node is one thing the coach stops your hand for today (a pawn takes it, a piece takes it, what takes back, their last move, what you leave behind, what is free, their check, finishing a won game), and the path is the order in which you stop needing to be told. It is a graph with soft prerequisites (the easier look before the harder one, their last move before their next move) and the current node is the zone of proximal development read straight off the log: the first look in order that still produces holds. A look is mastered by three kinds of evidence, all of them games, which is learno's three-source rule in Hold On's terms: it stopped happening (zero holds of the kind over three full games), you can answer it on the board (first tap right on its own look most of the time), and you survived one game with the coach's hand off for that look. Mastery is felt as the hand fading for that look before anything is shown, and it decays if the look comes back. It fits Hold On because every node is already a gate category or sub-case, every piece of evidence is already a recorded event, and the measure of progress is the one the product already believes in: the silence of a coach who stops interrupting. Claude's part is to say where you are in your own words and to ask the remembered question the way a person who read your last three games would ask it.

nodes.name_as_result: I stop leaving pieces where a pawn takes them.
nodes.what_it_is: The three looks from their chair, pawns first: before the piece lands, which enemy pawn reaches that square. The gate's hanging_after_move where the engine's taker (answer.best) is a pawn.
evidence: Negative: a HoldRecord with category hanging_after_move, san without 'x', and the piece on record.best in record.fen a pawn (the same test gate.remembered() already uses), any outcome: back, anyway, ended, or the new 'unheld'.

Positive, the tap: the record's first tap graded 'right' with taps[0].ask null or 'what_takes_it' (the hold's own look; a right tap on a K2-chosen safe_square does not count, which is why holdRecord() must stop dropping ask).
Positive, the game: a full game (plies >= 40, or result mate-win, mate-loss or resign) with zero records of this node.
Positive, the constraint: a GameSummary with handsOff === 'pawn-takes' and no 'unheld' record of this node with netLoss >= 2.
nodes.mastery_rule: PLAYED: zero records of this node in the last three full games; AND TAPPED: over the last ten records of this node in holdon.v1.holds, first-tap-right (as defined in evidence) in at least seven of ten, or in all when there are three to nine, vacuous when the whole log holds fewer than three; AND HANDS-OFF: one full game stored with handsOff === 'pawn-takes' and zero 'unheld' records of this node with netLoss >= 2. Mastered the moment all three hold; stored as an event {id, gameId} so it survives the five-game window.
nodes.how_it_is_practised: While current: the next hold of this node opens with the remembered question instead of the template at 0 ms ('Hold on. The pawn again: which one reaches that square? Tap it.', Claude's words from K3 or COPY.PATH.QUESTION['pawn-takes']); the opening line names it ('Before the piece lands, find the pawn that reaches that square.'); a played-anyway hold of this node is offered as 'Play it again from here' on the close card; when PLAYED and TAPPED hold, the next game is announced hands-off for pawns ('This game I will not stop your hand for a pawn. It is real.') and gate.verdict receives gameState.handsOff = 'pawn-takes' and returns suppressed: 'handsoff' for this node, except ALWAYS_HOLD and netLoss >= 5, logging the moment as outcome 'unheld'.
nodes.retire_or_decay: On mastery the next game's opening line says once 'You stopped leaving pieces where a pawn takes them.' and the node's remembered question is dropped; a later hold of this node is a quiet hold ('Hold on.' alone, the tap graded with the ring, buttons after the tap or three seconds). Decay: two records of this node in the last three full games, or one anyway/unheld record with netLoss >= 3, removes the mastery event; the node is current again and the opening line says 'The pawns again. Watch them.'

nodes.name_as_result: I stop leaving pieces where one of theirs takes them.
nodes.what_it_is: The same look with a dearer taker: a knight, bishop, rook, queen or king that reaches the square. hanging_after_move where answer.best is not a pawn and the move was not a capture.
evidence: Negative: hanging_after_move, san without 'x', the piece on record.best not a pawn.
Positive: first tap right on what_takes_it; a full game with zero records; a hands-off game for this node with no unheld loss.
