The drill positions are verified (re-run this session at depth 30: R3K2R mate in 5, 4K2Q mate in 8, R3K3 mate in 13) and the early queen is measured at 81 cp, so the opening rung is honestly a move-list fact and not a hold. Gifts change kind by rung with zero new enumeration because the bot's filter already splits 'attacked by a pawn' from 'attacked and undefended'.
critiques.weaknesses: Ten rungs is not one iteration: finish needs a drill mode and a store key, count-before-taking a new gift kind, opening-alive a move list and a third reward, two-targets a gate category that does not exist. The hand goes from asking straight to off with no middle stage, so the first faded loss is the first time he practises the look without the hint; learno's R2 (the same question without the board's hint) is skipped. 'Quiet for three games' with no tap evidence can let go of a look he answers 'named' every time it fires. The cost tie-break between the two prerequisite-free rungs imports the map's flicker. Too many templates to maintain in COPY.
critiques.what_i_would_add: A 'holding' stage between asking and off (the game designer's 'You know this one', the designer's bare question) as the R2 review inside the game; first-tap grades on holding-stage holds as a gate on letting go, never as mastery; cut to the seven hold-evidenced rungs plus the finishing drill this iteration, opening-alive when moves[] lands, two-targets not drawn.

critiques.model: Chess master: The map of your own games
critiques.strengths: Cost in net material is what a coach reads from a stack of a student's games, and gifts aimed at the costly look is the right instinct. Honest about its own cold start.
critiques.weaknesses: The argmax flips between games and a beginner feels pulled about. The global hand budget switches off holds for looks he never learned once he has three clean games, which is the one thing a coach must not do. Weighting by netLoss makes one queen hang outweigh five knight hangs, the opposite of how habits form.
critiques.what_i_would_add: Nothing as a model. Keep two pieces inside the ladder: the netLoss tie-break when two rungs are both eligible, and the narration of the shape across games ('both knights to the fifth rank in front of their pawns').

critiques.strengths: The most honest evidence model on the table: exposures as the denominator, a credible bound that refuses to call one slip in eighty 'learned' and sixty clean exposures 'luck', forgetting per game, one-stage regression so a false mastery costs one felt slip. The three-stage fade (ask, pause, let go) is learno's harder-at-each-interval review made of real moves. The opponent as the review scheduler (ASK_RATE for attacked, GIFT_RATE by stage) is a lever a calendar cannot be. I checked the arithmetic: Beta(1, 19+B) crosses the 1/40 bound at B of about 45, as stated.
critiques.weaknesses: For the two rungs that lose the most games the exposure predicate is near-vacuous: nearly every middlegame position has a non-capturing piece move onto a pawn-covered square, so the denominator for 'pawns' and 'reach' is simply player moves, and the ledger collapses to the ladder's count with extra machinery. Forty-five clean exposures is a game and a half of open play, and no coach calls a look learned after a game and a half; the 'no fail in the last two exposed games' guard is doing the real work and the model should say so. The posterior is folded and stored rather than recomputed from the log, which is less testable than a pure function over synthetic games. Beta quantiles and lambda cannot be explained to Sambudh, which is fine until the page says 'tested often' about one game. Nine sentences read as a syllabus.
critiques.what_i_would_add: Use its exposure predicates only where they bite (attacked, guard, free, both mates, finish) and plain counts over full games for the two hanging rungs; keep pause and let-go as the hand's stages; keep ASK_RATE as the measured lever for the attacked look.

critiques.strengths: It is my own project rule (three of five clean) turned into a scaffold with review games at plus one, three and eight; cheap, transparent, and honest about being coarse.
critiques.weaknesses: Censored: a passive clean game counts as clean. Coupled: one node mixes six looks, so neither the remembering question nor the gifts can be chosen. Slow: five qualifying games per node is weeks at his pace, and short games count for nothing. The 'open' node can only be named, never practised.
critiques.what_i_would_add: Nothing; as its author says, it is the words layer. Its three headings are the MISSION patterns and can label the ladder's lanes on the path face.

critiques.model: Product designer: The hand you no longer need
critiques.strengths: The best-stated 'shown' in the set: six one-line sentences in the board's own footprint, three inks, the hold's amber as the single mark, reached only from the close card and ply 0, nothing scrolls. The 'watching' state is honest hysteresis. The let_land sentence ('That one was yours; I let it land.') is the right tone for a withdrawn hand. Fourteen idle days bringing the hand back for one game is a real coach's rule.
critiques.weaknesses: their_last_move first is the order of the check in lesson 0001, not the order in which habits are won: the pawn look has thirty chances a game and goes quiet first; the attacked look has three or four and needs the opponent to attack something. Merging pawn and piece takers in where_it_lands throws away the one split the gate already computes and that beginners learn in two distinct steps (the pawn is the taker they do not see because it is small). Yours after three games with no middle stage. where_it_lands has no for-evidence beyond absence, which is defensible against this opponent but should be said. finishing sits at 'Not come up yet' forever without a rep source.
critiques.what_i_would_add: The pawn/piece split, the ladder in order of reps per game, the bare stage before the hand withdraws, and set drills for finishing. Keep its page design nearly whole.

critiques.model: Product designer: Three looks, in your words
critiques.strengths: The fading voice (full question, bare question, silent hold) is the harder review inside the game, exactly learno's R2 and R3, and the only practice mechanism in the set that needs no new screen. 'In my words' is a real Claude use: turning 'im attacking his king' plus a log of knight-for-pawn holds into a sentence he recognises as his.
critiques.weaknesses: Three nodes is too coarse to say what he is working on; 'theirs' mixes four categories, so the opening line and the gifts cannot aim. Stages are stored, not derived. The mates sit outside the path. The silent hold after a break reads as a bug. Advancing on three right first taps measures seeing when asked, not looking before the move.
critiques.what_i_would_add: Keep the bare stage and 'In my words'; drop the model.

critiques.strengths: The beginner's own words for the states (watching, quiet, yours) are the ones the page should use. The two-step rule (three clean games, then three more with the hand off before it is 'yours') is how a coach actually withdraws. Weighting played-anyway at two and taken-back at one is right. 'Observed' moves as the denominator (engine-cold moves excluded) is a detail the others missed. The once-a-game extra graded tap is a drill inside the game at zero cost.
critiques.weaknesses: Eight nodes for one iteration. GIFT_RATE 0.16 is unmeasured. Playing on in every won position while finish is current is a thirty-move conversion inside his fifteen minutes; the set drill is cheaper and more honest. The mate rung needs three games of twenty observed moves with zero allowed_mate, but mates are rare, so it sits at 'watching' for weeks with nothing to say. No middle hand stage.
critiques.what_i_would_add: The bare stage; finishing from the verified set positions; keep the state words and the two-step rule.

critiques.strengths: This is what I tell every student: a mistake you made is the lesson you remember. The moment becomes a real game from that position, the opponent punishes as always, and 'answered' is the gate's own verdict, not a stored answer. Today, then another day, then gone is spacing cut to the size of a phone. Correctly never counted as habit evidence (foreknowledge).
critiques.weaknesses: Not a pathway on its own: no habit nodes, no order, no way to say what he is working on. A page that opens on a moment reads as homework unless 'Fresh game instead' is as easy as Again. One moment per FEN, but near-identical positions repeat.
critiques.what_i_would_add: Adopt it whole as the ladder's drill arm: the moment offered is the current rung's kind first, due the next day, retired after two answers on two days.

critiques.strengths: Three hand states per look (asking, quiet, off) with 'Hold on. You know this one. Tap it.' as the un-hinted review; the opponent climbing with the player (free minors, then threats, then mate threats, then a free mate, then an opponent that will not resign) is the strongest statement in the set of how the games should change; the summit game announced before it starts is the one earned moment a beginner would tell a friend about. Two-game climb and two-event decay as hysteresis.
critiques.weaknesses: Five new bot shapings in one iteration, each needing bot_sim: threat moves within 100 cp of the full-strength move at Skill 3 will make the opponent measurably stronger and the held-1320 score must be re-run before it ships. 'Quiet' requires every first tap right over two games, which is perception when asked, not the habit. Nine looks in four lanes under the board is a lot of serif on a 400 px phone. The deeper book is unverified work.
critiques.what_i_would_add: Ship the shapings in cost order with a bot_sim gate on each (gift kind first, then the mate gift, then threat moves); keep the three states and the lane headings.

critiques.strengths: SM-2 on his own positions with the help fading per visit (ask, bare, off) is learno's review rule made of games; set doors for the ending; the close card's 'Tomorrow: the knight from today is waiting.' is the only pull-back line in the product and it is true by construction.
critiques.weaknesses: A week and a month outrun a player who plays three times a week; a stage-2 'hand off for ten moves' inside a position he already lost once is a trap; one door per session and mid-game FENs need a warm engine on a cold phone; eight open doors is a backlog with a name.
critiques.what_i_would_add: Take the next-day, then-another-day rhythm from the beginner's moments instead of week and month; keep the set doors only for finishing.

critiques.model: LLM engineer: The hand that fades
critiques.strengths: Three sources of mastery that are all games (it stopped happening, he can answer it on the board, he survived a game with the hand off) is learno's three-source rule in Hold On's terms, and the hands-off game is the project under a new constraint. Pawn, piece and takes-back split. One K3 call per game returning four outputs (where, next, again, question), validated against an empty allowed-square set with per-rung piece words and run against the real validator. The honest list of log fixes, which I confirmed in game.js. Templates keyed by node so the page is identical without Claude.
critiques.weaknesses: TAPPED (seven of ten first taps right) measures seeing when asked, not looking before the move; it belongs as a gate on fading, not as a source of mastery. A single hands-off game is a one-game test, and a coach wants three; a lucky quiet game masters the rung. Mastered rungs are stored as events rather than recomputed. The free rung counts freeTaken without an 'offered' denominator. Entering the path by tapping the brand is a tab in disguise.
critiques.what_i_would_add: The hands-off game as a three-game stage (holding to off), tapped-right as the fade gate, giftsOffered on the summary, and the drill as a game from the moment rather than a tap over a still.

critiques.strengths: Honest about being small; it is a trust model and says so; the hands-off game announced in one sentence is the fading hand made exact.
critiques.weaknesses: A global budget spends the same patience on a look he has learned and one he has not, so after three clean games a knight lands on a pawn he never learned to see. The look of the week is a pointer, not a node. Five words joined by rules on the close card is a progress bar wearing a serif.
critiques.what_i_would_add: Nothing; its hands-off game lives on inside the per-rung ladder.

critiques.model: Frontend architect: Five questions, one hand
critiques.strengths: The best engineering in the set: path.compute pure over the stored games and a clock; the hand as one additive suppression reason inside gate.verdict with the facts attached; losses[] so the faded hand cannot hide a relapse; gifts {offered, taken}; a db merge by set-union on game id behind a permissions.state check so no dialog lands at boot; norm() for old records. The thirty-day re-check folded into play.
critiques.weaknesses: Qualifying at 24 plies is twelve player moves, too short to say anything about a look. Pawn and piece merged. one_move_mates mixes allowed, missed and stalemate, which are three different looks. 'Light' (the first hold fires, the rest of the game it does not) is odd on the board: the second knight of the game lands silently. No opportunity conditions beyond gifts. The opening node is rightly first to cut.
critiques.what_i_would_add: Forty plies; the pawn/piece split; the bare stage instead of 'light'; keep the persistence and merge design wholesale.

critiques.model: Frontend architect: Your own positions, spaced
critiques.strengths: Cheapest drill possible: no engine, the stored answer set, the hold UI with no game behind it.
critiques.weaknesses: A hold with no game behind it is a puzzle, and a right tap on it is seeing when asked; the position should become a game with the opponent punishing. A drill before the game is a quiz gate, the thing the beginner closes the tab on. Nothing in it is a path.
critiques.what_i_would_add: Store answer and refutation on every record (needed anyway) and turn the drill into the beginner's moment-as-game.
