merged_proposal.name: The ladder of looks: ask, then only hold, then let go
merged_proposal.one_sentence_for_a_beginner: Each rung is one look before you let go of the piece: first I ask, then I only hold, then I let go; a rung is yours when I have gone three whole games without needing to stop your hand for it.
merged_proposal.the_idea: A ladder of looks in the order they are won under 1000, each rung named as a result, each evidenced by the same thing a coach watches for: whether the hand had to stop him, over whole games that were long and full enough for the look to have chances to fail. A human coach never knows a habit is formed from a quiz; he knows it when he goes three whole games without saying the word, and then he stops saying it and watches whether the silence holds with his hand off. That is the rule here, with one thing the log makes possible: gate.verdict() keeps judging every move after the hand stops showing, logging what it would have held as outcome 'quiet', so silence is measured without the scaffold. The hand has three stages per rung, which are learno's three reviews inside a real game: asking (today's hold with its question, and the remembering variant when the rung is current), holding (the piece lifts, the square breathes amber, the board dims, but the line says only 'Hold on. You know this one. Tap it.'; the first wrong tap gets 'Not that one.' with no hint; the second names it as today; this is R2 without the board's hint), and off (the move lands, the opponent takes as it always does, and after the capture one honest sentence: 'There it goes. A knight for a pawn. That one was yours; I let it land.'). Mates and stalemate (ALWAYS_HOLD) never go below holding; a loss of five or more always holds. The games change as he climbs: the gifts change kind with the rung (a minor a pawn can take while the pawn look is open, an undefended one after, fewer as the material rungs go quiet, none at the top), the mate gift appears only while the mate rung is current, the finishing rep comes from four verified set positions against a full-strength defender, and his own played-anyway moments come back as the start of a real game the next day. Claude never decides a rung, a stage, a gift or a hold; it writes four lines per game from path state rendered in words: where he is in his own words, the line that opens the next game, the remembering question for the current rung, and the frame for the position he is about to play again. Where it lives on the page: nothing before the first close card; the close card gains one serif line in the coach's voice under the counts ('The pawns: not once this game. Two more like this and I only hold.') and one muted link, 'Where you are'. Tapping it keeps the board as the hero: it becomes a still of the current rung's last held position from his own log (record.fen with record.san replayed, the piece lifted, the square amber, the board dimmed, input locked), the serif line reads the rung's result sentence and the narration, and under the board, where the close card sits, the rungs as serif sentences in three inks: --coach for rungs the coach still asks about ('I still ask.'), --ink for rungs it only holds ('I only hold now. Two more quiet games and I let go.'), --muted for rungs let go ('Yours. Quiet since Tuesday.'); the current rung alone carries the amber dot in the margin; a rung that came back reads 'Back for now.'; counts are words up to twelve, then 'many'; rungs the page cannot measure are not drawn. One quiet [Back]. Never a numeral, bar, tick, streak, lock, road, date as a figure, rating, or anything red; the copy test covers every template. Honest scope for this iteration: rungs one to seven with the three-stage hand, the gift-kind filter and rate notch, the 'quiet' outcome records and the four log fixes (taps[].ask kept, said stored, answer and refutation on records, escaped and giftsOffered and captures on the summary), KEEP raised to twelve games and eighty holds, the db mirror by set-union on id, the close line, the path face, K3; second slice: the finishing drills (data-mode=drill, holdon.v1.drills) and the mate gift through bot_sim; cut list in order: the opening rung (needs moves[]), threat shaping for their-last-move, the K5 idea line.
nodes_in_order: 1. pawn-look: 'I stop leaving pieces where a pawn takes them.' Against: HoldRecords with category hanging_after_move, variant null, pawnAmongTakers true, any outcome (back, anyway, ended, quiet). Opportunity: none beyond the floor; every board has pawns. Practised while current: the opening line built from his last game ('Three pawns took a piece last game. Before the piece lands, the pawns that touch that square.'); the remembering question at 0 ms ('Hold on. The pawns again. Which one reaches that square? Tap it.'); gifts of kind pawn (a bot minor a pawn can take, the existing filter's first branch). Prerequisites: none.

2. piece-look: 'I stop leaving pieces where one of theirs takes them.' Against: hanging_after_move, variant null, pawnAmongTakers false, any outcome. Opportunity: the floor, and pawn-look at holding or off (a quiet piece look while the pawn look still needs the hand is luck). Practised: question 'Hold on. Not a pawn this time. What reaches that square? Tap it.'; gifts of kind undefended (a bot minor attacked and defended by nothing), so the free piece in front of him needs this look to see. Prerequisite: pawn-look.

3. take-what-is-free: 'I take what is free.' Against: free_piece_ignored, any outcome. Positive: game.freeTaken. Opportunity: game.giftsOffered summed over the window at least two, and freeTaken at least giftsOffered minus one (he took nearly everything he was given). Practised: GIFT_RATE held at 0.12 while current (the step-down waits for this rung); gift kind follows the lower of rungs one and two; a walked-past free piece played anyway is offered as 'Play it again from here'; question 'Hold on. Something of theirs is free again. Tap it.' Prerequisites: none (eligible beside pawn-look; the tie goes to the rung with the larger summed netLoss in the last five full games, ties to ladder order).

4. their-last-move: 'I answer what their last move pointed at.' Against: ignored_attack with sub 'already', any outcome. Positive and opportunity: game.escaped (the 'You looked' reward computed by gate.reward whatever the budget said, now persisted) at least two in the window, which proves the opponent attacked something and he answered. Practised: the escaped reward wins the quiet budget over 'Free knight' while current; question 'Hold on. Their last move pointed at something of yours. Tap it.'; opening line 'Before your move, their last move. What did it touch?'; the measured lever, shipped only when bot_sim reproduces the 1320 and held-1320 scores within one game in ten: the sampler prefers, at ASK_RATE 0.3, a move that attacks a piece of his worth two or more, verified at depth 10 within 100 cp of the full-strength move. Prerequisite: pawn-look.

5. count-before-taking: 'Before I take, I count what takes back.' Against: hanging_after_move with variant takes_back and netLoss at least two, any outcome. Opportunity: window of four full games, eighty player moves, and at least six captures by him (game.captures, a counter incremented at commit when the applied move captured; no move list needed). Practised: question 'Hold on. Before you take there: count what takes back. Tap the first one.'; opening line 'Before you take, count. Theirs on that square, then yours.' Prerequisite: piece-look.

6. guards-and-lines: 'I notice when my move takes a guard away or opens a line onto my own piece.' Against: ignored_attack with sub lost_guard or opened_line, any outcome. Opportunity: four full games, eighty player moves (the events are rarer). Practised: questions 'Hold on. Your move leaves something of yours alone. Tap it.' and 'Hold on. Your move opens a line again. Tap along it.'; 'Play it again from here' is the main practice here because opened lines are perception before they are habit. Prerequisite: their-last-move.

7. mate-both-ways: 'I see a mate in one before it lands, theirs and mine.' Against: allowed_mate and missed_mate, any outcome. Positive: result mate-win. Rule: five full games, zero records, at least two mate-wins. ALWAYS_HOLD: the top stage is holding, worded 'quiet', never off; the holding form keeps the category word ('Hold on. Their check again. Tap where it lands.'). Practised while current: the mate gift, a bot.js change measured with bot_sim before it ships: from the bot's fifteenth move, when he is three or more points ahead, at the gift rate, a sampled move that allows exactly one mate in one and hangs nothing else is kept (the guard's own hasMateInOne enumeration run the other way), logged as a gift of piece 'mate'; missed_mate then holds as today. Any record after quiet wakes the rung to asking at once: a mate is a game. Prerequisites: none.

8. finish: 'I can finish a won game with the queen or a rook, without a stalemate.' Evidence: drill records in holdon.v1.drills {id, date, kind: two_rooks|queen|rook|again, fen, result: mate|draw|over|gaveup, moves, stalemateHolds}; conversions in real games (the bot's king-and-pawns play-on) counted as drills of the piece he had; allowed_stalemate anywhere in the last five games is negative. Set positions, verified this session with engine_check.py mate at depth 30 and recorded in data/positions.json with the command: two rooks 8/8/8/4k3/8/8/8/R3K2R w - - 0 1 (mate in 5: 1.Rh5+ Kd4 2.Ra4+ Kc3 3.Rh3+ Kc2 4.Rb4 Kc1 5.Rc3#), queen 4k3/8/8/8/8/8/8/4K2Q w - - 0 1 (mate in 8), rook 4k3/8/8/8/8/8/8/R3K3 w - - 0 1 (mate in 13); caps 15, 20, 25, about twice optimal, where a beginner with the box technique lands. Rule: two two_rooks within 15, three queen within 20, two rook within 25, on at least three distinct dates, and the last five drill-or-game records hold no stalemate hold, draw or cap. Practised: one drill a day offered on the close card as a quiet button beside Again ('Finish one with two rooks', then the queen, then the rook); the board loads the FEN in data-mode=drill with one sentence ('Mate with two rooks. Their king must be driven to the edge one rank at a time.'), the defender is Stockfish at Skill 20 depth 12 so the stalemate tricks are real, the stalemate hold and the hanging-the-rook hold are active, mate ends with 'Checkmate. Well played.', the cap with 'Twenty moves. From the start, once more?' [Again] [A game]. Decay by time: thirty days without a drill or a conversion offers one again; a failed drill wakes the rung; one passed drill of that kind re-quiets it. Prerequisite: mate-both-ways at holding.

9. opening-alive (defined now, drawn only when moves[] ships): 'I get out of the opening alive: a pawn in the centre, knights and bishops out, king castled by move ten, queen at home.' The gate can never see it: 2.Qh5 costs 81 cp at depth 18 (pgn trace this session: e4 e5 Qh5 Nc6 Bc4 g6 Qf3 Nf6), under the 200 threshold. Evidence from the SAN list on the summary, derived at write time by chess.js: castledMove at most 10, minorsOutBy10 at least 3, earlyQueen false, centrePawnBy3 true, and no given-away record with ply at most 30; a game counts only when it reached his tenth move. Rule: the last three such games pass all five. No hold: a third reward kind under the quiet budget said once at move ten when the facts hold ('Castled, knights and bishops out. The opening is done.'), silence when they do not; the close card names what was missing in words. Not a rung and not drawn: two-targets, the 1000-1200 band's door, until the gate has a threat category.
merged_proposal.next_rule: path.js exports state(games, holds, drills, {today}) and plan(state), pure, deterministic, with no state of their own; the log is the only authority and the path is recomputed at newGame() and endGame(). Full game: plies at least 40, or result in {mate-win, mate-loss, resign} at any length; 'again' games and drills never count as games. Rung states: asking, holding, off (ALWAYS_HOLD rungs top out at holding, worded 'quiet'), plus 'later' when a prerequisite is unmet or the rung is unmeasurable. Transitions, evaluated in ladder order in one pass so prerequisites are known: asking to holding when the last two full games hold zero records of the rung's kind (holds and quiet outcomes), at least forty player moves summed, and the rung's opportunity condition holds; holding to off when three further consecutive full games hold zero records, sixty player moves, the opportunity condition holds, and the first taps on any holding-stage holds of the kind in that window were right at least as often as not (a look he cannot see without the hint is not let go). A woken rung needs two full games of silence, not three, to re-quiet. Decay: off to holding on one record of the kind (the slip is named on the close card and in the next opening line, the bare hold returns, the fade is never a trap); holding to asking on a second record within three full games, or on any play-anyway or 'named' answer on a holding-stage hold; mate-both-ways to asking on any record; fourteen days without a game turns every off rung to holding for one game ('It has been a while. I will hold a little more today.'); finish decays by thirty days. Current rung: the first in ladder order whose state is asking or holding with prerequisites met; when two prerequisite-free rungs are both eligible, the one with the larger summed netLoss in the last five full games, ties to ladder order. plan(state) returns one JSON object game.js reads: hand = for every category, sub-case and the pawn and takes_back splits, the stage of the rung that owns it (gate.verdict receives gameState.hand and returns held for asking, held with bare copy for holding, and suppressed 'faded' for off, except ALWAYS_HOLD and netLoss at least five; game.js logs every suppressed verdict, pair, quiet or faded, as a HoldRecord with outcome 'quiet' and the suppression reason, counted into givenAway as today); gifts = {kind: pawn while pawn-look is not off, undefended while piece-look is not off, none when rungs one, two, three and five are off; rate: 0.12 while take-what-is-free is current, 0.08 once it is off, 0.05 once the four material rungs are off (a new notch, measured)}; mateGift = true while mate-both-ways is current; skill = 3 (the one notch to 4 only when every material rung is off, measured by bot_sim first); drill = the first unmet finishing drill when finish is current and none was played today, else {kind: 'again', holdId} when the last game has a played-anyway or quiet record of the current rung's kind (offered on the close card now, and due as the next day's first game start with 'One of yours, from Tuesday. Your move.' and 'Fresh game instead' beside it; answered twice on two different days retires it; never counted toward silence); openingLine = the stored K3 next_game line if its rung still equals current, else the template for current keyed by last game's evidence in words; questions = the remembering variants for the current rung's categories (K3's validated question or the template); closeLine = the template for what this game did to the current rung plus the slip line when an off rung slipped. scripts/test_path.mjs builds logs with game({plies, result, holds: [{category, sub, pawnAmongTakers, variant, netLoss, ply, outcome, taps}], escaped, giftsOffered, freeTaken, captures}) and asserts: two clean full games move pawn-look to holding and three more to off; three clean games of 24 plies move nothing; a quiet slip returns off to holding and a second within three returns asking; a 'named' tap on a holding hold returns asking; an allowed_mate record wakes the mate rung at once; drills on three dates quiet finish and a stalemate inside a drill does not; the hand excludes an off category and always includes ALWAYS_HOLD and netLoss at least five; the gift kind and rate by state; fourteen idle days make off read as holding for one game; every template line at most 28 words with no digit, passing validate's rules; the same log gives the same state twice.
merged_proposal.why_this_wins: Well defined and computable: nine named rungs with the exact category, sub-case and split that evidence each, a three-stage hand with written transitions, opportunity conditions per rung, and a pure path.js tested over synthetic logs with no browser and no engine. Honest about sparse evidence: full games only, player-move floors, exposure conditions where they bite (escapes, gifts offered, captures, reaching move ten, mate-wins), a longer window for the rare rungs, the gate still judging after the hand stops so silence is real, and a fade that returns on one slip so a false mastery costs one felt loss and never a second. Felt before shown: the opening line names his rung from his own last game at 0 ms; the hold's voice thins per rung (the question, then only the hand, then nothing); the gifts change kind as he climbs; a mate appears for him to find when that is his rung; the ending is a real defender who will not resign; his Tuesday moment is Wednesday's first position. Beautiful when shown: his own held position as the still, the rungs as sentences in his words in three inks with the hold's amber as the single mark, no numerals anywhere, reached only from the close card and never first. Buildable in one iteration because the first seven rungs are the gate's existing categories and splits, the gift kinds are the bot's existing filter reordered, the 'quiet' outcome is written where givenAway is counted today, and the drill and the mate gift are the second slice with bot_sim as their gate; the opening rung and threat shaping are the cut list and are not drawn until measured. And Claude does what a table cannot: from his Hear me out sentences across games and the shape of his slips it writes where he is in his own words, the one question the coach asks on the look he keeps missing, and the frame for the position he is about to play again, all prefetched so they are on screen at 0 ms, all validated against an empty square set and the fixed list of rung phrases, all with a template standing underneath so the ladder is identical without it. It is the coach's own measure of a habit, the silence of a hand that is no longer needed, turned into a model a beginner can state in one sentence and a test can prove over a log.

reviews.persona: The learning scientist: skill acquisition, mastery learning, deliberate practice, spaced retrieval, knowledge tracing (Bayesian and Elo-style), zone of proximal development, interleaving. I judged every model on one question first: does its evidence unit let silence from passivity pass as mastery? Then on whether the scaffold fades with the test retained, whether a false mastery is cheap to reverse, whether the state is recomputable from the log, and whether it ships in one iteration. Facts I verified in the code before writing: app/js/game.js holdRecord() (line 737) keeps only {square, grade} per tap and drops ask; a suppressed verdict (line 514) only increments givenAway and is never logged; the escaped reward (line 556) is never persisted, only freeTaken; factsBefore() is cached per FEN (line 260) and S.pre is set before the verdict (line 307), so an exposure predicate can be computed where the verdict runs. Measured with a node probe over the sixteen recorded positions in app/data/positions.json: open middlegame positions offer two to five legal moves that would hang a piece to a pawn and zero to five that would hang it to a piece; the start position and 1.f3 e5 offer none (book moves are not exposures, correctly); the scratch loop (move, pieceInfo, undo over the non-pawn, non-king legal moves) costs 8 ms mean in node on top of the 14 ms buildFacts the page already pays per position.

critiques.strengths: The best ordering in the room, because it is the order in which looks lose games, and the gate already splits the evidence the way the rungs need (pawnAmongTakers, the takes_back variant, the three ignored_attack sub-cases). Two things here are the right instincts: the gate keeps computing after the hand stops showing, so silence is measured and not assumed (the 'quiet' outcome), and the hand fades per rung rather than by a global budget, which is the one thing a scaffold must never do (fade on a skill not yet learned). The per-rung opportunity conditions (at least two escapes, at least two gifts offered, at least six captures, reaching move ten) are the first honest attempt at a denominator, and the two-slip wake with a shorter re-quiet window is proper hysteresis. The cost tie-break borrowed from the map is bounded and sensible.
critiques.weaknesses: The evidence unit is still the hold count over whole games with 'player moves' as the opportunity, and a move is not a test: sixty player moves in a book-heavy or closed game can hold a dozen real pawn-trap chances, and a player who keeps his pieces home passes three games with nothing tested. The fade is binary (hand on, then off after three games): the first test of the un-cued habit costs a real piece, and the model tolerates two such slips before the hand returns, which is lenient on the thing the product's own measure counts. Mastery is a zero count, so one honest slip in eighty chances reads the same as a habit not formed. Ten rungs, three new gift kinds, a mate gift, Skill 5, a drill store, the move list and opening facts are three iterations of work, each needing bot_sim re-measurement. No time-based review for the game rungs: three weeks away and the hand is still off.
critiques.what_i_would_add: Replace 'player moves' with exposures counted per position (the scratch loop over factsBefore, 8 ms), make the mastery rule 'N clean trials since the last fail' with N per rung instead of three clean games, insert a bare-question stage between asking and off so the un-cued test is cheap, and cut to the six rungs the gate evidences today, deferring the mate gift, the counted gift, Skill 5 and the set-position drills.

critiques.model: The map of your own games (chess master)
critiques.strengths: It is what a human coach does with a stack of games: find the bleeding and work there. Cost from netLoss is a sum the log already carries, the gifts target the costly look, and the master's own honesty about its flaws (cold start, flapping, the global budget) is exemplary.
critiques.weaknesses: From skill acquisition this is the wrong unit twice: cost is a loss measure, not a habit measure (one queen hang outweighs five knight hangs, the reverse of how habits form), and the global hand budget (6, 4, 2, 0) fades the scaffold uniformly across looks at different stages, so a clean game switches off the hold for a look he has never been tested on. The argmax over five games is high-variance and makes 'now' flip, which pulls a beginner about. Five games of cold start.
critiques.what_i_would_add: Keep exactly what the master keeps: cost as a bounded tie-break between eligible rungs and as the gift targeter. Drop the budget entirely.

critiques.model: The Looks Ledger (learning scientist, my own)
critiques.strengths: The only model with an exposure denominator for every node, which is what makes a clean game that never tested a look count as nothing. The credible bound refuses both errors (one slip in eighty is not mastery; sixty clean is not luck), per-game forgetting handles staleness, the three-stage scaffold makes the un-cued stage the real test, one-step regression makes a false mastery cost one felt slip, the opponent is the review scheduler, and the fold is idempotent by game id. My probe today confirms the predicates are cheap and dense enough: two to five pawn-trap moves per open position, 8 ms per pass.
critiques.weaknesses: Over-parameterised for the brief: Beta(1 + A, 19 + B), lambda 0.85, the 0.8 quantile under 1/40 are defensible and unsayable; the one sentence hides the arithmetic. It stores a path document that the log cannot recompute once games age out of the window, which the architect rightly refuses (derived state that can drift). Nine nodes with three stages each is a wall of copy. The 'pause' stage with both buttons at once and no tap graded throws away a grade; the designer's bare question keeps it. The current() cost formula with priorRate and lossPoints is more machinery than the ladder order plus a bounded tie-break. Claude's part is narration only, weaker than the LLM engineer's use of the player's own words.
critiques.what_i_would_add: Replace the posterior with a sliding window in trials ('N clean trials since the last fail', N sized from the same credible-bound analysis but stated as a constant), store per-game trial strings on the GameSummary so the state is a pure function of the stored games, cut to six nodes, use the bare question as the middle stage, and take the LLM engineer's K3.

critiques.model: The Game Ladder (learning scientist, my own)
critiques.strengths: Cheap, transparent, exactly the mission's three-of-five measure, needs no per-move computation, and honest that it is censored and coarse. Its best use is the words layer: the three headings over the per-look ledger.
critiques.weaknesses: A clean game with no contact counts as clean, so a passive player masters 'give' without the look; three of five is weak inference (a player clean half the time passes half the time); one node mixes six looks so the question that remembers cannot choose; five qualifying games per node is weeks at the master's session rate.
critiques.what_i_would_add: Nothing as a model; keep its three headings on the path state.

critiques.model: The hand you no longer need (designer)
critiques.strengths: The four states (not come up yet, the coach's, watching, yours) give a real intermediate stage, and the rule that 'yours' needs either a prior against-event or positive for-evidence is the first attempt in the room to say a look must have been tested before it can be owned. let_land is logged with the gate's facts, the hold policy is frozen per game, fourteen idle days bring every hold back for one game (a review game folded into play), and the visible state is the best designed: the board's footprint, six serif sentences under 34 characters, three inks, one amber dot, measured at 400 px, reachable only from two reading moments. The K3 contract (where, next_game, focus, ask) with 'said' is a strong use of Claude.
critiques.weaknesses: For where_it_lands the designer writes 'absence is proof on its own because the opponent punishes everything', and that is the censoring error: twenty player moves against a punish-always opponent are not twenty tests when the pieces stay home. Three counted games of forty plies is a sample size on games, not on chances. Merging pawn takers and piece takers into one node loses the first and soonest fade, which is the one he will feel first. what_it_leaves can only be proven by having failed before, so a careful player can never own it. The consent dialog landing on a 'Where I am' tap outside a hold is a new place for a dialog.
critiques.what_i_would_add: Exposures as the denominator instead of absence; split pawns from pieces; keep every pixel of the shown state.

critiques.strengths: The fading voice (full question, bare 'Hold on. Tap it.', silent hold) is the best scaffold fade in the room from a deliberate-practice view: the cue thins while the test (the tap, graded) stays, so every stage still yields evidence, and the silent hold is retrieval under withdrawn cue without a lost piece. 'In my words' from the Hear me out log is a true LLM-only thing.
critiques.weaknesses: Stage advancement by the last three first taps measures recognition when asked, not the look before moving; stages are stored rather than derived; three nodes merge allowed_mate into 'theirs' and missed_mate into 'free'; mastery is still counted games with no exposure; a silent hold after a break can read as a bug, as the designer admits.
critiques.what_i_would_add: Take the bare stage as the middle rung of the per-look fade in the ladder; drop the silent stage (off is silence enough, and it is logged).

critiques.strengths: The strongest mastery shape among the ladders: quiet needs three clean games with the hand on, 'yours' needs three more with the hand off, so the un-cued test is required, not optional. Observed moves (moves that had a verdict) as the denominator excludes engine-cold moves, and the free and finish nodes carry real exposure flags (a gift offered, a free capture found by the pre-search, a won position). Suppressed verdicts logged as 'unheld', the reducer rebuilt from the log on corruption, weights of 1 for back and 2 for anyway, and copy that never nags are all right.
critiques.weaknesses: Observed moves are still moves, not chances, so the passive player passes. 'Current' is the watching node with the highest weighted count over three games, which flips like the map; the ladder order is only the tie-break. No time decay at all, so a month away changes nothing. GIFT_RATE 0.16 and the bot playing on in every won position while finish is current are unmeasured opponent changes, and the second conflicts with the ten-to-fifteen-minute constraint. Eight nodes of copy.
critiques.what_i_would_add: Exposures; ladder order first with cost as a bounded override; a fourteen-day review game.

critiques.strengths: Retrieval practice with spacing (today, another day, gone) on the player's own positions, where the moment becomes a real game rather than a puzzle, which is the closest a replay can get to transfer; two answers on two dates is a sound retirement rule; the skip is never counted; the thirty-day silent drop keeps it from becoming a backlog; the beginner correctly says moment games must never feed the habit estimate.
critiques.weaknesses: Answering a position you remember is recognition with foreknowledge, not the habit; it is a drill arm, not a pathway model. The page opening on a moment risks the homework feeling the beginner himself warns about. It needs stored answer sets, which v1 records lack.
critiques.what_i_would_add: Keep as the drill behind 'Play it again from here', one per session at most, logged as kind 'again' and excluded from every trial window.

critiques.strengths: Three hand states per look (asking, quiet with 'You know this one' and no hint on the first wrong tap, off) keep the tap and the grade through the fade, and the climb needs first-tap-right evidence as well as silence. The decisive idea for sparse looks: the opponent manufactures the exposure (threat moves, mate threats, the mate gift, no resignation) and the page logs each as an event with an outcome (gift taken or not, threat parried or not), which is a trial, the honest unit. Derived from the log at every boot, two-event decay plus two-game climb as hysteresis, the summit game announced before it starts.
critiques.weaknesses: For the dense looks (pawns, takers) the evidence is still hold counts over counted games with no exposure denominator, so the same censoring. quiet to off needs three clean games, which a passive player gets for free. The shaping is four bot changes (threat enumeration, mate threats, mate gift, no resignation), each a bot_sim re-measurement, plus events and four summary fields in game.js and bot.js: not one iteration. 'You know this one' can read as smug after a wrong tap. out_alive needs the move list.
critiques.what_i_would_add: Keep the three stages and the event-as-trial idea; add exposures for pawns and takers; this iteration, shape the opponent only with the gift machinery that exists (gift rate by stage, gift kind ordered by the current look).

critiques.strengths: SM-2 made of the player's own positions with the hand fading per visit (asking, quiet, off) and a ten-move tail that turns the walk into a habit test rather than a recall test; closing after three walks is a clean criterion; the close card's 'Tomorrow: the knight from today is waiting' is the only honest pull-back line proposed.
critiques.weaknesses: Identical positions test recognition; a week and a month outrun a once-a-week player; doors are stored state with a clock; opening the session on a door is the homework risk; mid-game FENs need a warm engine; set doors need positions and bot changes. A complement, not the spine.
critiques.what_i_would_add: If 'Play it again' ships, borrow the ten-move tail as the definition of 'Answered'.

critiques.strengths: Three evidence sources per node (PLAYED, TAPPED, HANDS-OFF) is learno's three-source rule translated correctly, and the hands-off game as a required constraint is the one thing a mastery rule must contain: a test under withdrawn cue. The four log defects were found and I verified them today (ask dropped, said unstored, no answer or refutation on records, suppressed verdicts unlogged). One K3 call per game producing where, next, again, question and ask_first, with the player's own «im attacking his king» quoted three times against three pawn fails, is the strongest 'what a table cannot do' in the room, and validateK3 with an empty allowed-square set was run against the real validator. The remembered question is prefetched and stored so it never swaps under his eyes; the drill rebuilds its verdict from the record with no engine.
critiques.weaknesses: TAPPED measures recognition when asked (seven of ten first taps right), a different construct from the look before moving; it is fine as the gate between drill and reps, not as a mastery source. PLAYED is zero holds in three full games with no exposure denominator, the censoring error again. One hands-off game is about twenty-five chances and a single pass, thin alone. The fade goes from asking straight to a hands-off game with no bare stage, so the first un-cued test costs a real piece. The --ok ring beside a done look is a tick by another name, and entry by tapping the brand is odd when the close card link exists.
critiques.what_i_would_add: Exposures for PLAYED; a bare stage before hands-off; drop the rings; keep K3 whole.

critiques.strengths: Honest about being small: the mission's own measure and nothing else; trivially testable; the budget announced in words once.
critiques.weaknesses: A per-game budget is the wrong unit for learning: it fades the scaffold uniformly over skills at different stages, so a clean game removes the hold for a look never tested, and a hold not made is a piece lost. No node-level evidence, no denominator, five rungs that are a streak. It is a trust ladder, not a learning model.
critiques.what_i_would_add: Nothing; its one good line ('This game I will not stop your hand. It is real.') belongs to the per-look off stage.

critiques.strengths: The most buildable model and the best persistence design: path.compute(games, now) with no state of its own, the hand as a strictly additive suppression reason in gate.verdict with the full facts logged in losses[], the 'light' stage between full and off, the thirty-day 'due' re-check as a one-game review folded into play, free_pieces with a real denominator (gifts taken at least two thirds of gifts offered, offered at least two), five-game windows and a five-game history minimum for the rare sub-cases, v2 records with a norm() reader, set-union merge on game id, the permissions.state gate before any db call, and a cut list in order.
critiques.weaknesses: pawn_takes merges pawn takers, piece takers and the takes_back variant into one node, losing the first and most felt fade and the master's first rung. Qualifying at plies >= 24 is twelve player moves. For every node but free_pieces mastery is three clean qualifying games with no exposure denominator. 'light' as 'the first hold of the kind still fires, then none' is an arbitrary shape (why the first). The opening node depends on moves[], already first on the cut list.
critiques.what_i_would_add: Split pawns, pieces and captures; exposures from the loop; replace 'light' with the bare question; keep everything about persistence and the gate hook verbatim.

critiques.strengths: A drill graded by the hold's own tap against the stored answer set, spaced [0, 1, 7] days, skipped for a kind whose hand is off so the two models never contradict; the merge rule recomputes stage and due from the merged tries; a day's work on top of model one.
critiques.weaknesses: It tests the tap before the game, pure recognition with no transfer, weaker than the beginner's moment that becomes a game; the queue fills with one kind; v1 records have no answer sets so it starts empty.
critiques.what_i_would_add: Keep only its stored answer and refutation on every new record, which the 'Play it again' drill needs anyway.

ranking: The hand you no longer need (designer)
The map of your own games (chess master)

merged_proposal.name: One look at a time
merged_proposal.one_sentence_for_a_beginner: Each look is yours once the game has tested it many times since you last missed it; then my hand lets go of that look, and it comes back the moment you miss it again.
merged_proposal.the_idea: A ladder of six looks in the chess master's order, each named as a result in the player's words and each tied to one split of the gate's own verdict, with three honest changes to how the room measured them. First, the unit of evidence is the trial, not the hold or the game: on every player move the page already has factsBefore and the pre-search, and an 8 ms scratch loop over the legal non-pawn moves says which looks this position tested (my probe over the sixteen recorded positions: two to five moves per open position would hang a piece to a pawn, up to five to a piece, none in the start position or after 1.f3 e5, so book moves are not trials); a trial fails when the gate's verdict of that kind fires, whether held, suppressed by the pair or quiet rule, or let through by a faded hand (all three now logged as HoldRecords, the latter two with outcome 'unheld' and a why), and passes otherwise. A player who keeps his pieces home accumulates no trials and never advances, which is the truth. Second, the mastery rule is a window in trials, not a count over games: a look climbs when it has N clean trials since its last fail, spread over at least two games (N = 40 for the pawn and piece looks, 20 for captures, 8 for the three sparse looks; the sizes are where an eighty percent credible bound on the fail rate, from a Beta(1,19) prior for dense looks and Beta(1,4) for sparse ones, drops near one in forty and one in eight respectively; they are named constants in contract.js and the first three weeks of the log decide them). Third, the scaffold fades in three stages with the test retained: asking (the hold as today), bare (the hold fires, the piece lifts, the line says only 'Hold on. Tap it.', no hint on the first wrong tap, the second names the answer as today, every tap still graded), off (no hold: the gate still judges and logs 'unheld' with why 'faded', the move lands, the opponent takes, one honest sentence after the reply, and the first off game of a look is announced before his first move). Asking to bare needs N/2 clean trials over two games; bare to off needs N clean trials over three games with at least a third of them taken at bare; 'yours' in words after two more games with trials and no fail. A fail at off drops to bare, a fail at bare drops to asking, and re-climbing needs half the trials (savings: the look was learned once). Mates and stalemate are outside the ladder, always held, words only ('always held: it comes back when the game asks'). Fourteen days without a game turns every off look to bare for the first game back, said once. The current look is the first in ladder order at asking whose prerequisites are at bare or beyond, overridden only when a later eligible look has at least twice its fails in the last five games (the master's cost rule, bounded), decided at game end only. The opponent follows the ladder with levers that exist: GIFT_RATE 0.12 while free is asking and 0.08 at bare or off (replacing the clean-game step-down), gift candidates sorted pawn-takeable first while pawns is current and undefended first after (a sort inside giftCandidates, re-run through bot_sim.py), nothing else this iteration. The state is a pure function of the stored games: each GameSummary carries trials per look as a short pass/fail string, so path.compute(games, now) recomputes everything from the last twelve games with no stored path document, and two devices merge by set-union on game id as the architect specified. Claude gets the LLM engineer's one call: K3 at the close, after consent only, with the player's own Hear me out words quoted, returning where, next, again, question and ask_first, validated with an empty allowed-square set and a per-look piece-word allowlist, stored and shown at 0 ms; without Claude the pathway is identical with the templates. It is one sentence for a beginner, it is felt as the hold's voice thinning and then stopping on one look at a time, and the only thing shown is the designer's six sentences in the board's footprint with one amber dot.
nodes_in_order: pawns: 'I see the pawn before my piece lands.' Evidence: hanging_after_move with variant null and pawnAmongTakers true, any outcome (back, anyway, ended, unheld). Trial: the pre-position has at least one legal non-capturing move of a piece worth two or more after which that piece hangs with a pawn among its attackers (the scratch loop over factsBefore, cached with it while the pre-search runs). N = 40. Prerequisites: none. Practised: the opening line of the next game ('One thing this game: before the piece lands, the pawns.'), the remembering question at 0 ms when it has two or more fails in the last five games ('Hold on. The pawn again. Which one reaches that square? Tap it.', template or K3's validated question), gifts sorted pawn-takeable first while current. Side channel: the first tap's grade on the hold's own look (taps[].ask kept) marks the look perception-weak under half right, which chooses the drill over reps and feeds K3; it never moves the stage.

takers: 'I see what reaches the square.' Evidence: hanging_after_move with variant null and pawnAmongTakers false. Trial: the same loop, cheapest attacker not a pawn. N = 40. Prerequisite: pawns at bare or beyond. Practised: 'One thing this game: before the piece lands, what reaches that square.'; the remembering question names no piece ('Hold on. Something of theirs reaches that square. Which? Tap it.'); gifts sorted undefended first.

takes-back: 'Before I take, I count what takes back.' Evidence: hanging_after_move with variant 'takes_back'. Trial: the pre-position has at least one legal capture after which the capturing piece hangs (the loop's capture branch; even trades the gate never holds are passes by construction). N = 20. Prerequisite: takers at bare or beyond. Practised: 'One thing this game: before you take, what takes back.'; the remembering question 'Hold on. This one again. Before you take: what takes back? Tap it.'

their-last-move: 'I answer what their last move attacked.' Evidence: ignored_attack with sub 'already'. Trial: factsBefore.hanging.w holds a piece worth two or more. Pass includes the 'escaped' reward (now recorded on the GameSummary as escaped, said or not). N = 8. Prerequisites: none. Practised: 'One thing this game: what their last move attacked.'; the escaped reward wins the quiet budget over the free-piece reward while current; K2's offered asks list attacked_piece first.

free: 'I take what is free.' Evidence: free_piece_ignored, plus a verified gift not taken (GameSummary.gifts {offered, taken}, counted from state().lastGift and his capture on its square). Trial: factsBefore.hanging.b holds a piece worth two or more and pre.best captures it, or the opponent's last move was a verified gift. N = 8, and off additionally needs gifts offered at least two over the window with every one taken. Prerequisites: none. Practised: GIFT_RATE 0.12 while asking, 0.08 after; 'One thing this game: when something of theirs is free, take it.'; a free piece walked past this game offers 'Play it again from here' on the close card, graded by the gate from the stored record, logged as kind 'again' and excluded from every window.

guards: 'I keep my guards on.' Evidence: ignored_attack with sub 'lost_guard' or 'opened_line'. Trial: factsBefore has a White piece worth two or more that is attacked and not hanging (held by a guard); an opened_line fail counts as a trial whatever the predicate saw. N = 8, and the narration never calls it 'yours' before five games with at least one trial of it. Prerequisite: their-last-move at bare or beyond. Practised: 'One thing this game: the piece that guards another stays where it is.'; the drill from the last fail is the main tool, because opened lines are perception.

always held (outside the ladder, words only): allowed_mate, missed_mate, allowed_stalemate. Trials: a mate in one for Black found by chess.js on the pre-position with the turn flipped (skipped in check), pre.mateIn === 1, and a position five or more up with the bot on king and pawns. Never current, never faded (ALWAYS_HOLD stands), never shown as 'yours'; the path state reads 'always held: it comes back when the game asks', and a mate-loss keys the next opening line ('When their queen is near your king, their check first.'). The opening pattern is not a node this iteration: the gate cannot measure it and the page never claims what it cannot measure.
merged_proposal.next_rule: Decided at game end only, by path.compute(games, now) in app/js/path.js, pure, no DOM, no engine, over the last KEEP.GAMES = 12 stored summaries: (1) stage per look from its trial string across games ('N clean trials since the last fail, spread over two or three games, a third at bare' for the climbs; one stage down on a fail; half the trials to re-climb; fourteen idle days turn off into bare for one game); (2) current = the first look in ladder order at asking whose prerequisites are at bare or beyond, unless a later eligible look has at least twice its fails in the last five games; pawns before any game ends; null when none is at asking, and then the opening line is 'Your move.'; (3) the plan for the next game: hand = {hanging_after_move: {pawn: stage, piece: stage, takes_back: stage}, ignored_attack: {already: stage, lost_guard: stage, opened_line: stage}, free_piece_ignored: stage} read by gate.verdict as a third suppression reason beside pair and quiet (suppressed: 'faded', category and facts intact, ALWAYS_HOLD and netLoss >= 5 never suppressed), and by hold.js as the bare question for looks at bare; giftRate by free's stage; giftOrder by current; review flag; openLine = the stored K3 next line when its look equals current, else COPY.PATH.OPEN[current] prefixed by the promise or the confession when a stage changed since the last game ('I will not hold a piece that lands where a pawn takes it today. That look is yours.' / 'The pawns, once, and I said nothing. I will ask again.'); questions = the stored K3 question for current when it has two or more fails in the last five games, else the template; drill = {record} when this game had a fail of the current look with a wrong or named first tap (the record's fen, san, answer and refutation rebuild the verdict at 0 ms as tutorialVerdict does), else null, offered as a muted link beside Again, never primary. The hold policy is frozen for the whole game. scripts/test_path.mjs builds games with a helper game({plies, result, date, trials: {pawns: '0000100', ...}, holds, escaped, gifts}) and asserts: a passive log (all trial strings empty) never leaves asking however many clean games; twenty clean pawn trials over two games reach bare, forty over three with a third at bare reach off, one fail in eighty does not; a fail at off drops to bare and twenty more clean trials restore it; a fourteen-day gap makes the next game a review game and a clean one restores off; current follows ladder order and the twice-the-fails override; the hand excludes a faded split and includes ALWAYS_HOLD; the same log gives the same state twice; every template line is at most 28 words and passes templateRules with no digit. scripts/test_gate.mjs gains: with gameState.hand.hanging_after_move.pawn = 'off', Nxe5 in the 6...d6 position returns suppressed 'faded' with category, netLoss and answer intact, while g4 after 1.f3 e5 and a hanging queen still hold. A node test runs the exposure loop over the sixteen recorded positions and asserts the counts measured today.
merged_proposal.why_this_wins: It is the only combination in the room that passes all six tests at once. Well defined and computable: six looks keyed to the gate's own splits, trials from facts the page already builds (factsBefore, pre.best, lastGift) plus one 8 ms loop, stages from named constants, all recomputed from the stored games by one pure function with no path document to drift. Honest about sparse evidence: the denominator is the chance, not the move or the game, so silence from a passive player or a book-heavy opening is not mastery; a look must be tested at bare before the hand comes off; the window sizes come from a credible-bound analysis but are stated as constants a beginner never sees; one slip at off costs one felt piece and brings the bare hold back the same game, never a trap; fourteen days away brings a review game. Felt before shown: the hold's voice thins on one look ('Hold on. Tap it.'), then stops on that look alone, announced before it happens; the opening line names the one thing; the question remembers; the gifts follow the look. Beautiful when shown: the designer's state in the board's footprint, six serif sentences in three inks with one amber dot and words-only captions ('not tested much yet', 'I ask with fewer words now', 'yours', 'always held'), reached from the close card and from idle at ply 0, never during a hold, no digit anywhere (asserted). Buildable this iteration: path.js plus its node test, the loop in game.js's drop path beside factsBefore(), one additive suppression reason at gate.js line 302, five record fields the LLM engineer and I both verified are missing (taps[].ask, said, answer and refutation, outcome 'unheld' with why, escaped and gifts on the summary, trials on the summary), KEEP.GAMES 12 and KEEP.HOLDS 60, the architect's db mirror, one page state, the bare-question copy, and no new bot search (the gift notch and the candidate order are the only opponent changes, re-run through scripts/bot_sim.py in 25 seconds); the mate gift, counted gift, threat moves, Skill 5, set-position drills and the opening node are deferred with their rungs honestly absent rather than shown as 'later'. And Claude does what a table cannot: one quick call at the close, after consent, turns «im attacking his king» three times beside three pawn fails into the sentence about where he is, writes the one question that is true of every hold of the look he keeps missing, frames the position he is about to replay, writes the line that opens the next game, and breaks a tie between two eligible looks from the texture of his taps, every word through validate.js with no square allowed, while path.js alone decides every stage, every hand and every gift.

reviews.persona: Product designer on the Hold On team: owns how the pathway is felt before it is shown, the one visible pathway state inside the page's visual world (the serif line in the coach's blue, the sand and sage board, amber as the only raised voice, nothing red, no numbers), how a beginner reads where he is in five seconds, how the first visit and the hundredth differ, the copy the path speaks in, and what to refuse (XP bars, streak fire, badges, percentages, ticks, locks, roads). Judged with the page open at 400 x 800 in idle, held, answered, close-card and next-game states: header 44 px, the fixed four-line coach box 103 px, the 24 px link row at y 147 (empty in state over and at ply 0), the board 368 px at y 173-541, the action bar giving up its 56 px when the game is over, the close card 179 px tall with one hold in --ink serif 17 px and --muted Plex 14 px captions, nothing scrolling.

critiques.strengths: The order is a coach's, not a syllabus's, and the mastery rule is the one a human uses: three whole games without needing the word, with an opportunity floor (sixty player moves, gifts offered, escapes) so three short clean games prove nothing. Logging outcome 'quiet' so the gate keeps judging after the hand stops is the honest core every good model in this round shares. The gifts changing kind per rung (a knight a pawn can take, then an undefended one) is the most felt lever an opponent can offer without getting stronger. The shown face has the right grain: the close card's second face, 'Now:' in ink, counts in words to twelve, 'Quiet since Tuesday', and a 'Later.' that never claims what it cannot measure.
critiques.weaknesses: Ten rungs is a course on a 400 px phone: ten serif lines with captions run past 400 px under the board and scroll past the fold on every visit; it reads as the lesson list the beginner closes. Three rungs need things the page does not have (set-position drills with a data-mode, the move list, a threat category), so the first visit already shows a 'Later.' rung and a drill button beside Again, which turns the close card into a menu. The mate gift and the 'counted' gift are two opponent recipe changes with re-measurement each, and the drills bring 'Checkmate. Well played.' from a position he never reached: a puzzle app wearing the hold's clothes. Twenty-eight-word lines are long for a list.
critiques.what_i_would_add: Cut to the seven rungs the log already evidences; keep the gift kind as a sort order inside the existing enumeration; keep 'Now:', 'Quiet since Tuesday' and the words-to-twelve rule; leave finishing from set positions to learno's project.

critiques.model: The map of your own games (chess master)
critiques.strengths: Cost in piece words ('a knight and two pawns in three games') is the most personal sentence on the table, and an opening line that names what cost him most is a coach who has read his games. The master's own verdict, to use it only as a tie-break, is right.
critiques.weaknesses: A list that re-sorts itself by cost every game is not a path: the current look flipping between games is the opposite of reading where you are in five seconds. The global hand budget switches off a look he never learned. Five games of cold start during which the page shows a default it cannot defend. 'Next game I stop your hand four times at most' turns the hand into a counter, which is a number in words.
critiques.what_i_would_add: The cost-in-piece-words sentence as the close card's path line when two looks tie, and nothing else.

critiques.strengths: The exposure denominator is the only honest answer to the censoring problem (a passive clean game is no evidence), and it is computed from facts the page already builds. The three-stage fade with the un-cued stage as the real test is the right arc. The words-only captions ('yours', 'nearly: my hand is lighter here', 'working on it', 'later', 'not tested much yet', 'always held: it comes back when the game asks') are the best captions of the round and should outlive whichever model ships. 'Where I am' with one button, 'Your move', is right.
critiques.weaknesses: A Beta posterior's 0.8 quantile under 1/40 with a 0.85 forgetting factor cannot be felt or predicted: he cannot count toward it on his fingers, so the hand letting go arrives as a surprise rather than as a promise kept. The 'pause' stage (the piece lifts, 'Look once more', both buttons at once, nothing graded) breaks the one rule the product is built on, that the buttons come after the look, and on a phone it reads as a hold with no question, which is a bug. Nine sentences under three headings is a syllabus with headings. A scratch pass per position is engineering risk on a phone for a denominator the page can never say out loud.
critiques.what_i_would_add: The opportunity floors in countable terms (player moves observed, gifts offered, escapes); the caption vocabulary; the three stages, with the game designer's quiet line in place of 'pause'.

critiques.strengths: It is the mission's own measure, four sentences, cheap, and it says plainly that it is coarse. Review games at plus one, three and eight are SM-2 made of games, which is the right unit for a product whose only sessions are games.
critiques.weaknesses: Censored and coupled, as its author says; a path of four sentences where three read 'later' for a month is a wall, and the question that remembers cannot choose a look inside a node that mixes six. It should not be shown as a model at all.
critiques.what_i_would_add: Nothing as a model; its four result sentences could serve as headings if a page ever needed them, and I argue it does not.

critiques.model: The hand you no longer need (product designer, mine)
critiques.strengths: The one state fits exactly the board's footprint so nothing on the page moves; one amber dot as the single mark; state carried by ink and a sub-line in the coach's voice; reached only from the close card and ply 0; the first and the hundredth visit written down.
critiques.weaknesses: Mastery by absence over three counted games has no opportunity floor beyond 'the opponent punishes everything', which the learning scientist is right to call censored. Hiding the board to show six lines throws away the page's strongest object, his own held position, which the game designer and the architect keep as a still. A node whose 'yours' changes nothing on the board (mates) is decoration. Six 'I ...' sentences in two inks edge toward a checklist, and two nodes sit at 'Not come up yet' for months.
critiques.what_i_would_add: The board still of his own last hold above the list; an opportunity floor per node; the beginner's rule that never-seen looks collapse into one muted line.

critiques.model: Three looks, in your words (product designer, mine)
critiques.strengths: The fading voice is the most Hold-On-shaped lever (progress is the coach saying less); no new screen; three sentences on the card he already reads; 'In my words' is a true LLM job.
critiques.weaknesses: The silent hold (a lifted piece, an amber square, no words) will read as a broken page the first time it happens after a week away. 'Hold on. Tap it.' hides the look, and for an ignored attack the look is the lesson. Stored stages drift from the log. Three nodes put the mates outside the path, and the hundredth visit is three 'Yours.' lines on a card with nothing to look at.
critiques.what_i_would_add: Keep the thinning voice as the quiet stage, phrased with the game designer's 'Hold on. You know this one. Tap it.', never silence.

critiques.strengths: The clearest sentence in the round. Four states, with quiet proven into yours by staying clean with the hand off, make mastery something he did rather than something counted. 'Observed' moves as the denominator (engine-cold moves count for nothing) is cheap and honest. The 'Where I am' list shows only looks that have ever come up plus the next one, so day one cannot look like a syllabus. 'The pawns, yours since Tuesday' and a close card that ends with one path sentence instead of a count are exactly the voice.
critiques.weaknesses: 'And one more: tap a square where it is safe' adds a second graded question inside a hold; the beat is one question, one tap. The opponent playing on in every won position while finishing is current spends his ten minutes on a thirty-move conversion. GIFT_RATE 0.16 is a new notch to measure. The path state dims the board as in a hold with no hold on it, borrowing the amber grammar for a non-hold; the still of his own position is better.
critiques.what_i_would_add: The only-looks-seen rule and the observed denominator go straight into the merge; the second tap, the 0.16 notch and the play-on rule stay out.

critiques.strengths: 'Answered. That one is yours today.' is the strongest I-got-somewhere a beginner can have in one sitting, and a game that starts at move twelve fits a queue better than a fresh one. 'Fresh game instead' is always one tap away.
critiques.weaknesses: The page opening on a moment is a welcome-back screen by another name: day two's first frame becomes homework, the thing the beginner himself said he would close. A stack of captions with 'answered once' is a to-do list even capped at twelve, and 'Two of yours waiting' is a backlog in words. Two answers on two days is a schedule the once-a-week player never clears.
critiques.what_i_would_add: Only its explicit form: 'Play it again from here' as a --muted link beside Again on the close card, never on load, never counted toward the hand.

critiques.strengths: The three hand states give every look a curve he feels in his wrist: the question, then 'Hold on. You know this one. Tap it.' with no hint on the first wrong tap, then nothing. That quiet line is the best single line of the round because it keeps the hold, keeps the tap, and removes only the help. The promise and confession opening lines ('I will not ask about the pawns today. They are yours.' / 'The pawns, once, and I said nothing. I will ask again.') are checkable at the close, which is what makes a promise a design and not a slogan. The shown state keeps the board as the hero on his own last held position, lifted and amber, input locked; 'Today I keep my hands in my pockets' is a summit a beginner can picture.
critiques.weaknesses: Five opponent changes (threat moves, mate threats, the mate gift, a forced gift, no resignation, a deeper book), each needing bot_sim, are not one iteration. The three inks are inverted: --coach for what is his and --ink for what the coach has gone quiet on reads against the page, where the serif line is the coach's blue and the close card's sentence is the player's ink; ink should be his, blue the coach's. Four lanes as paragraphs with headings is a syllabus shape. A link that appears in the idle row for ten seconds is a flicker.
critiques.what_i_would_add: Take the three states, the quiet line, the promise and confession lines and the board still; drop every opponent change but the gift sort order; map ink to his and blue to the coach's.

critiques.strengths: The ghost of his own old move replaying once and rewinding is the most beautiful reuse of Show me in the round, and 'Tomorrow: the knight from today is waiting.' is true by construction. Help fading per position across visits is SM-2 the player can feel.
critiques.weaknesses: A session that opens on a door is again homework on the first frame. A 04:00 due time, weeks and months are a clock the page must store, the one thing the log cannot derive, and they outrun a once-a-week player. A cold phone cannot play from a mid-game FEN, so the door is skipped silently. 'Where you have been' grouped by look with 'Closed.' is a done-list.
critiques.what_i_would_add: The ghost-as-memory for 'Play it again from here' only; nothing scheduled.

critiques.strengths: One K3 call per game producing four stored strings (where, next, again, question) is the cleanest LLM design here: prefetched, on screen at 0 ms, never swapping under his eyes, validated with an empty allowed-square set so narration can never name a square it has not seen. The 'where' built from his own Hear me out words is what a table cannot do. The hands-off game as an announced test, one look at a time, is a strong felt moment.
critiques.weaknesses: TAPPED (seven of ten first taps right) is a quiz hidden inside the game and measures seeing when asked, not before; it also hangs on a field the log drops today. The path state is entered by tapping the brand in the header, a gesture nobody discovers and a wordmark that becomes a button. The done rows carry a small --ok ring, which is a tick by another name. Eight rows of short names (Pawns first, What takes it) are a table of contents.
critiques.what_i_would_add: The K3 contract and validator whole, and the 'again' line; refuse the ring, the brand tap and the tap quota.

critiques.strengths: Honest about being small; the budget announced once in words and then silent; a hands-off game and a win with the hand off as the top is a story a beginner can tell a friend.
critiques.weaknesses: Five words joined by hairlines on the close card is a progress bar in serif, as its author admits. A global budget does not know which look he learned, so a hold not made is a piece lost on a look he never had. Rungs are events, not habits, so the hundredth visit says nothing about him.
critiques.what_i_would_add: Nothing; the summit game lives better inside a per-look model.

critiques.strengths: The spine I would build: the path a pure function over the log with no state of its own, nodes mapped one to one onto gate categories and sub-cases, a hand per kind at full, light, off with 'light' (the first hold of the kind fires, the rest of the game it does not) as a gentler fade than off, losses[] so a faded hand cannot hide a relapse, every data change additive and verified in the code. The shown state is the best grounded: view=path only from the close card, the board a still of the current look's last hold with a static ring, the list in the close card's own type pair, and the captions ('This is where we are.' / 'You stopped doing that.' / 'Later.' / 'Again, for now.' / 'A month on; I will check once.') are the exact register. The cut list is honest.
critiques.weaknesses: One node for pawn and piece takers and both variants fades the commonest look under 1000 and the second-commonest together, and the copy already splits them ('the pawns' versus 'what reaches that square'). No remembered question: the hold's own words never change, so the path is felt only as the hand and the opening line. The mates node has no felt consequence. Reached from the close card only, never at ply 0, where a returning player reads.
critiques.what_i_would_add: Split pawns from takers and takes-back; add the quiet stage's line; add the ply-0 entry; keep everything else.

critiques.strengths: The drill is the hold UI with no game behind it and shows nothing new, which is the right instinct; timing in words, never dates.
critiques.weaknesses: A game that begins with a held position is a quiz before the game, the beginner's named reason to close the tab, and it competes with his ten minutes. v1 records cannot feed it. First on the cut list after the opening node, and I agree.
critiques.what_i_would_add: Nothing this iteration.
