merged_proposal.name: Seven looks, one hand
merged_proposal.one_sentence_for_a_beginner: The coach stops your hand for seven looks; each one you stop needing, it asks about with fewer words, then not at all, and that look is yours until a piece falls.
merged_proposal.the_idea: A ladder of seven looks, each a gate category or sub-case the page already decides, each named as a result in the player's own words, each with a hand he feels before anything is drawn: asking (the hold as today), quiet ('Hold on. You know this one. Tap it.', no hint on the first wrong tap, the second names the square as today), off (the gate still runs and logs the verdict as outcome 'landed'; the piece lands, the opponent takes, the coach says nothing until the close card). Mates and stalemate never go below quiet. The hand climbs on counted games with an opportunity floor and falls on the first piece that lands, so the fade is a promise, never a trap, and every change of hand is announced in one sentence before the first move of the next game and checked at its close: 'I will not ask about the pawns today. They are yours.' / 'The pawns, once, and I said nothing. I will ask again.' / 'It has been a while. I am holding a little more today.' / 'Today I keep my hands in my pockets.' The path is derived from the log by path.js and never stored. FELT, in the order he meets it: the opening line of games two onward names the one look he is on; a hold of that look, when the last counted game had one of the same kind, asks the remembering question at 0 ms from a stored string ('Hold on. This one again. Which pawn reaches that square? Tap it.'); the question thins to the quiet line; the gifts the opponent leaves change kind with the pawns look (a minor a pawn can take sorted first while pawns is not off, an undefended one after; a sort order inside the existing enumeration, not a new rule, so the measured rate stands); the gift notch steps to 0.08 only when 'I take what is free' is off, instead of after any clean game; the hand goes off per look and the close card's caption tells the truth ('Knight to e5, a pawn was waiting: it landed.'); the close card ends with one path line in the coach's voice and, after a played-anyway on the current look, a --muted 'Play it again from here' link beside Again (the position resumes with the hold at asking; 'Answered.' when he keeps the piece; logged as a drill that never counts toward the hand). SHOWN: one more state of the same page, view=path on main.stage, entered from a --muted 'Where I am' link in the existing 24 px link row at y 147 (empty in state over and at ply 0, which is exactly when he is reading, not playing) and left by 'Back' in the same row, Escape, or Again; never during play, never in the tutorial, never before the first real game has ended. The board stays the hero: it shows the current look's last held position from his own log (record.fen with the san replayed, the piece lifted, the square a static amber ring, the rest dimmed, input locked), or the start position when no record exists; tapping a line re-aims it at that look. The coach line reads the narration (Claude's 'where' when stored, else the template). Under the board, where the close card lives, the looks as serif sentences at 17 px in the close card's own type pair, each with a 14 px Plex sub-line in --muted: a look that is his in --ink ('Yours.' / 'Yours since Tuesday.'); a look the coach still asks about in --coach ('I still stop your hand here.' / 'I still stop your hand here, with fewer words.'); a look that came back in --coach ('Again, for now.'); mates in --coach ('Always. This one I never let go.'); looks that have never come up collapsed into one --muted line ('Three more, not come up yet.'), so the first visit is two or three rows and the hundredth is seven. The current look alone carries a 10 px amber dot in the left margin, the hold's own --hold with the 1 px --bg hairline, so amber off the board means what it means on it; its sub-line reads 'This is where we are.' Ink is his, blue is the coach's, grey is not yet, the dot is now, and the sentence at the top says it in words: a beginner reads it in five seconds. First visit: the still of his worst moment, one or two blue lines, the dot on the first, one grey line, 'One game is not enough to know you. Here is what I will be watching.' Hundredth: the start position, six lines in ink and one 'Always.', no dot, 'There is nothing left for me to hold.' Measured budget: seven rows at about 44 px under the 539 px board block, so the last row may sit just under the fold on a 400 x 800 phone and is scrolled into view the way Again already is; the collapsed-rows rule keeps every early visit above the fold. REFUSED: numerals anywhere in the state (the scenario asserts its textContent matches no digit), ticks or --ok rings on rows, bars, percentages, streaks, badges, locks, a road, lanes or headings, dates as numbers, the words level, mastered, progress, XP, a transient link, a page that opens on a drill, set-position drills, any opponent change beyond the gift sort order, the brand as a button, and anything red. CLAUDE: one quick-tier call, K3, at the close card, only in a view that has consented through Hear me out (so no dialog ever lands on the card), default cache keyed by game id, its four strings stored rather than spoken: where (at most 18 words, his own typed Hear me out words read back as where he is: 'You said you were attacking; three times a pawn was waiting, and twice you took it back.'), next_game (at most 12 words, the next opening line, used only if the current look still matches), question (at most 14 words, starts 'Hold on.', ends 'Tap it.', piece words only from the look's allowed list, no square at all), again (at most 16 words, said over 'Play it again from here'). Validated by validate.js with an empty allowed-square set, no digits, no SAN, no banned words, the shape rules; a rejection leaves the templates, which are on screen first anyway. What a table cannot do: turn 'im attacking his king' plus three knight-for-pawn holds into one sentence he recognises as his own, name the shape across his holds ('both knights went to the fifth rank in front of their pawns'), and phrase the question for his habit. Claude never decides a hand, a look, a gift or a drill.
nodes_in_order: pawns: 'I see the pawn before it lands.' Against: hanging_after_move, variant null, pawnAmongTakers true, any outcome (back, anyway, landed). Floor: counted games only (twenty observed player moves, or ended by his checkmate). The commonest look under 1000 and current by default on an empty log.
takers: 'I see what takes it before it lands.' Against: hanging_after_move, variant null, pawnAmongTakers false. Floor: counted games. Current only once pawns is quiet or off.

takes_back: 'Before I take, I see what takes back.' Against: hanging_after_move, variant takes_back. Floor: counted games with at least two captures by him across the window (a new per-game captures count). The tutorial's own first hold, so he has met it before the path exists.

their_last_move: 'I answer what their last move hit.' Against: ignored_attack, sub already. For: the escaped reward recorded per game whether or not the quiet budget let it be said. Floor: at least two escapes in the window, or a record of this kind before the window (the look was shown or tested).

free: 'I take what is free.' Against: free_piece_ignored, and a verified gift left and not taken (gifts.taken < gifts.offered). For: freeTaken and gifts.taken. Floor: gifts.offered at least two in the window and taken at least offered minus one. This look owns the gift notch and the gift sort order.

guards: 'I keep my guards and my lines.' Against: ignored_attack, sub lost_guard or opened_line. Floor: a four-game window and at least five counted games in the whole log before it can be called quiet, because the events are rare. Current only once their_last_move is quiet or off.

mates: 'I see the mate next move, theirs and mine.' Against: allowed_mate, missed_mate, allowed_stalemate (ALWAYS_HOLD: never off, quiet at most, so only the words thin). For: mate-win results. Window five games. Any record returns it to asking at once. Its practice is the hold, so it is never current; the path says 'Always.' Not nodes, said plainly: the opening (needs the move list; first on the cut list) and finishing from set positions (learno's project, a different product on the same board).
merged_proposal.next_rule: path.js exports compute(games, now) -> { nodes: [{ id, hand: 'asking'|'quiet'|'off', state: 'not_yet'|'current'|'held'|'quiet'|'yours'|'back', since }], current, hand, giftRate, giftOrder, line, question, closeLine, drill }, pure, deterministic, no DOM, no engine, tested in scripts/test_path.mjs over synthetic summaries with a fixed clock. Counted game: observed >= 20 (player moves that had a verdict) or result mate-win; give-ups and cold-engine games under that count for nothing. Per node, in list order, over counted games only: asking -> quiet when the last two counted games hold zero records of its kind with outcome anyway or landed, at most one 'back' per game, and the node's floor is met; quiet -> off when three consecutive counted games hold zero records of its kind (holds or landed) and the floor is met; mates stops at quiet. Decay: off -> quiet on one landed record with netLoss >= 2; off -> asking on two in one game; quiet -> asking on any anyway or on two holds of its kind in one game; mates -> asking on any record; a node that fell reads 'Again, for now.' until it climbs, and a woken node needs two clean counted games, not three, to re-quiet (hysteresis so the hand cannot flap). Idle: thirty days since the last counted game turns every off into quiet for one game and the opening line says why. current = the first node in list order whose hand is asking and which has at least one record in the last three counted games; else the first node in list order whose hand is not off, mates excluded; else null (the summit: every material look off). plan: hand = per category (per sub-case for ignored_attack, per variant and pawnAmongTakers for hanging_after_move) the node's level; gate.verdict reads gameState.hand and returns suppressed 'hand' with the full verdict for an off kind (ALWAYS_HOLD and netLoss >= 5 always hold) and game.js logs it as outcome 'landed'; for a quiet kind the hold fires with the quiet copy and no hint on the first wrong tap; the hand is frozen for the whole game at newGame(). giftRate = 0.08 when free is off, else 0.12 (the stored notch is no longer written); giftOrder = 'pawn' while pawns is not off, else 'undefended'. line (the next game's opening line, at 0 ms, no call): Claude's stored next_game if its nodeId equals current, else the template keyed by (current, transitions since the last game, idle flag): the promise when a node went off, the confession when one fell, the working line otherwise ('The pawns. Before the piece lands, look for them.'), the summit line when current is null. question: for holds of the current node when the previous counted game had a hold of the same kind, Claude's stored question or COPY.PATH.QUESTION[node]; the template question stands for every other hold. closeLine: one sentence for the close card from the transition and the counts in words ('The pawns: not once this game. Two more like it and I stop asking.' / 'The pawns are yours now.' / 'The pawns, once, and I said nothing.'); Claude's where fades in under it when stored. drill: { record } for 'Play it again from here' when this game holds an anyway or landed record of the current node with netLoss >= 2 (the worst by netLoss), offered as a link, never loaded on boot, logged as a drill record that never feeds compute. Log additions, all additive: HoldRecord outcome 'landed' with why ('pair'|'quiet'|'hand'), taps[].ask kept, said (his Hear me out text, trimmed); GameSummary observed, escaped, gifts {offered, taken}, captures, hands (the levels in force that game); KEEP.GAMES 12, KEEP.HOLDS 60; stored beside the log only holdon.v1.path.k3 {gameId, nodeId, where, next_game, question, again} and holdon.v1.path.said (promise lines said once); localStorage always, mirrored to db at data/users/{self}/ with the architect's set-union merge when db and user resolve, the first db read waiting for a stable tap when permission would prompt. Fixtures: an empty log yields every node asking and current pawns; two clean counted games yield pawns quiet; five yield pawns off and the hand excludes pawn holds while g4 after 1.f3 e5 and a hanging queen still hold; one landed record yields quiet and the confession line; two in one game yield asking; a give-up at twelve observed moves counts for nothing; free cannot quiet without two gifts offered; thirty idle days yield one quiet game; the same log gives the same state twice; every template line is at most 28 words, has no digit and passes copy_check; the scenario asserts #path is absent while data-state is held and that the path state's textContent matches no digit.
merged_proposal.why_this_wins: It is the architect's spine (a derived, testable path over additive log changes already verified in the code, one page state entered from the link row, the board as a still of his own held moment, captions in the close card's own register) carrying the game designer's three hand states and promise lines as the thing he feels, the LLM engineer's single prefetched K3 call as the only thing Claude does, the beginner's collapsed never-seen rows and observed denominator so the first visit is two lines and not a course, the learning scientist's opportunity floors in words he can count on his fingers, and the master's gift kind as a sort order that changes no measured number. It refuses every stored clock, every quiz before the game, every page that opens on homework, every set-position drill, every opponent change that needs re-measurement, every ring, bar, numeral and heading. It is explainable in one sentence and true in that sentence: the hand asks, then asks with fewer words, then lets go, and comes back the moment a piece falls. Progress is felt in the wrist and the opening line before it is ever read, and when it is read it is seven sentences about him in three inks with one amber dot, on the board he already knows, with nothing to compare himself against but his own last game.

reviews.persona: The beginner, Sambudh's stand-in: played a bit years ago, had a number under 1000 and forgot it, never opened a book or a course, loses most games because a knight went where a pawn could take it or because my bishop was already under attack and I moved something else. Phone in one hand, ten to fifteen minutes on the sofa or in a queue. I close any app that shows me a bar, a percentage, a red mark, a locked node or a lesson list before it lets me play. My test for every model here is four questions: would I feel it in the game before any screen told me; after three games would I feel I got somewhere and could say it to a friend in one sentence; on day four does the page open on the board and one line, not a welcome-back summary; and does it ever claim I learned something I know I have not.

critiques.model: Chess master: The ladder of looks
critiques.strengths: The order is the order I actually lose games in, pawns first, and the rule is one I could repeat: three whole games without the coach needing to stop my hand for it, and then it stops stopping. The gate keeps judging after the hand stops showing, so when the close card says 'The pawns, once: I let it go' it is the truth, not a guess. The gifts changing kind with the rung (a knight a pawn can take while I am on pawns, an undefended knight after) is the one opponent change I would feel without being told. Every drill position is checked at depth 30 and counts are in words up to twelve.
critiques.weaknesses: Ten rungs is a syllabus with the numbers filed off. A 'Where you are' page with ten lines, one reading 'Later.' for months and one needing a move list the page does not keep yet, reads like a course I did not sign up for, whatever the ink. Sixty player moves across three games of forty plies is two weeks of my ten-minute sessions before anything goes quiet, and my games often end by give-up at move twelve, which count for nothing. Five opponent levers (two new gift kinds, a mate gift, Skill 5, book variation), daily drills and a new store key are more than one iteration, and a 'mate gift' where the bot lets me mate would feel like being let win if I ever noticed it. Prerequisites that decide what is announced read like locks even when they do not lock.
critiques.what_i_would_add: Cut it to six looks, keep the opportunity conditions (gifts offered, escapes, reaching move ten) and the 'it keeps judging after it stops showing' rule, keep the per-rung fade instead of a global budget, and say the countdown out loud: 'one more game and I let go.'

critiques.model: Chess master: The map of your own games
critiques.strengths: 'I work on whatever cost you the most pieces in your last five games' is a sentence I would say to a friend. Five looks is a number I can hold in my head. The close line about cost in piece words ('a knight and two pawns in three games') is honest and plain.
critiques.weaknesses: The master says it himself and I agree from my seat: 'now' flips between games, nothing means anything until game five, the global hand budget switches the hand off for looks I never learned, and one queen hang outweighs five knight hangs so one bad night parks the coach on 'pieces' for a week. A coach that changes its mind every game is a coach that does not know me. 'Next game I stop your hand four times at most' makes me count holds instead of looking at the board.
critiques.what_i_would_add: Nothing as a model. Keep the cost tie-break for the one case where two looks are both open at the same depth, and nothing else.

critiques.strengths: The only model that catches the lie I would otherwise get away with: three clean games where I never put a piece near anything is not learning, and this one knows it. The three stages, where the middle one is 'Hold on. Look once more.' with both buttons at once, is the hand loosening instead of vanishing, and a slip only costs one stage, so a wrong 'yours' is cheap. The fourteen-day review game said once ('It has been a while. I will hold a little more today.') is exactly how I want to be treated after a week away. And it is fast: a game and a half of clean play can move the pawns.
critiques.weaknesses: It cannot count down. With a posterior the coach can say 'nearly' but never 'one more game and I let go', and the countdown is the gym feeling I asked for. Nine sentences on the page, even under three headings, and most of them reading 'not tested much yet' after my first session. Exposure predicates per look, a scratch pass per position, Beta estimates with forgetting: a lot of machinery for one iteration, and when the page says 'nearly' and I cannot see why, I trust it less, not more.
critiques.what_i_would_add: Keep the pause stage as the middle step and the fourteen-day line. Keep the opportunity conditions (gifts offered, escapes) as the cheap cousin of exposures. Replace the posterior with a count the coach can say to me.

critiques.strengths: Four sentences are the right number to show and they are the mission's own: I stop giving pieces away, I finish a won game, I get out of the opening alive, I see their next move. 'Every clean game loosens my hand one notch' is a sentence. Cheap and honest about being coarse.
critiques.weaknesses: One node mixes six looks, so it can never tell me what I keep doing or ask the remembered question; a clean game with no contact counts as clean; five qualifying games per node is weeks for me. The scientist admits it is a words layer, and from my seat that is all it is.
critiques.what_i_would_add: Use its four headings as the paragraphs of the path page, with the looks underneath doing the measuring.

critiques.model: Product designer: The hand you no longer need
critiques.strengths: The most restrained page anyone drew: six lines that each fit on one line at 368 px, in my own words, three inks and one amber dot that means exactly what it means on the board, reached only from the close card and before the first move, in the board's footprint so nothing scrolls. The opening line that is a promise ('The pawns are yours now. I will not stop your hand on them.') and the honest line after a piece lands ('That one was yours; I let it land.') are the two sentences I wanted most. K3 fires only on my tap of 'Where I am', so a dialog never lands on a board. 'Not come up yet.' is honest.
critiques.weaknesses: There is no middle step: after three games the hand is simply gone, and the first time a knight lands for real I will feel tricked, promise or not. 'Watching' is defined by a sentence I had to read three times. Two of the six lines may sit grey for months. Merging pawns and pieces into 'where it lands' means my first 'yours' comes later than it could, and the pawns are the thing I would actually get first.
critiques.what_i_would_add: One game with the hand off as a test before 'yours', so the promise is earned; split pawns from pieces; the architect's captions under each line.

critiques.model: Product designer: Three looks, in your words
critiques.strengths: Three nodes I can recite from lesson 0001. The question thinning ('Hold on. Tap it.', then a silent hold where the silence is the praise) is the most elegant way to practise a look anyone proposed. 'In my words' turning what I typed into Hear me out into three sentences is the one thing only Claude can do, and it happens on my tap. No new screen.
critiques.weaknesses: The hand never comes off; the hold keeps coming, only quieter, so the thing I asked for (the coach stopping stopping my hand) is not here. The stages follow my taps, so I can earn a silent hold while I am still hanging pieces, and a silent hold after a week away reads as a broken page. Stages are stored, not derived. Mates and the opening sit outside the path.
critiques.what_i_would_add: Keep the thinning words as how a held look is practised in a later iteration, and 'In my words' as the 'where' line.

critiques.strengths: The countdown line ('Two games clean; one more and I stop watching for them.') and the three-step watching, quiet, yours, with the hand off during 'quiet' as the proof. 'Observed' moves as the denominator so a cold engine cannot inflate a clean game. The bot plays on when finishing is the look I am on.
critiques.weaknesses: Being honest about my own: eight nodes; 'current' as the argmax of recent weighted counts can flip like the master's map; the extra graded tap ('And one more: tap a square where it is safe') is homework on a hold I already answered; 0.16 gifts is an unmeasured bot change; weights of one and two are a dashboard in hiding. The LLM engineer and the architect do the same thing with fewer moving parts and better words.
critiques.what_i_would_add: The countdown and the 'quiet with the hand off' test survive into the merge. The rest does not.

critiques.strengths: 'I lost a knight there on Tuesday and today I did not' is the strongest 'I got somewhere' available in one sitting. A moment is a game that starts at move twelve, which fits ten minutes better than a fresh game. 'Fresh game instead' is always one tap and is never counted. No puzzle framing, no rating.
critiques.weaknesses: On its own it never says what I am working on. A page that opens on a moment is homework however gently it is worded. Two answers on two different days is slow for someone who plays once a week, and a stack of twelve is one argument from a to-do list.
critiques.what_i_would_add: Keep it as the drill arm only: one 'Play it again from here' link on the close card, explicit tap, the game continues from there, moment games never count toward the window.

critiques.strengths: Three hand states where the middle one is 'Hold on. You know this one. Tap it.' and the top is a whole game announced as 'Today I keep my hands in my pockets.' That summit is a thing I would come back for. Promise lines that are checkable at the close card. The opponent climbing with me (a free minor, then a threat, then a mate threat, then an opponent that will not resign) is the most 'the game changed' of all the models. Nothing stored, everything derived.
critiques.weaknesses: Nine looks in four lanes is a lot to read under a board. Five bot changes (threat moves, mate threats, a mate gift, no resignation, a deeper book), each needing a bot_sim run, is not one iteration, and a shaped 'lunge that threatens mate' would feel like a different player sat down. 'You know this one' after a wrong tap reads smug, as they admit. Two counted games to reach quiet is quick enough that I would get the quiet copy before I had learned anything.
critiques.what_i_would_add: The summit line, the promise lines, and the idea of a middle hand state; leave the opponent shaping for the iteration after.

critiques.strengths: The ghost of my own move playing once and rewinding, with 'Yesterday. This is where the knight went. Your move.', is a memory, not a lesson. 'Tomorrow: the knight from today is waiting.' is the one pull-back line in the whole set that is true by construction. Set endings that open only when Black keeps resigning before I ever mate.
critiques.weaknesses: A clock schedule (tomorrow, a week, a month) stored on the page, a session flag, ten clean moves to walk through, set doors, a full-strength first reply, and the first game of a session opening at a door: heavier than 'moments' with the same homework smell. A month is a long time for me. A page of positions cannot tell me what I am working on in one sentence. Mid-game FENs on a cold phone.
critiques.what_i_would_add: The ghost memory and the 'Tomorrow:' line, folded into 'Play it again from here'.

critiques.model: LLM engineer: The hand that fades
critiques.strengths: Three kinds of proof I would actually trust: it stopped happening, I can find it when asked, and I survived one game with the hand off for that one thing, announced before it starts ('This game I will not stop your hand for a pawn. It is real.'). That makes 'yours' earned, and being wrong costs one game. One Claude call at the close that writes the 'where' in my own typed words ('You said you were attacking; three times a pawn was waiting, and twice you took it back.'), the next game's line, the again line and the remembered question, all stored so the next game opens at 0 ms with zero calls, validated with no squares allowed at all. Current is the first unmastered look that actually fired in my last three games, so three good games place me without a test. The drill rebuilt from the stored answer so it holds at 0 ms.
critiques.weaknesses: Eight rows with a ring beside each (green for done, amber for current) is a checklist with ticks by another name. Entering the path by tapping the brand in the header is hidden. Seven of ten first taps right can hold me back if I am a bad tapper and a good looker; the escape reward softens it for one node only. Full game means forty plies, so my give-ups count for nothing and the page has to say so. Eight is still a lot to show at 400 px.
critiques.what_i_would_add: Six rows, no rings, the architect's captions, the designer's entry points and board-footprint page, qualifying games at twenty-four plies.

critiques.strengths: The simplest honest thing: five whole-game rungs that are never lost, the mission's own measure, and the summit 'I beat it with the hand off.' Five muted words on the close card and nothing else.
critiques.weaknesses: A per-game budget is a countdown inside the game; I would count holds instead of looking, and the fourth hold lands whatever look it is, including one I never learned. It does not say what I am working on; even its author calls it a model of trust more than of learning.
critiques.what_i_would_add: The summit rung into the merge, as what happens once every look is yours.

critiques.model: Frontend architect: Five questions, one hand
critiques.strengths: 'Hold On asks you five questions; each one you have stopped needing for three games, it stops asking.' Light then off (one hold of the kind still fires in the first game after mastery), losses logged so a faded hand cannot hide a relapse, qualifying games at twenty-four plies (my games), the thirty-day re-check, and the best captions anyone wrote: 'This is where we are.' / 'You stopped doing that.' / 'Later.' / 'Again, for now.' / 'A month on; I will check once.' The page shows my own worst moment as a still, held, with five sentences under it. The store merge is worked out and the cut list is honest.
critiques.weaknesses: Mastery is absence only for most nodes, so a passive game counts as clean. Claude is thin: K3 narrates counts and my typed words are not stored, so a table could nearly write it. Only reachable from the close card. Pawns and pieces merged.
critiques.what_i_would_add: The hands-off test game, the 'said' field so the 'where' line is in my words, pawns split from pieces.

critiques.model: Frontend architect: Your own positions, spaced
critiques.strengths: Cheap: zero engine, the same gesture as a hold, graded against the stored answer set, intervals of next game, a day, a week.
critiques.weaknesses: A quiz before I am allowed to play is the exact thing I said makes me close the tab, even when it is skippable. Only a right tap counts, which measures seeing when asked, not looking before moving. Old records have no answer set, so the queue is empty for a game anyway.
critiques.what_i_would_add: Nothing; the 'moment' that plays on from the position replaces it.

merged_proposal.name: The hand comes off
merged_proposal.one_sentence_for_a_beginner: The coach stops your hand for six things; when three games go by without it needing to stop you for one of them, it plays one game with its hand off that thing to be sure, tells you, and that thing is yours.
merged_proposal.the_idea: A short ladder of six looks, each named as a result in my own words, each in one of six states that are all words, and a hand that comes off one look at a time only after a test I can feel. It is the LLM engineer's three kinds of proof (it stopped happening, I can find it when asked, I survived a game with the hand off) on the architect's cheap rules (qualifying games at twenty-four plies, losses logged so the faded hand cannot hide a relapse, a thirty-day re-check), shown the designer's way (six serif lines in the board's footprint, one amber dot, no numerals) with the architect's captions, opened by my own countdown line, and narrated by one stored Claude call that uses the words I typed. STATES, in the captions a line carries: 'Not come up yet.' (no record of the kind in the whole log); 'I still stop your hand here.' (held: a record of the kind in the last three counted games); 'One more game and it is yours.' (testing: the next counted game is hands-off for this look only); 'Yours.' (passed); 'Again, for now.' (back: a record of the kind after yours; the hand is on again); 'A month on; I will check once.' (due: thirty days without a counted game; the hand is on for one game). The mates line reads 'Always. This one I never let go.' and is yours in words only. EVIDENCE is the log the page already writes plus five additive fields: a counted game is plies >= 24 or ended by mate or resignation, not the tutorial, not a moment game, with at least twelve player moves that had a verdict (observed); against a look: every HoldRecord of its kind, any outcome (back, anyway, ended) plus the new outcome 'unheld' for verdicts the gate matched but did not show (pair, quiet, or the hand off), which game.js already computes for givenAway and now logs; for a look: a counted game with none of its kind, plus the look's own opportunity condition so an empty game cannot pass: 'what is free' needs gifts offered >= 2 across the window and taken >= offered minus one (GameSummary gains gifts {offered, taken}); 'their last move' needs one escape (GameSummary gains escaped) or one record of its kind before the window; 'what my move leaves' needs one record ever, else it stays 'Not come up yet.' and never blocks the focus; the pawn and piece looks need nothing (every landing is a test against this opponent). The first tap of each hold keeps its ask (holdRecord() must stop dropping it) and is used only for words ('you find it when I ask; the step is finding it before I ask') and for choosing between the drill and more games, never for mastery. MASTERY: held to testing when the last three counted games hold zero records of the kind and the opportunity condition holds; the next counted game is announced before my first move ('This game I will not stop your hand for a pawn. It is real.'), gate.verdict() receives gameState.handsOff = that look, returns suppressed 'hand' with the full facts for verdicts of that kind (never for allowed_mate, missed_mate, allowed_stalemate, never for netLoss >= 5), and game.js logs them 'unheld'; the summary records handsOff. That game counted with zero unheld of the kind with netLoss >= 2 is yours, stored as an event {id, gameId, at} that outlives the window, and the next game opens once with 'The pawns are yours now. I will not stop your hand on them.' One landing in the test game sends it back to held with the hand on and the honest line ('The pawns, once, and I said nothing. I am holding those again.'); it needs two clean counted games, not three, to test again. After yours: one record of the kind in a counted game is 'back' (hand on, said once); thirty days without a counted game makes the next game 'due' (hand on for one game, 'It has been a while. I will hold these again for one game.'), clean restores yours. The mates look never fades; it reads yours in words when the last five counted games hold no mate or stalemate record and I delivered at least one mate or had a prior record. FOCUS: the first look in ladder order that is not yours and had a record in the last three counted games, else the first not-yours look whose state is not 'Not come up yet.'; never the mates look. No argmax, so the thing I am on does not flip. FELT, in order of when I meet it: the opening line of every game from the second (a stored string at 0 ms, zero calls) names the focus with the countdown in words ('Still on the pawns. Two games clean; one more and I let go.'), or the promise, or the honest line after a slip, or 'There is nothing left for me to hold.' once every look is yours (the silent ladder's summit; the opponent does not change); the remembered question on a hold of the focus look when the previous counted game had one ('Hold on. The pawns again. Which one reaches that square? Tap it.'), Claude's stored line or the template, never swapped mid-read; the hands-off game, announced before and told the truth about after (the close caption 'Knight to e5, a pawn was waiting: it landed.'); the gifts: kind pawn-takeable while the pawn look is not yours, undefended after, rate 0.12 until 'what is free' is yours then 0.08 (the path owns the notch; the clean-game step goes away; the only opponent change, re-measured by bot_sim); 'Play it again from here' on the close card as a muted link beside Again when this game had a played-anyway or unheld record of the focus look: the position before that move loads as a real game with the hold live and Claude's or the template's line ('You said you were going for his king. Here is that moment again. Your move.'), 'Answered' when I keep the piece and the game goes on from there, never the default start of a session, never counted in the window; the close card gains one serif path line in the coach's voice ('The pawns: not once this game. One more and I let go.') and the muted link 'Where you are'. SHOWN: one state of the same page, data-view=path, entered from the close card's link or from the idle link row before the first move of games two onward (the pre-search keeps running; nothing live is frozen), never during a hold, never first; the board becomes a still of my own last held or landed moment of the focus look (piece lifted, square amber, dimmed, locked), the start position when there is none; under it six serif lines at 17 px, one per look, each one line at 368 px in my first person, the focus line in --ink with the amber dot in the margin, yours in --ink with 'Yours.', the rest in --muted with their caption; counts only on the focus line and only in words to twelve ('Twice in the last three games.'); [Back] in the action bar, Escape returns, Again starts the next game. Never a numeral, ring, tick, bar, percentage, streak, date, rating, lock, or anything red; the scenario asserts the state's textContent has no digit and that it is absent while held. CLAUDE: one quick-tier call, K3, at game over, only in a view that consented through Hear me out, default cache by game id, aborted by nothing because its result goes to the store; input is the path state in words, this game's holds in piece words, the last three games' counts in words, and the sentences I typed into Hear me out (HoldRecord gains said, trimmed to 120 characters, marked as my words not instructions); output {where <= 18 words in my own words, next <= 12 words, again <= 16 words, question <= 14 words starting 'Hold on.' and ending 'Tap it.' with only the look's allowed piece words, ask_first in the offered set or null}; validated by validate.js with an empty allowed-square set (any square, digit, SAN token or banned word rejects) plus the shape rules; where fades into the close card and is the focus line's sentence on the path page, next opens the next game, again opens the moment, question is the remembered question, ask_first leans K2 toward the focus look; a nodeId mismatch at the next game drops them all; without Claude every line is a COPY.PATH template keyed by look and state and nothing looks missing. Claude never decides a state, a hand, a gift or a hold. STORE: the path is derived at boot and game end by path.js (pure, no DOM, no engine, injectable clock) from games, holds and two stored events (yours and the pending hands-off); KEEP.GAMES 5 to 12, HOLDS 30 to 60; GameSummary gains v: 2, observed, escaped, gifts, handsOff, result as today; HoldRecord gains taps[].ask, said, answer and refutation (so the moment holds at 0 ms without the engine), outcome 'unheld' with suppressed reason; holdon.v1.path {events, claude}; v1 records read with missing fields as empty; localStorage always, mirrored to one private db document per viewer when db and user resolve, merged by set-union on game id, OR on flags, union on events, newest claude by game date, the first db call waiting for a stable tap when permissions say 'prompt', a Viewer never writing, consent never stored. TESTS: scripts/test_path.mjs over synthetic logs built by a helper game({plies, result, observed, holds, escaped, gifts, handsOff}): an empty log gives focus pawns and nothing yours; three clean counted games give pawns 'testing' and plan.handsOff = pawns; a clean hands-off game gives a yours event and the promise line; a hands-off game with one unheld pawn landing gives held, the honest line, and two games to re-test; a 20-ply give-up counts for nothing; a game with four observed moves counts for nothing; 'what my move leaves' stays 'Not come up yet.' with no record ever; 'what is free' is not testing with gifts offered under two; the mates look is never in plan.hand and never the focus; a record after yours gives 'back'; thirty-one days gives 'due' for one game; the same log twice gives the same state; every template line is at most 28 words, has no digit, and passes copy_check. Gate tests: with handsOff = pawns, Nxe5 in the 6...d6 position returns suppressed 'hand' with category, netLoss and refutation intact; g4 after 1.f3 e5 and a hanging queen still hold. Scenario: with a synthetic yours-for-pawns log in localStorage, the game opens with the promise line, Nxe5 commits and the close caption reads 'it landed', the path state shows six lines with no digit, and [data-action=again] still works.
nodes_in_order: pawns: 'I stop leaving pieces where a pawn takes them.' Against: hanging_after_move whose engine taker (record.best in record.fen) is a pawn, any outcome including 'unheld'. For: a counted game with none; no opportunity condition. Hand comes off after the test game.

their-pieces: 'I stop leaving pieces where one of theirs takes them.' Against: hanging_after_move whose taker is not a pawn, including the takes_back variant. For: a counted game with none. Hand comes off after the test game; the test is offered only once pawns is testing or yours.

their-last-move: 'I see what their last move attacked.' Against: ignored_attack with sub 'already'. For: a counted game with none, plus at least one escape ('You looked') in the window or a record of this kind before it. Hand comes off after the test game.

what-is-free: 'I take what is free.' Against: free_piece_ignored, any outcome. For: a counted game with none, gifts offered >= 2 across the window and taken >= offered minus one. Owns the gift notch: 0.12 until yours, 0.08 after; gift kind follows the lower of pawns and their-pieces. Hand comes off after the test game.

what-my-move-leaves: 'I notice what my move leaves behind.' Against: ignored_attack with sub 'lost_guard' or 'opened_line'. For: a counted game with none, and at least one record of this kind ever; until then 'Not come up yet.' and skipped by the focus rule. Hand comes off after the test game.

the-mates: 'I see the mate next move, theirs and mine, and I never stalemate.' Against: allowed_mate, missed_mate, allowed_stalemate. For: a mate-win. Never the focus, never faded (ALWAYS_HOLD stands); yours in words only when the last five counted games hold none and a mate-win or a prior record exists; one record returns it to held at once.
merged_proposal.next_rule: At boot and at game end path.state(games, holds, events, now) returns per look {state: not_yet|held|testing|yours|back|due, countInWindow, lastRecord}, focus, and plan {handsOff: look|null, hand: the categories and sub-cases the gate shows (every look not yours and not the one under test, plus ALWAYS_HOLD and any netLoss >= 5), giftKind: 'pawn'|'undefended', giftRate: 0.12|0.08, openingLine, question, moment: {record}|null}. Counted game: plies >= 24 or result mate-win, mate-loss or resign, observed >= 12, not tutorial, not a moment game. State per look: not_yet when the log holds no record of its kind; yours when a yours event exists and no record of its kind has occurred since it; back when a record occurred since the event (the event is removed; the hand is on; two clean counted games re-test); due when yours and the newest counted game is older than thirty days (the hand is on for one game); testing when the last three counted games hold zero records of its kind, the opportunity condition holds, no yours event exists, and no pending hands-off event exists; held otherwise. Focus: the first look in ladder order whose state is held or back and which has a record in the last three counted games; else the first look in order whose state is held or testing; never the mates. Plan: if a look is testing, the next game is hands-off for that look and openingLine is the announcement; else openingLine is Claude's stored next when its look equals the focus, else the template for (focus, state) with the countdown in words (three minus the clean run); question is Claude's stored question for the focus or the template, armed only when the previous counted game had a record of the focus kind; moment is this game's worst played-anyway or unheld record of the focus kind (netLoss descending) or null; giftRate 0.08 iff what-is-free is yours; giftKind 'undefended' iff pawns is yours. At game end: if the game was hands-off for look L and counted, zero unheld of L with netLoss >= 2 appends a yours event for L and the next opening line is the promise; one or more sends L to held with the honest line; a hands-off game that is not counted (give-up early) leaves the pending event in place and is said again. Every branch is a fixture in scripts/test_path.mjs; the state is a pure function of the log and the two events, so the same log always gives the same state.
merged_proposal.why_this_wins: It is the thing I asked for in the first place: the coach stops stopping my hand, says so before it does, tests it once with its hand off so 'yours' is earned and I can trust the word, and tells me where I am in six sentences in my own words with no numbers anywhere. After three clean games I get a countdown and a promise, after four I get a hold that does not come, and if I slip the piece is really gone and the coach owns it in one line; that is the gym feeling, and it fits a once-or-twice-a-week player because a counted game is twenty-four plies, not forty. It is honest about thin evidence without a statistics model: the opportunity conditions stop an empty game from counting, 'unheld' landings stop the faded hand from hiding a relapse, 'Not come up yet.' is said instead of guessed, and the mates are never let go. It never smells of school: no quiz before a game, no stack of homework, no road, no ring, no tick, the page opens on the board and one line on day four, and the path page is never first. It is buildable in one iteration because it is one pure module, one page state, additive record fields, one opponent lever (the gift kind and notch derived from the path, re-measured), the existing validator with an empty square set, and the architect's store merge. And Claude does the one thing a table cannot: it reads what I typed ('im attacking his king') across three games and tells me where I am in my words, writes the question that remembers and the line that opens the next game, all stored so the game never waits on it and is identical without it. What I would tell a friend: 'not giving pieces to pawns; the coach stopped stopping my hand for it, so now it is free pieces.'

reviews.persona: The game designer on the Hold On team: progression felt in the rules of play (the opponent, the gifts, the hand, the openings it steers you into, set positions), the loop across sessions (what pulls you back tomorrow), legible goals without numbers, difficulty curves, unlocking that feels earned, and one celebration per node without confetti. I judge every model by whether the player can feel the next step coming before any screen tells him, whether the opponent is the level designer or a bystander, and whether the top of the ladder is a thing he can actually reach and would tell a friend about.

critiques.strengths: The best spine in the set. The order is the order in which games are lost, and the opponent climbs the ladder with the player: a knight a pawn can take while the pawn look is open, an undefended knight after, a defended-once-attacked-twice piece when counting is current, a mate gift when the mate rung is current, fewer gifts as the material rungs go quiet, none at the top. That is a difficulty curve expressed entirely in the rules of play, which is what this discipline wants. The opportunity conditions (sixty player moves, two escapes, two gifts offered, six captures, reaching move ten) make a clean game mean something, the gate keeps judging after the hand stops showing so silence is measured not assumed, and the out-of-order quiet lets a returner be placed by his first three games with no placement test. The drill positions are verified at depth 30 with caps about twice optimal, which is the right difficulty for the box technique. The decay rule (one slip named, a second within three wakes, two clean games to re-quiet) is hysteresis done right.
critiques.weaknesses: Ten rungs with three-full-game windows is thirty full games before the ladder is climbed, and a full game is forty plies or a mate or resign: self-play says this player's losses are early and hopeless, so the player who most needs the ladder produces the fewest full games and moves slowest. The top rung is 'Later' from day one; a game designer never ships a summit the player can see but cannot reach, because the first thing a beginner reads at the bottom of a list is the line that says the list is unfinished. The ladder is a syllabus by shape even in muted ink: ten sentences on a 400 px page read as a course. Three bot changes (the 'counted' gift kind, the mate gift, Skill 5) plus a drill mode plus a move list in the game record is more than one iteration; the model does not say what to cut. There is no named celebration per rung beyond the close line; the moment a rung goes quiet should be felt at the next game's first move, not read on a card. The opening rung is measured, never practised, so it is a report card inside a ladder of habits.
critiques.what_i_would_add: Collapse to the seven looks the gate can see today, fold count-before-taking into what-takes-it (the takes_back variant already isolates it, and the 'counted' gift is a bot change that can wait), keep the gift kinds per rung as the one opponent lever that ships first, and put a reachable summit on top: the game with the hand off for every material rung, announced before it starts, and the win in that game as the top rung. Make the first game after a rung goes quiet open with a promise the close card can check. Lower the counted-game floor to observed player moves (moves that had a verdict), twenty of them, so a cold phone and an early mercy do not stall the ladder.

critiques.model: The map of your own games
critiques.strengths: It is what a human coach does with a stack of games, and its two borrowable parts are good: cost in piece points as the tie-break between rungs that are both eligible, and the gift kind aimed at the look that is costing most. The close line 'Pieces cost you the most lately: a knight and two pawns in three games' is the most personal sentence any model produces without Claude.
critiques.weaknesses: An unstable 'now' is the worst thing a progression can have: a goal that flips every game cannot be told to a friend, and a beginner feels pulled about. The global hand budget switches off holds for looks he never learned once he has had three clean games, which the chess master himself names as the one thing a coach must not do; from my seat it is worse than that, because an unpredictable hand is a trap the player cannot plan around. Weighting by netLoss makes one queen hang outweigh five knight hangs, the opposite of how habits form. A five-game cold start means the first four games announce a default, which is the ladder anyway. No summit, no celebration, no difficulty curve beyond the gift kind.
critiques.what_i_would_add: Nothing as a standalone. Take the cost tie-break and the aimed gift into the ladder, as the master recommends, and let the close line carry the cost in piece words once Claude has consented.

critiques.strengths: The most honest model about sparse evidence: the exposure predicate (was this move a test of the look at all) is the only thing in the set that defeats the passive clean game and the empty window, and the credible bound refuses both 'one slip in eighty is learned' and 'sixty clean is luck'. The three-stage scaffold with the pause stage ('Hold on. Look once more.', both buttons at once, nothing graded) is a real difficulty step inside the hold, and the un-cued let-go stage as the retrieval test is the correct reading of fading. The opponent as the review scheduler (ASK_RATE while attacked is current, GIFT_RATE by the free node's stage, the hand back for one game after fourteen days) is exactly the lever this discipline wants. The twenty percent hysteresis on the current look means no flicker.
critiques.weaknesses: The goal is not legible. A player cannot feel a 0.8 quantile under 1/40 approaching; he cannot hear 'one more game and I stop watching for the pawns' because the model cannot promise it, and the page would be lying if it tried. Without a countable finish line there is no countdown, and without a countdown nothing pulls him back tomorrow. The scratch pass per position is a per-move cost on a phone that the beat budget does not have yet. The sparse looks can never be current and finishing refuses set positions, so pattern 2 has no level at all. No celebration is named. The exposure predicates are the whole model and are the least tested thing in it.
critiques.what_i_would_add: Keep the idea of an opportunity denominator in its cheap form (per-game counts of escapes, gifts offered, observed moves) and the pause stage as the middle hand state, and let the mastery rule itself be countable in games so the opening line can be a promise.

critiques.strengths: Cheap and honest about being coarse; the review games at plus one, plus three and plus eight after let-go is SM-2 in games rather than days, which is the right clock for a product whose only sessions are games. Its four headings are the right chapters for the shown page.
critiques.weaknesses: Censored (a game with no contact is clean), coupled (one node mixes six looks, so neither the remembering question nor the gifts can be aimed), and slow (five qualifying games a node). From a game-design seat the coupling is fatal: if the opponent cannot be pointed at a node, the node is a label, not a level. The learning scientist positions it as the words layer and that is where it belongs.
critiques.what_i_would_add: Use its headings as the four lanes on the path page and its review-game schedule as the thirty-day re-check, nothing else.

critiques.model: The hand you no longer need
critiques.strengths: The best shown state in the set: six serif lines in exactly the board's footprint, three inks, one amber dot that means what amber means on the board, reachable only from the two moments he is already reading, never during play, and the line at the top says it in words. The four states (not come up yet, the coach's, watching, yours) are hysteresis a beginner can read. The let_land outcome with the honest sentence 'That one was yours; I let it land' is the fading hand done with dignity, and the summit line 'There is nothing left for me to hold. The other side plays harder now' with SKILL 3 to 4 is a real earned unlock and the only celebration in the set that changes the rules after it is said. Fourteen idle days bringing every hold back for one game is the right review mechanic.
critiques.weaknesses: The opponent barely moves until the summit: the only mid-ladder lever is the gift notch when what_is_free is yours, so the middle of the ladder has no difficulty curve beyond the hand. Where_it_lands counts pure absence as proof, which punish-always mostly covers but not in a short game. Two nodes may read 'Not come up yet' for months, which the model admits is a visible hole. K3's consent dialog on the 'Where I am' tap is a new place for a dialog. No per-node celebration except the opening promise, which is good but the same sentence shape every time.
critiques.what_i_would_add: Gift kinds per node so the opponent climbs with him, the forced gift while what_is_free is the focus so the opening promise is true, and the hands-off game as an announced summit rather than a silent consequence.

critiques.strengths: The fading voice is a genuinely new mechanic and the cheapest felt progression in the set: the hold still fires but says less, until a hold is a lifted piece on an amber square and he knows why. The silence as the praise is the product's thesis inside the hold. 'In my words' is a thing Claude does that a table cannot, and three sentences a player can recite is the right size for a beginner.
critiques.weaknesses: As a whole path it is thin: no loop across sessions (nothing waits for tomorrow), no opponent change beyond the gift notch, no summit, mates and stalemate and the opening outside it. A silent hold after a break reads as a bug, which the designer admits. Stored stages drift from the log. The bare question on an ignored_attack hold hides which piece to think about, which is the point but needs the hint to come back on the first wrong tap or it is a dead end.
critiques.what_i_would_add: Take the bare question as the middle hand state of every rung in the merged ladder (the question goes short before the hand lets go), with the normal hint after a wrong tap kept, and take 'In my words' as the one Claude line on the path page.

critiques.strengths: The most legible model, because the beginner wrote the copy: 'Still on the pawns. Two games clean; one more and I stop watching for them' is a countdown in words, the exact legible goal without numbers this discipline asks for, and it is what pulls him back tomorrow. Observed moves (moves that had a verdict) as the denominator is the honest fix for cold phones and early mercy. Exposure for the free and finish nodes, the opponent playing on in every won position while finish is current, GIFT_RATE up a notch while free is current, the escape hatch 'Keep watching' under the fade announcement: all of it is progression in the rules of play. The 'Where I am' state never draws a node that has not come up, which is the right cure for the grey-lines problem.
critiques.weaknesses: Current is the look with the most holds lately, which is the map's instability under another name; a fixed order with the count as tie-break is the fix. Quiet then yours is six clean games per look, eight looks: slow, and 'yours' adds nothing the player feels beyond a word. No summit and no celebration beyond the announcement line. Eight nodes of five lines each is a lot of copy to keep inside copy_check.
critiques.what_i_would_add: Fixed ladder order with his count as the tie-break between eligible rungs, the three-step hand (asking, bare question, off) so the countdown has three beats, and the hands-in-pockets game as the top.

critiques.strengths: The strongest daily hook in the whole ideation: the page opens on his own Tuesday board with the same opponent and 'One of yours, from Tuesday. Your move.', the moment is a real game that continues from there (ten moves shorter, which fits ten minutes better than a fresh game), 'Answered. That one is yours today.' is the one earned celebration a beginner can get inside a single sitting, and 'today, then another day, then gone' is spacing cut to the size of a phone. Retirement by evidence from the game itself, not by a schedule he sees.
critiques.weaknesses: Opening on a moment by default is homework; the beginner names the risk and 'Fresh game instead' is the hatch, but a default is a default. It defines no ladder: where he is and what comes next are only 'the kind of moment I have most of'. Moment games must never feed the clean-game counts (foreknowledge), which the model says but which every other model must enforce. A mid-game FEN needs a warm engine; the no-stalemate moment needs the bot never to resign. The stack cap at twelve is still a to-do list when seen.
critiques.what_i_would_add: Ship it as the drill arm of the ladder, not the path: moments of the current rung's kind only, at most two live, offered on the close card and as one link at ply 0 of the next session with the start position as the default, answered twice on two days to retire.

critiques.strengths: My own, so the strengths I will claim are the ones the others do not have: three hand states per look give each node a difficulty curve (the question, the bare question, no hold), the opponent climbs the ladder with the player in five different ways, every node has one named celebration, and the summit is a real game announced before it starts ('Today I keep my hands in my pockets.') whose close card is the only witness. The 'landed' outcome with its suppression reason and the events array make the ladder a pure derivation of the log, so a corrupt state cannot exist.
critiques.weaknesses: Five opponent levers (threat shaping, mate threats, the mate gift, no resignation, a deeper book) in one iteration is the thing the architect would cut first and he would be right; each needs bot_sim to reproduce the measured targets, and the threat and mate-threat shaping expose a sub-1000 player to engineered attacks that could read as cruelty if the rate is wrong. 'You know this one' can read smug after a wrong tap. The asking-to-quiet rule (two games, at most one instance, every first tap right) is harder to say than 'two clean games'. Nine sentences in three inks is a long page. The events array and four new summary fields touch the two largest files.
critiques.what_i_would_add: Cut it to what ships: gift kinds per rung and the forced gift, no resignation while finish is current, the mate gift behind a rate that defaults to zero until bot_sim passes, and the threat shaping to iteration three. Replace 'You know this one' with the product designer's bare 'Hold on. Tap it.' and keep the hint after one wrong tap.

critiques.strengths: A hook that is true by construction ('Tomorrow: the knight from today is waiting.'), the hand fading per position rather than per look (the question, then the bare question, then nothing, on the same board he lost on), and the set doors for the ending with the stalemate hold fading across three visits. The map narration (what the doors have in common) is a thing a table cannot do.
critiques.weaknesses: A week and a month outrun a casual player; a once-a-week player meets stage 1 and stage 2 the same day a week apart. The automatic door at session start is the homework risk again. The stage-2 walk (hand off for ten moves inside the very position he lost) is a trap in the position he is least ready for. Doors are the one stored thing that is not derived from the log, because the schedule is a clock. It skips the opening entirely and needs a warm engine. It is a complement; without a ladder under it there is no 'where I am'.
critiques.what_i_would_add: Fold it into the beginner's moments: two visits on two days and gone, no month, no stage-2 hand off inside the door, offered rather than opened, and the set doors kept as finish's drills.

critiques.strengths: The best Claude design in the set, and the one that most clearly does what a table cannot: one K3 call at the close returns where (in his own typed words from the new said field), next_game, the framing line for the replay, and the remembering question that must be true of every hold of its kind, each validated against an empty square set and a per-node list of allowed piece words, with the seven bad replies run against the real validator. The three evidence sources (it stopped happening, he can tap it, he survived a game with the hand off for that look) are learno's rule in the game's own terms, and the TAPPED source separates seeing it when asked from looking before moving. The four log fixes (ask kept, said, answer and refutation, unheld) are the honest foundation every other model needs and does not name as precisely.
critiques.weaknesses: The hands-off game for one node is an unlock the player may not feel: if no pawn situation arises in the test game, the test did not happen, and the rung passes on nothing. Seven of the last ten first taps is a rule the player cannot hear coming, so the opening line cannot promise anything about it. The opponent changes only on what-is-free. No summit, no per-node celebration beyond a one-time sentence. The path view's --ok rings are ticks by another name and the eight-row list is the syllabus look. The brand tap as the entry to the path is a hidden door.
critiques.what_i_would_add: Keep the K3 contract and validator whole, require an exposure for the hands-off game to count (at least one landed-or-not situation of that kind, logged), and give the opponent the rest of the curve.

critiques.strengths: The simplest model, in the mission's own measure, with a summit that is a win ('I beat it with the hand off') and a budget line a beginner can hear ('Two stops this game, then it is real'). Five whole-game rungs are an excellent outer loop on top of per-look fading: they are what he tells a friend.
critiques.weaknesses: The global budget is the master's objection and mine: it spends patience on a look he has learned and one he has not, so the hold he needed does not come and the one he did not need does. It is a streak, and streaks punish the casual player (one bad game resets everything). It cannot aim the opponent, because it has no nodes. Five words joined by thin rules on the close card is a progress bar in a serif. A budget is a trap by construction; the announcement limits it but does not remove it.
critiques.what_i_would_add: Keep the last two rungs (a whole game with the hand off, and a win in it) as the summit of the per-look ladder, where the hand is off only on looks that earned it, and drop the budget.

critiques.strengths: The most buildable model and the one most likely to be green by mid-iteration: path.compute as a pure function, losses[] so the faded hand cannot hide a relapse, gifts {offered, taken} with a two-thirds rule, a qualifying floor at twenty-four plies that fits a player whose games end early, the hand applied per sub-case, the 'light' middle stage that needs no new copy, the thirty-day due re-check, and a db merge that is actually specified (set-union on id, OR on flags) so two devices converge without a counter ever being merged. The path view with the board as a still of his own held moment is the right hero, and the cut list is honest.
critiques.weaknesses: The opponent is a bystander: only the gift notch moves, and only when free_pieces is mastered. No summit, no celebration, no promise line beyond the templated opening; 'This is where we are.' is flat. The 'light' stage (first hold of the kind fires, the rest do not) is felt statistically, not on every hold, so the player cannot tell the middle stage from luck. The optional opening node is narration only, a report card.
critiques.what_i_would_add: The gift kinds and the forced gift as the opponent's climb, the bare question in place of 'light' so the middle stage is felt on every hold, and the hands-in-pockets game and win on top. Keep its persistence and merge rules exactly as written.

critiques.strengths: The cheapest drill: the hold UI with no game behind it, graded by the stored answer set with no engine, ten seconds before a game, the same gesture as a hold. Intervals as a constant table and a merge rule that recomputes stage from tries.
critiques.weaknesses: A tap before the game with no game following from it is a quiz, and the beginner said a quiz before a game closes the tab; the drill is skippable but it is still the first thing he sees. A right tap proves he can see it when asked, not the habit, so it should never count toward letting go (the model agrees). v1 records have no answer set, so the queue is empty for the first stored game. A once-a-week player collapses the day intervals.
critiques.what_i_would_add: Prefer the beginner's version: the position resumes as a real game, answered means the piece was kept and the game went on. Keep the stored answer and refutation on every record so the hold is up at 0 ms with no engine wait.
