merged_proposal.name: Seven looks and a summit
merged_proposal.one_sentence_for_a_beginner: Each look you go three games without needing, I first ask about with fewer words and then stop asking about; when I have stopped asking about everything that costs pieces, you play a whole game with my hands in my pockets, and if you win it the other side gets a little harder.
merged_proposal.the_idea: A short ladder of seven looks in the chess master's order, with a reachable summit on top and his own moments as the drill arm. Each look is one reason the coach stops his hand today, named as a result in his own words. Each has three hand states that he feels on every hold before any page shows them: asking (the category question, as today), quiet (the piece lifts, the square breathes amber, the line says only 'Hold on. Tap it.', the hint after a wrong tap unchanged), and off (the piece lands, the opponent takes, the gate still judges and logs the verdict as 'landed', and the close card tells the truth). The climb is countable so the coach can promise it: two consecutive counted games with nothing of that kind make the question go quiet, a third lets the hand go, and the opening line counts him down in words ('Still on the pawns. Two clean; one more and I stop watching for them.'). The opponent climbs with him, one lever per rung, each a chess.js enumeration the bot already has or a one-line rule change, re-measured with scripts/bot_sim.py before it ships: pawn-takeable gifts while the pawn look is open, undefended gifts after, a gift forced once a game while 'free' is current so the promise is true, the bot refusing to resign while 'finish' is current, the gift notch stepping down as rungs go off, none at the summit. The summit is the earned unlock: when the five material rungs are off, the game opens 'Today I keep my hands in my pockets.' and only mates, stalemate and five-point losses are held; a clean one is a rung, a win in one is the top, and after the win the sampler steps one measured notch. Every rung has one celebration without confetti: the first game that opens with a promise about it, checkable at the close. The drill arm is the beginner's moments: a played-anyway or landed position of the current rung's kind comes back as a real game continuing from there, offered on the close card and as one link at the start of the next session (the start position stays the default), answered twice on two days and gone, never counted as a game. The path is a pure function of the log (path.js: state and plan, tested over synthetic logs), the only stored path things are the moments and the said-once flags, and the one visible state is a still of his own last held position with seven serif sentences under it in three inks and one amber dot, never a numeral. Claude writes four lines at the close in a consented view (where he is in his own typed words, the line that opens the next game, the remembering question for the current rung, the framing line for a moment), validated against an empty square set and per-rung piece words; it never decides a state, a hand, a gift or a drill. The opening pattern is deferred: it needs the move list in the game record and has no hold to practise it, so it ships as narration only when moves[] lands and is the first cut.
nodes_in_order: 1. pawns: 'I stop leaving pieces where a pawn takes them.' Gate: hanging_after_move, variant null, pawnAmongTakers true, any outcome (back, anyway, ended) plus the new outcome 'landed' (the verdict matched but was suppressed by the pair rule, the quiet rule or the off hand; logged with its suppression reason, category, sub, netLoss, ply, best and refutation). Counted game: twenty observed player moves (moves that had a verdict; cold-engine moves do not count) or a game ended by his mate; mercy and give-ups under that are skipped, never counted either way. Opportunity: none beyond observed moves (punish-always makes every landing a test). Climb: asking to quiet after two consecutive counted games with zero records of this kind; quiet to off after a third. Opponent while current: gift kind 'pawn' (a bot minor a pawn can take, the existing attacked-by-a-pawn branch of giftCandidates) at 0.12, verified at depth 10 as gifts are now. Opening line while current, built from his own last game with counts in words to twelve: 'Still on the pawns. Two clean; one more and I stop watching for them.' Remembering question at 0 ms when the previous counted game also had one: 'Hold on. The pawns again. Which one reaches that square? Tap it.' (Claude's validated variant or the template). Decay: off to quiet on one landing with netLoss >= 2, said the same game after the opponent takes ('There it goes. A knight for a pawn. I was not watching for the pawns; I am again.'); quiet to asking on a second record within three counted games; two clean counted games to re-climb. Celebration: the first off game opens 'I will not ask about the pawns today. They are yours.' and, if nothing of this kind landed, closes 'I never asked about the pawns. Nothing landed on one.' Said once per rung (holdon.v1.path.said).

2. what-takes-it: 'I see what takes my piece before it lands, and what takes back before I take.' Gate: hanging_after_move with no pawn among the takers (variant null) and every takes_back variant, any outcome including landed. Prerequisite: pawns at quiet or off (a piece look that is quiet while the pawn look still needs the hand is luck). Same counted-game rule and three-game climb. Opponent while current: gift kind 'undefended' only (a bot minor attacked by his piece and defended by nothing, the other existing branch), so the free piece in front of him needs the piece look and the pawn-takeable gifts stop. Remembering questions: 'Hold on. Not a pawn this time. What reaches that square? Tap it.' and, for a capture, 'Hold on. Before you take there: what takes back? Tap it.' Decay as pawns. Celebration: 'I will not ask what takes it today.' at the first off game, and the close card's caption voice drops 'was waiting' for 'you saw it' on the first right tap of that game.

3. their-last-move: 'I answer what their last move pointed at.' Gate: ignored_attack sub 'already'. Prerequisite: pawns at quiet or off. Opportunity: the three-game window must hold at least two 'escaped' rewards (a new per-game count written whether or not the quiet budget let the line be said), which proves the opponent attacked something and he answered; three clean counted games with fewer than two escapes stay asking and the path reads 'Not tested much yet.' Opponent: unchanged (it attacks on its own); while current the 'You looked' reward wins the four-line budget over 'Free knight' when both apply in one move, so the line he reads most often is the one about his look. Remembering question: 'Hold on. Their last move pointed at something of yours. Tap it.' Decay as pawns. Celebration: the first off game opens 'I will not ask about their last move today. Look there first anyway.'

4. free: 'I take what is free.' Gate: free_piece_ignored (against, any outcome including landed); per game, giftsOffered and giftsTaken (new counts from state().lastGift.verified and his capture on the gift square) and freeTaken (existing). Prerequisite: none; it sits beside pawns at the bottom, and when both are asking the one with the larger summed netLoss in the last five counted games is the one announced and the one the gifts serve (the chess master's cost tie-break), ties to pawns. Mastery: three clean counted games with zero records, giftsOffered summed >= 2 and giftsTaken >= giftsOffered - 1 (he took nearly everything he was given). Opponent while current: giftDue forced once between the bot's third and eighth move when no roll has succeeded, so the opening line 'Something of theirs will be free today. Take it.' is true; GIFT_RATE held at 0.12 (the clean-game step-down is suspended while this rung is current). Off: the notch is derived from path state (0.08; holdon.v1.giftRate is read once as a fallback and no longer written). Decay: a verified gift walked past while off returns quiet and the 0.12 notch; a second within three counted games returns asking. Celebration: the first off game whose gifts were all taken closes 'Everything it left, you took.'

5. what-my-move-leaves: 'I notice what my move leaves behind.' Gate: ignored_attack sub lost_guard or opened_line, any outcome including landed. Prerequisite: their-last-move at quiet or off. Window: four counted games (the events are rare) and at least five counted games in the whole stored log before it can go quiet; until then the path reads 'Quiet so far.' and never claims it. Opponent: nothing (the bot cannot make him move his own guard). Remembering questions: 'Hold on. The piece you are moving was guarding something. Tap it.' and 'Hold on. Your move opens a line again. Tap along it.' Decay as pawns, but a decay to asking is announced in the next opening line so it does not feel arbitrary: 'A guard went missing last game. I will ask about those again.' Celebration: 'I will not ask what your move leaves today.'

6. the-mate-next-move: 'I see the mate next move, theirs and mine.' Gate: allowed_mate and missed_mate, which are ALWAYS_HOLD: the hand never lets go here, so 'off' means the bare question and nothing more. Prerequisite: none. Window: five counted games with zero records and at least one mate-win (he delivered a mate he saw). Opponent while current: MATE_GIFT_RATE, a named constant defaulting to 0 until bot_sim reproduces the 1320 and held-1320 targets within one game in ten; when on, from the bot's fifteenth move while he is three or more points ahead, the sampler's mate-in-one guard is relaxed with that probability so a mate for him appears, logged as a gift of piece 'mate'. The rung works without it on natural events. Remembering questions: 'Hold on. Their check again. Where does it land? Tap it.' / 'Hold on. You have a checkmate on the board again. Tap the square.' Decay: any record returns asking at once (a mate is a game; no hysteresis). Celebration: the first mate he plays while the question is bare: 'You found it with nobody pointing.'

7. finish: 'I can finish a won game, without a stalemate.' Gate: allowed_stalemate (ALWAYS_HOLD) against; a draw while five or more points up against (new GameSummary field materialAtEnd from chess.js); a mate-win with finishPlies <= 40 for (plies from the first position where the bot was nine or more points down or had only king and pawns, to the mate). Prerequisite: the-mate-next-move at quiet or off. Drills: the chess master's set positions verified at depth 30 (two rooks 8/8/8/4k3/8/8/8/R2RK3 w mate in 8; queen 4k3/8/8/8/8/8/8/4K2Q w mate in 8; rook 4k3/8/8/8/8/8/8/R3K3 w mate in 13), offered once a day as a quiet secondary button on the close card while this rung is current ('Finish one with two rooks', then the queen, then the rook), the board in data-mode=drill, the defender at Skill 20 depth 12 so the stalemate traps are real, caps 15, 20 and 25 moves felt as one line at the cap ('Twenty moves. From the start, once more?'), recorded in holdon.v1.drills; Again stays primary. Mastery: two two-rook, two queen and one rook drill passed on at least three dates (conversions in games count toward the queen and rook totals) and no stalemate hold or draw-while-ahead in the last five counted games. Opponent while current: the resignation exception widens from king-and-pawns to any position where he has a queen or a rook (one rule change in bot.js, measured by bot_sim mean plies), so the ending is played instead of conceded. Decay: a failed drill or a stalemate hold returns asking; thirty days without a drill or conversion offers one again ('Still got it? Finish one with the rook.'). Celebration: the first mate against a bot that did not give up closes 'It did not give up and you finished it anyway.'

8. hands-in-pockets: 'I play a whole game on my own, and I win it.' Not a look: the earned unlock, two rungs read off GameSummary. Enabled when pawns, what-takes-it, their-last-move, free and what-my-move-leaves are all off. The game opens 'Today I keep my hands in my pockets.'; gate.verdict receives gameState.hand with every material category off and fires only ALWAYS_HOLD and netLoss >= BIG_LOSS, logging everything else as landed; GameSummary records handsOff true. First rung: a hands-in-pockets counted game with givenAway 0 ('A whole game with my hands in my pockets.'). Top rung: a hands-in-pockets game with result mate-win or resign ('I beat it with my hands in my pockets.'). Opponent: the gift notch steps to a third value, 0.05, at the summit; after the win SKILL steps 3 to 4 (a named lever shipped only after a ten-game bot_sim at that notch meets the gift, length and guard targets) and the next game opens once 'The other side plays harder now.' Decay: a landing in a hands-in-pockets game sends that rung back to quiet and the next game is ordinary again, said in one line; the two summit rungs, once reached, are kept as events {id, gameId} that outlive the window. The drill arm, every rung: a played-anyway or landed record of the current rung's kind with netLoss >= 2 and evalBefore >= -300 (stored on the record, never shown) becomes a moment, at most two live and one per fen, holding the record's fen, san, answer and refutation so the hold is up at 0 ms with no engine wait; offered as 'Play it again from here' beside Again on the close card and, next session, as one --muted link at ply 0 ('One of yours, from Tuesday.') with the start position as the default; it resumes as a real game from that position with the hold at asking and the opponent punish-always; a clean first move reads 'Answered. That one is yours today.' and the game goes on; a moment answered on two different days is retired ('That one is gone.'); untouched thirty days it is dropped silently; moment games are excluded from counted games for every rung.
merged_proposal.next_rule: path.js exports state(games, holds, drills, moments, {today}) and plan(state), both pure, deterministic and run in node over synthetic logs; nothing of the path is stored except moments, the drill records, the summit events and the said-once flags, so a missing key loses nothing. state: counted games are those with twenty observed player moves or ended by his mate, moment games excluded; rungs are evaluated in ladder order in one pass; each rung's hand is the highest state its climb supports (asking, quiet after two consecutive clean counted games, off after three; the opportunity conditions per rung apply; mates and stalemate never go below the bare question) then lowered by its decay rule over the newest games; a rung whose prerequisite is not at quiet or off reads 'later' and its hand is asking; summit rungs are kept events. current = the first rung in ladder order whose hand is asking, else the first whose hand is quiet, with one exception: when pawns and free are both asking, the one with the larger summed netLoss in the last five counted games is current, ties to pawns; when every material rung is off, current = hands-in-pockets. plan(state) returns one frozen object for the next game, read by game.js at newGame() and endGame() and never changed mid-game: hand = the state per category and sub-case (hanging_after_move split by pawnAmongTakers and takes_back, ignored_attack by sub), which gate.verdict reads as gameState.hand and honours as one more suppression reason ('hand') with the full facts attached, ALWAYS_HOLD and netLoss >= 5 excepted; copy = the bare question for quiet categories, the remembering question for the current rung's categories when the previous counted game had a hold of that kind (Claude's stored validated variant or COPY.PATH.QUESTION[rung]); gifts = {kind: 'pawn' while pawns is not off, else 'undefended' while what-takes-it is not off, else 'none'; forced: true while free is current; rate: 0.12 while free is not off, 0.08 after, 0.05 at the summit}; mateGiftRate = MATE_GIFT_RATE while the-mate-next-move is current else 0; playOn = true while finish is current; skill = 3 until the top summit rung is kept, then 4; drill = the first unmet set position when finish is current and no drill was played today, else null; moment = the oldest due moment of the current rung's kind not created today, else null; openingLine = Claude's stored next_game line if its rungId equals current, else COPY.PATH.OPEN[current][state] filled with counts in words and piece words from the newest record, prefixed once by the promise or decay sentence when a hand changed since the last game (the diff of state over the last N games and over N minus one), 'Today I keep my hands in my pockets.' at the summit, 'The other side plays harder now.' once after the win; closeLine = the template for what this game did to the current rung ('The pawns: not once this game. One more and I stop watching for them.') plus a slip line for any rung that decayed. scripts/test_path.mjs builds logs with a helper game({observed, result, holds: [{category, sub, pawnAmongTakers, variant, netLoss, ply, outcome}], escaped, giftsOffered, giftsTaken, freeTaken, materialAtEnd, finishPlies, handsOff, moment}) and asserts: three clean counted games make pawns off and current moves on; two make it quiet with the bare question in the plan; three games of twelve observed moves change nothing; three clean games with zero escapes leave their-last-move asking; a landing while off returns quiet and a second within three returns asking; alternating clean and one-landing games stay quiet (hysteresis); gifts offered 2 and taken 1 pass free, offered 2 taken 0 do not; the hand excludes an off category and includes ALWAYS_HOLD and a netLoss 6 verdict; the gift kind and rate follow state; drills on three dates make finish off and a drill stalemate does not; five material rungs off yield the summit plan with every material category off and 'hands in my pockets' in the line; a hands-in-pockets win keeps the top event and sets skill 4; a moment answered twice on one day is still live and on two days is retired, and a moment game never counts; the same log gives the same state twice; every line is at most 28 words, has no digit, and passes validate.templateRules. scripts/test_gate.mjs gains: g4 after 1.f3 e5 and a hanging queen still hold with every material category off. The scenario asserts the path view's textContent matches no digit and that #path is never present while data-state is held.
merged_proposal.why_this_wins: It is defined and computable: every rung is a gate category or sub-case the page already logs, every piece of evidence is a stored record or a per-game count (five small additive fields: landed outcomes with a reason, escaped, giftsOffered and giftsTaken, materialAtEnd and finishPlies, taps[].ask kept and said and answer and refutation on the record), and the whole model is a pure function over the log with named constants in contract.js. It is honest about sparse evidence without becoming opaque: observed moves are the denominator, every rung has a countable opportunity condition (escapes, gifts offered, five games of history, a mate-win, drills on dates), the gate keeps judging after the hand lets go so silence is measured, and the climb is three games so the coach can promise it in words and be checked. It is felt before it is shown, in the rules of play: the question goes bare before the hand lets go, the gifts change kind as he climbs, a gift is guaranteed while free is current, the bot plays the ending out while finish is current, the gift rate thins as rungs go off, and the summit is a real game announced before it starts with a win on top and a measured notch of difficulty after it; every rung has one celebration that is a sentence the close card can verify, and the thing that pulls him back tomorrow is a true promise ('One more and I stop watching for the pawns.', 'One of yours, from Tuesday.'). It is beautiful when shown because it is one state of the same page, the board as a still of his own held moment and seven serif sentences in three inks with one amber dot, words-only captions, never a numeral, never a tick, never a lock, reachable only from the close card and ply 0, and a rung that has not come up is not drawn. It is buildable in one iteration because it borrows the architect's persistence and merge rules whole, needs two bot levers that are existing enumerations plus two one-line rule changes (the forced gift, no resignation while finish is current), keeps the mate gift and the skill step behind constants that default to today's values until bot_sim passes, and has a cut list in order: the skill step, the mate gift, the set drills, the opening narration, the ply-0 moment link, Claude's again line. And Claude does what a table cannot, exactly where the LLM engineer put it: one consented call at the close that reads his typed plans across games into the sentence about where he is, writes the one question that remembers in words true of every hold of its kind, frames his own moment in his own words, and opens the next game, every word validated against an empty square set and per-rung piece words, with the template on screen first and the game identical without it. It takes the ladder's order and evidence from the chess master, the hand states and the hysteresis from the learning scientist and the product designer, the countdown copy and the moments from the beginner, the summit and the climbing opponent from my own model, the K3 contract from the LLM engineer and the data shapes from the architect, and leaves out the one thing every discipline flagged: a global budget, an unstable now, or a summit the player can see but cannot reach.

reviews.persona: The LLM engineer: owner of app/js/coach.js and app/js/validate.js. I decide when Claude is called, what facts the prompt holds, what shape the reply must have, how it is checked before a word reaches the line or a mark reaches a square, and what the page does, identically, without Claude. For this critique I re-read coach.js (PERSONA/K2_TASK/K1_INSTRUCTION, the fact-sheet builder, k1Context/k2Context, the lazy claude.use('sample'), the error map) and validate.js (the ordered pipeline: squares against the allowed set with piece-on-square checks, masking, SAN, digits, banned stems, caps), confirmed in game.js that holdRecord() drops taps[].ask (line 741), that the escaped reward is never persisted, that suppressed verdicts bump givenAway but are never logged, and that no record stores the Hear me out text, answer, refutation, variant or pawnAmongTakers; and I ran a validateK3 wrapper over the real validate.js (scratchpad k3_probe.mjs, 14 cases, all as expected after one fix: a question of the shape 'Hold on. ... ? Tap it.' is THREE sentences to validate.js's splitter, so the question cap must be three sentences, not two).

critiques.strengths: The most complete curriculum and the single most important data decision in the whole round: the gate keeps computing after the hand stops and logs outcome 'quiet' with netLoss, so silence is measured without the scaffold. Per-rung opportunity conditions (sixty player moves, two escapes, two gifts offered, six captures, reaching move ten) are the right defence against three empty games. The LLM role is bounded exactly as it should be: four moments, all quick tier, all after consent, facts rendered by path.js first, K4 prefetched at newGame so the remembering question is on screen at 0 ms, template always on screen first. The idea of masking rung result-phrases against a fixed list is a good validator primitive.
critiques.weaknesses: Not one iteration: ten rungs, a drills store, move lists on the summary, three bot changes (a 'counted' gift kind, the mate gift, Skill 5) each needing bot_sim, and Skill 20 depth 12 drill defence on a phone. The validator rule 'Claude may name a rung only by its result-phrase' is only half enforceable: a validator can reject strings, not claims, so a paraphrase ('you stopped hanging knights') passes while being false; the honest contract is that Claude never names a rung at all and the page's template carries the rung. K4's input carries squares from the last three games' holds while its output forbids squares, which is right, but the prompt must say why or the quick tier names them and every reply rejects. K3 'cached 24 h by game id' is fine; K5 on 'Play it again' is a third call shape for one line the K3 call could already have written.
critiques.what_i_would_add: Keep the 'quiet' outcome (as 'unheld' with a why), the opportunity conditions and the tie-break by last-five-games cost. Fold K5's drill line into K3's single call as an 'again' field keyed to the record, and drop the rung-phrase mask in favour of a flat rule: no rung names in Claude's text, the template names the rung. Cut the drills and bot changes to a later iteration and keep the 10-rung order as the ladder order of a 7-node first cut.

critiques.model: The map of your own games
critiques.strengths: Cost by netLoss is a sum the log already carries, and the master's own use of it, as the tie-break between eligible rungs and the gift kind, is right. Claude reading five games' holds as one shape ('both knights went where a pawn could reach them') is the one narration a table cannot write and it is validated by the same pipeline.
critiques.weaknesses: The global hand budget switches off a look he never learned after three clean games, which the master names and which from my seat makes the 'unheld' records lie about what was learned. 'Now' flips between games, so the stored K3 next line and the prefetched question are stale half the time (the nodeId check drops them and the templates stand, so no harm, but Claude's part is wasted). Cold start of five games means the only Claude line for a week is a template.
critiques.what_i_would_add: Only the tie-break and the 'cost in piece words' line in the K3 facts block; nothing else from this model ships.

critiques.strengths: The most honest evidence model on the table: an exposure denominator computed from facts the page already builds, a Beta posterior with a credible bound, forgetting per game, one-stage regression on a slip. It refuses both 'one slip in eighty is unlearned' and 'sixty clean is luck'. The LLM role is exactly bounded: Claude never sees counts, only the model's words; K3 validated with an empty allowed-square set, no digits, no question mark; K1 gains a pathway block; K2 lists the current look first; the 'play it again' lead has a template fallback. Idempotent folding by gameId is the right persistence discipline.
critiques.weaknesses: Heaviest to build: a scratch pass per position, a posterior per look, three stages with their own copy, an ASK_RATE sampler change needing bot_sim, a stored path doc and trials on the summary. Nine looks of which four are never current is a lot of copy for words-only status. The 'pause' stage ('Hold on. Look once more.' with both buttons at once and nothing graded) breaks the one rule every hold has kept, that the buttons come after the look; it also produces holds with no graded tap, which K1 cannot write for. Explaining a 0.8 quantile of Beta(1+A, 19+B) is not one sentence, though the stage words are.
critiques.what_i_would_add: Take the principle (a clean game with no exposures is no evidence) and ship its cheap proxies: observed moves (moves that had a verdict), gifts offered and taken, escapes. Keep the 14-day review rule and the one-stage regression. Leave the posterior and the scratch pass for when the first real log shows the proxies are not enough.

critiques.strengths: The mission's own three-of-five rule made exact and testable in ten lines; cheap; honest about being censored and coarse. Fine as the words layer over a finer model.
critiques.weaknesses: Censoring: a passive clean game masters 'give'. Coupled: one node mixes six looks so the remembered question and K2's ask preference cannot be chosen, which removes the two things Claude is for in this iteration. The LLM role is identical to the Ledger's and adds nothing of its own.
critiques.what_i_would_add: Its four headings as the grouping of the path view's sentences; nothing else.

critiques.model: The hand you no longer need
critiques.strengths: The best-specified shown state: the path takes exactly the board's footprint, six serif lines in three inks, one amber dot that means what amber means on the board, no numerals (a scenario can assert it). K3's contract adds 'focus' and 'ask' validated against the held-or-watching set and the node's offered asks, so Claude chooses which look to work on from the texture of the log and the page can overrule it: that is the brief's 'chooses which look to ask' done safely. The 'said' field on HoldRecord and the honest let_land sentence are right.
critiques.weaknesses: K3 fires only on the explicit 'Where I am' tap, so the next game's opening line is Claude's only when he visited the path page; most games open with the template. The consent dialog can land on that tap for a view that never pressed Hear me out, the first dialog outside a hold in the product. The 'watching' rule ('exactly one against-event in W and the rule was true one counted game earlier') is computable but hard to say in words. Three counted games with no opportunity condition for the hanging looks is thin.
critiques.what_i_would_add: Move K3 to the close card after consent (stored, shown on the path page from cache), keep 'focus' and 'ask' in the contract, keep the footprint layout and the amber dot.

critiques.strengths: The fading voice (full question, bare question, silent hold) is a practice mechanic that costs nothing in the model and is felt immediately. The K3b call is the cleanest in the round from a validation standpoint: three first-person lines, no squares, no digits, explicit tap, cached by game id, template lines when absent, and the link simply absent without sample.
critiques.weaknesses: Stored stages that are not derivable from the log without a replay; three nodes leave mates and the stalemate outside the path; a silent hold with an empty line reads as a bug after a break. Lines written 'in the player's words' from one typed sentence can misread a joke, and the validator checks words, not taste; the designer admits it lives at most one game, but it is a line in his voice attributed to him.
critiques.what_i_would_add: The 'bare' stage as how a 'light' hand speaks on a hold that still fires ('Hold on. Tap it.'), and the 'said' field. Not the stored stages.

critiques.strengths: Two honesty points nobody else states as plainly: 'observed' (moves that had a verdict) as the denominator, so engine-cold moves on a slow phone cannot inflate clean games; and suppressed verdicts logged as 'unheld' with a suppressed reason. One K3 call at the close card, cached 24 h by gameId, never at load; output {one_thing, next_game, focus} with focus allowed to break a tie between the top two only and never override the count; a rejected reply shows the template and increments __coachRejects. The extra graded tap once a game ('And one more: tap a square where it is safe') reuses ASKS exactly as K2 does. The fade is announced before the game and comes back on one slip with a sentence that owns it.
critiques.weaknesses: The validator rule 'squares only from this game's holds' is wrong for next_game, which is read over the start position of a different game; next_game and one_thing should allow no squares at all. The GIFT_RATE 0.16 notch and play-on-when-won while 'finish' is current are bot changes without bot_sim numbers. Eight nodes with five or six lines each is a lot of COPY to keep under copy_check.
critiques.what_i_would_add: Keep 'observed', 'unheld', the per-look fade with its announcement and the focus-as-tie-break contract. Give K3 an empty allowed-square set for every field.

critiques.strengths: The strongest 'I got somewhere' available in one sitting: the moment resumes as a real game, 'answered' is the gate's own clean verdict on his first move, not a stored answer, and the game continues. One quick call per created moment at the close card, cached by moment id, output a 16-word line that names no answer square, validated with the moment's allowed set minus its answer squares, stored on the moment and said at 0 ms when it reopens: exactly the K1 context reused. Claude choosing among due moments the one matching the current look is a bounded choice.
critiques.weaknesses: 'Answered' depends on a warm engine at the first move; a cold phone commits with no verdict and the moment reads as answered falsely. Opening the page on a moment by default is homework. The validation sentence in the 'took' node's evidence trails off mid-thought ('or the pre-search's best move... no:'), which is the kind of spec text that becomes a bug.
critiques.what_i_would_add: Make 'answered' require engineReady, else chess.js only (the lost piece not hanging after his move). Offer the moment from the close card link and the next game's opening line, never as the default start position.

critiques.strengths: The best felt-progression design: three hand states per look (asking, 'You know this one', off), an opponent that climbs with the player, a summit game announced before it starts, one celebration per node without confetti. events[] on the summary (gift offered/taken, threat parried, mate chance) is the right log of opportunities and makes mastery rules honest. The LLM role is clean: K3 at close cached by game id, K5 narration cached by a hash of hand states, K1 gains the current look and the hold's hand state so 'This one again' is only said when true, every output with a template twin.
critiques.weaknesses: Five unmeasured bot changes (threat moves at depth 10, mate threats, the mate gift, no-resign at Skill 20, a deeper book) is not one iteration and each must pass bot_sim before it ships. Nine nodes in four lanes shown under the board is close to a syllabus. 'You know this one' with no hint on the first wrong tap reads smug after a miss, and K1 then has nothing to write for that hold.
critiques.what_i_would_add: events[] (gift, free_taken, you_looked, mate_chance) on the summary and the two K1 facts. Leave the shaped opponent for a later iteration with bot_sim numbers.

critiques.strengths: The question travelling through time is a real idea, the memory ghost (Show me reused as memory) costs nothing, and the door lines are a bounded call: K4 per door at the close card, cached by door id, a 14-word open line in piece words with the K1 fact sheet's allowed squares, a 12-word through line, templates without Claude.
critiques.weaknesses: Clock-driven stored state (dueAt, stages, walks), one door per session set in sessionStorage, mid-game FENs that need a warm engine, three set positions with a Skill 20 defender, and a map page of doors: too much for one iteration beside any ladder. K5's map narration cached by a hash of door ids is fine but it is a third narration surface.
critiques.what_i_would_add: Only the memory ghost for 'Play it again from here' (the stored refutation played once and rewound before the hold asks).

critiques.strengths: My own earlier model, and its LLM contract is the one I still want: ONE quick-tier call per game end, after consent only, default cache because the prompt is a deterministic function of game id plus log, five outputs (where, next, again, question, ask_first) each with a template twin, validateK3 reusing validateText with an EMPTY allowed-square set so any square rejects, shape rules on the question (starts 'Hold on.', ends 'Tap it.', piece words only from the node's allowlist so the question is true of every hold of that kind without Claude seeing a position), ask_first in the offered set; K5 over one of his own held positions with the K1 context; five named log fixes. Today's probe over the real validate.js confirms the example passes and each bad reply rejects for its own reason.
critiques.weaknesses: TAPPED is weak evidence: 'vacuous under three records' means a node is in practice mastered by PLAYED plus HANDS-OFF, and seven-of-ten first taps on the own look needs taps[].ask kept, which the log does not do yet. The reply was all-or-nothing like K1; one bad field should not cost four good ones. The question cap I wrote (two sentences) rejects every well-formed question, because validate.js splits 'Hold on.' and 'Tap it.' as sentences; it must be three. Eight short names in a row under the board can read as a syllabus on a 400 px phone.
critiques.what_i_would_add: Per-field acceptance in validateK3 (kept fields used, rejected ones templated, __coachRejects per field); the three-sentence question cap; replace TAPPED with opportunity conditions and the beginner's 'observed' denominator; render the path as sentences, not a row of names.

critiques.strengths: Small and honest about it: the mission's measure as a path, the fading hand made exact, the same K3 contract with the budget line appended by the page so the announcement is always true.
critiques.weaknesses: A global budget is a trap by construction: a hold not made is a piece lost, and after three clean games it is off for a look he never learned; the master, the beginner and I all say so. The 'look of the week' is a pointer, not a node, so the remembered question and K2's ask preference have nothing to be keyed to across games. Five words with rules between them on the close card is one argument from a progress bar.
critiques.what_i_would_add: Nothing beyond the K3 shape it shares with the first model.

critiques.strengths: The most buildable and the most precisely specified: path.compute(games, now) pure over the stored summaries with no state of its own; the hand applied inside gate.verdict as one more suppression reason with the full facts attached (so a faded hold is logged with the same category, sub, netLoss and target); losses[] and rewards[] on the summary (escaped recorded whether or not the budget let it be said); gifts {offered, taken}; v: 2 with a norm() reader so v1 games keep working; KEEP.GAMES 12 at under 10 KB; the db mirror with a set-union merge by id, a permissions.state check so no dialog can appear at boot, one write at a time, and nothing ever said about it. K3 fires at endGame after storeGame and only after consent, default cache, aborted by Again, validated with the empty allowed-square set, stored as holdon.v1.pathLine and read at 0 ms at the next newGame; K1 and K2 gain one path sentence; Claude never decides a status, a hand level or the gift rate.
critiques.weaknesses: The thinnest LLM role on the table: narration and the opening line only, so of the brief's four 'what tables cannot' items it does two; no remembered question, no choice of look, no drill line. pawn_takes merges the pawn taker, the piece taker and the takes-back variant into one node, which loses the master's first and second rungs as separate habits (the copy splits them, the mastery does not). 'light' as 'the first hold of the kind fires, then not' is a per-kind budget of one, acceptable but unannounced inside the game.
critiques.what_i_would_add: Split pawn_takes into pawns, what-reaches and takes-back using pawnAmongTakers and variant (both must be stored on the record). Widen K3 to the five-field contract with per-field validation, and add K5 on the path row tap.

critiques.strengths: The drill arm that needs no engine: the answer set, best, partial and refutation stored with the record, graded by gate.grade offline, Show me from the stored refutation on a scratch Chess, the real game's pre-search started only after the drill closes. One call per drill at the close that created it, after consent, with the K1 fact sheet rebuilt from the stored fen and san so the allowed squares are the hold's own, stored as lines, 'This one again.' without Claude. Intervals as a constant table, due dates recomputed from tries[] so a device never trusts another's derived fields.
critiques.weaknesses: A held position with no game behind it is a puzzle, and the beginner says the moment that continues as a game is what he would believe; it also adds a second place a session can open. v1 records have no answer set, so the queue is empty until the next stored game and the close-card sentence must not promise what the store cannot build.
critiques.what_i_would_add: Keep the stored answer/refutation and the offline verdict rebuild, but open the drill from the close card as 'Play it again from here' and let the game continue from the position after the decision, as the beginner's moments do.

ranking: The hand you no longer need
The map of your own games

merged_proposal.name: The hand that goes quiet
merged_proposal.one_sentence_for_a_beginner: The coach stops your hand for seven looks; each one it has had nothing to stop you for in three real games, it stops stopping, and if you stay clean with its hand off, that look is yours.
merged_proposal.the_idea: A short ladder of seven looks (the architect's pure path.compute spine with the master's pawn/piece/takes-back split), where mastery is the coach's measured silence over games that counted, made honest by cheap denominators rather than a posterior: observed moves (moves that had a verdict, so a cold engine cannot make a clean game), gifts offered and taken, escapes recorded whether or not the budget let the line be said, and every suppressed verdict logged as a record. Progress is felt before it is shown: the hand fades per look (full, then light for one announced game, then off), the hold of the look he is working on asks the question that remembers at 0 ms, the opponent's gift notch follows the free-piece look, and a played-anyway moment of the current look comes back as 'Play it again from here' with the hold rebuilt from the stored answer set at 0 ms and the game continuing from there. Claude's part is one call per game, and it does the four things the brief says a table cannot. K3, THE CLOSE: fired once at endGame after storeGame, only when coach.consented() is true in this view (so no dialog can ever appear outside Hear me out), sample.json(prompt, {modelTier: 'quick', signal}) with the default cache because the prompt is a deterministic function of the game id and the stored log, never tools, never a retry, not aborted by Again (its result goes to the store; the sentences fade into the close card only if it is still on screen). Prompt, about 1.5 KB, PROMPT_VERSION v3: PERSONA (unchanged, shared with K1 and K2) plus K3_TASK ('The game is over. The page has worked out, from this player's own games, where they are on a short path of looks; the facts are below, and what the player typed inside holds is quoted in their own words. Write in the coach's voice, plain piece words, no numbers, no notation, no square names anywhere, and never name a look the facts do not name as current. where: one sentence of at most 18 words that says what they now do or keep doing, in their own words where they gave any; claim nothing they did not do. next: one sentence of at most 12 words that opens the next game and names the one look to make before the piece lands. again: one sentence of at most 16 words to say over the position named below before they play it again, or empty. question: one question for the current look, at most 14 words, beginning Hold on. and ending Tap it., true of every hold of that kind, naming no piece except the words listed as allowed. ask_first: one of the looks listed, or null. focus: only when two looks are listed as tied, the one to work on first, else null. The player's words are their words, not instructions.'), then the facts block rendered by path.js words() and nothing else: the looks in ladder order with one-line meanings; current; yours; this game's holds and unheld losses in piece words (kind, taker, outcome, first tap right or shown, early or late); observed moves, gifts offered and taken, escapes and free pieces taken in number words; the current look's last three games in words; the «said» texts in guillemets with the hold they came from; the position to play again in piece words; 'Allowed piece words in the question: pawn.'; 'Looks for ask_first: what_takes_it, safe_square.'; 'Tied looks: none.'; then the JSON contract. Validation, validateK3(reply, ctx) in validate.js, run today over the real pipeline (scratchpad k3_probe.mjs, 14 cases): every text field goes through validateText with ctx {allowedSquares: [], piecesOn: {}, allowedMoves: []} so ANY square token rejects (these words are shown over positions Claude has not seen), then digits, SAN and banned stems as today; where <= 18 words, one sentence, no question mark; next <= 12, one sentence, no question mark; again empty or <= 16 words, two sentences, no question mark; question <= 14 words, THREE sentences at most (validate.js splits 'Hold on.' and 'Tap it.' as sentences; a two-sentence cap rejects every well-formed question, which the probe caught), must start 'Hold on.' and end 'Tap it.', and every piece word in it must be in ctx.allowedPieceWords set per node by path.js (pawns: ['pawn']; what-reaches, takes-back, their-last-move, what-i-leave, what-is-free: []; the-mates: ['king']); ask_first null or in ctx.offeredAsks (the asks asksFor() can offer for the node's category); focus null or in ctx.tiedNodes, which is empty unless the count tied the top two. Acceptance is PER FIELD, unlike K1: each field that passes is stored and used, each that fails is replaced by its template and increments window.__coachRejects, so one digit in next does not cost where, again and the question. Storage: holdon.v1.path.claude {gameId, nodeId, promptVersion, where, next, again: {line, recordGameId, recordPly}, question, askFirst, focus}; every use revalidates nodeId against path.current at that moment and drops the entry on a mismatch, so a stale line never opens a game about a look he is no longer on. How each field is used: where fades in under the close card's counts and is the path page's sentence for the current look; next is the next game's opening line at 0 ms with zero calls at boot (and reaches the phone through the db mirror); again is said above the page's own question when 'Play it again from here' opens, only if the stored record reference matches; question replaces the category template at 0 ms on holds whose nodeOf(verdict) === current, never swapping under his eyes because it was stored before the game began; ask_first, when the hold's asksFor() offers that kind, makes the page ask that look's own question graded by that look's answer set (the K2 mechanism exactly); focus breaks a tie between the top two only. K5, THE IDEA: on an explicit tap of a look's sentence on the path page, after consent only, default cache keyed by the immutable record, aborted on leaving the page; prompt = PERSONA + the K1 fact sheet rebuilt by chess.js from record.fen, record.san, record.answer and record.refutation + 'The look: pawns: a piece left where a pawn takes it.' + 'Say in one sentence of at most 20 words what this look finds in this position, naming only squares from the list with the piece on them. No question.'; validateText(idea, k1Context(factsAfter, hold), {maxWords: 20, maxSentences: 1, noQuestion: true}); the template COPY.PATH.IDEA[node] otherwise. K1 gains two facts ('The player's current look: pawns.' and 'This hold's hand: full | light.') so and_then and anyway may say 'Third time this week a pawn was waiting' only when the log says so; K2 gains 'The player's current look: X' so the chosen ask leans toward it; both validated exactly as today. Call budget: zero at load, zero in the tutorial, zero in any game before consent, one K3 per game end after consent, K5 per explicit tap. Without Claude (sample null, declined, resting, rejected, a friend's Viewer copy): the identical pathway from path.js; COPY.PATH templates keyed by node and status for OPEN, LIGHT, OFF, BACK, DUE, QUESTION, WHERE, AGAIN ('You played this one. Look first this time.') and IDEA; ask_first by path.js's own rule; no control shown disabled; no copy mentions Claude; the only thing missing is his own words. Log changes that must land first, all additive, v: 2 on new summaries with norm() filling v1 records: HoldRecord keeps taps[].ask, gains said (the Hear me out text, 120 chars, or null), answer {squares, best, partial}, refutation, variant, pawnAmongTakers, and the outcome 'unheld' with why 'pair' | 'quiet' | 'light' | 'faded' for every suppressed verdict, logged where givenAway is incremented today; GameSummary gains observed, rewards: [{kind, ply, piece, said}], gifts: {offered, taken}, handsOff: nodeId | null; KEEP.GAMES 12, KEEP.HOLDS 60; holdon.v1.giftRate read once as a fallback and no longer written. Persistence: localStorage always; the architect's mirror to one private db document per viewer at data/users/<uid>/holdon with the set-union merge by game id, flags ORed, pathLine and path.claude from the newer game, permissions.state('db') read first so the first db call never prompts at boot (it waits for Again or 'Where you are' over state over), one write at a time, errors silent, Viewers never write. Shown: one more state of the same page, view=path on the stage, reached only from the close card's --muted link 'Where you are' and left by Back or Again, never during play; the board becomes a still of the current look's last held position (record.fen with san replayed, the piece lifted, the square amber, the rest dimmed, input locked); the serif line reads K3's where or the template; under the board the seven looks as serif sentences in his own first person, --ink with 'This is where we are.' for current, --muted with 'Yours.' for mastered, --muted with 'Later.' or 'Not come up yet.' for the rest, 'Again, for now.' for a look that came back, 'A month on; I will check once.' for a due one, one amber dot on the current look; a scenario asserts #path textContent matches no digit and that #path is absent while data-state is held. First session: identical until the first close card, which gains one template sentence and the link; if he pressed Hear me out, K3 fires behind the card and where fades in in about a second; game two opens with next and its first hold of the current look asks the remembered question.
nodes_in_order: pawns: 'I stop leaving pieces where a pawn takes them.' (hanging_after_move, pawnAmongTakers true, variant null)
what-reaches: 'I see what reaches the square before the piece lands.' (hanging_after_move, no pawn among takers, variant null; needs pawns quiet)
takes-back: 'Before I take, I see what takes back.' (hanging_after_move, variant takes_back; needs what-reaches quiet)
their-last-move: 'I see what their last move attacked.' (ignored_attack sub already; escapes as the opportunity)
what-is-free: 'I take what is free.' (free_piece_ignored; gifts offered and taken as the opportunity; owns the gift notch)
what-i-leave: 'I notice what my move leaves behind.' (ignored_attack sub lost_guard or opened_line; four-game window; needs their-last-move quiet)
the-mates: 'I see the mate next move, theirs and mine, and I never stalemate.' (allowed_mate, missed_mate, allowed_stalemate; five-game window; the hand never fades, status is words only)
out-alive (words only, from moves[] on the summary; first on the cut list): 'I get out of the opening alive.'
merged_proposal.next_rule: path.compute(games, now) -> { nodes: { id: { status, hand } }, current, tied, giftRate, line, next }, pure over the stored summaries (holds embedded, v1 records normalised by norm()) and a fixed clock, deterministic, unit-tested in scripts/test_path.mjs over synthetic logs. Definitions: nodeOf(record) maps category, sub, variant and pawnAmongTakers to a node id; a record is any HoldRecord of a node with outcome back, anyway, ended or unheld (unheld = a suppressed verdict with why pair, quiet, light or faded, so a faded hand cannot hide a relapse). A qualifying game has observed >= 20 (player moves that had a verdict), or result mate-win or resign at any length; a v1 game qualifies by plies >= 40 or a win; give-ups under the floor count for nothing. Status per node, in ladder order in one pass: not_yet while fewer than three qualifying games exist or the node has never produced a record; working while the window has records; quiet when the last three qualifying games (four for what-i-leave with at least five qualifying games in the log, five for the-mates) hold zero records of the node AND the node's opportunity holds (pawns, what-reaches, takes-back, what-i-leave: observed summed >= 60, or 80 for the four-game window; their-last-move: rewards of kind escaped summed >= 2; what-is-free: gifts.offered summed >= 2 and gifts.taken >= two thirds of offered; the-mates: at least one mate-win) and its prerequisite is quiet or better; yours when the node was quiet and the one subsequent qualifying game played with hand light had zero unheld losses of the node with netLoss >= 2 (the-mates: words only, yours when quiet); back when a yours node has one such loss in the newest qualifying game; due when a yours node's newest qualifying game is older than thirty days. Hand per node: full for not_yet, working and back-after-a-second-slip; light (the first hold of the kind fires with its question, every later verdict of the kind that game is logged unheld why light and the move lands) for the first qualifying game after quiet, for back, and for due; off (every verdict of the kind logged unheld why faded, the move lands, the opponent takes, the close caption reads 'it landed') for yours; the-mates always full; ALWAYS_HOLD and any netLoss >= 5 ignore the hand, exactly as they ignore the quiet-after-two rule. gate.verdict(pre, post, before, after, gameState) reads gameState.hand[category] then [sub] (and the pawn and takes_back split for hanging_after_move) and returns {held: false, suppressed: true, why, ...facts}; game.js logs it. Decay: one unheld loss of a yours node (netLoss >= 2) -> back, hand light, the next game opens 'The pawns, once, and I said nothing. I am holding those again for a game.'; a second within the same or the next qualifying game -> working, hand full; a clean light game from back -> yours again. current = among nodes not yours whose prerequisites are quiet or better, the node with the most records in the last three qualifying games; ties by ladder order, except that when the top two are tied and a validated K3 focus for the game just ended names one of them, that one; an empty log -> pawns; all yours -> null and the line is 'Your move.' tied = the top two when tied, else []. giftRate = 0.12 until what-is-free is yours, then 0.08 (replacing the clean-game step; the notch is derived, not stored). next = { kind: 'again', record } when the game just ended holds an anyway or unheld record of current with netLoss >= 2: the close card shows 'Play it again from here' beside Again (Again stays primary); the drill loads record.fen, replays record.san and rebuilds the verdict from the stored answer and refutation the way tutorialVerdict() does, so it holds at 0 ms with no engine wait, says the stored again line above the page's own question, and after the decision the game continues from there against the normal opponent; 'Answered' means he kept the piece (gate clean when the engine is ready, else chess.js: the lost piece not hanging after his move); drill records are logged with gameId suffixed ':again' and never count toward quiet. Else next = { kind: 'game', node: current, line } where line = the stored K3 next when its nodeId equals current, else COPY.PATH.OPEN[current][status], prefixed by the light or off announcement when a hand changed since the last game ('This game I will not stop your hand for a pawn. It is real.'), and the remembered question for current is armed (stored K3 question if its nodeId matches, else COPY.PATH.QUESTION[current]). Fixtures in scripts/test_path.mjs: an empty log -> current pawns, hand full everywhere, next game; two pawn holds then three clean qualifying games with observed 22, 24, 26 -> pawns quiet, hand light; a fourth clean game with handsOff pawns -> yours, hand off; three clean games of observed 12 -> nothing quiet; a clean window with gifts.offered 0 -> what-is-free not quiet; an unheld pawn loss while yours -> back and light, a second -> working and full; a 31-day gap -> due and light for one game; a played-anyway of current -> next 'again'; the-mates never off; a stale K3 nodeId -> template line; the same log twice -> the same state; every COPY.PATH line at most 28 words passing templateRules and copy_check with no digit. scripts/test_validate.mjs gains the fourteen validateK3 cases run today plus the per-field case; scripts/test_gate.mjs gains gameState.hand cases (Nxe5 in the 6...d6 position suppressed why faded with the facts intact; g4 after 1.f3 e5 and a queen hang still held under any hand).
merged_proposal.why_this_wins: It is the only combination that passes all six judgments at once. Well defined and computable: the architect's pure path.compute over the stored log, with no state of its own, so a corrupt key loses nothing but Claude's lines and the whole model runs in node over a synthetic array. Honest about sparse evidence: the beginner's observed denominator, the architect's logged losses, the master's opportunity conditions and the scientist's principle that a game with no exposure proves nothing, all as cheap fields the summary can carry this iteration, plus a light game before the hand goes off and a one-slip return so a false mastery costs one felt piece. Felt first: the opening line, the question that remembers at 0 ms, the per-look fade announced before it happens, the gift notch tied to the free-piece look, and a played-anyway moment that comes back as a game, none of it needing a call. Beautiful when shown: the designer's board-footprint page with seven first-person sentences in three inks, one amber dot and no numeral anywhere, asserted by a scenario. Buildable: additive log fields with a norm() reader, one gate suppression reason, one page state, one validator wrapper whose fourteen cases already pass against the real validate.js, and nothing in the opponent that needs bot_sim beyond the notch it already has; the opening node and K5 are the named cuts. And Claude does what a table cannot, in one call per game whose every field has a template twin: it says where he is in his own typed words, writes the question the coach asks on the look he keeps missing (true of every hold of that kind because the piece-word allowlist and the empty square set make it so), frames the moment he is about to replay, writes the line that opens the next game, and breaks a tie between two looks from the texture of his taps; it never decides a status, a hand, a gift or a hold, never sees a FEN it could act on outside K5's own fact sheet, and the page is identical without it.

reviews.persona: Frontend architect: owner of store.js, contract.js (KEYS, KEEP), the game.js state machine, window.__app and the headless harness. I think in modules, data shapes, keys, migrations, merge rules and scenarios. Verified in code this pass: holdRecord() drops taps[].ask (game.js line 741); the 'escaped' reward is applied in applyReward() but only freeTaken is persisted; a verdict suppressed by the pair or quiet rule sets `loss`, increments givenAway after the reply and writes no record; game ids are Date.now().toString(36) with no suffix; a stored game with two holds is 776 bytes and a 70-move SAN list 421 bytes; the close card is #close (.close-sum, .close-holds, [data-action=again]) under .stage and the empty action bar collapses in state over; KEEP is {GAMES: 5, HOLDS: 30}; store.js is {get, set, remove, list, append} with node tests over a fake localStorage. Verified in the capability contract (runtime 0.2.75): data/users/<id> is a collection, so one document per viewer is db.doc('data/users/' + uid + '/holdon') (four segments); a document body is at most 256 KiB; writes below interact or into another viewer's subtree reject invalid_argument; unavailable is retried once; a non-empty capabilities declaration revokes what it omits, so the republish declares {sample: {}, db: {}, user: {}} in full; permissions is built in, never declared, and permissions.state('db') reads without prompting; claude.use() resolves after first paint and null outside the viewer; user.id() needs {user: {}} and a null id means no private subtree.

critiques.strengths: The most complete evidence table on the team, and state(games, holds, drills, {today}) plus plan(state) is exactly the pure-module shape path.js should have. The opportunity floors (sixty player moves in the window, two gifts offered, two escapes, six captures) are the cheap honest cousin of an exposure denominator, and the 'quiet' outcome for a verdict the faded hand let through is the log change the whole team converges on. Out-of-order quiet (the first three games are the placement) and the cost tie-break borrowed from the map are both one pass over fields the record already carries (category, sub, pawnAmongTakers via the piece on record.best, san with 'x', netLoss).
critiques.weaknesses: Ten rungs need nine new GameSummary fields (moves, escaped, giftsOffered, captures, castledMove, minorsOutBy10, earlyQueen, centrePawnBy3, conversion), a new key of DrillRecords, a drill mode with a Skill-20 defender (engine.setOptions per mode, a move cap, a new data-mode on the board) and five opponent levers (gift kinds pawn/undefended/counted, the mate gift that inverts a sampler guard the acceptance suite asserts, Skill 5), each needing a bot_sim re-measurement. That touches bot.js and game.js, the two largest files, deeply, and two-targets is defined on a gate category that does not exist. It is two iterations of work and the first would ship nothing visible.
critiques.what_i_would_add: Ship rungs 1 to 5 and 7 as the node set with its opportunity floors and its suppressed-verdict logging, derived entirely from games[].holds plus three cheap counters (observed moves, rewards[], gifts {offered, taken}); put the gift kind and the mate gift behind a plan.gifts field that exists in the state from day one so bot.js can read it in iteration three once bot_sim has measured it; defer the drills and the move-list rungs.

critiques.model: The map of your own games (chess master)
critiques.strengths: Cost is a sum of netLoss over records the log already carries: one reducer, trivially testable. The targeted gift kind is one filter on giftCandidates(). The author's own verdict that it belongs inside the ladder as a tie-break, not above it, is right.
critiques.weaknesses: Argmax flips between games, so the opening line and the remembered question can contradict last game's; a five-game cold start on a five-game store; and the global per-game budget suppresses holds of looks never learned, which the gate test would have to encode as 'g4 after 1.f3 e5 still holds at budget 0' for every look. The budget is derived from givenAway, which today counts only losses that landed, so a game with two pair-suppressed losses that the opponent did not collect reads as clean and lowers the budget.
critiques.what_i_would_add: Keep cost as the tie-break among eligible nodes with a hysteresis margin (current changes only when a rival's cost exceeds it by two points), never as the ordering, and never a global budget.

critiques.strengths: The only model with a real denominator; the trial shape (exposure flags per position, pass or fail per move) is the honest unit, and a fold that is idempotent by gameId is the right property for a two-device merge. Per-look fading with one-stage regression, the opponent as the review scheduler through a derived gift rate rather than a stored notch, and the test list (a passive player never masters anything) are what the other models lack.
critiques.weaknesses: Exposures need a scratch pass over every legal non-capturing piece move with pieceInfo() on the drop path, where the budget is 300 ms headless and 600 ms on a phone with the pre-search already running. The 0.8 posterior quantile needs an incomplete-beta routine in a plain ES module with no dependencies, which nobody on the team can verify by reading. The model is a folded document (A, B, stage, sinceFail per node) that is not derivable from the log, so a corrupt key loses the path and the 'larger games counter wins' merge drops the other device's games. The 'pause' stage is a third hold rendering (both buttons at once, nothing graded) that hold.js and the harness's held assertions do not have, and trials per move grow the GameSummary per move, not per hold. The mastery rule cannot be said to Sambudh in his own words.
critiques.what_i_would_add: Keep the denominator as one integer per game (observed: player moves that had a verdict) plus the per-node opportunity floors, and keep 'a fail counts as an exposure'; drop the Beta, the scratch pass and the folded document so the log stays the only authority.

critiques.strengths: Zero new per-move computation; four nodes that map onto the master's patterns; three of five is the mission's own measure; review games at plus one, three and eight are a cheap SM-2; the stage reducer over consecutive clean games is five lines.
critiques.weaknesses: Censored (a passive clean game counts as clean), coupled (one node mixes six looks, so neither the remembered question nor the gift kind can be chosen), slow (five qualifying games per node), and the opening node needs moves[]. reviewAt as an array of game numbers is stored state that must survive a merge.
critiques.what_i_would_add: Use its four pattern names as the words layer over the seven looks on the path view (quiet captions, not nodes), and its review game as the one-game bare re-check after an idle gap.

critiques.model: The hand you no longer need (product designer)
critiques.strengths: Six nodes in four states computed over W = the last three counted games, focus = the first held node, the hold policy frozen per game, let_land logged with the honest sentence, one loss to watching and two to held, fourteen idle days to watching for one game. The path view is specified to the pixel (the board's footprint, 348 px inside 368, one amber dot, no numerals, Escape returns) and '#path is never present while data-state is held' is the right harness invariant. Games raised to ten and holds to sixty with the new outcomes, said and answered; a Viewer never writes.
critiques.weaknesses: K3 fires on the 'Where I am' tap, so the platform's consent dialog can land outside a hold for a view that never pressed Hear me out; the designer names it and accepts it, I would not. 'watching' needs 'the same rule over the window one counted game earlier', a second compute over games.slice(0, -1) that path.js must state as such. The 'ever before W' tests need history beyond W, so the migration must treat a v1 five-game array as 'no history', never as 'never happened'. Entry from idle at ply 0 is reachable while the pre-search runs and the scenario must assert fen() and state().pre survive the round trip. Fading the board out loses the one thing the board can show there, his own position.
critiques.what_i_would_add: Fire K3 at endGame after consent and store it so the tap only reads; keep the board as a still of the focus node's last held record instead of fading it; take its let_land logging, its W and its watching rules as written.

critiques.model: Three looks, in your words (product designer)
critiques.strengths: No new page state. The bare question ('Hold on. Tap it.') is the cheapest intermediate hand level there is: a copy key, not a rendering. 'In my words' is a true explicit-tap moment, and the stages are recomputable by a replay migration.
critiques.weaknesses: Stages are stored state (the retreat rule depends on the stage at the time of each hold), which is the one kind of state path.js must never own. The silent hold (an empty coach box while held) breaks the hold acceptance (the question at 0 ms, .coach starting with 'Hold on.') and the aria-live contract. Three nodes cannot drive the gift kind or the mate holds, and Claude's lines in the player's words go stale the moment a stage changes.
critiques.what_i_would_add: Keep only the bare question as the middle hand level, derived from the log; drop the silent stage and the stored stages.

critiques.strengths: observed (moves with a verdict) as the denominator, so a cold engine on a phone cannot inflate clean games; suppressed verdicts logged as 'unheld' with a reason; two per-game exposure counters (freeOffered, wonPosition); the path lists only looks that have been seen, so the first visit cannot read as a syllabus; the reducer is rebuilt from holds and games when the key is missing; 'Nothing on my list. Your move.' as the top state.
critiques.weaknesses: It stores a reducer state (cleanRun, fadeRun, since) that is also derivable, so two copies can disagree after a merge. GIFT_RATE +1 notch to 0.16 and the bot playing on in every won position while 'finish' is current are unmeasured opponent changes (0.16 is not in GIFT_RATE_STEPS and the play-on rule was rejected in the MVP for his ten minutes). The extra graded tap after a right tap is a second question inside a hold that the hold state machine does not have, and eight nodes times five lines of copy.
critiques.what_i_would_add: Derive instead of store (the reducer becomes compute over the log); keep observed and the suppressed-verdict logging; leave the opponent at its two measured notches.

critiques.strengths: The strongest felt proof on the team ('I lost a knight there on Tuesday and today I did not'); one moment per fen; the five-points-down filter; the thirty-day silent drop; 'Fresh game instead' never counted.
critiques.weaknesses: 'Answered' is the gate's live verdict on the first move, which needs a warm engine; on a cold phone the first move commits with no verdict and the moment cannot be judged. A session that opens on a moment changes the first screen of a session. A moment is a real game id, so a thirty-second missed-mate moment would be stored and counted as evidence unless excluded. A mid-game FEN resets the book and the gift roll (botMoveNo comes from the FEN's move number). A new key with twelve objects and a clock.
critiques.what_i_would_add: Keep the close card's 'Play it again from here' slice only, graded at 0 ms from the record's stored answer set with no engine, logged as outcome 'again' and excluded from mastery; the stack and the schedule wait for the next iteration.

critiques.strengths: Derived, never stored, recomputed at boot and Again. The three hand states (asking; the quiet copy 'Hold on. You know this one. Tap it.'; off) are the cleanest fade I have read: the middle one costs a copy key and no rendering. 'landed' outcomes carry the suppression reason (pair, quiet, hand) so every givenAway has a record. Transitions as the diff between derive over N and N minus 1 games need no stored transitions. Hysteresis (two-game climb, two-event decay), the summit game, and a path view that keeps the board as a still of the look's last position.
critiques.weaknesses: Five opponent levers (threat moves, mate threats, the mate gift, no resignation, the deeper book) each need a bot.js enumeration plus depth-10 verification and a bot_sim re-measurement, and 'forced once by the twelfth move' changes the measured gift rate. An events[] array per game grows the summary per bot move. Four lanes and nine sentences is the most copy on the team; castledPly and minorsOutPly need the move list; the --coach underline on the current sentence is a second mark beside the amber.
critiques.what_i_would_add: Ship its hand trio and its 'landed' logging exactly; hold every opponent lever behind plan.gifts until bot_sim measures it; replace the events array with three counters (observed, rewards[], gifts {offered, taken}).

critiques.strengths: The question travelling through time is the brief's own novel object. The cold-boot fallback (a 2 s engine check; the door stays due) and sessionStorage for one door per session are the right mechanics, and the stage-based hand on a stored position is SM-2 made exact.
critiques.weaknesses: Doors are stored state with a clock (dueAt), eight objects plus three set doors; walks are judged at the tenth move by game.js (a new mid-game judge in the controller); the first reply at full strength is a bot.js branch; set doors need a Skill-20 defender and a forty-ply clock; and a session opens on a door. Every one of those is a module I own or a file I do not, and none is a day's work.
critiques.what_i_would_add: Nothing this iteration; its 'Tomorrow: the knight from today is waiting.' close line is the one sentence worth keeping once Play it again exists.

critiques.strengths: The three-source mastery rule with TAPPED (first tap right on the hold's own look, which is why taps[].ask must be kept) and HANDS-OFF. One K3 call per game at the close, after consent, producing where, next, again, question and ask_first; validateK3 with an empty allowed-square set and per-node allowed piece words, run against the real validate.js; the drill rebuilt from the record's answer and refutation at 0 ms the way tutorialVerdict() does; stored Claude lines revalidated against the current node before use. The five log gaps are named exactly (taps[].ask, said, answer and refutation, 'unheld', escaped), and they match what I verified.
critiques.weaknesses: Mastery is a stored event list merged with a derived state (removed only by the decay rule), a hybrid two devices can disagree on. The announced hands-off game per node costs a whole real game per node and a handsOff field on GameSummary. Entry by tapping the brand in the header is an affordance nobody will find; the --ok ring beside a done look is a mark the design refuses; eight 44 px rows under the board is a list.
critiques.what_i_would_add: Keep its K3 contract, its validator wrapper and its drill mechanism verbatim; replace the hands-off game with an 'off' level reached through the bare level, derived; keep the entry on the close card only.

critiques.strengths: The deferred fading hand made exact (budget = max(0, 3 minus cleanStreak)); computable from givenAway today; four fixtures that fit in twenty lines.
critiques.weaknesses: A global budget suppresses looks never learned (the mate and five-point exceptions are not enough). Five words joined by rules on the close card is a progress bar in a serif. A 'look of the week' pointer is not a pathway of looks, and givenAway as the only measure ignores holds taken back, so a game with six holds all taken back reads as clean.
critiques.what_i_would_add: Nothing of the budget; its look-of-the-week argmax survives as the tie-break between eligible nodes.

critiques.model: Five questions, one hand (frontend architect, mine)
critiques.strengths: path.compute(games, now) over the stored summaries only, never stored; losses[] and rewards[] as additive record changes with norm() for v1; KEEP.GAMES 12 measured under 10 KB; view=path on .stage entered from state over only so nothing live is frozen and the board is a still of his own position; the db mirror as one document per viewer with permissions.state gating the first prompt onto a stable tap, a pure sync.js merge (set-union by id, flags OR) tested in node, one write at a time, ids with a random suffix.
critiques.weaknesses: On rereading the others: the 'light' level ('the first hold of this kind fires, the rest do not') is a hand the player cannot read, where the bare question is one he can. Qualifying at plies >= 24 is low against the measured 68 to 80 plies and the team's 40. No denominator (observed) and no tap evidence. one_move_mates lumps three categories. losses[] as a second array beside holds[] is one shape too many; a hold record with outcome 'landed' is simpler and lets closeCaption() work unchanged. Mastery on silence alone over three games.
critiques.what_i_would_add: The bare level, observed, plies >= 40, 'landed' hold records instead of losses[], and the LLM engineer's K3 contract.

critiques.model: Your own positions, spaced (frontend architect, mine)
critiques.strengths: A drill graded at 0 ms from the stored answer set with no engine, the one mechanism Doors and the moments lack; intervals as a constant table; KEEP.DRILLS 12; skip-when-faded so the two models never contradict; merge by the longer tries[].
critiques.weaknesses: v1 records have no answer sets so the queue starts empty; a game can begin in the drill state, which is a session opening on something other than the idle board; data-drill as a sub-state of held is a second place the first screen of a session can land; a second feature's worth of copy and scenarios.
critiques.what_i_would_add: Only its first slice this iteration, as the close card's 'Play it again from here'; the schedule waits.
