final.the_model: KIND. A ladder of seven looks in a fixed order, each named as a result in the player's words, each mapped one-to-one onto a gate category, sub-case or split the record already carries. A ladder and not a map because the current rung moves only by rule. The order (pawns, takers, takes_back, their_last_move, free, guards, mates) is a deliberate departure from the chess master's lesson order, which puts their-last-move first: the gate's data says the pawn landing is the commonest and cheapest event, so it is placed first and stated as such. NODES: pawns, takers, takes_back, their_last_move, free, guards, mates. nodeOf(record) is a pure function with pawnAmongTakers as the FIRST split: hanging_after_move with pawnAmongTakers true is pawns whether or not the move captured (Nxe5 in the 6...d6 position, where dxe5 answers, is pawns); hanging_after_move with pawnAmongTakers false and variant 'takes_back' is takes_back (Bxf7+ with the king taking back); hanging_after_move with pawnAmongTakers false and variant null is takers; ignored_attack sub 'already' is their_last_move; sub 'lost_guard' or 'opened_line' is guards; free_piece_ignored is free; allowed_mate, missed_mate and allowed_stalemate are mates. For a v1 record the split is derived by chess.js (the pawn attackers of record.to in record.fen after record.san, and 'x' in san), and the expected look for every recorded move in data/positions.json and tutorial.json is written as an explicit table in test_path.mjs (italian_d6 Nxe5 pawns, Bxf7+ takes_back, queen_hang Qxe5+ and Qxf7+ takes_back, tutorial Nd4/Ba6/Be6 pawns, ruy_a6 O-O their_last_move, nc4_rook Nc4 takers, italian_nxe4 Nc3 guards, f3_e5 g4 mates, scholars Qh3 mates, kq_stalemate Qf7 mates). A RECORD of a look is any HoldRecord with nodeOf(record) === look and outcome back, anyway, ended or landed (a verdict the gate matched but did not show, why 'pair', 'quiet' or 'hand'), in any game that is not an 'again' game; tutorial holds are excluded. OBSERVED is the count of committed player moves with a non-null verdict (taken-back moves and cold-engine moves excluded). A COUNTED game is a digest with again false and (observed >= PATH.OBSERVED_MIN (20) or (result in {mate-win, mate-loss, resign} and observed >= PATH.OBSERVED_DECISIVE_MIN (8))); the plies clause is gone (it was implied). Give-ups and mercy under those floors count as clean evidence for nothing, but their records still count against (next paragraph). HAND STATES per look: asking (the hold fires with its category question), quiet (the hold fires, the piece lifts, the square breathes amber, the board dims, every tap is graded as today, but the line says only 'Hold on. You know this one. Tap it.'; the hint after a wrong tap and the naming after a second are unchanged), off (the hold does not open: gate.verdict returns suppressed 'hand' with the full facts, the move lands, the opponent takes as it always does, the record is logged 'landed' why 'hand', givenAway counts it, the close card captions it 'Knight to e5, a pawn was waiting: it landed.'). ALWAYS_HOLD (the mates look) and any verdict with netLoss >= GATE.BIG_LOSS (5) ignore the hand in every state. THE DIGEST. At storeGame every game appends one permanent digest line to holdon.v1.path.digest: { id, date, result, observed, again, captures, escapes, gifts: {offered, taken}, looks: { lookId: { n, w, netLoss } } } (n records, w their summed weight), about 120 bytes, kept to PATH.DIGEST_MAX (200) newest, never trimmed with the summaries. compute(digest, now) runs over the digest, so trimming the twelve full summaries and merging another device's games can never rewrite a stage he was shown. THE FOLD, game-major: for each digest line oldest to newest, for each look in ladder order, update state {stage: 'asking'|'quiet'|'off', run, woken, everFired}. Weight of a record: 1 when outcome is back and the first graded tap (taps[0]) was right or partial on whatever look it was graded on (a right tap on a K2 ask is not punished), else 2 (anyway, ended, landed, a back after a named or wrong first tap). DECAY runs over every non-again game, counted or not: at off, one record of any weight sends the look to quiet with woken true (the slip is named, the bare hold returns); two or more records in one game send it to asking; at quiet, any weight-2 record or two or more records send it to asking, a single weight-1 record keeps quiet; at asking nothing changes; run = 0 in every case; everFired = true. CLIMB runs only over counted games with zero records of the look: run += 1; asking -> quiet when run >= PATH.CLEAN_TO_QUIET (2) and the floor holds and the prerequisite (its stage after its own update for this same game) is at quiet or off, then run = 0; quiet -> off when run >= (woken ? PATH.WOKEN_TO_OFF (2) : PATH.QUIET_TO_OFF (1)) and the floor holds and the last PATH.OFF_WINDOW (5) counted games hold zero records of the look and (everFired or the look's positive evidence exists: gifts taken for free, escapes for their_last_move), then run = 0 and woken = false. A look with no record ever and no positive evidence therefore caps at quiet and is never announced as 'yours'. FLOORS are opportunity conditions read over a fixed trailing window of the last PATH.FLOOR_WINDOW (3) counted games including the current one, at every climb, independent of the run: pawns and takers none beyond the counted floor; takes_back captures summed >= PATH.CAPTURES_MIN (3); their_last_move escapes summed >= PATH.ESCAPES_MIN (2) or everFired; free gifts.offered summed >= PATH.GIFTS_MIN (2) and gifts.taken >= gifts.offered - 1; guards the digest holds at least PATH.GUARDS_HISTORY (5) counted games in all. PREREQUISITES gate the climb, never the measurement: takers needs pawns at quiet or off; takes_back needs takers; guards needs their_last_move; a gated look keeps counting its run and climbs in the same game its prerequisite does, judged against the prerequisite's stage in that game, not its final one. MATES: the hand never fades; words only: 'back' when the newest stored game of any kind holds a record of the kind; 'quiet' when the last PATH.MATE_WINDOW (5) counted games hold zero records and a record exists earlier in the digest; else 'asking'; a mate-win is not evidence either way. IDLE: when now minus the newest digest line's date (any kind) >= PATH.IDLE_DAYS (14), every off look reads quiet for the next game (plan.review true; 'It has been a while. I will hold a little more today.'); the ordinary fold restores or wakes it. NOT-YET on the face: a look with everFired false and fewer than three counted games collapses into one muted line; its hand is asking. CURRENT: the first look in ladder order at asking (mates excluded); when pawns and free are both at asking, the one with more records in the last three counted games, then the larger netLoss3 (material at stake), ties to pawns; if no look is at asking, the first at quiet; if every material look is off or capped quiet with everFired false, current is null and the next game opens 'There is nothing left for me to hold. Your move.' TRANSITIONS are a diff against holdon.v1.path.shown, the stages at the last time a line was said, written at newGame and endGame, and computed only when the newest digest line is the game this view just played; after a merge, shown is reset silently to the merged stages, so an OFF, SLIP or WAKE sentence is said only for a change his own last game caused. NEXT, in one sentence: the next game is always a real game from the start position, played with each look's hand at its stage, the gift notch following free, the opening line and the remembering question following current; the only other thing the model offers is the player's own worst moment of the current look as a link on the close card, never on load.

nodes.name_as_result: I see the pawn before my piece lands.
nodes.what_it_is: The look from their chair at the landing square, for the cheapest taker: before a knight, bishop, rook or queen lands, which enemy pawn reaches that square, whether or not the landing was itself a capture. The commonest way a game is lost under 1000 and the tutorial's own lesson (Nxe5 in the 6...d6 position, dxe5 answers). hanging_after_move with pawnAmongTakers true. Current by default on an empty log.
evidence: Against: every HoldRecord with category hanging_after_move and pawnAmongTakers true (any variant), outcome back (weight 1 when taps[0] was right or partial on whatever look it was graded on, else 2), anyway, ended or landed (weight 2), in any non-again game counted or not. v1 records: a pawn attacks record.to in record.fen after record.san per chess.js.

For: a counted game (observed >= 20, or a decisive result with observed >= 8; again false) with zero records of this kind. Punish-always makes every landing a test, so no further floor; the five-game off window and the one-record-ever rule carry the evidence for 'yours'.
Copy only, never the stage: the first tap's grade (taps[].ask kept) feeds the K3 facts and the close caption.
Ignored: tutorial holds, records in again games, cold-engine moves (not observed).
nodes.mastery_rule: asking -> quiet after two consecutive clean counted games (PATH.CLEAN_TO_QUIET 2); quiet -> off after one further clean counted game (QUIET_TO_OFF 1; WOKEN_TO_OFF 2 when woken) AND zero records in the last PATH.OFF_WINDOW (5) counted games AND at least one pawns record ever in the digest. Fixtures: one game with a pawns record then five clean counted games (observed 22-30) -> off at the sixth game, quiet at the third; the same with the clean games at observed 12 -> asking; five clean counted games with no pawns record ever -> quiet, never off, no OFF transition.
nodes.how_it_is_practised: While current: the next game's opening line names it with the countdown in words ('Still on the pawns. One more clean game and I ask with fewer words.'); a hold of this kind asks the remembering question at 0 ms when the newest stored game (counted or not) holds a record of this kind ('Hold on. The pawns again. Which one reaches that square? Tap it.', K3's validated question or COPY.PATH.QUESTION.pawns); the K2 prompt names it so a chosen ask leans toward what_takes_it or safe_square. The opponent is unchanged (the gift order is on the later list). At quiet: the hold fires with 'Hold on. You know this one. Tap it.'; Show me stays available. At off: no hold; the piece lands, the opponent takes, the close caption reads 'it landed'; the first off game opens 'I will not ask about the pawns today. They are yours.' (said once; holdon.v1.path.said).
nodes.retire_or_decay: off -> quiet (woken) on one record in any non-again game, counted or not (a knight hung at move eight of a game given up at move twelve wakes the hand), the next game opening 'The pawns, once, and I said nothing. I will ask again.'; off -> asking on two records in one game; quiet -> asking on any weight-2 record or two records in one game, the next game opening 'The pawns again. I am holding those once more.'; a woken look needs two clean counted games, not one, to re-quiet, and then five clean counted games in the off window to go off again. Fourteen days without a stored game makes off read quiet for one game. Nothing retires for good.

nodes.name_as_result: I see what takes my piece before it lands.
nodes.what_it_is: The same look when the taker is a knight, bishop, rook, queen or king and the move was not a capture: the line is longer and the counting of defenders starts to matter. hanging_after_move with pawnAmongTakers false and variant null (nc4_rook Nc4).
evidence: Against: HoldRecords with category hanging_after_move, pawnAmongTakers false, variant null, any outcome including landed, weighted as pawns.
For: a counted game with zero records of this kind; off needs the five-game window and one record ever, as pawns.
Copy only: first-tap grades.
nodes.mastery_rule: The same fold and constants as pawns, climbing only while pawns is at quiet or off in the same game (judged on pawns' stage after its own update for that game, game-major). Fixture: pawns and takers both fire in game 1 and are clean in games 2-7 -> takers quiet in the game pawns goes quiet and off in the game pawns goes off; a pawns weight-2 record appended as game 8 drops pawns to asking and leaves takers' stage and the earlier transitions untouched.
nodes.how_it_is_practised: While current: the opening line 'What takes it. Before the piece lands, look from their chair.'; the remembering question 'Hold on. Not a pawn this time. What reaches that square? Tap it.'. Quiet and off as pawns, with the look's own words in the announcements. No opponent change.
nodes.retire_or_decay: As pawns.

nodes.name_as_result: Before I take, I see what takes back.
nodes.what_it_is: The capture that loses to the recapture when no pawn is among the takers: a bishop takes on f7 and the king takes back (the tutorial's own first hold), a queen takes a defended pawn and a piece takes her. hanging_after_move with pawnAmongTakers false and variant 'takes_back'. Placed after the piece look because a player who still hangs pieces to quiet moves is not ready to count exchanges.
evidence: Against: HoldRecords with category hanging_after_move, pawnAmongTakers false, variant 'takes_back' (v1: 'x' in san and no pawn attacker), any outcome including landed, weighted as pawns.
For: a counted game with zero records of this kind.

Floor: captures summed over the last three counted games >= PATH.CAPTURES_MIN (3), from the per-game count of his applied moves that captured (a v1 game reads null and cannot satisfy it), read at every climb independently of the run.
nodes.mastery_rule: The same fold as pawns with the captures floor, climbing only while takers is at quiet or off. Fixtures: one game with a record, then five clean counted games with captures [1,1,1,1,1] -> off at the sixth; captures [0,0,0,0,0] -> asking; captures [2,2,1,1,1] -> off.
nodes.how_it_is_practised: While current: the opening line 'Before you take, what takes back.'; the remembering question 'Hold on. This one again. Before you take there: what takes back? Tap it.'; the Show me ghost (the capture and the recapture) is the practice. No opponent change. Quiet and off as pawns.
nodes.retire_or_decay: As pawns.

nodes.name_as_result: I answer what their last move pointed at.
nodes.what_it_is: The chess master's first look (lesson 0001): what did their last move attack, and is it answered. The look that castles into a lost bishop in the Ruy after 3...a6. ignored_attack with sub 'already'. Its place fourth on the ladder, with no prerequisite, is a deliberate departure from the curriculum order, because the gate's data shows the pawn landing is the commoner and cheaper event.
evidence: Against: HoldRecords with category ignored_attack and sub 'already', any outcome including landed, weighted as pawns (a partial tap on the attacker counts as right for the weight).

For: a counted game with zero records of this kind, plus escapes: the escaped reward (a non-pawn piece of his worth >= 2 attacked by the opponent's last move before his move, nothing of his hanging after, cpLoss < 200) recorded per game whether or not it was said, and produced beside free_taken on the same move rather than instead of it.

Floor: escapes summed over the last three counted games >= PATH.ESCAPES_MIN (2), or everFired; three clean games in which the opponent never attacked anything stay at asking and the face reads 'This is where we are.' without a count.
nodes.mastery_rule: The same fold as pawns with the escapes floor; no prerequisite. Fixtures: five clean counted games with escapes [1,1,0,1,1] and one earlier record -> off at the sixth; escapes [0,0,0,0,0] with no prior record -> asking.
nodes.how_it_is_practised: While current: the opening line 'Before your move, their last move. What did it touch?'; the remembering question 'Hold on. Their last move pointed at something of yours. Tap it.'; the 'You looked' reward wins the quiet budget over 'Free knight' when both apply in one move while this look is current (both are recorded either way); the K2 prompt names it so a chosen ask leans toward attacked_piece. The opponent is unchanged (threat shaping is on the later list). Quiet and off as pawns.
nodes.retire_or_decay: As pawns.

nodes.name_as_result: I take what is free.
nodes.what_it_is: A piece of theirs that nothing guards, walked past, including the opponent's own verified gifts. free_piece_ignored on the way down, the 'Free knight. You looked.' reward and the gift taken on the way up. The one look the opponent manufactures at a measured rate, and the look that owns the gift notch.
evidence: Against: HoldRecords with category free_piece_ignored, any outcome including landed (a landed record of this kind loses nothing of his and never counts in givenAway), weighted as pawns. A walked-past verified gift is already measured by the gate as free_piece_ignored held or landed, so no synthetic record is added for it.

For: rewards[] of kind free_taken and gifts.taken per game (offered when state().lastGift.verified, taken when his capture lands on gift.square), and a counted game with zero records of this kind; gifts taken count as positive evidence for the one-record-ever rule.
Floor: gifts.offered summed over the last three counted games >= PATH.GIFTS_MIN (2) and gifts.taken >= gifts.offered - 1, reachable at the measured 1.5-1.85 gifts per game.
nodes.mastery_rule: The same fold as pawns with the gifts floor; no prerequisite; eligible beside pawns at the bottom of the ladder. Fixtures: five clean counted games with gifts offered [1,1,1,1,1] taken the same -> off at the sixth; offered [0,0,0,0,0] -> asking; one verified gift walked past at off gives exactly one free record, quiet woken, not asking.
nodes.how_it_is_practised: This look owns the opponent's notch: plan.giftRate is 0.12 while free is at asking or quiet and 0.08 once it is off; the clean-game step-down in storeGame goes away and holdon.v1.giftRate is read once as a fallback and never written. While current: the opening line 'Something of theirs may be free today. Look before you plan.'; the remembering question 'Hold on. Something of theirs is free again. Tap it.'; the K2 prompt leans toward what_is_free; a free piece walked past this game (anyway or landed, netLoss >= 2) is offered as 'Play it again from here' on the close card. At off the walked-past piece lands silently and the close caption (COPY.CLOSE.FREE_STAYED, copy-checked) reads 'A free knight was there: it stayed.'
nodes.retire_or_decay: As pawns; a woken free returns the notch to 0.12 for the next game, which is the decay he feels: the opponent starts leaving pieces again.

nodes.name_as_result: I notice what my move leaves behind.
nodes.what_it_is: The two-piece look: the piece I move was guarding something, or standing in a line, and after it moves something else of mine falls. ignored_attack with sub 'lost_guard' or 'opened_line'. Rarer and subtler, so it sits later and climbs on a longer history. positions.json records opened_line (italian_nxe4 Nc3) and no lost_guard, so the lost_guard branch of nodeOf is covered by a synthetic record only.
evidence: Against: HoldRecords with category ignored_attack and sub 'lost_guard' or 'opened_line', any outcome including landed, weighted as pawns.
For: a counted game with zero records of this kind.
Floor: the digest holds at least PATH.GUARDS_HISTORY (5) counted games in all; and, as every look, off needs one record ever, so a guards look that has never fired caps at quiet and is never 'yours'.
nodes.mastery_rule: The same fold as pawns with the history floor, climbing only while their_last_move is at quiet or off. Fixtures: six clean counted games with no guards record ever -> quiet, not off, no OFF transition, and not_yet on the face until three counted games exist; seven counted games with one guards record in the first and six clean after -> off.
nodes.how_it_is_practised: While current: the opening line 'When a piece moves, what was it guarding?'; the remembering questions 'Hold on. The piece you are moving was guarding something. Tap it.' and 'Hold on. Your move opens a line again. Tap along it.'; 'Play it again from here' is the main practice. No opponent change. Quiet and off as pawns, for these two sub-cases only.
nodes.retire_or_decay: As pawns, with the decay announced in the next opening line ('A guard went missing last game. I will ask about those again.').

nodes.name_as_result: I see the mate next move, theirs and mine, and I never stalemate a won game.
nodes.what_it_is: Their check that mates, my mate on the board, and the stalemate that throws a win away: allowed_mate, missed_mate, allowed_stalemate. ALWAYS_HOLD; the hand never withdraws; the look lives on the ladder so the face can say so, and its state is words only.
evidence: Against: HoldRecords with category allowed_mate, missed_mate or allowed_stalemate, any outcome, in any non-again game (a four-move Scholar's loss counts).
Window: the last PATH.MATE_WINDOW (5) counted games for the 'quiet' word; the newest stored game of any kind for 'back'. A mate-win is not evidence (it says nothing about their check being seen).
nodes.mastery_rule: Words only: 'back' when the newest stored game holds a record; 'quiet' when the last five counted games hold zero records and a record exists earlier in the digest; else 'asking'. plan.hand always carries 'full' for all three categories; a unit test asserts the hand never excludes them whatever the log, and that a Scholar's mate loss (observed 3) sets 'back'.
nodes.how_it_is_practised: The hold itself, every time, with its full question in every state; never current; after a mate-loss the next opening line is 'When their queen is near your king, their check first.'; the face reads 'Always. This one I never let go.' and, when words-quiet, 'Always. Quiet for five games.' 'Play it again from here' is offered for a missed_mate or allowed_stalemate played anyway. The mate gift and the set finishing positions are on the later list.
nodes.retire_or_decay: Any record returns the words to 'back' at once. Nothing on the board changes, because nothing on the board ever faded.

Never the first screen, never reachable during play, a hold, the tutorial or before the first real game has ended. #close hides; #path, a sibling section in the same slot under the board, shows. The board stays the hero: a still of the current look's newest record (a scratch Chess from record.fen with record.san applied, board.setPosition, the moved piece lifted over record.to with a static amber ring, every other square dimmed by a .stage[data-view=path] rule, input locked, #board.dataset.state still 'over'); the start position when no record exists. Tapping a sentence re-aims the still at that look's newest record. Leaving restores the final position and the close card. The mirror's deferred read, when permissions.state('db') is 'prompt', fires when the close card is shown, so the platform dialog can sit over the card and never over this view or a board.

persistence.layers: localStorage is the always-there layer, every read and write through store.js in try/catch. The stages are never stored: compute() runs over the digest at boot, newGame() and endGame(). The digest (holdon.v1.path.digest, append-only, 200 newest lines) and shown (holdon.v1.path.shown) are stored facts, not stages; a missing or corrupt path key costs the announcements and Claude's lines, and the digest is rebuilt from the surviving summaries by digestOf(). The db + user mirror lights up only when both resolve in the viewer: the republish declares capabilities {sample: {}, db: {}, user: {}} in full with no rules. One document per viewer, db.doc('data/users/' + uid + '/holdon'), body { v: 2, updatedAt, games, flags, path: { k3, said, digest, shown } }; theme per device; consent per view and unstored. Flow and invariants, each with a scenario: (1) boot paints from localStorage at 0 ms; after first paint Promise.all([claude.use('db'), claude.use('user'), claude.use('permissions')]), uid = await user.id(); null anywhere means local only, silently. (2) permissions.state('db') 'granted' reads at boot; 'prompt' or no namespace defers the first read to the moment the close card is shown (state over, no tap, so the dialog sits over the card and never over a board, and Again waits on nothing); 'denied' or 'unavailable' means local only. (3) A view never writes before a successful read in that view (an exists:false snapshot counts); a first-session endGame on a fresh device queues its write behind that read, so one game on the phone can never overwrite twelve on the laptop. (4) The endGame write is get-then-set on one promise chain per document (a laptop tab left open for days merges the phone's games instead of overwriting them); the only loss case is a true simultaneous write. (5) After a merge localStorage is rewritten, shown is reset silently, and the opening line and this game's hand refresh from the merged path only while S.plies === 0, nothing is picked and S.tutorial is false; otherwise from the next game. (6) A new device plays the tutorial and one full game before any merged line can show unless permissions.state is 'granted' at boot, and the copy promises nothing across devices. sync.js exports merge(local, remote), pure and node-tested: games set-union by id sorted by date and trimmed (KEEP.GAMES non-again plus three again), digest set-union by id sorted by date trimmed to 200, flags OR, path.k3 from the newer game's date, said union, shown from the newer updatedAt; idempotent and commutative. Errors: invalid_argument marks the view read-only, unavailable retries once after a one-to-two-second random delay, quota_exceeded, resource_exhausted and revoked stop the mirror for the view; nothing is ever said about any of it; no onSnapshot. The harness stubs all of it: scripts/app_check.js's STUB_SCRIPT gains an in-memory db (get answering exists:false first, set replacing), a user with id 'u_test' and permissions.state() scripted through window.__stubCaps, with one store shared across two page instances for the two-device scenarios; only the live consent dialog and the real uid stay with Sambudh.
persistence.data_shape: GameSummary v2: { v: 2, id: Date.now().toString(36) + two random base-36 characters, date, result, givenAway, holds: [HoldRecord], freeTaken, playedAnyway, plies, backs, observed (committed player moves with a non-null verdict), captures, rewards: [{ kind: 'free_taken'|'escaped', ply, piece, said }], gifts: { offered, taken }, again, hand, review }. HoldRecord v2: { fen, san, category, sub, variant, pawnAmongTakers, taps: [{ square, grade, ask }], outcome: 'back'|'anyway'|'ended'|'landed'|'again', why: null|'pair'|'quiet'|'hand', answered, coachShown, said (trimmed to 120 characters, stored raw; masked only when it enters a prompt), netLoss, piece, to, best, answer: { squares, best, partial }, refutation, refutationFrom, ply, gameId }. Digest line: { id, date, result, observed, again, captures, escapes, gifts, looks: { lookId: { n, w, netLoss } } }. Keys: holdon.v1.games (KEEP.GAMES 12 non-again plus three again), holdon.v1.holds (unchanged at KEEP.HOLDS 30, still written for compatibility, read by nothing new), holdon.v1.path { v: 1, k3, said: [lookId], digest: [...], shown: {lookId: stage} }, holdon.v1.sync { uid, at }; holdon.v1.giftRate read once as a fallback and never written again.
persistence.migration_from_v1: None destructive; no key is renamed. path.norm(game) fills a v1 game at read time: observed = ceil(plies / 2), captures = null, rewards = [], gifts = { offered: 0, taken: 0 }, again = false, hand all 'full', review = false; each v1 hold gets pawnAmongTakers from chess.js (a pawn attacks record.to after record.san), variant from 'x' in san, taps[].ask = null, said = null, answer = null (never offered as a drill), why = null. On first boot after the update digestOf() builds the digest from the stored summaries (at most five), and from then on storeGame appends. A v1 game counts as counted by observed alone and as clean on the silence of its holds. The store test's KEEP.GAMES expectation (5 kept of 7 appended) is updated to the new trim rule. A unit test asserts that a v1 games array and its normalised v2 twin derive the same stages, and that norm() and digestOf() are idempotent.

final.first_session: Identical to today until the first close card: the tutorial dare on the Italian, the first hold, Show me, both buttons, no dialog, a real game, the holds, the counts. Nothing of the path is visible or felt before the first game ends: every look is at asking, the opponent gifts at 0.12 as today, and compute() has read an empty digest. On the first close card, under the counts, one template sentence in the coach's voice built from that game's holds ('Both holds today were a pawn you did not see. The pawns are what we are on.' or 'I never stopped your hand. The pawns are the first thing I watch.'), the --muted link 'Where you are', and, if he played a pawns hold anyway, 'Play it again from here' beside Again. If he pressed Hear me out at least once, K3 fires behind the card and his own sentence, with his squares masked, comes back in about a second; if not, no call and no dialog. In the viewer, the mirror's first read happens here, over the card, never over a board. If he taps 'Where you are', the board becomes a still of his own worst moment of that game, lifted and amber, and under it 'I see the pawn before it lands.' in ink with the amber dot and 'This is where we are. Twice this game.', one or two coach-blue lines for other looks that fired, the mates line, and one muted line 'Four more, not come up yet.'; [Back] returns him to the card. Game two opens with the pawns line and its first pawns hold asks the remembering question. He has felt the path twice before he has seen it once, and has seen no number anywhere but the close card's counts. Nothing fades in session one: the first thing he feels change is the opening line, the second the question that remembers, the third, around game three if games one and two were clean and counted, a hold that comes with fewer words; the hand comes off no earlier than game six, after five clean counted games of a look that has actually fired, and it is announced before it happens.

risks: The faded hand lets a real piece fall that the MVP would have held: the defences are the bare stage before off, five clean counted games and a record ever before 'yours', the announcement before the first off game, mates and five-point losses never faded, slips counted in every game so a wrong 'off' costs one landed piece and no more, and the slip named on the same close card; if the first landed piece reads as a trap, QUIET_TO_OFF rises to 2, a named constant.

Silence is thin evidence for the rarer looks and the counted floor measures moves, not chances: the trailing-window floors, the off window, the one-record-ever cap and the observed denominator are the cheap defence; the synthetic-player test prints the false-'yours' share before the first real week; the exposure proxy is first on the later list.

The digest is a second copy of the facts: digestOf() rebuilds it from the summaries, a unit test asserts digestOf is idempotent and that the rebuilt digest gives the same stages, and the digest line is written in the same storeGame call as the summary.

Changing gate.verdict touches the recorded-position test: the hand is a strictly additive suppression reason with the 2195 checks unchanged when it is absent; rewards() is a new export beside reward().

The log additions, the view and the drill all touch game.js in one iteration: every field is additive, v1 records are normalised at read time, and the cut list is ordered (the drill, then K3, then the still in the path view, then the mirror) if path.js is not green by mid-iteration.

K3's question must be true of every hold of its kind without Claude seeing a position: the piece-word allowlist and the empty square set make that safe; masking his quoted words keeps the where line possible; a high __coachRejectsBy on real calls means the prompt is tightened, never the validator loosened.
Quoting his own words back: the prompt marks the text as data, the validator caps and bans, but taste is not validated; the where line is one sentence on his private page.
Views that never press Hear me out never consent, so K3 never fires for them; accepted as the MVP accepted it for K1.

The mirror is now proven headless against a stub, which is a model of the platform and not the platform: the live dialog, the real uid and the real error codes are the two-device check, stated as Sambudh's.
'Hold on. You know this one. Tap it.' can read smug after a wrong tap: the hint and naming stay, and the line is one COPY key.

The path view is one argument away from a dashboard: the no-digit assertion, the one-dot rule, the collapsed line, the refusal of rings, headings and lanes, and copy_check are the defence; if the first phone screenshot reads as a syllabus, the list collapses to the current look plus 'and six more'.

A short-game player never produces a counted game and never climbs: honest, said once in words, and his slips still count; OBSERVED_MIN and OBSERVED_DECISIVE_MIN are named constants the first week's log can move.

The harness budget is now measured rather than hoped: two scenario files and a five-minute budget per pass; if the machine is slower the budget is raised in one place, never the scenarios cut silently.

The build has not started and the chess study holds no games: every rule here is designed against synthetic logs, and the first real week may move the constants; that is what the named constants are for.

nodeOf: pawnAmongTakers is now the first split, so Nxe5 in the 6...d6 position is the pawns look whether or not it captured; Bxf7+ with the king taking back stays takes_back; an explicit expected-look table over positions.json and tutorial.json is a test.

Counted game: observed redefined as committed moves with a non-null verdict; the plies clause dropped; a decisive result counts at observed >= 8 (OBSERVED_DECISIVE_MIN), so quick resignations and quick mates are no longer censored.
Decay runs over every non-again game, counted or not; only the clean-game climbs require a counted game; the mates 'back' word reads the newest stored game.
Floors read a fixed trailing window of the last three counted games (FLOOR_WINDOW), never the run; CAPTURES_MIN lowered to 3 to match; all floor fixtures rewritten per game.

The fold runs over an append-only digest (holdon.v1.path.digest, 200 lines) so trimming the summaries and merging another device's games cannot rewrite a stage; transitions are a diff against the stages last shown (holdon.v1.path.shown), computed only for the game this view just played, and reset silently after a merge.
Fold order pinned: game-major, looks in ladder order within a game, prerequisites judged on their stage in that game; fixture added.

Off now requires zero records in the last five counted games (OFF_WINDOW) and at least one record of the look ever (or its positive evidence); a look that has never fired caps at quiet and is never 'yours'; a reported synthetic-player test prints the false-'yours' share.
Record weight: a right or partial first tap on any graded look (including a K2 ask) is weight 1.

Rewards: gate.rewards() returns both free_taken and escaped; escaped requires the opponent's last move as the attacker; both are recorded with a said flag; the synthetic 'gift not taken' record is deleted (the gate already measures it).
Mates words: a mate-win is no longer positive evidence; 'quiet' needs five clean counted games and a prior record.
Idle clock reads the newest stored game of any kind; pawns/free tie-break is record count then material at stake.

K3 question cap raised to four sentences to match validate.js's splitter; test case corrected; a node check runs every COPY.PATH.QUESTION through validateK3; his quoted words are masked (squares and SAN replaced) before entering the prompt; rejects counted per field.
Shown holds separated from landed verdicts: 'times', holdsCount, remembered() and K1's holdsSoFar count only back/anyway/ended; the quiet-rule scenario asserts the close line still says two stops.

Persistence invariants written as rules with scenarios: never write before a read in a view, the deferred read fires over the close card and never from Again, get-then-set at endGame, the ply-0 refresh excludes the tutorial, a new device plays one game before any merged line; the mirror is stubbed in app_check.js (db, user, permissions via window.__stubCaps, a store shared across two pages) and asserted headless.

decisions_rejected: Declined the nodeOf option (a) (keep variant first and move every pawns acceptance to Nd4/Ba6 or a new recorded position): option (b), pawnAmongTakers first, keeps the tutorial's own Nxe5 as the pawns lesson, keeps every acceptance on recorded positions, and matches the beginner's sentence (the pawn before the piece lands, capture or not).

Declined the cheap exposure proxy (pieceMoves floored over the window) for this iteration: with the five-game off window and the one-record-ever rule the false-'yours' rate is bounded and printed by the synthetic-player test; the proxy is first on the later list and is added if the first real weeks show passive games passing.
Declined dropping holdon.v1.holds: nothing new reads it, but removing it changes the MVP's store test and the live page's key set for no gain; it stays at 30 and keeps being written.

Declined moving their_last_move to the top of the ladder to match the curriculum: the gate's data makes the pawn landing the commoner and cheaper event; the departure is now stated in the node rather than hidden.

Declined removing the mates row from the ladder: the face needs to say 'Always. This one I never let go.' somewhere, and a row with words-only state is the cheapest honest place; it stays an open question.

Declined onSnapshot: get-then-set at endGame closes the open-tab clobber the critic found; the remaining loss is a true simultaneous write, which one person on one device at a time does not produce; it stays an open question.

Declined storing the stages: the digest and shown are stored facts (what happened, what was said), not the ladder; compute() stays a pure function recomputed at every boot, which keeps the model testable and drift-free.

Declined 'play five real games before the build starts' as a spec change: it is the right next action for Sambudh and is named in the progress entries, but it does not block committing the contract or building the pure module, which is the next milestone either way.

Declined keeping the three-minute harness criterion with a faster harness: the measured run is already 221 s, so the honest fix is a measured budget per pass and a second scenario file, not a promise the machine cannot keep.
